findings.impact: No correctness bug at present (160.5 cycles is enough for both the divider and VREFINT). It removes the headroom the two-slot design was meant to give. Only matters if a future high-Z channel is added.
findings.recommendation: Optional: set SamplingTimeCommon2 to a longer time (e.g. 640.5 cycles) and assign VBAT/VREFINT to COMMON_2 to harden against settling error on the 86k divider. Verify against actual PCLK1 first.

findings.description: The load-bearing logic introduced by commit 04d06d1 ('distinguish ADC HAL failure from a genuine 0 reading') — i.e. ADC_ReadValueChecked returning false without writing *out, and SWS holding s_last_valid_adc on false vs accepting a true-0 — has no unit test. test_sws.c does not reference ADC_ReadValueChecked; test_bat_auto_shutdown.c reimplements VBAT logic locally rather than driving MGR_BAT/adc. NULL-out guard (line 115) also untested.
findings.impact: The exact regression the commit fixed (dead ADC flipping SWS to SURFACE → spurious TX in a sealed unit) is unguarded by CI. A refactor that makes ADC_ReadValueChecked write *out on failure, or makes SWS accept the failure value, would pass all 506 tests silently.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit case with a mockable ADC_ReadValueChecked: assert (a) false leaves *out untouched and SWS keeps last valid sample, (b) true+0 is accepted as a real reading, (c) NULL out returns false. Mock HAL_ADC_* per the existing framework.

dead_code: ADC_ReadValue() (adc.c:101-106, proto adc.h:32) is a genuine orphan — no live caller in the whole tree (only mgr_sws uses ADC_ReadValueChecked). Not config-gated; it is a retained-but-unused legacy public API. The trailing `return;` after Error_Handler() at adc.c:40 and adc.c:53 are unreachable in practice (Error_Handler never returns) — defensive/dead but harmless. No other dead code; all of MX_ADC_Init/DeInit, MspInit/MspDeInit, ADC_ReadValueChecked are reached in the UW_DOPPLER sealed config.
test_coverage: Partially covered. The HW glue (MX_ADC_Init/DeInit, Msp*) is not unit-testable (real registers). The testable policy logic — ADC_ReadValueChecked's failure==don't-touch-*out contract and NULL guard — is NOT covered by any Tests/unit suite (test_sws.c and test_bat_auto_shutdown.c reimplement/avoid the real path). Concrete gap: no test pins the 04d06d1 regression fix (HAL-fail vs genuine-0). Recommend a mocked ADC read test as described in the test-gap finding.

role: Defines the const 256-byte application_header struct placed at flash 0x08000200 (.app_header section) that the bootloader reads to validate/locate the app before jumping.
compiled_in: all (in TARGET_SRCS at Makefile:176, every APP/BOARD/COMM; section kept via KEEP in STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:57-62 and -j .app_header in objcopy Makefile:702)

findings.description: The header is shipped with permanent placeholder values: app_size=0xFFFFFFFF (:91), app_entry_point=0xFFFFFFFF (:92), app_crc32=0xFFFFFFFF (:96), header_crc32=0xFFFFFFFF (:97). The file comments repeatedly claim these are 'filled by create_dfu.py'. They are NOT. Tools/create_dfu.py (the only DFU tool the Makefile invokes, Makefile:722) merely extracts the binary, prints a CRC, and discards it (create_dfu.py:111-127) -- it never patches the .app_header bytes. No post-link patch step exists in the Makefile (verified: only -j .app_header at Makefile:702, no objcopy --update-section, no separate patcher). The only code that builds a real header is Tools/dfu_tool.py:create_app_header (dfu_tool.py:262-294), a separate manual host tool that fabricates its OWN 256-byte header and prepends it to a raw .bin -- it never modifies the compiled application_header struct. So the struct ships exactly as written here.
findings.impact: The bootloader's strong validation path is permanently dead in production. bl_validate_app_header (Bootloader/Src/bl_main.c:713) rejects the shipped header because app_size==0xFFFFFFFF > APP_MAX_SIZE, so bl_validate_app_crc (bl_main.c:730, which CRC-checks the whole app image against app_crc32) is never reached. bl_check_app_valid silently falls back to the legacy vector-table-only sanity check (bl_main.c:680-692). Net for the sealed deployment: the promised app-image integrity check (catch a corrupted/partial DFU before jumping) NEVER runs. A truncated or bit-rotted app that still has a plausible SP/PC at 0x08000000 will be jumped into. Not an immediate brick, but it removes the anti-brick guarantee the header was built to provide.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) wire a real post-link patch into the Makefile .bin/.hex/dfu recipe (objcopy --update-section .app_header=patched, computing app_size + CRC-32/MPEG-2 over the app image and writing header_crc32), OR (b) if the header is intentionally decorative and the BL legacy fallback is the real boot gate, delete the false 'filled by create_dfu.py' comments and document that app_size/app_crc32 are unused so no one trusts a non-existent integrity check. Do not leave the comments asserting a guarantee the build does not deliver.

findings.description: header_crc32 is a genuine orphan field. No code anywhere reads it: the bootloader never validates the header's own CRC (grep of Bootloader for header_crc32 finds only the struct definition in bl_app_header.h:52; bl_validate_app_header at bl_main.c:695-722 checks magic/version/app_start_addr/app_size/min_bl_version but never header_crc32). It is also never written (placeholder 0xFFFFFFFF, per finding above). dfu_tool.py computes a header_crc but only for the header IT fabricates, not this struct.
findings.impact: Tamper/corruption of the header block itself goes undetected even on the path where the header is honored. Pure latent confusion -- a maintainer may assume header self-integrity exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement a bl_validate_header_crc check in the bootloader OR drop the field's pretense (keep as reserved). At minimum remove the 'Filled by create_dfu.py' comment at :56/:97.

findings.description: hw_compatibility is hardcoded to HW_COMPAT_STM32WL55 | HW_COMPAT_KINEIS_V10 | HW_COMPAT_SPI (:106). For the sealed target (APP=UW_DOPPLER, COMM=UART) the SPI flag is wrong and HW_COMPAT_UART (0x10, defined in bl_app_header.h:98) is never set. The value is also config-blind: it does not vary with the COMM/BOARD build flags. Note the bootloader never reads hw_compatibility (bl_app_compatible at bl_app_header.h:136-139 only checks min_bl_version), so this is currently inert.
findings.impact: Field is misleading metadata; if a future bootloader ever gates the jump on hw_compatibility, a UART-sealed unit would advertise SPI-only and could be rejected (brick on update). Today: cosmetic only.
findings.recommendation: Derive hw_compatibility from the build flags (set HW_COMPAT_UART for USE_UART_DRIVER, HW_COMPAT_SPI for USE_SPI_DRIVER) or drop the SPI flag for the UART build. Document that the BL currently ignores it.

findings.description: build_date is initialized from __DATE__, whose format is 'Mmm dd yyyy' (e.g. 'Jun 20 2026'), but bl_app_header.h:56 documents the field as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' and dfu_tool.py:282 writes that ISO-ish format. The two header producers disagree on format, and __DATE__ carries no time. The comment '__DATE__ is 11 chars' (:101) is correct (11 chars + NUL = 12 <= 16, no overflow), but the format contract is violated.
findings.impact: Cosmetic/provenance only -- a host tool parsing build_date as ISO will misparse the compiled-in value. No memory issue.
findings.recommendation: If build provenance matters, have the Makefile inject a real BUILD_DATE string (it already computes $(BUILD_DATE), Makefile:722) via -D into this field, matching the documented format; otherwise relax the header-comment contract to accept __DATE__ form.

findings.description: git_commit is hardcoded to "unknown" and never overwritten (no build patches the struct). The repo build already computes $(current_repo_commit) (passed to create_dfu.py at Makefile:722) but it never reaches this compiled field.
findings.impact: Field-deployed/sealed units carry no traceable firmware commit in the in-flash header. Forensic/provenance gap for a 12-month unrecoverable deployment.
findings.recommendation: Inject the short commit via -DGIT_COMMIT=... from the Makefile into this initializer (string, <=15 chars + NUL), or stop advertising the field as meaningful.

findings.description: Duplicated source-of-truth: APP_HEADER_MAGIC/VERSION/SIZE, the struct layout, and the version-pack expression are independently redefined here, in Bootloader/Inc/bl_config.h:199-200, bl_app_header.h:36-73/:83, and Tests/unit/test_app_header.c:15-55. The app uses an ad-hoc pack ((MAJOR<<16)|(MINOR<<8)|PATCH at :26) instead of bl_app_header.h's APP_VERSION_PACK macro (:83). There is no _Static_assert(sizeof(app_header_t)==256) in THIS file (only in bl_app_header.h:73), so a layout drift in app_header.c alone would not be caught at app compile time.
findings.impact: Layout/constant drift between the four copies would silently break BL<->app contract; the app TU itself has no size guard.
findings.recommendation: Add _Static_assert(sizeof(app_header_t)==256,...) and _Static_assert(offsetof checks) in app_header.c, or share a single header. Reuse APP_VERSION_PACK rather than the inline shift expression.

dead_code: No dead functions (file has no functions). header_crc32 field is a genuine orphan (never read or written by any live consumer -- see finding). app_crc32/app_size/app_entry_point are not dead per se (the BL reads them in bl_validate_app_crc/bl_jump_to_app) but are shipped with placeholder 0xFFFFFFFF, which forces the BL down its legacy fallback so the header-CRC branch is effectively unreachable in the production image. signature[16], reserved1/2/3, reserved[144] are intentional config-gated/future-reserved padding (zero-init, contributes to the required 256-byte size). The struct itself is force-kept via __attribute__((used)) (:80) + KEEP in the linker (.ld:60), so it is NOT removed despite having no C-code referrer.
test_coverage: Partial and misaligned. Tests/unit/test_app_header.c exercises validation logic but against a LOCALLY redefined struct/constants, NOT the real application_header instance -- and it uses APP_FLASH_BASE=0x08008100 (test_app_header.c:18), the stale pre-flip address, whereas the shipped app uses 0x08000000 (app_header.c:20,:90). Gaps: (1) no test asserts the shipped application_header has a VALID app_size/app_crc32 (would have caught the 0xFFFFFFFF placeholder shipping bug -- the central finding); (2) no test verifies app_header.c's struct layout/size matches bl_app_header.h byte-for-byte (offsetof per field); (3) no test that create_dfu.py output actually patches the .app_header bytes (it doesn't). Recommend a build-artifact test that parses the produced .bin at offset 0x200 and asserts magic==KINE, header_size==256, app_size in (0, APP_MAX_SIZE], app_crc32 matches a recompute, app_start_addr==0x08000000.

role: CubeMX-generated MX_GPIO_Init(): enables GPIOA/B/C/H clocks, blankets unused pins to analog (config-gated per COMM/BOARD/APP), and configures PC0 (PA_PSU_EN) and PC1 (PA_PSU_SEL/VSEL) as push-pull outputs. Called at boot and on every STOP2 wake (mgr_lpm_uw.c:1067).
compiled_in: all (always linked; body branches on USE_SPI_DRIVER/USE_UART_DRIVER, SMD_STDALONE, USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP). Sealed target = UART + SMD_STDALONE + UW_DOPPLER.

findings.description: On SMD_STDALONE, MX_GPIO_Init() unconditionally configures PC1 (PA_PSU_SEL = TPS63901 VSEL) as OUTPUT_PP and drives it HIGH (lines 168/174). This is INTENTIONAL at boot (matches main.c:733-745 which drives PC1 HIGH bare-metal pre-clock for 3V3-mode robustness), but MX_GPIO_Init is ALSO re-invoked on every STOP2 wake (mgr_lpm_uw.c:1067). mcu_misc.c:106-111 documents the opposite rule: 'on STDALONE leave PC1 high-Z, driving it re-programs the buck-boost output while PA pulls inrush = guaranteed brownout.' The two are reconciled only by sequencing (VSEL is re-driven HIGH=3V3 at wake, PA inrush happens later via MCU_MISC_turn_on_pa which does NOT touch SEL on STDALONE). The risk: any future wake path that calls MX_GPIO_Init while VSEL was deliberately set LOW (1V8 power-save via MCU_MISC_VSEL_set(false)) will silently snap it back to 3V3, defeating the power-save and momentarily glitching VSYS. mgr_lpm_uw.c relies on this exact 're-drive HIGH on wake' behavior (comment at mgr_lpm_uw.c:160), so it is currently load-bearing and correct — but it is an implicit, undocumented coupling on a brownout-sensitive pin.
findings.impact: Sealed deployment: if any code drops VSEL to 1V8 and then a wake/re-init runs MX_GPIO_Init, VSEL is forced back to 3V3 with no log — power-save silently lost. Worse, the runtime drive itself is a glitch source on the TPS63901 feedback node; the codebase elsewhere treats driving SEL as a brownout hazard. The behavior is only safe because of an undocumented call-ordering invariant.
findings.recommendation: Document the invariant explicitly at gpio.c:167 ('PC1 is re-driven HIGH on every wake by design; any 1V8 power-save MUST be re-applied AFTER MX_GPIO_Init, never before'). Consider gating the PC1 drive in MX_GPIO_Init behind a 'first boot' check, or centralizing VSEL ownership in MCU_MISC_VSEL_* so gpio.c does not silently override it.

findings.description: Comment rot / contradictory guidance. Lines 58-61 wrap the non-STDALONE PA_PSU_SEL SET in '#if !defined(SMD_STDALONE)' with the comment 'on STDALONE, PC1 = TPS63901 SEL — leave high-Z.' But 100 lines later (167-174), the SAME file unconditionally drives PC1 HIGH as OUTPUT_PP on STDALONE. A reader of lines 58-61 concludes PC1 is left analog/high-Z on STDALONE, which is FALSE. The line-145-149 comment block gives the correct, opposite rationale ('drive actively, R11 10M alone could droop'). Two comments in one file assert contradictory pin states for the same net.
findings.impact: High-confusion landmine on a brownout-critical pin. A future maintainer trusting lines 58-59 could 'fix' the line-167 drive by removing it, reverting to high-Z and reintroducing the LSE/PLL-at-1V8 margin problem main.c:733-740 was written to prevent. No runtime effect today.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the line-59 comment to: 'On STDALONE we SKIP this early non-STDALONE SET; PC1 is driven HIGH below at lines 167-174 instead (active 3V3, see line 145 block).' Remove the misleading 'leave high-Z' phrasing.

findings.description: Dead store. GPIO_InitStruct.Pin is assigned a 10-pin mask (PA12|PA11|PA0|PA6|PA7|PA4|PA5|PA8|PA10|PA9) at lines 64-66, but the very next use of GPIO_InitStruct.Pin is an unconditional reassignment in BOTH the USE_SPI_DRIVER branch (line 82) and the USE_UART_DRIVER branch (line 91). The mask written at 64-66 is never read. The trailing '|GPIO_PIN_8|GPIO_PIN_10|GPIO_PIN_9' also no longer matches the descriptive comment at 62-63 ('PA12 PA11 PA0 PA6 PA7 PA4 PA5').
findings.impact: None functionally (optimizer drops it). Misleads readers into thinking these pins are configured by this statement; the stale comment compounds it.
findings.recommendation: Delete lines 62-66 (the orphan assignment and its stale comment), or fold them into the active per-driver assignments.

findings.description: No #else for the COMM selector. The GPIOA config sets GPIO_InitStruct.Pin and .Mode only inside '#if defined(USE_SPI_DRIVER) ... #elif defined(USE_UART_DRIVER) ... #endif' (lines 81-105). If a build defines neither (or misspells the macro), neither .Pin nor .Mode is set for this block, yet HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOA, ...) at line 108 still runs — using the stale .Pin from the dead store at 64-66 and .Mode left from the {0} init (GPIO_MODE_INPUT=0). That silently reconfigures 10 PA pins as floating inputs with no diagnostic. The GPIOB block (121-138) has the same structure (no #else; .Pin/.Mode only set per-driver), so on a no-driver build HAL_GPIO_Init(GPIOB) runs with whatever .Pin survived from the GPIOA path.
findings.impact: Mis-configuration is build-system-dependent and silent. Today both COMM modes are always defined, so unreachable — but there is no compile-time guard (no #error) catching a future Makefile flag rename, which the project's own CLAUDE.md flags as a recurring trap ('make does not track flag changes').
findings.recommendation: Add '#else\n#error "COMM driver (USE_UART_DRIVER/USE_SPI_DRIVER) not defined"' after the #elif, for both the GPIOA and GPIOB selectors. Compile-time, zero runtime cost.

findings.description: Commented-out pin fragment '//GPIO_PIN_3 |' left inline in both the SPI and UART GPIOB masks. PB3 = SWO on this board (and the optional REED_WKUP3 wake pin). Leaving it as a dangling comment inside an expression obscures intent: it is unclear whether PB3 is deliberately NOT forced to analog (to preserve SWO / a reed wake source) or was an oversight. The omission appears intentional (PB3 must stay available for SWO/REED), but the dead '//' fragment reads like leftover debugging.
findings.impact: Maintainability only. A future edit could un-comment GPIO_PIN_3, forcing PB3 to analog and killing SWO / the BSP_REED_ON_WKUP3 wake path on a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Replace '//GPIO_PIN_3 |' with a real comment: '/* PB3 deliberately omitted: SWO + optional REED_WKUP3 wake — must not be analog */'.

findings.description: All four GPIO port clocks (GPIOA/B/C/H) are enabled and left enabled. GPIOH only carries PH3 (set to analog at 177-180; it is the only PH pin used, likely OSC). On the sealed UW_DOPPLER path MX_GPIO_Init runs on every STOP2 wake; the IOPENR bits persist but GPIO clock gating is negligible vs STOP2 retention, so this is informational. No teardown of unused-port clocks, but STOP2 gates them anyway.
findings.impact: Negligible (microamps-level, and STOP2 stops the clock tree). Listed for completeness only — not a deploy concern.
findings.recommendation: No action required. If micro-optimizing wake energy, GPIOH clock could be disabled after PH3 init, but the saving is below measurement noise.

findings.description: No unit test exercises the config-selection logic of MX_GPIO_Init. The function is pure register/HAL setup (HW glue), so direct unit testing has limited value, BUT the per-config pin-mask selection encodes load-bearing invariants that ARE testable as compile-time assertions: (a) on UW_DOPPLER, SWS pins PA11/PA12 must NOT be in the GPIOA analog mask (currently guaranteed by the line-100 '#if !defined(USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP)' guard); (b) on STDALONE, LED/REED/LATCH/VBAT_EN pins (PA1, PB4-7, PB9) must NOT be in the analog masks. These are silent if a future edit drops a guard. Grep of Tests/ found no reference to MX_GPIO_Init or gpio.c.
findings.impact: A regression that accidentally forces a SWS or REED pin to analog (e.g., dropping a #if guard) would brick the dive/wake path on a sealed unit and pass all existing unit tests.
findings.recommendation: Add _Static_assert-style compile-time guards (or a small host-compiled test) asserting that the GPIOA analog mask excludes SWS_IN_Pin/SWS_OUT_Pin under UW_DOPPLER, and the GPIOB mask excludes REED/LATCH pins under STDALONE. Cheap insurance against guard-drop regressions.

dead_code: One dead store (gpio.c:64-66: GPIO_InitStruct.Pin mask overwritten before any read on every reachable config — genuine orphan, not config-gated). The '#if !defined(SMD_STDALONE)' branches (lines 58-61, 92-94, 97-99, 128-135) are config-gated dead code on the sealed STDALONE target — intentional, correct (those pins are LEDs/REED/I2C/latch owned by other drivers on STDALONE). The '#if !defined(USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP)' PA11/PA12 exclusions (lines 84-86, 100-102) are config-gated — intentional (SWS owns PA11/PA12 on UW_DOPPLER). No truly orphaned functions (single public symbol MX_GPIO_Init, called from main.c:806 and mgr_lpm_uw.c:1067).
test_coverage: n/a as direct unit test (pure HAL/register glue, no mockable logic return). However the config-gated pin-mask SELECTION is a testable invariant currently uncovered: nothing asserts SWS pins (PA11/PA12) stay out of the analog mask under UW_DOPPLER, nor that REED/LATCH/LED pins stay out under STDALONE. A dropped #if guard would silently brick the dive/wake path and pass all 506 existing tests. Recommend compile-time _Static_assert guards (see test-gap finding).

role: MCU entry point: early reset/wake handling (SRAM-preserve OB, DFU-jump, LSE/LSI clock, retention init), peripheral bring-up, Kineis task/queue registration, IDLE-task LPM gate, and Error_Handler.
compiled_in: all (single TU per build; large parts config-gated by APP/BOARD/COMM. Sealed target = APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART)

findings.description: The cold-boot vs fault-reset gate that decides whether to run Sram2_Init() reads the LIVE RCC->CSR ('uint32_t csr = RCC->CSR;' at 877, 'boot_rcc_csr = RCC->CSR;' at 893). But __HAL_RCC_CLEAR_RESET_FLAGS() at line 753 already wiped CSR (sets RMVF) whenever PINRSTF was set. Per RM0453 §RCC_CSR (p.341, bit 26): on STM32WL an internal reset (IWDG/SFT/BOR/WWDG) also drives the bidirectional NRST line, so PINRSTF is set alongside IWDGRSTF/SFTRSTF on essentially every reset. The PINRST branch (752-755) therefore fires and clears the flags before line 877 reads them — so '!(csr & (RCC_CSR_IWDGRSTF | RCC_CSR_SFTRSTF))' evaluates TRUE on an IWDG/software reset, and Sram2_Init() runs. The correct, pre-clear value was already captured into g_boot_rcc_csr_raw at line 712 but is not used here.
findings.impact: On a watchdog (IWDG) or software reset (MGR_ERR_logAndReset / Error_Handler / fault-handler NVIC_SystemReset) in the sealed UW_DOPPLER unit, Sram2_Init() wrongly re-initialises the .data2/.bss2 RAM2 sections — wiping the forensic event log (mgr_evtlog .retentionRamBss), TX stats (mgr_txstats/mgr_rate) and other .retentionRamData/.retentionRamBss that were deliberately placed in retention RAM to SURVIVE these exact reset classes. Directly defeats the retention design described in the same comment (872-879) and in the linker (.bss2/.data2 vs .retention_noload). Crash-loop counter itself survives (it is in NOLOAD) but post-mortem forensics on a fielded brick are lost.
findings.recommendation: Use the preserved pre-clear value, not the live register: 'if (!(g_boot_rcc_csr_raw & (RCC_CSR_IWDGRSTF | RCC_CSR_SFTRSTF))) Sram2_Init();' at 878, and replace the line-893 'boot_rcc_csr = RCC->CSR;' with g_boot_rcc_csr_raw (it is only used for logging anyway). Add a unit test mirroring the decision table (IWDG/SFT/BOR/PIN/cold -> Sram2_Init yes/no).

findings.description: Three unbounded busy-waits run at the very start of main(), long before the IWDG is armed (MGR_WDG_init is only reached via KNS_APP_uw_doppler_init at main.c:1034 -> kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1616). 'while ((FLASH->SR & FLASH_SR_BSY) != 0U);' (484, 493) and 'while ((PWR->CR1 & PWR_CR1_DBP) == 0);' (521) have no timeout.
findings.impact: If FLASH never clears BSY (latched flash error during a marginal-VDD OB program) or DBP never reads back set, the sealed unit hangs forever with no watchdog to recover it — an unrecoverable field brick. Low probability (these are software-settable / self-clearing bits) but the consequence is terminal for an epoxy-sealed deployment.
findings.recommendation: Bound each wait with a loop counter (a few ms worth of iterations) and on timeout fall through / NVIC_SystemReset() rather than spin forever. The OB-program path is already correctly gated behind the PVD; extend the same defensive posture to its waits.

findings.description: g_boot_pwr_sr1_raw is written at 896 (mirrored from boot_pwr_sr1) but never read anywhere in the firmware — the only other reference is a doc comment in mgr_lpm_uw.h:244. By contrast g_boot_pwr_extscr_raw (693/715) and g_boot_rcc_csr_raw (686/712) ARE read by mgr_lpm_uw.c / mgr_gesture.c / kns_app_uw_doppler.c. So g_boot_pwr_sr1_raw is a write-only global (dead store).
findings.impact: Harmless but misleading: a future reader assumes the SR1 wake flags are consumed by the app (the comment at 693-694 implies so). Slight code rot.
findings.recommendation: Either remove g_boot_pwr_sr1_raw (and the local boot_pwr_sr1 mirror) or add the intended reader. If kept for forensic logging only, mark it as such; it is already logged in the DEBUG BOOT trace, so the global mirror is redundant.

findings.description: Seven non-static global g_dfu_debug_* variables and their write sites in check_dfu_request() are explicitly labelled 'DFU debug variables'. No code in the repo reads them (grep: only main.c). They are unconditionally compiled (not behind DEBUG) and ship in the production image. CLAUDE.md mandates removing debug markers in the same PR as the fix and forbids shipping them.
findings.impact: ~28 bytes of always-resident .bss plus dead writes on every boot in the early, watchdog-less path. No functional harm, but violates the project's no-ship-debug rule and adds RAM/cycles to the sealed build.
findings.recommendation: Gate the g_dfu_debug_* capture behind #ifdef DEBUG (matching request_dfu_mode's own debug block at 621-634) or remove entirely. Keep only the functional flag read/clear and the bootloader jump.

findings.description: RTC_WKUP_IRQHandler() is invoked synchronously from main thread context to 'simulate' a possible RTC wake after SHUTDOWN/STANDBY exit; RTC_Alarm_IRQHandler() is commented out just above (1069). Calling an ISR from thread context is intentional here (HAL handler is reentrant-safe and only acts if the flag is set), but it is fragile and only covers the SHUTDOWN/STANDBY exit cases. For the sealed UW_DOPPLER target the duty path uses STOP2 (LPM_getMode()==STOP/STOP2), which takes the 1072 'case STOP/SLEEP: break;' branch and does NOT run this simulated handler.
findings.impact: Not a defect for STOP2 (real RTC IRQ fires normally on STOP exit), but the commented-out RTC_Alarm line (1069) is comment-rot: if any path ever relied on an alarm-driven wake from SHUTDOWN, it would be silently dropped. Confirm the sealed design never uses RTC alarm wake.
findings.recommendation: Delete the commented-out RTC_Alarm_IRQHandler() line (1069) if alarms are unused, or document why only the wake-up-timer handler is simulated.

findings.description: Bare-metal PC1 drive-HIGH for the SMD_STDALONE 1V8/3V3 VSEL strap enables GPIOC clock (RCC_AHB2ENR_GPIOCEN), writes BSRR, then read-modify-writes GPIOC->MODER/OTYPER directly before MX_GPIO_Init(). The MODER RMW assumes PC1 is at its reset MODER state; on a warm reset where MX_GPIO_Init already configured PC1 as AF/analog earlier, the prior firmware image's MODER bits are not guaranteed reset. The comment notes MX_GPIO_Init re-applies the same drive later (idempotent), which holds, but the OTYPER/MODER writes here do not clear PUPDR — relying on PWR->PDCRC clear at 724 to remove any pull-down.
findings.impact: Low: the sequence is idempotent and the PWR pull-down is cleared at 724. Edge case only if a future change leaves a PC1 pull configured in PUPDR (not PWR_PDCR) across reset. Functionally correct today.
findings.recommendation: Optional: also clear GPIOC->PUPDR bits for PC1 here for completeness, so the bare-metal pre-clock-config drive does not depend on reset-state PUPDR. Not urgent.

dead_code: g_boot_pwr_sr1_raw (692/896): write-only global, no reader — genuine dead store (see finding). g_dfu_debug_* (140-147): set in check_dfu_request, never read by any module incl. bootloader — debug orphans shipped in release (config-gated only by being unconditional; should be DEBUG-gated). Commented-out code: line 781-782 (LPM_forceMode on wakeup-from-reset), line 846 (GPIO_DisableAllToAnalogInput), line 986 (stressTest registration), line 1069 (RTC_Alarm_IRQHandler) — all intentional/dev leftovers, not reachable. Config-gated (NOT dead, correct): the USE_GUI_APP default block 74-77 is inactive for the sealed UW_DOPPLER build; the per-APP IDLE_task / init blocks are mutually exclusive via #error at 79-81; SMD_STDALONE PC1/PB7 PWR-pulldown clears (717-746) compile only for that board.
test_coverage: Partial. DFU magic/proto constants covered by Tests/unit/test_dfu_protocol.c; boot-loop/crash retention covered by test_boot_loop_crc.c / test_boot_loop_time.c / test_crash_forensics.c. GAP: the reset-cause -> Sram2_Init() cold-boot gate (lines 868-887) — the load-bearing logic broken by the HIGH finding — has NO unit-test mirror (no test references IWDGRSTF/SFTRSTF -> Sram2 decision). The mspFillup/assertMspOverflow stack-canary logic (192-238) is HW-coupled but its single-word-canary decision could be unit-tested with a mocked memory window. Recommend a host test that mirrors '!(csr & (IWDGRSTF|SFTRSTF)) -> Sram2_Init' across {cold/BOR/PIN/IWDG/SFT, with-and-without PINRSTF co-set} to lock the correct (g_boot_rcc_csr_raw) behaviour and prevent regression.

role: CubeMX-generated RTC peripheral init: configures hrtc handle/prescalers, selects RTC clock source (LSE preferred, LSI fallback), provides HAL_RTC_MspInit/MspDeInit. Re-inits hrtc on wake from SHUTDOWN/STANDBY without a full HAL_RTC_Init.
compiled_in: all (MX_RTC_Init called unconditionally from main.c:812 for every APP/BOARD/COMM; LSI-fallback branch is live, sealed target is APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE)

findings.description: On a wake from SHUTDOWN/STANDBY where the LSE crystal was alive at the previous boot but is now dead, g_rtc_use_lsi=1 so MspInit requests RTCCLKSOURCE_LSI while the backup-domain BDCR still has RTCSEL=LSE (it survives shutdown). HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig detects current(LSE) != requested(LSI) and performs __HAL_RCC_BACKUPRESET_FORCE()/RELEASE(), which wipes the ENTIRE backup domain: the RTC calendar/counter AND the RTC backup registers that hold the LPM mode (lpm_ctxt in .lpmSection, see main.c:771-772) and the MGR_ERR/TAMP forensic state. This MspInit runs at main.c:812, i.e. AFTER LPM_getMode() was read once (main.c:854) but BEFORE the second LPM_getMode() at main.c:1059 and before any code that relies on the backup-register LPM context. A wiped BKPR makes the second LPM_getMode() return NONE, so the wake-from-shutdown RTC_WKUP_IRQHandler simulation (main.c:1070) is skipped and timed-wake bookkeeping is lost. On the sealed unit this degrades a marginal-LSE recovery boot rather than recovering cleanly.
findings.impact: Sealed-deploy degraded-LSE recovery path: the backup-domain reset silently destroys the LPM-mode context and RTC time exactly in the LSE-death scenario the LSI fallback exists to survive. Wake-cause dispatch and any RTC-time continuity is lost on that boot. Low probability (needs LSE alive-then-dead across a shutdown) but high impact because it is the corner the fallback is meant to harden.
findings.recommendation: On the wake-from-shutdown branch (rtc.c:35-66) the RTC is already configured; do not call the full HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig clock-source reselect via HAL_RTC_MspInit when the source would change. Either (a) read RTCSEL from BDCR and skip the PeriphCLKConfig if it already matches, or (b) gate the RTCClockSelection switch so a backup-domain reset is never triggered on a wake path — only on the NONE/cold path. Confirm with a bench test: boot on LSE, force g_rtc_use_lsi at wake, verify lpm_ctxt/RTC counter survive.

findings.description: The prescalers (127+1)*(255+1)=32768 are hard-wired for LSE=32768 Hz. When g_rtc_use_lsi=1 the RTCCLK is LSI=32000 Hz (Core/Inc/stm32wlxx_hal_conf.h:132), so the calendar runs at 32000/32768 = 0.9766 Hz, ~2.4% slow, and the prescalers are never adjusted for the LSI case. The code comment in main.c:1116 explicitly accepts '±5% LSI timing', so this is within the documented tolerance, but rtc.c itself carries no note that its prescalers assume 32768 Hz and are wrong for the LSI branch it (indirectly) selects.
findings.impact: Degraded-LSE (LSI) boots keep all timed wakes ~2.4% off real time. Accepted by design (±5% budget); no functional break. Becomes a real concern only if a future change tightens a wake interval's tolerance below ~3%.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment at rtc.c:45 noting the prescalers target 32768 Hz and the LSI branch accepts the ~2.4% drift (cross-ref main.c:1116). Optionally derive SynchPrediv from g_rtc_use_lsi (255->249 for 32000 Hz) if exact LSI timing is ever required; not needed under the current ±5% budget.

findings.description: MX_RTC_Init arms the wake-up timer for 5 s (HAL_RTCEx_SetWakeUpTimer_IT, rtc.c:101) and then immediately deactivates it (HAL_RTCEx_DeactivateWakeUpTimer, rtc.c:107). The arm is pure CubeMX boilerplate with no effect — the wake timer is owned later by the MCU wrapper / mgr_lpm_uw.c. main.c:828 also calls HAL_RTCEx_DeactivateWakeUpTimer again immediately after MX_RTC_Init returns, so the deactivate here is redundant too. The magic literal 5 has no meaning.
findings.impact: No functional impact (net effect is 'timer disabled'). Minor: wastes a few cycles arming+disarming and the redundant deactivate at main.c:828 obscures intent; a reader may think 5 s is a real wake interval.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the arm/deactivate pair at rtc.c:99-110 entirely (the timer is configured by mgr_lpm_uw.c at use time) or add a comment that this is CubeMX boilerplate intentionally neutralized. Confirm rtc.c:107 vs main.c:828 redundancy is intended.

findings.location: Core/Src/rtc.c:132 (extern volatile uint8_t g_rtc_use_lsi declared mid-block, after statements)
findings.description: The extern declaration of g_rtc_use_lsi is placed mid-function inside HAL_RTC_MspInit, after executable statements (the PeriphClkInitStruct assignment at line 128). A file-scope extern (or one declared in a shared header) is cleaner and avoids a function-local extern of a cross-module volatile. There is no compile-time check that the type here (uint8_t) matches main.c:1108; a future type change in one place would not be caught. Also duplicates the hrtc Init block verbatim between the wake path (rtc.c:43-52) and the cold path (rtc.c:84-93) — two copies that can drift.
findings.impact: No runtime defect. Maintainability: silent type-mismatch risk on g_rtc_use_lsi, and duplicated init block can diverge (e.g. someone changes a prescaler in one copy only — which would reintroduce a real LSE/LSI bug).
findings.recommendation: Declare g_rtc_use_lsi in a shared header (e.g. main.h) so both definition and use share one type. Factor the duplicated hrtc.Init assignment into a single static helper to prevent drift between the wake and cold paths.

findings.location: Core/Src/rtc.c:55 (HAL_RTC_MspInit called on wake path) and rtc.c:136-139
findings.description: On the SHUTDOWN/STANDBY wake path, HAL_RTC_MspInit is called manually but its return-bearing inner call HAL_RCCEx_PeriphCLKConfig (rtc.c:136) routes failure to Error_Handler() — which on this firmware can NVIC_SystemReset (main.c:1213+). A transient DBP/LSE-ready timeout inside PeriphCLKConfig (HAL_TIMEOUT path, rcc_ex.c:139-144,171-176) on a wake would therefore reset the chip rather than degrade. For a sealed unit, a reset is acceptable here (cold boot re-runs the LSI fallback), but the wake path silently inherits the cold-path Error_Handler reset semantics without that being stated.
findings.impact: A marginal LSE-ready timeout on a wake-from-shutdown causes a full reset instead of a graceful continue. Tolerable (reset re-enters fallback) but means wake latency/extra boot on a flaky crystal; not the lowest-power outcome.
findings.recommendation: Document that HAL_RTC_MspInit on the wake path may reset via Error_Handler on a clock-config timeout, and that this is the intended fail-safe (cold boot re-selects LSI). No code change required if the reset-and-fallback behavior is the accepted contract.

findings.location: Core/Src/rtc.c (no dedicated unit test; Tests/unit has no rtc_* suite — grep of Tests for RTC hits only test_shutdown_sequence/test_lpm_uw/test_lpm_deadline/test_cooldown_persist, none cover MX_RTC_Init branch selection)
findings.description: The branch selection in MX_RTC_Init based on LPM_getMode() (wake-vs-cold init, the load-bearing logic of this file) has no host unit test. The LSI-vs-LSE source selection in HAL_RTC_MspInit (the sealed-deploy survival feature) is also untested. These are mockable: LPM_getMode() and the HAL_* calls are already mocked elsewhere in Tests/unit per the framework.
findings.impact: A regression that, e.g., made the wake path fall through to full HAL_RTC_Init (re-running SetWakeUpTimer and clobbering the running wake config) or inverted the g_rtc_use_lsi ternary would not be caught by CI — it would only surface on a sealed-unit field failure.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_rtc_init.c: (1) assert wake-from-SHUTDOWN/STANDBY takes the early-return path and calls HAL_RTC_MspInit but NOT HAL_RTC_Init; (2) assert STOP/SLEEP returns without touching hrtc; (3) assert NONE/default does the full init; (4) assert RTCClockSelection follows g_rtc_use_lsi (LSI when 1, LSE when 0). Mock LPM_getMode and the HAL_RTC*/HAL_RCCEx* calls.

dead_code: The 5 s wake-timer arm at rtc.c:101 is immediately disarmed (rtc.c:107) and re-disarmed at main.c:828 — functionally dead config, intentional CubeMX boilerplate (not config-gated, just neutralized). No genuine orphan functions: MX_RTC_Init is called from main.c:812 in every config; HAL_RTC_MspInit/MspDeInit are HAL weak-override callbacks invoked by the HAL (rtc.c:55 directly on wake, and indirectly via HAL_RTC_Init/DeInit). The wake-path switch cases (SHUTDOWN/STANDBY vs STOP/SLEEP vs NONE) are all reachable: SHUTDOWN is the sealed default (LPM_SHUTDOWN_ENABLED), STOP is used by mgr_lpm_uw/mgr_err STOP2 paths, NONE is cold boot.
test_coverage: Not covered. No rtc_* suite in Tests/unit. The branch-by-LPM-mode init logic and the g_rtc_use_lsi clock-source selection — both load-bearing for the sealed deployment — are mockable but untested (LPM_getMode and HAL_* are already mocked in sibling suites). Concrete gap: a regression flipping the wake path to a full HAL_RTC_Init (which re-arms+disarms the wake timer and could clobber an in-flight wake config) or inverting the LSI/LSE ternary would pass CI silently. See test-gap finding for the proposed cases.

role: CubeMX-generated SPI1 slave init/deinit: configures SPI1 in 8-bit slave mode with RX/TX DMA (DMA1 Ch1/Ch2), HW-NSS input, and the GPIO MspInit/MspDeInit (PA15=NSS, PA1=SCK, PB4=MISO, PB5=MOSI). Used only by the SPI console/A+ protocol path.
compiled_in: COMM=SPI only (Makefile:412-417 adds Core/Src/spi.c and defines USE_SPI_DRIVER; MX_SPI1_Init call at main.c:832 is #if USE_SPI_DRIVER). NOT compiled in the sealed target (APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART).

findings.description: On SMD_STDALONE the SPI1 AF pins collide with load-bearing GPIO: PA1=LED_RED, PB4=LED_GREEN, PB5=LED_BLUE, and the adjacent PB6=REED / PB7=PWR_LATCH (per gpio.c:93,129-130 and BSP_LED_wiring memory). MspInit forces PA1/PB4/PB5 to AF5_SPI1 push-pull. The UW_DOPPLER #error guard (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:92-96) only checks BSP feature macros, NOT the COMM choice, so `APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=SPI` is a fully buildable configuration. In that build the LED pins become the SPI clock/data lines and the state-indication LED logic (mgr_gesture/UW state) would drive/conflict with the SPI bus on the same pads.
findings.impact: A mis-specified sealed build (SPI instead of UART) would silently repurpose the deploy-status LEDs as the SPI bus. No compile-time guard catches it. While the documented sealed target is UART (so not the default), there is no defense-in-depth: one wrong COMM= flag produces a board where the field-diagnostic LEDs and SPI are wired to the same pins. Given the 'never brick a sealed unit' bar this is a latent landmine.
findings.recommendation: Add a compile-time guard (e.g. in kns_app_uw_doppler.c or a board header) that errors on `USE_SPI_DRIVER && SMD_STDALONE` (or more precisely USE_SPI_DRIVER together with BSP_HAS_LED_RGB on the same pads), mirroring the existing UW_DOPPLER #error pattern. This is a one-line _Static_assert/#error, not a code change to spi.c itself.

findings.description: SCK (PA1) and the data pins are GPIO_NOPULL. PA1 is also the EXTI/wake landscape on STDALONE; in SPI slave mode with NOPULL on SCK/MOSI, when the master is absent or tristated these lines float. Comment on line 88 only justifies NOPULL for NSS ('let master control NSS'), but the same NOPULL is applied to SCK/MISO/MOSI without rationale. A floating SCK on an idle slave can clock in noise; floating inputs also raise quiescent current — relevant to the µA budget.
findings.impact: Potential spurious SPI clocking / increased leakage when the master is disconnected. Only affects COMM=SPI builds, so not the sealed UART target, but contradicts the project's lowest-power default for any SPI deployment.
findings.recommendation: Document why NOPULL is acceptable on SCK/MOSI for this master, or set a defined idle level (the SPI peripheral idle state is well-defined, but the floating-input leakage in STOP remains). At minimum add a one-line comment so the NOPULL choice on the clock/data lines is intentional and reviewed.

findings.description: Init failures route to Error_Handler() (an infinite loop in CubeMX default). MX_SPI1_Init is re-invoked from the STOP-exit path (lpm.c:400) on every wake. If HAL_SPI_Init or HAL_DMA_Init ever returns non-OK at runtime (e.g. transient peripheral state after STOP2), the device hangs in Error_Handler instead of recovering — a hang path. For COMM=SPI this re-init runs on the hot wake path.
findings.impact: A wedged SPI/DMA re-init after a STOP wake would hang the MCU in Error_Handler with no IWDG-style recovery visible here. Sealed-deployment hang risk, but confined to COMM=SPI builds (not the UART sealed target).
findings.recommendation: For the SPI build, consider whether the wake-path re-init (lpm.c:400) should tolerate a failed HAL_SPI_Init by logging+resetting (MGR_ERR_logAndReset) rather than spinning in Error_Handler. Not a spi.c change per se, but spi.c's hard Error_Handler on the re-init path is the mechanism.

findings.description: `volatile uint32_t spi_irq_count` is incremented in SPI1_IRQHandler purely as a debug counter and is never read anywhere (no other reference in the tree). It is a leftover debug instrument, against the CLAUDE.md rule that debug markers must not ship. Minor: it is volatile so the increment is not optimized away, adding a tiny per-IRQ cost. (Same pattern as subghz_irq_count.)
findings.impact: Negligible runtime cost; code-hygiene/debug-leftover only. COMM=SPI builds only.
findings.recommendation: Remove spi_irq_count (and the increment) or mark it clearly as DBG and strip before release, per the project's no-ship-debug-markers rule.

findings.description: DMA1 Ch1/Ch2 and SPI1 IRQ are set to preempt priority 2 (below Radio=0). Comment is correct. No conflict found: DMA1 Channel1/Channel2 are used exclusively by SPI1 across the codebase (grep confirms no other peripheral claims these channels). Noting for completeness — this is correct, not a defect.
findings.impact: None.
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.description: No unit test exercises this file's logic. Tests/unit/test_spi_protocol.c covers the mgr_spi protocol layer, not the MCU/HAL init glue. The only logic-bearing content here is the static register-config values (mode=SLAVE, 8-bit, CPOL=0/CPHA=0, HW NSS input, DMA byte-align). That is HW register glue and is appropriately near-untestable in the host unit harness.
findings.impact: None directly — this is HW glue.
findings.recommendation: n/a — leave as HW glue. The pin-conflict guard recommended above belongs in a build-config static_assert, which is verifiable by a compile test, not a unit test.

dead_code: No dead code within spi.c itself: MX_SPI1_Init, HAL_SPI_MspInit, HAL_SPI_MspDeInit are all reachable in COMM=SPI builds (MspInit/MspDeInit are HAL weak-override callbacks invoked by HAL_SPI_Init/DeInit). The entire file is config-gated dead in non-SPI builds (intentional — Makefile only compiles it for COMM=SPI), which includes the sealed UART target. The three globals (hspi1, hdma_spi1_rx, hdma_spi1_tx) are all used (main.c, lpm.c, stm32wlxx_it.c). No unused statics/params/returns inside the file (spiHandle param is used in both Msp callbacks).
test_coverage: n/a (HW glue). All logic is static SPI/DMA register configuration plus HAL MspInit/DeInit GPIO+NVIC setup, which the host unit harness cannot meaningfully exercise. The one item that COULD be a compile-time test is a build-config guard against USE_SPI_DRIVER+SMD_STDALONE pin collision (see findings) — verifiable via a _Static_assert/#error, not a runtime unit test.

role: CubeMX-generated global MSP init stub. Provides the strong (non-weak) definition of HAL_MspInit() that overrides the HAL driver's __weak default; body is empty.
compiled_in: all (no config guards; always compiled and linked in every APP/BOARD/COMM combination)

findings.description: HAL_MspInit() has a completely empty body. It is the only project-level MSP function in this file; all per-peripheral MSP init/deinit (GPIO mode/pull, RCC clock enable, NVIC priority) is implemented elsewhere (Core/Src/usart.c, adc.c, spi.c, rtc.c, subghz.c, tim.c, and Kineis/Lpm/Src/lpm.c). Nothing is missing or wrong here — the empty global HAL_MspInit is the standard CubeMX pattern (no global system interrupts to configure on STM32WL55 baremetal). No action needed; noted only so the auditor of the per-peripheral MSP code knows the real GPIO/clock setup is NOT in this file.
findings.impact: None. Empty function is correct behavior; this is not a defect.
findings.recommendation: No change. The peripheral GPIO/clock/NVIC config that actually matters for the sealed deployment (pin conflicts across boards, peripherals left enabled in low-power, ISR priorities) must be audited in the per-peripheral *_MspInit/*_MspDeInit functions in usart.c/adc.c/spi.c/rtc.c/subghz.c/tim.c/lpm.c, not here.

dead_code: none. HAL_MspInit() is live in every config: it is a strong override of the HAL driver's __weak HAL_MspInit (Drivers/STM32WLxx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32wlxx_hal.c:240) and is invoked once from HAL_Init() at stm32wlxx_hal.c:196. All other sections are empty CubeMX USER CODE placeholders (no code, not dead code). No unused statics, params, or returns (function is void, takes void).
test_coverage: n/a (HW glue). HAL_MspInit() is an empty hardware-init hook with no logic, no inputs, no outputs and no observable behavior — there is nothing to unit-test. The testable hardware-config logic lives in the per-peripheral MSP files.

role: Cortex-M4 exception/interrupt vector handlers: core fault forensics (HardFault/MemManage/BusFault/UsageFault), SysTick, RTC wakeup, TIM16, SPI1/DMA, LPUART1, SUBGHZ radio, and SPI-NSS EXTI wakeup.
compiled_in: all (this CubeMX IT file is compiled in every config). Forensic fault path gated USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP||USE_DOPPLER_APP; minimal reset-only faults otherwise. SPI/DMA/EXTI15_10 blocks gated USE_SPI_DRIVER (sealed target is UART -> those are excluded). RGB SysTick hook gated BSP_HAS_LED_RGB.

findings.description: fault_handler_c() runs in the HardFault exception context and calls HAL_UART_Transmit(&hlpuart1, ..., 100) (a blocking, up to 100ms poll loop) plus snprintf() into a 168-byte buffer, gated on MGR_LOG_passes(). In a fault context the UART peripheral or its clock may be in any state (e.g. fault hit mid-reconfigure, or LPUART clock gated in a low-power transition). HAL_UART_Transmit will then spin until its 100ms timeout each call. This delays the guaranteed NVIC_SystemReset() that the comment at the top of the file promises ('Tracker must always reset — never stay stuck').
findings.impact: On the sealed UW_DOPPLER unit a CPU fault adds up to ~100ms of blocking UART before reset. Not a brick (snprintf/HAL_UART_Transmit are bounded; reset still fires), but it is forensic-print work executed before the safety reset, against the 'reset first, never stay stuck' intent. Worst case the log gate is open during a clock-glitch fault.
findings.recommendation: Persist the crash record (MGR_ERR_captureFault, already first-class and bounded) and reset FIRST; emit the human-readable UART forensic on the NEXT boot from the retained struct (which the code already supports via MGR_ERR_takeRetainedCrash). Or drop the blocking timeout to a few ms in the fault path.

findings.description: MemManage_Handler / BusFault_Handler / UsageFault_Handler (both the forensic trampolines and the minimal stubs at 189-191) are effectively unreachable: no application code sets SHCSR.MEMFAULTENA/BUSFAULTENA/USGFAULTENA (verified — no SHCSR/EnableFault/SCB_SHCSR write exists in Core/ or Kineis/). With the configurable fault handlers disabled at reset, all mem/bus/usage faults escalate to HardFault, so only HardFault_Handler ever executes. The dedicated handlers are dead.
findings.impact: No functional harm (HardFault still captures the fault via CFSR/HFSR). But the per-fault MemManage/BusFault/UsageFault forensic discrimination the code is written to provide never happens — the captured fault_type is always ERR_HARDFAULT in practice, which can mislead post-mortem analysis of a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Either enable the three configurable faults in SystemInit/Hardening (SCB->SHCSR |= MEM/BUS/USG FAULTENA), to actually use the discrimination, or document that they are intentionally disabled and the dedicated handlers are belt-and-braces only. Decode CFSR in the HardFault path to recover the real sub-fault type instead.

findings.description: subghz_irq_count is a global volatile incremented on every SUBGHZ radio IRQ but is never read anywhere in the project (grep across Core/ and Kineis/ finds only the definition+increment here). It is unconditionally compiled (not under DEBUG), so it ships on the sealed build. Same for spi_irq_count (line 294/318) but that one is at least USE_SPI_DRIVER-gated and excluded from the UART sealed target.
findings.impact: Negligible: 4 bytes RAM + one load/store/store per radio IRQ on the hot TX/RX path. Pure orphan debug instrumentation that adds a tiny per-interrupt cost during active comms. No correctness impact.
findings.recommendation: Remove subghz_irq_count (and spi_irq_count) or guard them under #if defined(DEBUG) so production/sealed builds don't carry write-only counters in the radio ISR.

findings.description: The `volatile uint32_t subghz_irq_count = 0;` definition is placed between the Doxygen comment block (340-342, '@brief This function handles SUBGHZ Radio Interrupt') and the function it documents (345). The comment now visually documents the variable, not the handler. Comment-to-declaration association rot.
findings.impact: Readability only; a maintainer scanning the file sees the handler doc detached from its function by a variable definition.
findings.recommendation: Move the counter definition above the Doxygen block (or into the USER CODE PV section).

findings.description: In the fault path both MGR_ERR_captureFault() (writes SRAM2 retention struct) and MGR_ERR_LOG_FAULT() (writes TAMP_BKP4/5/6R via raw volatile addresses) persist overlapping crash metadata (fault_type, app_state, tick) to two independent stores. The SCB->HFSR/CFSR fault status bits are read but never cleared (write-1-to-clear) before NVIC_SystemReset — they are sticky and a system reset clears them anyway, so this is fine, just worth noting the double-store of redundant state.
findings.impact: None functional — system reset clears HFSR/CFSR; dual persistence is intentional redundancy (SRAM2 + TAMP) so a torn SRAM2 write still leaves TAMP breadcrumbs. Listed for completeness of the ISR-state audit.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Optionally note in the comment why both stores exist (SRAM2 = rich struct, TAMP = minimal survivor).

findings.description: NMI_Handler wraps Core_Error_Handler() in `while(1)`. Core_Error_Handler for UW_DOPPLER does __disable_irq()+NVIC_SystemReset() (never returns), so the outer while(1) is defensive dead code. In the DEBUG (non-UW) branch Core_Error_Handler spins in its own while(1). Either way the outer loop is belt-and-braces and harmless. On STM32WL an NMI is typically a clock-security-system (CSS) event or a flash ECC double-error.
findings.impact: No functional issue. The UW_DOPPLER path correctly resets; consistent with the 'never stay stuck' rule.
findings.recommendation: No change required.

findings.description: fault_handler_c() decodes the stacked exception frame indices (frame[0]=R0, frame[4]=R12, frame[5]=LR, frame[6]=PC, frame[7]=xPSR) for both the UART print and MGR_ERR_captureFault. The mapping is duplicated between this file (149-153) and mgr_err.c (297-313). There is no unit test asserting these frame indices match the ARMv7-M stacking order, nor that buf[168] is large enough for the worst-case format (HARDFAULT tag, all-FF registers).
findings.impact: If the frame index convention is ever edited in one place and not the other, forensics silently report wrong PC/LR on a sealed unit and the bug is invisible until a real crash. The buffer-size assumption (~158 bytes worst case vs 168) is also untested.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit case that feeds a synthetic 8-word frame array through a thin wrapper and asserts the extracted PC/LR/R0/R12/xPSR, and a snprintf-into-168 size check with max-width hex. Keep the frame-index constants in one shared header used by both stm32wlxx_it.c and mgr_err.c.

dead_code: 1) MemManage/BusFault/UsageFault handlers (both forensic trampolines @182-184 and minimal stubs @189-191): unreachable because no code enables SHCSR fault-enable bits — all such faults escalate to HardFault. WHY dead: HW config never enables them; not config-gated, genuine reachability dead-code (harmless). 2) subghz_irq_count @343: genuine orphan, written in ISR @348, read nowhere (ships on sealed build). 3) spi_irq_count @294/318: same orphan, but USE_SPI_DRIVER-gated so excluded from the UART sealed target. 4) NMI outer while(1) @110-114: defensive dead code (Core_Error_Handler never returns on UW_DOPPLER). 5) `while(1) {/*unreachable*/}` @161 after NVIC_SystemReset: intentional belt-and-braces, dead by design.
test_coverage: Partial. The forensic data path (frame-index decode, crash struct CRC/commit) is exercised indirectly via Tests/unit/test_memory_safety.c and test_evtlog.c which stub g_uw_doppler_state_for_err and replicate the e->state = (uint8_t)g_uw_doppler_state_for_err logic — but those test mgr_evtlog/mgr_err, NOT this file's frame[] index mapping or the buf[168] sizing. The ISR handlers themselves (HAL_*_IRQHandler dispatch, EXTI15_10 line-15 clear) are HW glue, not unit-testable. Concrete gap: no test pins the ARMv7-M stacked-frame index convention used at :149-153, which is duplicated in mgr_err.c and could silently desync.

role: CubeMX-generated SubGHz (SX126x sub-GHz radio) bring-up: MX_SUBGHZ_Init resets/wakes the radio, runs HAL_SUBGHZ_Init, parks it in STANDBY_RC and enables the radio IRQ; plus HAL MspInit/MspDeInit clock+NVIC glue.
compiled_in: all (no APP/BOARD/COMM guards in this file; hsubghz + MX_SUBGHZ_Init are referenced by libkineis undefined-symbols, so always linked). For the sealed target it is on a HOT path: called at boot (main.c:810) AND on every STOP2 surface-wake (mgr_lpm_uw.c:1079) and on-demand TX re-arm (mgr_lpm_uw.c:1172 via MGR_LPM_UW_ensureRadioReady).

findings.description: Hardcoded NVIC enable targets the WRONG interrupt. `NVIC->ISER[1] = (1UL << 12)` sets bit 12 of ISER[1], i.e. IRQ 32+12 = IRQ 44 = SUBGHZSPI_IRQn — NOT the radio IRQ. On the CM4 core SUBGHZ_Radio_IRQn = 50 (stm32wl55xx.h:165), which would need ISER[1] bit 18 ((1UL<<18)). The inline comment even says '/* Direct write for IRQ 44 */', confirming the author mistargeted. SUBGHZSPI_IRQHandler is .weak-aliased to Default_Handler (startup_stm32wl55xx_cm4.s:425-426 / startup_stm32wl55jcix.s:379-380), an infinite loop.
findings.impact: Spuriously enables an unhandled peripheral IRQ at the NVIC on a sealed device. If SUBGHZSPI ever asserts an interrupt at NVIC level (e.g. an unexpected SPI error/overrun condition while the lib drives the radio), the CPU vectors to Default_Handler and hangs forever — no watchdog escape unless IWDG is armed. The intended radio IRQ is in fact still enabled correctly via HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ(SUBGHZ_Radio_IRQn) at line 112 and via HAL_SUBGHZ_MspInit (line 134), so the radio works DESPITE this line — making the line both useless for its stated purpose and a latent landmine.
findings.recommendation: Delete line 115-117 entirely (the manual ISER write + DSB/ISB). The radio IRQ is already enabled by HAL_NVIC_EnableIRQ at line 112. If a belt-and-suspenders direct write is truly wanted, it must target IRQ 50: `NVIC->ISER[1] = (1UL << 18);`. Do NOT leave it enabling IRQ 44.

findings.description: The radio responsiveness probe is performed but its result is thrown away. `status = HAL_SUBGHZ_ExecGetCmd(...RADIO_GET_STATUS...)` then `(void)status;` and `radio_status` is read into but never tested. The three follow-up ExecSetCmd calls (CLR_ERRORS, CLR_IRQSTATUS, SET_STANDBY at lines 100/104/108) also ignore their HAL_StatusTypeDef returns. So a radio that is wired but not responding (stuck in sleep, SPI desync after bootloader jump, brownout on PA rail) passes init silently; MX_SUBGHZ_Init returns 'success' and the MAC later fails to TX with no early signal.
findings.impact: On the sealed deployment a degraded/non-responding radio is not detected at init. The unit keeps cycling STOP2<->surface, burning battery on wake+SWS+(failed) TX attempts for the full ~12 months with no self-recovery trigger keyed off radio health. Lower severity because HAL_SUBGHZ_Init itself (line 79) does catch a hard SPI/RFBUSY timeout and routes to Error_Handler->reset; this only misses the 'SPI works but radio command layer is wrong' middle ground.
findings.recommendation: At minimum check the GET_STATUS chip-mode/command-status field and the ExecSetCmd returns; on a clearly-bad status, log a WARN and/or route to Error_Handler (which resets for UW_DOPPLER) instead of silently continuing. Keep it cheap (no retry loop on the STOP2 hot path).

findings.description: Five spin-delay busy-waits using `for (volatile int i = 0; i < N; i++);` (10000, 1000, 1000, 5000, 5000 iterations). These are uncalibrated magic-count delays whose real duration depends on CPU clock (which differs between the boot path at PLL/48MHz and the STOP2-exit path — uw_restore_clock_from_stop runs AFTER... actually MX_SUBGHZ_Init at mgr_lpm_uw.c:1079 runs after uw_restore_clock_from_stop at :1064, so clock is restored, but the boot path clock may differ). Because MX_SUBGHZ_Init is on the STOP2 surface-wake hot path, these spins add CPU-active time (energy) to every wake where the radio is re-armed.
findings.impact: Wasted active-mode energy on each radio re-arm during a battery-critical 12-month deployment. Also fragile: if a future clock change speeds the core, the reset/NSS settle delays silently shrink and may become too short to guarantee the radio exits deep-sleep, intermittently bricking the radio bring-up. Note the lazy-radio comment at mgr_lpm_uw.c:1069 explicitly says the deinit/init pair 'dominated the wake window' — these spins are part of that cost.
findings.recommendation: Replace the count-based spins with clock-independent timed waits (e.g. a short HAL_Delay or a DWT/us delay sized to the SX126x datasheet wake/reset spec). At minimum #define the magic counts with a comment citing the required settle time.

findings.description: On every re-init (STOP2 wake, ensureRadioReady) the handle is forced to HAL_SUBGHZ_STATE_RESET (line 64), which makes HAL_SUBGHZ_Init perform a FULL radio reset (LL_RCC_RF_DisableReset, RFBUSY wait, NSS re-assert — hal_subghz.c:278-310). The HAL documents (hal_subghz.c:213-215) that to re-init after a low-power exit WITHOUT resetting the radio you set HAL_SUBGHZ_STATE_RESET_RF_READY via __HAL_SUBGHZ_RESET_HANDLE_STATE_RF_READY. The bootloader-jump comment (lines 45-47) justifies a full reset at COLD boot, but the same code now runs on warm STOP2 wakes where the radio context is intact.
findings.impact: Extra radio reset + RFBUSY settle on each warm re-arm = more active time/energy and longer surface-detect-to-TX latency than necessary. Functionally correct, but counter to the lowest-power mandate. Not a correctness bug because UW_DOPPLER does a full STOP2 (radio loses state) so a full reset is arguably needed anyway — hence low.
findings.recommendation: If/when measuring wake energy: consider RESET_RF_READY on the warm-wake path (pass a flag into MX_SUBGHZ_Init, or have the LPM path set the handle state) while keeping full RESET only on cold boot after a bootloader jump. Verify the radio actually retains state across the specific STOP2 entry used.

findings.description: Large hand-written block lives inside CubeMX USER CODE regions and duplicates work HAL_SUBGHZ_Init already does: HAL_SUBGHZ_Init->HAL_SUBGHZ_MspInit re-enables the SUBGHZSPI clock (line 130) and the radio NVIC (line 134), de-asserts radio reset and toggles NSS (hal_subghz.c:283-310), and enables EXTI line 44 (hal_subghz.c:272-274). The manual pre-reset (lines 56-72), the post-init NSS toggle (89-92), the second HAL_NVIC_SetPriority/EnableIRQ (111-112), and the ISER write (115) are largely redundant with the HAL. This makes the init hard to reason about and is exactly the kind of layered workaround the project guidelines warn against.
findings.impact: Maintenance/robustness risk rather than a live defect: redundant peripheral resets/NSS toggles increase the chance of a future edit fighting the HAL, and they pad the hot-path wake time. The manual __HAL_RCC_SUBGHZSPI_CLK_DISABLE at line 56 followed by FORCE/RELEASE_RESET then re-ENABLE at 68 is safe but indicates the sequence was tuned empirically ('working version ... still fixing DMA', commit a244406).
findings.recommendation: Once the IRQ-44 line is removed and the radio bring-up is re-validated on HW, prune the redundant manual reset/NSS/NVIC steps to just what the bootloader-jump recovery genuinely requires, and add a one-line comment stating which step exists for which reason.

findings.description: No unit test exercises any subghz logic. The one piece of testable, non-HW logic here is the IRQ-number/bitmask correctness of the manual NVIC write (a pure arithmetic invariant: SUBGHZ_Radio_IRQn==50 => ISER index 1, bit 18). A _Static_assert or a tiny host test mapping IRQn->(ISER index, bit) would have caught the IRQ-44 mistake at compile/test time. The bulk of MX_SUBGHZ_Init is HAL/HW glue and is appropriately not unit-tested.
findings.impact: The mistargeted-IRQ bug shipped undetected because nothing asserts the bit math. Low because most of the file is genuinely HW glue with no host-testable behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add a compile-time guard in subghz.c near the (corrected) NVIC write: `_Static_assert((SUBGHZ_Radio_IRQn >> 5) == 1 && (SUBGHZ_Radio_IRQn & 0x1F) == 18, "radio IRQ moved");`. This documents intent and prevents regressions. No new Tests/unit file strictly required.

dead_code: No dead functions. HAL_SUBGHZ_MspInit/MspDeInit are not dead — they are weak-override targets the HAL calls indirectly (hal_subghz.c:266 calls HAL_SUBGHZ_MspInit; DeInit is called from HAL_SUBGHZ_DeInit used by lpm.c:459/519/533). All three functions in the file are reachable. Dead/no-op STATEMENTS: (1) line 115 `NVIC->ISER[1] = (1UL << 12)` is effectively dead-for-its-purpose — it does not enable the intended radio IRQ (that is done at line 112); it instead enables an unhandled IRQ (see high finding). (2) `(void)status;` at line 96 deliberately discards a return; `radio_status` (line 86) is written by ExecGetCmd but never read — a genuinely unused result, not config-gated. None of the dead/redundant code is config-gated; it is leftover empirical bring-up code.
test_coverage: n/a (mostly HW glue). The only host-testable invariant is the NVIC IRQ-number bit math (IRQ 50 -> ISER[1] bit 18), which is currently wrong (line 115) and untested. Recommend a _Static_assert rather than a runtime test. Everything else (HAL_SUBGHZ_Init, ExecSetCmd/GetCmd, NSS toggling, peripheral reset) requires the radio HW and belongs in Tests/integration, not Tests/unit. No existing Tests/unit file references subghz.

role: STM32CubeIDE auto-generated minimal newlib syscall stubs (_read/_write/_close/_fstat/_isatty/_lseek/_open/_exit/etc.) to satisfy libc linkage on baremetal. No OS, no filesystem.
compiled_in: all (listed unconditionally in Makefile:196; no config guards in the file). Note: _sbrk lives in the separate sysmem.c, not here.

findings.description: The stdio retarget path is effectively dead at runtime. The firmware builds with -DUSE_LOCAL_PRINTF (Makefile:289) and emits all logging via MGR_LOG using vsnprintf + HAL_UART_Transmit directly (Kineis/Extdep/MGR_LOG/Src/mgr_log.c:280-394), bypassing newlib. A repo-wide search found zero live newlib printf/scanf/puts/fgets calls in firmware sources (the only 'printf(' hits in Core/Kineis/Bootloader are inside comments: kns_app.c:86, mcu_at_console.h:22-80). Therefore _write/_read are never invoked, and the weak externs __io_putchar/__io_getchar (declared here, defined nowhere) are never resolved to a real symbol.
findings.impact: No functional impact in the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE build: the console/logging path does not depend on this file. Genuinely dead but intentional boilerplate — newlib link-time requirement, kept by gc-sections only if referenced.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is (standard CubeIDE stub). Optionally document that stdio is retargeted via MGR_LOG, not via these stubs, to prevent a future dev from assuming printf() works.

findings.description: LATENT TRAP, not a current bug: if any future code calls a bare newlib printf()/putchar()/scanf(), _write/_read will loop calling __io_putchar/__io_getchar. Those are declared weak (line 35-36) and are defined NOWHERE in the firmware. A call through an unresolved weak symbol resolves to address 0 → branch to 0x00000000. On this build _read also loops `len` times writing into the caller buffer from a garbage return. So a stray printf would not 'just print nothing' — it would fault/UB.
findings.impact: Only triggers if someone adds a real printf/scanf later. In the sealed deployment that would be a hard fault on first call; the active IWDG (~2s, mgr_wdg.c:42-43 prescaler/reload) would reset the unit, so it self-recovers rather than bricking — but it is an avoidable crash path.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) provide a real __io_putchar that routes to HAL_UART_Transmit(&hlpuart1,...) so accidental printf is safe, or (b) add a build-time guard/comment that bare newlib stdio is unsupported (use MGR_LOG_* macros instead). Do NOT add (a) silently if it would change power/UART teardown behavior — gate behind DEBUG.

findings.description: _fstat and _stat dereference the caller-supplied `st` pointer (st->st_mode = S_IFCHR) without a NULL check before writing. Standard CubeIDE behavior; newlib never passes NULL here.
findings.impact: None in practice — these are only reached by newlib internals (e.g. during printf buffering setup) which always pass a valid struct. Since stdio is unused (finding above), they are not even reached. No sealed-deploy risk.
findings.recommendation: No action required. Noting only for completeness of the memory-safety dimension.

findings.description: _exit() ends in `while(1){}` (intentional hang, comment line 64). It is reachable only via libc exit()/abort()/__assert_func. No live exit()/abort() calls exist in firmware (verified by search), and assert_param is configured to ((void)0U) in the non-USE_FULL_ASSERT path (Core/Inc/stm32wlxx_hal_conf.h:329/333).
findings.impact: Not reachable in the sealed build. Even if it were, the active IWDG would reset the chip out of the spin within ~2s, so it would not permanently brick a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: No change. The infinite loop is correct semantics for a baremetal _exit; IWDG provides the recovery backstop.

findings.description: initialise_monitor_handles() declared with empty parameter list `()` (K&R, means 'unspecified args') instead of `(void)`. Minor MISRA/style nit; the rest of the file correctly uses (void).
findings.impact: None.
findings.recommendation: Change to `void` for consistency if the file is ever touched; not worth a dedicated edit.

dead_code: _read (67-78), _write (80-90) and the __io_getchar/__io_putchar externs (35-36) are dead at runtime: USE_LOCAL_PRINTF + MGR_LOG (HAL_UART_Transmit) is the logging path; no live newlib stdio caller exists in firmware. Dead but INTENTIONAL (CubeIDE newlib boilerplate, not an orphan). The remaining stubs (_getpid/_kill/_close/_fstat/_isatty/_lseek/_open/_wait/_unlink/_times/_stat/_link/_fork/_execve/initialise_monitor_handles) are newlib link requirements, not called at runtime — standard. __env/environ (39-40) satisfy libc globals. No genuine orphan code (no function here is unreachable due to a bug; all unreachability is by-design newlib stubbing).
test_coverage: n/a (HW/libc glue). These are trivial newlib stubs with fixed return values and no firmware logic; nothing here warrants a Tests/unit case. The only testable behavior (stdio retarget) is deliberately unused, so a unit test would assert dead-path behavior with no value. No coverage gap.

role: STM32CubeIDE-generated newlib syscall stub providing _sbrk() (heap allocator backing malloc). Manages the newlib heap between linker symbol _end and the reserved MSP stack region.
compiled_in: never — the file is absent from C_SOURCES (Makefile:172-202, 204-234) and from the bootloader build (Bootloader has no sysmem reference). It is not pulled by any wildcard. Genuine orphan in EVERY app/board/comm configuration, including the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART target.

findings.description: sysmem.c is not listed in any Makefile C_SOURCES and is not referenced by the bootloader build. Core/Src/syscalls.c IS compiled (Makefile:196) but does NOT define _sbrk. Therefore the _sbrk in THIS file is never compiled into any firmware image; if malloc were ever used, the linker would instead pull newlib-nano's default _sbrk from -lnosys/-lc (Makefile:619,621). This is a genuine orphan, not config-gated.
findings.impact: No runtime impact today. The risk is latent/maintenance: a reader assumes this file governs heap behavior (e.g. the _Min_Stack_Size stack-protection here), but it does not. A future change that adds malloc/printf-float would silently get the library _sbrk with different (or no) stack-overflow protection, not this implementation. Misleading source-of-truth.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the file from the tree, or add it to C_SOURCES so the project's own (stack-protected) _sbrk is the one linked. Pick one; do not leave a compiled-out copy that looks authoritative. No flash cycle / behavior change either way today since heap is unused.

findings.location: Core/Src/sysmem.c:53-79; (no malloc/calloc/realloc/free call sites exist anywhere in Core/ or Kineis/, and no %f/%g/%e printf specifiers were found)
findings.description: Even if this file were compiled, _sbrk would be unreachable: there are zero dynamic-allocation call sites in the application or in the way printf is used, and -Wl,--gc-sections (Makefile:621) would discard the unreferenced _sbrk and __sbrk_heap_end. The closed-source libkineis.a is the only thing that could call malloc; nothing in our code does.
findings.impact: Confirms the heap is effectively unused, consistent with the CLAUDE.md 'no dynamic allocation' rule. No leak/fragmentation exposure in the sealed deployment from our code.
findings.recommendation: None required. Worth a one-line note in the heap/linker docs that the heap is intentionally unused so nobody 'fixes' _Min_Heap_Size thinking it matters.

findings.description: _sbrk enforces only an UPPER bound (heap must not grow into the reserved MSP stack). It performs no LOWER-bound check: a negative incr (newlib calls _sbrk with negative incr to shrink the heap) could move __sbrk_heap_end below &_end without being rejected. Also note _Min_Heap_Size (0x600, STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:20) is reserved by the linker but is completely ignored here — this _sbrk lets the heap grow up to (_estack - _Min_Stack_Size), inconsistent with the linker's heap reservation.
findings.impact: Only reachable if malloc/free were used (it is not, and this file is not even compiled). In a hypothetical future with heap use, a malformed negative-incr release path could corrupt the heap base; in practice newlib never releases below the start, so probability is very low.
findings.recommendation: If this file is ever brought into the build, add a lower-bound guard (reject if __sbrk_heap_end + incr < &_end) and decide whether _Min_Heap_Size should be enforced. Low priority — purely defensive given heap is unused.

findings.description: `extern uint32_t _Min_Stack_Size;` then `(uint32_t)&_Min_Stack_Size`. _Min_Stack_Size is an ABSOLUTE linker symbol (a value 0x2000, STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:21), not a real object. Taking its ADDRESS yields the value — this is the intended ST idiom and is correct. Calling it out so it is not mistaken for a bug: one must NOT read it as a variable (`_Min_Stack_Size`), only as `&_Min_Stack_Size`. Declaring it `uint32_t` (an object type) rather than e.g. `extern char _Min_Stack_Size[];` is slightly misleading but harmless.
findings.impact: None. Documenting to prevent a 'fix' that dereferences the symbol and breaks the stack-limit computation.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is (matches ST template). Optionally add a comment that these are absolute linker symbols used by address only.

dead_code: Entire file is dead: _sbrk() and the static __sbrk_heap_end (sysmem.c:30,53) are never compiled (file absent from all Makefile source lists) and would be gc-section'd even if compiled, since no code path calls malloc/calloc/realloc/free (zero call sites in Core/ and Kineis/) and printf is not used with float specifiers. Genuine orphan in every config, NOT config-gated. syscalls.c (which IS built) provides no competing _sbrk, so a hypothetical malloc would resolve to newlib-nano's library _sbrk from -lnosys/-lc, never this one.
test_coverage: n/a (HW/toolchain glue). _sbrk is a newlib heap stub with no application logic worth unit-testing, and it is unreachable. No Tests/unit gap. The only meaningful 'test' is a build/link assertion that the heap stays unused — e.g. a map-file check that malloc/_sbrk are absent from the image — but that is a build-config check, not a Unity unit test.

role: CMSIS system init for STM32WL55 CM4: SystemInit() sets VTOR (app vs bootloader offset) + enables FPU; SystemCoreClockUpdate() recomputes SystemCoreClock from RCC registers; defines SystemCoreClock + prescaler tables.
compiled_in: all (compiled by both the app Makefile line 194 and the Bootloader Makefile line 62; the BL_BUILD-gated VTOR branch is only active in the bootloader build)

findings.description: The bootloader VTOR offset 0x00033000 is a hardcoded magic number that must stay in sync with the bootloader linker ROM origin (Bootloader/STM32WL55XX_BL.ld:31 ORIGIN=0x08033000) and _bootloader_addr in STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:24. There is no _Static_assert or shared header tying these together; a future relocation of the bootloader region (the layout has already moved once per commit af2f682 'move bootloader at end') that updates the linker but not this #define would make SystemInit() point VTOR at the wrong address.
findings.impact: If the constant desyncs from the linker, the bootloader would set VTOR to a wrong flash address; interrupts (incl. SysTick used by HAL_Delay during DFU, and the fault handlers) would vector into garbage, hanging or faulting the bootloader. On a sealed unit the bootloader is the only DFU recovery path, so a bricked bootloader = permanently dead unit. Mitigated today only because bl_main.c:918 re-asserts SCB->VTOR=BL_FLASH_BASE after SystemInit, but that mitigation is in separate code that could also drift.
findings.recommendation: Derive VECT_TAB_OFFSET for BL_BUILD from a single shared symbol (e.g. the linker-provided _bootloader_addr or a common bl_layout.h) and add a _Static_assert that (VECT_TAB_BASE_ADDRESS|VECT_TAB_OFFSET)==BL_FLASH_BASE. At minimum add a comment cross-referencing the two linker files so the coupling is discoverable.

findings.description: SystemCoreClockUpdate() has no live caller anywhere in the app, bootloader, or vendored HAL driver tree (grep across Core/Kineis/Bootloader/Drivers HAL .c finds only its own definition and doc comments). On this platform HAL keeps SystemCoreClock current via HAL_RCC_ClockConfig()->HAL_RCC_GetHCLKFreq(); the CMSIS updater is never invoked. It is a standard CMSIS public API kept for completeness, not an orphan.
findings.impact: None functionally; it is correctly computed dead code. Slightly inflates flash footprint (the function is not GC'd unless --gc-sections drops it; it is referenced via the public ABI so it links in). No runtime risk.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is (vendor CMSIS file). If flash is tight for the 32KB bootloader, confirm -ffunction-sections/--gc-sections removes it from the bootloader image since the BL never calls it.

findings.description: The CORE_CM0PLUS, VECT_TAB_SRAM, and DUAL_CORE branches are all dead for this firmware: the build is single-core CM4 baremetal (CORE_CM4 defined, CORE_CM0PLUS/DUAL_CORE never defined per build configs), and VECT_TAB_SRAM is commented out. The active path is always the CM4 / FLASH_BASE / non-SRAM branch (lines 155-163) and the HCLK1-prescaler branch (line 346).
findings.impact: None; these are config-gated vendor branches that compile out. No risk.
findings.recommendation: No action (vendor file). Noted only for completeness of reachability analysis.

findings.description: Duplicated comment block: 'Get MSI Range frequency' appears twice (line 275 then identical line 277) — a copy/paste artifact in the local modification. Cosmetic.
findings.impact: None. Minor readability noise.
findings.recommendation: Remove the duplicate comment line.

findings.description: MSIRangeTable[12..15] are 0UL ('incorrect cases'). If RCC->CSR/CR ever held a reserved MSIRANGE value (12-15), msirange becomes 0, then on the PLL path pllvco=0/pllr=0 and SystemCoreClock=0, and at line 350 'SystemCoreClock = SystemCoreClock / tmp' would propagate 0 (no div-by-zero since tmp from AHBPrescTable is always >=1). Reserved MSIRANGE values are not produced by HAL config in this firmware, so unreachable in practice.
findings.impact: Theoretical only: a SystemCoreClock of 0 would corrupt any SysTick/baud derivation, but the function is never called at runtime (see dead-code finding) and reserved MSIRANGE values are not configured. No real exposure in the sealed build.
findings.recommendation: No action required (vendor logic, unreachable). Acceptable as-is.

dead_code: SystemCoreClockUpdate() (lines 271-351): no live caller in app/bootloader/HAL — standard CMSIS API, intentional not orphan. CORE_CM0PLUS / DUAL_CORE / VECT_TAB_SRAM preprocessor branches (130-153, 341-347): config-gated dead (single-core CM4 baremetal, SRAM remap commented out). All dead code is intentional vendor/config-gated, no genuine orphans. The only live local logic is SystemInit()'s VTOR set (218-221) and the BL_BUILD offset selection (157-163).
test_coverage: n/a (HW glue). SystemInit/SystemCoreClockUpdate touch SCB->VTOR, SCB->CPACR and RCC registers directly — not unit-testable without register mocks, and SystemCoreClockUpdate is never called at runtime anyway.
