The one piece of WE-owned logic worth a guard is the VTOR/linker address coupling (finding #1); that is better enforced by a compile-time _Static_assert than a unit test. No Tests/unit coverage exists or is warranted for this file.

role: CubeMX-generated TIM16 init + HAL MSP init/deinit glue. TIM16 is the MAC "TX timeout" timer (MCU_TIM_HDLR_TX_TIMEOUT) consumed by Kineis/Extdep/Mcu/Src/mcu_tim.c.
compiled_in: all (Makefile:199 lists Core/Src/tim.c unconditionally; MX_TIM16_Init called at boot in main.c:811 for every APP/BOARD/COMM config, and again from MCU_TIM_init mcu_tim.c:187)

findings.description: Prescaler 31999 yields a 1 ms tick, but the consumer mcu_tim.c documents and codes a 500 us step. TIM16 is on APB2; with HSI16/PLLM4*PLLN32/PLLR4 = SYSCLK 32 MHz (main.c:1153-1157), APB2CLKDivider=DIV1 (main.c:1172), the APB2 timer clock is 32 MHz (no x2 because APB prescaler is /1). 32 MHz / (31999+1) = 1000 Hz = 1 ms per count. mcu_tim.c MCU_TIM_start computes cnt_val = timeout_ms*2-1 (mcu_tim.c:258) and MCU_TIM_getCount divides the counter by 2 (mcu_tim.c:303), both of which only hold if one count = 500 us. With a 1 ms tick the actual TX-timeout period is ~2x the requested timeout_ms, and getCount reports ~half the real elapsed time.
findings.impact: MAC TX-timeout safety timer fires at roughly double its intended duration. In the sealed UW_DOPPLER deployment a stuck/aborted TX is detected late, lengthening RF-on time and wasting battery; in the worst case the MAC's own watchdog/IWDG assumptions about timeout granularity are violated. Also halves the ARR headroom: at the assumed 500 us step the 16-bit ARR limit is ~32.7 s of timeout, but at the real 1 ms step the same cnt_val overflows checks are mis-scaled.
findings.recommendation: Confirm the intended tick with the Kineis MAC spec. If 500 us is required, set Prescaler=15999 (32 MHz/16000 = 2 kHz = 500 us). If 1 ms is intended, fix mcu_tim.c to stop multiplying/dividing by 2. Do not change one side without the other — add a _Static_assert or a comment tying tim.c prescaler to the mcu_tim.c step assumption.

findings.description: HAL_TIM_Base_MspInit re-enables the TIM16 SLEEP-mode clock via __HAL_RCC_TIM16_CLK_SLEEP_ENABLE() inside the USER CODE block. MX_TIM16_Init (hence this MspInit) runs at main.c:811, AFTER LPM_SystemClockConfig (main.c:802) has zeroed RCC->APB2SMENR (lpm.c:585). So this line leaves the TIM16 sleep clock asserted for all configs. For UW_DOPPLER it is intentional and also re-set in lpm.c:638; for STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER builds that do NOT re-enable it in lpm.c, it is a small unintended low-power leak (TIM16 keeps its clock in SLEEP).
findings.impact: Negligible-to-minor extra idle current (a few hundred nA) in SLEEP for non-UW_DOPPLER configs, where the MAC does not need TIM16 awake. Not relevant to the sealed UW_DOPPLER target (which wants it on), but it is config-leaky behaviour placed in shared CubeMX glue.
findings.recommendation: Move the sleep-clock enable out of the shared MspInit and keep it solely in lpm.c under #if defined(USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP), where the SLEEP power policy already lives, so non-UW configs do not silently leave TIM16 clocked in SLEEP.

findings.description: Init sets Period=65535 and AutoReloadPreload=DISABLE, but the period is never used as configured: mcu_tim.c overwrites ARR on every MCU_TIM_start via __HAL_TIM_SET_AUTORELOAD (mcu_tim.c:268). AutoReloadPreload DISABLE is the correct choice for this dynamic-ARR usage (new ARR takes effect immediately rather than at next update), so this is consistent, but the static Period=65535 is effectively a placeholder.
findings.impact: None functionally. The 65535 init value only governs the window between MX_TIM16_Init and the first MCU_TIM_start; since the timer is not started by init (no Base_Start here), it is inert.
findings.recommendation: No change required. Optionally note in a comment that ARR is set per-start by mcu_tim.c so the static Period is a don't-care.

findings.description: TIM16_IRQn priority is set to 4. The dispatch chain TIM16_IRQHandler -> HAL_TIM_IRQHandler -> HAL_TIM_PeriodElapsedCallback (mcu_tim.c:131) invokes a function pointer stored in timer[] which lives in .lpmSection (RTC backup). mcu_tim.c:137 already guards the call with mcu_tim_cb_is_valid() (flash-range check), so a stale pointer cannot HardFault here. tim.c itself defines no shared state and has no volatile/atomicity concern.
findings.impact: None — noting that the ISR safety actually lives in mcu_tim.c, not tim.c; tim.c's contribution (NVIC priority + handle) is correct.
findings.recommendation: No action. Cross-referenced for completeness.

dead_code: No genuine orphans in tim.c. MX_TIM16_Init is live (main.c:811 + mcu_tim.c:187). HAL_TIM_Base_MspInit/MspDeInit are HAL __weak overrides called indirectly by HAL_TIM_Base_Init/DeInit — live whenever TIM16 is init/deinit'd (mcu_tim.c:187,213). htim16 is consumed by mcu_tim.c and stm32wlxx_it.c:286. The TIM16_Init 0/1/2 USER CODE blocks are empty (CubeMX scaffolding, not dead code). No unused statics/params/returns: the file declares no statics; MspInit/DeInit use tim_baseHandle->Instance.
test_coverage: No unit test exercises the tim.c prescaler/ARR contract. Tests/unit has no tim/mcu_tim test (only test_boot_loop_time.c matched 'tim'). The high-severity finding (500 us vs 1 ms tick mismatch) is exactly the kind of contract that a host-side unit test should pin: feed MCU_TIM_start(timeout_ms) with the documented tick and assert the resulting ARR (cnt_val) and that MCU_TIM_getCount round-trips. Recommend a Tests/unit test that mocks __HAL_TIM_SET_AUTORELOAD/__HAL_TIM_GET_COUNTER and asserts the tick-rate invariant (32 MHz / (Prescaler+1) == expected step), plus the 16-bit overflow rejection path (mcu_tim.c:260-261). The MspInit/DeInit themselves are pure HW glue (n/a for unit test).

role: CubeMX-generated LPUART1 init/MSP (TX/RX on PA2/PA3, AF8) plus hand-written APP_UART power-gating helpers (enable/disable peripheral for CONFIG vs OPERATIONAL) and an RX-activity timestamp used by the CONFIG-mode LED indicator.
compiled_in: all (MX_LPUART1_UART_Init + MSP always compiled; baud/clock branches: USE_SPI_DRIVER or USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP -> HSI/115200, else LSE/9600. APP_UART_* helpers are unconditional. Sealed target APP=UW_DOPPLER hits the HSI/115200 branch.)

findings.description: Static `s_uart_enabled` is write-only: assigned at 4 sites in APP_UART_setEnabled but never read anywhere in the codebase. The public getter APP_UART_isEnabled() (line 233) deliberately ignores it and returns `hlpuart1.gState != HAL_UART_STATE_RESET` as ground truth. Confirmed by full-tree grep (only the 4 writes, zero reads).
findings.impact: No functional impact, but it is a misleading dead store: a reader assumes the cached flag matters when it does not. Costs a byte of .bss and invites future code to trust a flag that may diverge from HAL state.
findings.recommendation: Remove `s_uart_enabled` entirely (and its 4 assignments). The setter/getter already operate solely on hlpuart1.gState, which the comments at 199-202 and 231-233 correctly identify as the source of truth.

findings.description: LPUART1_EXTI_ENABLE_IT() sets EXTI->IMR1 IM28 (LPUART1 wakeup line) unconditionally at the end of every MX_LPUART1_UART_Init. HAL_UART_MspDeInit / HAL_UART_DeInit (called by APP_UART_setEnabled(false)) tear down the GPIO, peripheral clock and NVIC IRQ but never clear EXTI IM28. After a disable, the EXTI mask bit stays armed.
findings.impact: Benign in the sealed target because UW_DOPPLER runs LPM=NONE (uw_doppler_lpmReq returns LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE, kns_app_uw_doppler.c:900), so the STOP-mode wake line is never consulted. It only becomes a latent issue if STOP/STOP2 is ever enabled: a stale-armed IM28 on a de-initialized LPUART could allow a spurious wake (or, since the peripheral RX path is torn down, an unserviceable WUF). Not a current brick, but an inconsistency to note before any LPM=STOP work.
findings.recommendation: Either clear EXTI->IMR1 IM28 in HAL_UART_MspDeInit (symmetry with the enable), or document that IM28 management is intentionally owned by the LPM STOP path (lpm.c LPM_configWakeUpUart / HAL_UARTEx_Enable/DisableStopMode) and that MX init's EXTI enable is a no-op while LPM=NONE.

findings.description: Baud rate (115200 vs 9600) and LPUART1 clock source (HSI 16 MHz vs LSE 32.768 kHz) are selected by two independent #if blocks that must stay in lockstep (HSI<->115200, LSE<->9600). They share the same guard `defined(USE_SPI_DRIVER) || defined(USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP)`, so today they are consistent, but the pairing is implicit — a future edit to one block that misses the other yields an unachievable baud (LSE cannot clock 115200; HAL_RCCEx/HAL_UART_Init would then Error_Handler()).
findings.impact: No current defect. Risk is maintenance-time: a desynced edit produces an init failure (Error_Handler -> potential boot fault) rather than a quiet wrong-baud, so it would be caught at bring-up, not in the field. Low practical danger but worth a guard.
findings.recommendation: Couple the two choices: define one macro (e.g. LPUART1_FAST) in a single place and derive both baud and clock source from it, or add a _Static_assert / comment binding them so they cannot drift.

findings.description: All four init/config calls route failures to Error_Handler() (HAL_UART_Init, SetTx/RxFifoThreshold, DisableFifoMode). On a re-enable via APP_UART_setEnabled(true) during a sealed deployment, an unexpected HAL failure here would call Error_Handler() — whose behavior (hang vs reset) determines field survivability. This is generated code so the pattern is expected, but the re-init path (not just cold boot) now reaches it at runtime via the gesture FSM.
findings.impact: If Error_Handler() is a spin-loop, a transient HAL failure during a CONFIG-mode entry could hang a sealed unit until IWDG resets it (acceptable if IWDG is armed, which the project asserts). Not a usart.c bug per se, but the re-init reachability raises the importance of Error_Handler being reset-not-hang.
findings.recommendation: Confirm Error_Handler() leads to MGR_ERR_logAndReset / IWDG-bounded recovery (not an infinite spin) given that MX_LPUART1_UART_Init is now reachable at runtime, not only at boot. No change needed in this file if Error_Handler already resets.

findings.description: The hand-written, testable logic (APP_UART_msSinceRx sentinel/wraparound behavior, the no-RX-ever 0xFFFFFFFF return, the idempotent resync branches of APP_UART_setEnabled keyed on gState) has no unit test in Tests/unit (grep for APP_UART_/msSinceRx/setEnabled in Tests returns nothing).
findings.impact: Edge cases that gate field behavior are unverified: (a) msSinceRx returning UINT32_MAX when last==0 (drives the CONFIG LED 'idle' state), (b) the now-last unsigned subtraction across a HAL_GetTick() 32-bit wrap (correct as written, but untested), (c) setEnabled early-return consistency vs re-init. A regression here would silently break the CONFIG-mode 'session live' indicator or double-init the UART.
findings.recommendation: Add a small unit suite mocking HAL_GetTick() and hlpuart1.gState: assert msSinceRx()==UINT32_MAX before any RX, correct delta after noteRxActivity, correct wraparound delta, and that setEnabled(true)/setEnabled(false) are idempotent against a mocked gState.

dead_code: One genuine orphan: static `s_uart_enabled` (line 170) is written at 4 sites and never read — APP_UART_isEnabled() uses hlpuart1.gState instead (confirmed by whole-tree grep). Not config-gated; pure dead store. No dead functions: MX_LPUART1_UART_Init (main.c:807, usart.c:213), HAL_UART_MspInit/DeInit (HAL callbacks via HAL_UART_Init/DeInit), and all five APP_UART_* helpers have live callers (kns_app_uw_doppler.c, mgr_gesture.c, mcu_at_console_stm.c). The LSE/9600 baud+clock branch is config-gated dead for the sealed UW_DOPPLER target (live for STDLN/GUI), which is intentional.
test_coverage: Gap. MX_LPUART1_UART_Init and the HAL MSP callbacks are HW glue (n/a for unit test). But the APP_UART_* helpers contain pure, testable logic — msSinceRx() sentinel + tick-wrap subtraction, and setEnabled() idempotent resync on gState — and have zero coverage in Tests/unit. Recommend a mocked-HAL suite (see test-gap finding).

role: Minimalist baremetal cooperative scheduler: registers up to KNS_OS_TASK_MAX function-pointer tasks and runs them round-robin forever in KNS_OS_main, flushing the debug log each iteration.
compiled_in: all (built for every APP/BOARD/COMM under USE_BAREMETAL; the DEBUG/USE_SPI_DRIVER blocks in KNS_OS_main are config-gated within the always-compiled file)

findings.description: taskPool[] is a plain (non-volatile) array of function pointers read in the KNS_OS_main scheduler loop. KNS_OS_registerTask is only ever called from main() init before KNS_OS_main starts (Core/Src/main.c:968,985,1015,1038,1054,1056), and no ISR writes taskPool, so there is no live race today. However the array has no const-after-init protection and the read `if (taskPool[idx] != NULL) taskPool[idx]()` is non-atomic w.r.t. a hypothetical re-registration. A task that called KNS_OS_registerTask at runtime (none does now) could be torn.
findings.impact: No current defect. Latent: if a future task re-registers a handler at runtime, the scheduler could call a half-written pointer. For the sealed deployment this is only a risk if new code adds runtime registration.
findings.recommendation: Document the invariant that registration is init-only (single-threaded, pre-scheduler). Optionally guard with a `_Static_assert`-style comment or a one-time-init latch; not urgent.

findings.description: The scheduler dereferences taskPool[idx] with no protection beyond the NULL check. A registered handler that returns control normally is required for the cooperative model; any task that hangs (unbounded internal loop) permanently starves all other tasks including KNS_OS_TASK_IDLE (which is the LPM/power-down entry, Core/Src/main.c:262). There is no per-task watchdog or yield enforcement here.
findings.impact: In the sealed deployment a hung APP or MAC task means IDLE_task never runs, LPM_enter is never called, and the device neither sleeps nor (without an external IWDG) recovers. The OS layer provides no safety net; it fully delegates liveness to each task and the IWDG.
findings.recommendation: Confirm IWDG covers a stuck-task scenario (it is petted elsewhere, not in this loop). Consider noting in the header that the cooperative model has no preemption/timeout and tasks MUST be non-blocking.

findings.description: KNS_OS_main contains no WFI/WFE of its own. When the runtime LPM mode is LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE (set at Core/Src/main.c:1086 for normal run) and the app is between duty cycles, MGR_LPM_enter early-returns (notify-gating), so the loop is a CPU-bound busy-spin polling every task at full clock. Power-down for UW_DOPPLER is driven by the APP loop (STOP2/SHUTDOWN), not by this OS idle path — so this is the documented architecture, not a kns_os.c bug.
findings.impact: None for the intended UW_DOPPLER design (app loop owns sleep). Worth flagging only because a reader of this file alone would expect the IDLE task to sleep the CPU; the busy-spin is intentional and offloaded.
findings.recommendation: No code change. A one-line comment in KNS_OS_main noting that CPU idling/sleep is delegated to the registered IDLE task (LPM_enter) would prevent future misreading.

findings.description: Doxygen @retval for KNS_OS_registerTask states 'KNS_STATUS_OK ... KNS_STATUS_ERROR otherwise', but the implementation returns KNS_STATUS_BAD_SETTING on out-of-range tskHdlr (kns_os.c:44), not KNS_STATUS_ERROR. Both are distinct enum values (kns_types.h:35 vs :40). Comment rot.
findings.impact: Documentation mismatch only; callers use assert_param(... == KNS_STATUS_OK) so the exact error code is not consumed. No functional impact.
findings.recommendation: Fix the @retval to read KNS_STATUS_BAD_SETTING.

findings.description: tskHdlr is of type enum KNS_OS_taskHdlr_t and compared `tskHdlr < KNS_OS_TASK_MAX`. The enum is unsigned-or-signed implementation-defined; a negative enum value would be impossible from in-range callers but the check does not guard a lower bound. All call sites pass named enumerators so this is safe in practice.
findings.impact: No real-world defect; purely a completeness note on input validation of a public API.
findings.recommendation: Optional: the range check is adequate for the defined enum domain; no change needed unless the API is exposed to untrusted integer input (it is not).

dead_code: No dead code. KNS_OS_registerTask and KNS_OS_main are both live (called from Core/Src/main.c:968-1089) in every config. The taskPool[] global is used by both. The DEBUG and USE_SPI_DRIVER blocks in KNS_OS_main (lines 63-71) are config-gated, not orphans: USE_SPI_DRIVER applies to SPI-COMM builds (e.g. GUI/SPI), the plain MGR_LOG_flush() path applies to UART builds, and the whole flush is compiled out when DEBUG=0 (intentional, matches prod-UART-teardown). No unused statics or unreachable branches.
test_coverage: No unit test exists for kns_os (no Tests/unit file references KNS_OS_*; Glob for *os* unit tests returned none). The pure logic here is small but testable: (1) KNS_OS_registerTask returns KNS_STATUS_OK and stores the pointer for tskHdlr < KNS_OS_TASK_MAX, and returns KNS_STATUS_BAD_SETTING for tskHdlr == KNS_OS_TASK_MAX (boundary) and out-of-range; (2) taskPool entries default to NULL so KNS_OS_main skips unregistered slots. KNS_OS_main's infinite loop cannot be unit-tested directly but the registration/dispatch table can (extract or test via a single-iteration harness). Recommend adding Tests/unit/test_kns_os.c covering the register boundary and NULL-skip dispatch.

role: OS-selector dispatcher: #includes exactly one queue implementation (.c) based on the OS macro. For the sealed build (USE_BAREMETAL) it textually includes kns_q_baremetal.c, which provides the KNS_Q_create/push/pop/isEvtInHigherPrioQ/isEvtInSomeQ FIFO primitives used as the ISR<->main event transport between libkineis MAC and the app.
compiled_in: all (the dispatcher is always compiled; it selects one backend. Sealed target = USE_BAREMETAL -> pulls in kns_q_baremetal.c. FREERTOS/CMSIS_OS2 backends are #error-guarded against multi-OS and NOT compiled for us).

findings.description: The three OS branches only #error on PAIRWISE conflicts, and only inside an already-selected branch. If NONE of USE_BAREMETAL / USE_FREERTOS / USE_CMSIS_OS2 is defined, the file compiles to nothing: no KNS_Q_* symbols are produced and the link fails (or, worse, picks up a stale/weak definition). There is no #else/#error guarding the 'zero OS selected' case.
findings.impact: A Makefile typo or a refactor that drops -DUSE_BAREMETAL yields a confusing link-time error (undefined KNS_Q_push) instead of a clear 'no OS selected' diagnostic. Not a runtime risk for the current sealed build (USE_BAREMETAL is set), but removes a safety net on the most safety-critical TU.
findings.recommendation: Add a trailing `#if !defined(USE_BAREMETAL) && !defined(USE_FREERTOS) && !defined(USE_CMSIS_OS2)\n#error "KNS_Q: no Kineis OS selected"\n#endif` after line 39.

findings.description: Both KNS_Q_push and KNS_Q_pop busy-wait `while (q->mutex == true) ;` AFTER KNS_CS_enter() has already executed __disable_irq() (kns_cs.c:47 masks ALL interrupts). The mutex is only ever set true/false within these same IRQ-masked sections, by the same single bare-metal thread. Therefore: (a) in the current config the loop can provably never spin (no concurrent context can hold the mutex while IRQs are masked), so it is effectively dead code; but (b) if a prior call were ever aborted between `mutex=true` (push:87 / pop:141) and `mutex=false` — e.g. a HardFault/longjmp out of libkineis, or a future caller invoking push/pop with IRQs enabled where a nested same-context call hits a still-set mutex — this becomes an INFINITE busy-wait WITH ALL INTERRUPTS MASKED. That is an unrecoverable hard hang: no RTC wake, no reed wake, no IWDG kick path that runs in IRQ. Total brick.
findings.impact: Latent brick path in the sealed deployment. Probability is low today because KNS_CS masks IRQs and the bare-metal model is single-threaded, but the construct gives a false sense of mutual exclusion and is one refactor (e.g. making KNS_CS_enter a no-op, or calling push from a fault handler) away from a permanent hang with no watchdog escape.
findings.recommendation: The mutex is redundant given KNS_CS already gives full mutual exclusion via IRQ masking; remove the spin entirely, OR bound it with a max-iteration escape that breaks and returns KNS_STATUS_ERROR rather than spinning forever. At minimum add a comment stating the invariant (mutex only manipulated under IRQ mask) and a _Static_assert/runtime guard that the busy-wait is unreachable.

findings.description: KNS_Q_isEvtInSomeQ reads q->rIdx and q->wIdx for every queue WITHOUT entering a critical section (no KNS_CS_enter). These indices are mutated by KNS_Q_push/pop which can run from libkineis RF-driver ISR context (SRVC2MAC is fed from ISRs per kns_q.h:32-33). It is called from the LPM entry gate mgr_lpm.c:281/291 immediately before HAL_PWREx_EnterSTOP2Mode(WFI). This is a check-then-sleep TOCTOU: an ISR may push an event into the (rIdx!=wIdx) window after the check returns false but before WFI. rIdx/wIdx are plain uint8_t (not volatile) so the compiler may also cache them. KNS_Q_isEvtInHigherPrioQ (called inside KNS_Q_pop:133 BEFORE its own CS) has the same lock-free read.
findings.impact: On STM32WL55 STOP2 the queue-feeding wake sources (reed EXTI, SWS RTC) latch a pending IRQ that still wakes WFI, so a real lost-wake is unlikely for those. But if any event is pushed by an ISR whose IRQ is masked/cleared by the STOP2 entry sequence, the device could sleep with a pending queued event and not process it until the next periodic wake — a delayed (not lost) TX/event in the sealed unit. The non-volatile read is also a latent codegen hazard at higher -O.
findings.recommendation: Either wrap the index reads in KNS_CS_enter/exit, or declare rIdx/wIdx volatile in struct q_desc_t, and document that the LPM gate relies on the WFI-wake-on-pending-IRQ property. Verify with a bench race test (push from RTC ISR right at LPM entry).

findings.description: qIdx2Str[] is missing a comma after the first element: "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST" "KNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC" — adjacent string literals are concatenated by C into a SINGLE element "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LISTKNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC". The array is declared [KNS_Q_MAX] (=5) but the initializer now supplies only 4 elements, so qIdx2Str[4] (KNS_Q_UL_SRVC2MAC) is implicitly NULL, and every index >=1 is shifted/wrong. qIdx2Str is indexed by qHandle in MGR_LOG_DEBUG (kns_q_baremetal.c:96) and MGR_LOG_VERBOSE (111,163,176-177,193-194).
findings.impact: Only compiled when DEBUG||VERBOSE (kns_q_conf.h:130). In a DEBUG build, logging the highest-priority queue (KNS_Q_UL_SRVC2MAC, handle 4) dereferences a NULL char* in printf -> can fault or print garbage during MAC/RF debugging; all the mid queues print the wrong name, which actively misleads diagnosis. Not in the production (DEBUG=0) image, so no sealed-unit runtime risk, but it corrupts the exact debug logs an engineer relies on to chase a brick.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing comma after "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST" on line 111. Consider a _Static_assert that the table has KNS_Q_MAX entries (designated initializers [KNS_Q_UL_..]="..." would make such omissions self-evident).

findings.description: Asymmetric guard for the index-snapshot temporaries. push declares `wIdxPrev` under `#ifdef DEBUG` (77-79) but consumes it inside MGR_LOG_VERBOSE (line 111-112), which only expands to code when BOTH DEBUG and VERBOSE are set (mgr_log.h:74-75) — so it happens to compile. pop declares `rIdxPrev` under `#if defined(VERBOSE)` (126-128) and consumes it at line 163 in MGR_LOG_VERBOSE. If VERBOSE is defined WITHOUT DEBUG, rIdxPrev is declared but MGR_LOG_VERBOSE is a no-op (mgr_log.h:90) -> -Wunused-variable. The two functions use inconsistent guards (DEBUG vs VERBOSE) for the same MGR_LOG_VERBOSE consumer.
findings.impact: Cosmetic / build-warning only, and only in unusual flag combos (VERBOSE without DEBUG). No production impact. Worth noting because the project mandates make-clean on flag changes and treats warnings seriously.
findings.recommendation: Guard both temporaries with the exact condition under which MGR_LOG_VERBOSE emits code, i.e. `#if defined(DEBUG) && defined(VERBOSE)`, matching the macro in mgr_log.h.

findings.description: In the QFULL path, MGR_LOG_DEBUG references `wIdxPrev`, which is declared ONLY under `#ifdef DEBUG` (lines 77-79). MGR_LOG_DEBUG expands to real code under `#ifdef DEBUG` (mgr_log.h:68), so declaration and use are consistent here — OK. HOWEVER the QFULL branch also reads `((uint8_t *)qItem)[0]` (the event id) to log it: qItem is the caller-supplied pointer and is assumed to point to at least 1 byte. That is fine for the real event structs, but it is a silent assumption (no length check vs q->eltSize) that would read OOB if a caller ever passed a zero-length item type. Low likelihood given fixed struct sizes.
findings.impact: DEBUG-only. No production risk. Documented as a latent assumption for completeness.
findings.recommendation: None required for production. If hardening debug builds, gate the qItem[0] read behind `q->eltSize > 0`.

findings.description: KNS_Q_create indexes qPool[qHandle] (line 59) and dereferences q->nbElt without validating qHandle < KNS_Q_MAX. Same unchecked qPool[qHandle] indexing in push:76, pop:125. qHandle is an enum and all in-tree callers pass valid constants, but the API takes the enum by value with no defensive bound. A bad handle reads qPool out of bounds and dereferences a wild pointer.
findings.impact: No current defect (all callers use the enum constants). It is a missing-guard robustness gap on a trusted-boundary API also called by the closed-source libkineis. Given the file is on the brick-critical path, a one-line bound check is cheap insurance.
findings.recommendation: Add `if (qHandle >= KNS_Q_MAX) return KNS_STATUS_ERROR;` (or a _Static_assert that all enum handles are < KNS_Q_MAX) at the top of create/push/pop. Note KNS_Q_isEvtInHigherPrioQ also does `qHandle + 1` (line 173) on the enum; if qHandle == KNS_Q_MAX-1 the loop body is correctly skipped, so no OOB there.

findings.description: There is NO unit test for the bare-metal queue FIFO logic (confirmed: Tests grep for KNS_Q_push/pop returns no hits; only test_seq_mc.c and test_shutdown_sequence.c mention the queue header tangentially). The ring-buffer wrap (wIdx/rIdx modulo nbElt), the 'always one empty slot' FIFO-full rule (push:92-99), FIFO-empty (pop:146-151), the priority-preemption short-circuit (isEvtInHigherPrioQ at pop:133), and the LPM-gate isEvtInSomeQ filtering by isLpmBlocker (185-199) are all untested. These are exactly the bits whose correctness gates whether the sealed unit sleeps/wakes/loses events.
findings.impact: Regressions in queue wrap or the LPM-blocker gate (e.g. the isLpmBlocker=false on the evt-list queue, kns_q_conf.c:44) would not be caught before flashing a sealed unit. The qIdx2Str comma bug above is the kind of conf-table error a table-vs-enum length test would catch.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit suite that, with USE_BAREMETAL and a stub KNS_CS, drives a queue through fill-to-full, wrap, drain-to-empty, and verifies isEvtInSomeQ honors isLpmBlocker and isEvtInHigherPrioQ honors priority ordering. Add a _Static_assert / test that ARRAY_SIZE(qPool)==KNS_Q_MAX and qIdx2Str has KNS_Q_MAX entries.

dead_code: The dispatcher itself has no dead code (always-compiled selector). For the sealed build it pulls in kns_q_baremetal.c; within that: (1) The `while (q->mutex == true) ;` spin-waits (push:85-86, pop:139-140) are effectively UNREACHABLE-as-spinning in this config — mutex is only ever set under KNS_CS's __disable_irq() IRQ mask in a single-threaded bare-metal model, so no second context can observe it true. This is config-gated dead behavior (the mutex field is meaningful only for an RTOS port), not an orphan — but see the high-severity finding: it is a latent hang construct, not benign. (2) MGR_LOG_VERBOSE_array (kns_q_baremetal.c:43-50) and all MGR_LOG_* calls compile to no-ops in the production DEBUG=0 image (mgr_log.h:88-92) — intentional, config-gated. (3) The FREERTOS (kns_q_freertos.c) and CMSIS_OS2 (kns_q_cmsis_os2.c) backends are NOT compiled for us (no USE_FREERTOS/USE_CMSIS_OS2) — intentional config-gated dead files, guarded by #error against multi-OS selection.
test_coverage: Inadequate. The testable FIFO logic (ring wrap, full/empty boundary, priority preemption, isLpmBlocker LPM gate) lives in the included kns_q_baremetal.c and has ZERO direct unit coverage (Tests grep for KNS_Q_push/pop = no matches). The mutex/CS interaction is HW-glue-ish (depends on __disable_irq) but the pure ring-buffer index math is fully unit-testable with a stubbed KNS_CS and should be tested. Concrete gaps: full-slot-1 rule, modulo wrap of rIdx/wIdx, isEvtInSomeQ filtering by isLpmBlocker, isEvtInHigherPrioQ priority direction, and a table-length static assert (would have caught the qIdx2Str missing-comma bug).

role: Baremetal implementation of the Kineis OS queue abstraction (KNS_Q): create/validate, push, pop, and priority/LPM-blocker scan over the statically-defined qPool FIFOs shared between MAC ISRs and main-loop tasks.
compiled_in: COMM-independent; compiled when OS=baremetal (USE_BAREMETAL). This is the sealed-deploy OS (UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART use baremetal). The cmsis_os2/freertos siblings are the alternates and are NOT compiled for us.

findings.description: push/pop call KNS_CS_enter() (which does __disable_irq(), masking ALL maskable IRQs) and THEN busy-wait on `while (q->mutex == true);`. Because interrupts are already globally masked when the spin begins, the only context that could ever clear the mutex (another push/pop) cannot run. If the mutex is ever observed true at this point, the spin is an unbreakable hang. The design appears to assume push/pop is the only mutex user and that CS makes the section atomic — in which case the mutex+spin is entirely redundant. The redundancy is harmless only as long as the invariant 'mutex is always false on entry' holds; any future caller, a nested re-entry, or a stale `mutex=true` left by an interrupted/reset sequence turns it into a permanent CPU-stall with IRQs masked (watchdog is the only escape, and IWDG_STOP behaviour in STOP2 must be relied on).
findings.impact: Latent deadlock-with-IRQs-masked in a sealed unit. Cannot self-recover except via watchdog reset; if IWDG is frozen in the active LPM the unit bricks until power-cycle (impossible when epoxy-sealed). Low probability under current single-context use, but high consequence.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the now-redundant mutex+spin entirely (the KNS_CS_enter/exit already guarantees atomicity on this single-core baremetal target), or make the mutex the ONLY mechanism (test-and-set before disabling IRQs) — do not nest a spin-lock inside a global IRQ-disable. At minimum add a bounded retry/timeout so the spin cannot be infinite.

findings.description: `wIdxPrev` is captured only under `#ifdef DEBUG` (line 78) but is referenced inside the QFULL log at line 96-97 which uses MGR_LOG_DEBUG. In DEBUG=0 MGR_LOG_DEBUG is a no-op so the reference is preprocessed away and it compiles; however the guarding is by two different conditions (capture is `#ifdef DEBUG`, use is inside a macro that is empty when `!DEBUG`). They happen to align today, but the use is not itself wrapped in `#ifdef DEBUG`, so any change that makes MGR_LOG_DEBUG evaluate its args while DEBUG capture stays gated would reference an undeclared variable. Fragile coupling between two unrelated gates.
findings.impact: No active bug in current builds. Maintenance hazard: a logging-macro refactor could break compilation or read an uninitialized value.
findings.recommendation: Guard the capture and the use under the same single condition (ideally tie both to whether MGR_LOG_DEBUG expands to code), or just always compute wIdxPrev (it is cheap) and let the no-op macro discard it.

findings.description: Every log call here indexes qIdx2Str[qHandle]/[qHandleTmp]. The qIdx2Str[] definition in kns_q_conf.c:111-112 is missing a comma between "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST" and "KNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC", so adjacent-string-literal concatenation yields only 4 initialized elements for a KNS_Q_MAX==5 array. qIdx2Str[4] (KNS_Q_UL_SRVC2MAC) is therefore NULL, and the human-readable labels for indices 1..3 are all shifted/wrong. KNS_Q_isEvtInHigherPrioQ and the QFULL/push logs can pass that NULL to a %s formatter -> UB / potential fault, and every other label is mislabeled.
findings.impact: Only compiled when DEBUG=1 (and partly VERBOSE=1); the sealed deploy is DEBUG=0 so all these macros are no-ops and the path is dead — no sealed-binary impact. But in dev/bench builds it produces wrong queue names and a possible crash on the SRVC2MAC label, which can mislead exactly the on-bench diagnostics used to validate the seal.
findings.recommendation: Fix the missing comma in kns_q_conf.c:111-112. Add a _Static_assert or compile-time check that the qIdx2Str initializer has KNS_Q_MAX elements. (Finding lives in the paired conf file but is only ever exercised through this file's log calls.)

findings.description: MGR_LOG_VERBOSE_array() is a file-local static whose only call site is line 113 (inside MGR_LOG_VERBOSE). In DEBUG=0 (sealed) and in DEBUG=1/VERBOSE=0, MGR_LOG_VERBOSE expands to `do{}while(0)`, so this function has zero live callers and its body's MGR_LOG_VERBOSE_RAW is also a no-op. It survives -Wunused-function only because the call site textually remains. The `data` param carries __attribute__((unused)) but `len` does not — when the loop body is a no-op the loop still uses `len`, so no warning, but the whole function is effectively dead config-gated code in the production build.
findings.impact: None at runtime (compiled but unreferenced; linker may drop it). Config-gated dead code, intentional logging helper, not an orphan.
findings.recommendation: Optionally wrap the function definition in the same DEBUG/VERBOSE guard as its use to make the gating explicit and avoid a dangling static in release.

findings.location: kns_q_baremetal.c:57-66 (eltSize uint8_t in kns_q_conf.h:121); also note KNS_Q_create not called for KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST
findings.description: q_desc_t.eltSize is uint8_t while KNS_Q_create's qEltByteSize and the push/pop copy use sizeof(struct ...). If any queue item type ever exceeds 255 bytes, eltSize silently truncates in the static initializer (kns_q_conf.c) while qEltByteSize stays 16-bit, so KNS_Q_create returns BAD_SETTING — and worse, push/pop would copy only the truncated byte count, silently corrupting items. Currently all item structs are well under 255 bytes (KNS_SRVC_evt_t ~8B without USE_RX_STACK), so it is latent. Separately, KNS_Q_create is invoked from main.c for only 4 of the 5 queues (EVT_LIST handle 0 is never validated), so the create-time size/length sanity check does not cover that queue.
findings.impact: No active corruption today. Silent-truncation landmine with no compile-time guard if a queue item grows (e.g. enabling RX/DL frames pushes KNS_RX_frm_ctxt_t with DL_FRM_SZ data well past 255). The unvalidated EVT_LIST queue would also escape the create-time mismatch check.
findings.recommendation: Add a _Static_assert that every *_ITEM_BYTESIZE <= UINT8_MAX (or widen eltSize/nbElt to uint16_t consistently), and consider calling KNS_Q_create for the EVT_LIST queue too for symmetry.

findings.description: KNS_Q_isEvtInSomeQ is declared `(void)` in the header but defined `()` (empty parens) at line 185. In C an empty parameter list is an unprototyped/unspecified-args declaration, not `(void)`. The definition does not match the prototype's stricter form and weakens type checking at the definition.
findings.impact: Cosmetic / MISRA-style. No functional effect given the header prototype is in scope at all call sites.
findings.recommendation: Change line 185 to `KNS_Q_isEvtInSomeQ(void)`.

findings.description: Comment rot: the prose in kns_q.h (lines 27-33) lists the queue priorities with KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST as priority '4' (highest) and omits KNS_Q_UL_INFRA2MAC, whereas the authoritative enum in kns_q_conf.h orders lower-index = lower-priority (EVT_LIST=0 lowest, SRVC2MAC=4 highest) and includes INFRA2MAC. KNS_Q_isEvtInHigherPrioQ (line 173, scanning qHandle+1..MAX) correctly follows the enum/conf ordering, so the CODE is right and the header prose is stale/contradictory.
findings.impact: None functional. Misleading documentation that could cause a future maintainer to mis-order a new queue.
findings.recommendation: Update the kns_q.h prose to match the enum (lower index = lower priority, include INFRA2MAC).

findings.description: qPool[] and the q_desc_t fields (rIdx/wIdx/mutex) are shared between ISR-context producers (MAC RF-driver ISRs push SRVC2MAC) and main-loop consumers but are not declared volatile. Correctness currently rests entirely on KNS_CS_enter/exit bracketing every access, which is the right approach (volatile is not a substitute for the CS). One real gap: kns_cs.c's `idx` (nesting counter, kns_cs.c:39) is a non-static global, non-volatile, and `idx % PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE` wraps silently if nesting ever exceeds 8 — an over-deep nest would corrupt the saved-PRIMASK stack and could leave IRQs disabled on exit. KNS_Q_isEvtInSomeQ/isEvtInHigherPrioQ (lines 168-200) read rIdx/wIdx WITHOUT entering the CS, so they can observe a torn index update relative to a concurrent push; for the LPM-entry gate this is a benign race (worst case: one extra wake or one deferred sleep, re-checked under CS at the actual WFI per mgr_lpm.c:281-291).
findings.impact: No defect under current nesting depth and single-core ordering. The unguarded reads in the LPM gate are a theoretical race but self-correcting; flagged so it is understood, not silently assumed safe.
findings.recommendation: Document the 'all access via KNS_CS' invariant in the header; consider asserting idx < PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE in KNS_CS_enter to catch nesting overflow during test.

dead_code: MGR_LOG_VERBOSE_array() (lines 43-50) is config-gated dead code in the production/sealed build: its sole caller (line 113) is inside MGR_LOG_VERBOSE, which is `do{}while(0)` whenever DEBUG=0 or VERBOSE undefined. Not an orphan — it is an intentional verbose-logging helper, alive only in DEBUG+VERBOSE builds. All MGR_LOG_DEBUG/VERBOSE statements in the file (lines 96, 111-113, 149, 163, 176, 193) are no-ops in the sealed DEBUG=0 binary, so the entire qIdx2Str-indexing logging path (including the latent NULL-deref) is dead in deployment. KNS_Q_create/push/pop are __weak (lines 55,69,119) so libkineis could override them, but in this build the .a uses these (per undefined-symbols list); not dead. No genuine orphans.
test_coverage: Partially covered. KNS_Q_push/pop/create are exercised indirectly by kns_app.c self-test paths (kns_app.c:253-267 push/pop round-trips) and by app-level tests, but there is no dedicated unit test in Tests/unit for kns_q_baremetal itself. Concrete gaps that SHOULD have direct unit tests: (1) FIFO-full boundary — the 'always one empty slot' invariant (push until QFULL at nbElt-1 occupancy, line 92-93); (2) wrap-around of rIdx/wIdx via the %nbElt rollover (lines 92,158); (3) KNS_Q_isEvtInHigherPrioQ priority ordering (qHandle+1..MAX) and KNS_Q_isEvtInSomeQ isLpmBlocker filtering (line 192) — these gate LPM entry and are safety-relevant for the seal; (4) a _Static_assert/test that qIdx2Str has KNS_Q_MAX elements would have caught the missing-comma bug. The mutex+CS deadlock path cannot be unit-tested without an HAL mock that simulates a concurrent holder.

role: CMSIS-RTOS2 backend for the Kineis OS queue abstraction (KNS_Q_create/push/pop) — wraps osMessageQueueNew/Put/Get. Included into kns_q.c only when USE_CMSIS_OS2 is defined.
compiled_in: never — gated behind USE_CMSIS_OS2. The build defines USE_BAREMETAL=1 (Makefile:72,294-296) and never defines USE_CMSIS_OS2; kns_q.c:33-39 only #includes this file under USE_CMSIS_OS2. kns_q.c (Makefile:227) is the only TU; this .c is not in the source list itself. Dead for STDLN/GUI/UW_DOPPLER/DOPPLER and every BOARD/COMM combo.

findings.description: The entire file is config-gated dead code. It is text-included by kns_q.c only when USE_CMSIS_OS2 is defined, but the firmware builds with USE_BAREMETAL=1 and never defines USE_CMSIS_OS2 in any APP/BOARD/COMM configuration. The baremetal backend (kns_q_baremetal.c) is the one actually compiled. No test compiles this file either (no USE_CMSIS_OS2 anywhere in Tests/).
findings.impact: None on the shipped binary — it never links. It is an intentional, config-gated alternative OS backend kept for portability, not an orphan. Risk is only maintenance: the code below has latent defects that would bite if anyone ever switched OS=cmsis_os2.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is (intentional portability backend), but document that it is unmaintained/untested for this product. If CMSIS-OS2 is permanently not a target, consider removing the three KNS_Q backend variants to reduce audit surface.

findings.description: No bounds check on qHandle before indexing qPoolHandle[qHandle]. qPoolHandle is sized [KNS_Q_MAX] (line 32). KNS_Q_create writes qPoolHandle[qHandle], and push/pop read qPoolHandle[qHandle], all without verifying qHandle < KNS_Q_MAX. Although callers currently pass valid enum values, the public API takes an enum that a caller could pass out of range, yielding out-of-bounds read/write.
findings.impact: Would-be OOB array access if a bad handle is ever passed. Inert today because the file never compiles, but it is a genuine defensive gap relative to kns_q_baremetal.c which is more guarded.
findings.recommendation: Add `if (qHandle >= KNS_Q_MAX) return KNS_STATUS_ERROR;` at the top of create/push/pop before touching qPoolHandle.

findings.description: push/pop dereference qPoolHandle[qHandle] (passed to osMessageQueuePut/Get) without checking it is non-NULL. If KNS_Q_create was never called for that handle, or returned KNS_STATUS_ERROR (osMessageQueueNew failed) and the caller ignored it, qPoolHandle[qHandle] is NULL and is handed to the RTOS queue API.
findings.impact: NULL queue id passed to CMSIS-OS2 → osMessageQueuePut/Get returns an error code in a well-behaved impl, but behavior is implementation-defined and could fault. Inert today (file not compiled). The create() return value being ignored elsewhere is the real trigger.
findings.recommendation: Guard push/pop: `if (qPoolHandle[qHandle] == NULL) return KNS_STATUS_ERROR;` before the osMessageQueue call.

findings.description: Return-code contract violation. The header documents push as returning KNS_STATUS_QFULL when the queue is full and pop as returning KNS_STATUS_QEMPTY when empty (kns_q.h lines 107-108, 122-130; enum values exist at kns_types.h:67-68 as KNS_STATUS_QFULL/QEMPTY). This implementation collapses both into the generic KNS_STATUS_ERROR. The @todo at lines 75-78 explicitly acknowledges the pop gap.
findings.impact: A caller cannot distinguish 'queue full/empty' (a normal flow-control condition) from a real error. In a baremetal-equivalent scheduler this matters for back-pressure/idle decisions; here it is inert because the file is not compiled, but it is a real API-conformance bug for any CMSIS-OS2 build.
findings.recommendation: Map osMessageQueuePut full → KNS_STATUS_QFULL and osMessageQueueGet empty → KNS_STATUS_QEMPTY (osMessageQueueGet returns osErrorResource when empty with timeout 0). Keep KNS_STATUS_ERROR only for other osStatus values.

findings.description: The header states push/pop 'may be invoked from different ISR/TASK context' and should run under a critical section, and kns_q.h:101-102/118-119 carry a @todo to dispatch to the FromISR variants. This implementation always calls the thread-context osMessageQueuePut/Get with timeout 0 and never selects an ISR-safe path. Under CMSIS-OS2, calling these from an ISR is only valid with timeout 0 (which is satisfied), but no osKernelGetState/__get_IPSR check is done and no critical section wraps the qPoolHandle access.
findings.impact: For a CMSIS-OS2 build, calling from ISR is technically permitted at timeout 0, so this is mostly latent. Inert today (not compiled). Worth noting only as an unfulfilled documented requirement.
findings.recommendation: If CMSIS-OS2 ever becomes a target, add an IPSR-based ISR check or confirm timeout-0 ISR safety of the underlying RTOS; otherwise document that ISR use is restricted to timeout 0.

findings.description: if/else without braces (return KNS_STATUS_OK; ... else return KNS_STATUS_ERROR;). MISRA-like discipline in CLAUDE.md calls for braces on all control statements.
findings.impact: Style only; no functional effect. The else binds correctly.
findings.recommendation: Add braces to the else (and ideally the if) for MISRA conformance.

findings.description: Include guard KNS_Q_CMSIS_OS2_C on a .c file that is itself text-#included into kns_q.c. Harmless but unusual; it guards against double text-inclusion rather than the normal header re-inclusion. The freertos/baremetal siblings follow the same pattern.
findings.impact: None functional.
findings.recommendation: No action required; note the pattern for consistency only.

findings.description: The __weak__ attribute is stripped under UNIT_TEST (so a test could override these). This signals an intent to unit-test the CMSIS-OS2 backend, but no unit test exists for it (Tests/ has no USE_CMSIS_OS2 reference). The scaffolding is therefore unused.
findings.impact: None; just unused test scaffolding for an uncompiled backend.
findings.recommendation: Either add a CMSIS-OS2 unit test (low value, since not a build target) or drop the UNIT_TEST guard from this backend.

dead_code: ENTIRE FILE is config-gated dead code (intentional, NOT an orphan): included by kns_q.c:33-39 only under USE_CMSIS_OS2, which no build/test defines (Makefile forces USE_BAREMETAL=1). The static qPoolHandle[] and all three functions (KNS_Q_create/push/pop) never compile into any shipped image. The UNIT_TEST-conditional __weak__ stripping (lines 36-38,54-56,70-72) is dead scaffolding — no test exercises this TU. No genuine orphans; the dead-ness is purely OS-selection gating.
test_coverage: n/a for the shipped product (file never compiled). The active queue backend is kns_q_baremetal.c, which is what Tests/unit should cover. This CMSIS-OS2 backend has no unit test and warrants none unless CMSIS-OS2 becomes a build target; if it ever does, tests should cover: out-of-range qHandle rejection, NULL-queue (create-skipped) push/pop, and QFULL/QEMPTY return-code mapping — none of which are currently asserted anywhere.

role: FreeRTOS-backed implementation of the KNS_Q queue abstraction (create/push/pop) mapping kineis queue handles to FreeRTOS QueueHandle_t. Included (not compiled standalone) by kns_q.c only when USE_FREERTOS is defined.
compiled_in: never — dead in all configs. USE_FREERTOS is defined in NO Makefile; Makefile:72 hardcodes USE_BAREMETAL=1; kns_q.c:17-31 only #includes kns_q_baremetal.c under USE_BAREMETAL and gates this file behind #ifdef USE_FREERTOS (kns_q.c:25-31). It is also unbuildable: its includes FreeRTOS.h / queue.h (lines 25-26) do not exist anywhere in the repo, and the unit-test tree never references it.
dead_code: ENTIRE FILE is dead. All three functions (KNS_Q_create:41, KNS_Q_push:59, KNS_Q_pop:72) plus the static qPoolHandle[] (line 34) are unreachable in every shipped config (all 4 APP x 4 BOARD x 2 COMM). Reason: config-gated orphan — selected only by USE_FREERTOS, which is never defined; the baremetal twin kns_q_baremetal.c is the live implementation. This is INTENTIONAL multi-OS vendor scaffolding from Kineis (parallel baremetal/freertos/cmsis_os2 variants), but for THIS product it is permanently dead and additionally non-compilable (missing FreeRTOS headers). Not a hazard to the sealed deployment because it is never linked; flagged as info/low so a future OS switch does not adopt the latent bugs below.

findings.description: Entire file is dead code for this product. It is only included by kns_q.c (kns_q.c:25-31) under #ifdef USE_FREERTOS, but USE_FREERTOS is defined in no Makefile and Makefile:72 hardcodes USE_BAREMETAL=1 (the mutually-exclusive guard at kns_q.c:18-21 would #error otherwise). The live queue implementation is kns_q_baremetal.c. Additionally the file is not even compilable in this tree: #include "FreeRTOS.h" and #include "queue.h" (lines 25-26) resolve to no file in the repo, and there is no FreeRTOSConfig.h.
findings.impact: No runtime impact on the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE build — never linked. Risk is purely latent: if someone ever flips OS to FreeRTOS, this file activates with the unfixed defects listed below. Maintenance/audit noise.
findings.recommendation: Either delete the FreeRTOS/CMSIS_OS2 variants outright (product is baremetal-only per Makefile and #error in app), or move them behind a clearly-marked 'vendor unsupported' folder and add a build-time note. If kept, fix the defects below so a future OS switch is not a landmine.

findings.description: No bounds check on qHandle before indexing qPoolHandle[qHandle] (write at line 48, reads at 61 and 78). qHandle is enum KNS_Q_handle_t and qPoolHandle is sized [KNS_Q_MAX] (line 34), so a valid in-range handle is fine, but the API takes the enum by value with no validation. Any caller passing an out-of-range/garbage value (e.g. an int cast, or KNS_Q_MAX itself) writes/reads out of the static array. The baremetal twin has the same shape but operates on a separately-bounded qPool; here the array index is used directly with zero defense.
findings.impact: In a FreeRTOS build, an out-of-range handle corrupts adjacent .bss (write path in create) or dereferences a garbage QueueHandle_t (push/pop) -> queue API call on a bogus pointer -> hard fault or silent corruption. For a sealed device this is a brick/hang class bug. Dead today, but exactly the kind of unbounded-index hazard the audit targets.
findings.recommendation: Add `if ((unsigned)qHandle >= KNS_Q_MAX) return KNS_STATUS_ERROR;` (or _Static_assert + assert) at the top of all three functions before touching qPoolHandle[].

findings.description: KNS_Q_push never returns the documented KNS_STATUS_FULL/QFULL on a full queue. xQueueSendToBack with timeout 0 returns errQUEUE_FULL when full; the code only checks == pdPASS and collapses every non-pass into KNS_STATUS_ERROR (line 66). The header contract (kns_q.h:107-108) promises 'KNS_STATUS_FULL if no more place in queue'. Note also the header names KNS_STATUS_FULL/KNS_STATUS_EMPTY do not exist in the enum (kns_types.h: actual names are KNS_STATUS_QFULL=300 / KNS_STATUS_QEMPTY) — so even the documented contract is unimplementable as written.
findings.impact: Callers cannot distinguish 'queue full' (back-pressure, retry/drop policy) from a real error. In the MAC/APP event path a full queue is a normal transient condition; conflating it with hard error can cause incorrect event-loss handling. Dead today; matters if FreeRTOS path is ever enabled.
findings.recommendation: Return KNS_STATUS_QFULL on errQUEUE_FULL; fix the header doc to use the real enum names (QFULL/QEMPTY). Keep KNS_STATUS_ERROR only for genuinely unexpected returns.

findings.description: KNS_Q_pop never returns the documented empty-queue status. On an empty queue xQueueReceive(timeout 0) returns pdFALSE, which the code maps to KNS_STATUS_ERROR (line 83) and emits a [KNS_Q][ERROR] log every poll. The function's own @todo (lines 74-77) and header (kns_q.h:122-131) explicitly require KNS_STATUS_QEMPTY for the empty case. Empty is the normal steady-state for a polled queue, so this both returns the wrong status and spams the debug log on every idle poll.
findings.impact: Idle polling of an empty queue (the common case) is reported as ERROR and floods MGR_LOG_DEBUG, which on this firmware can churn the UART/log buffer and burn power; callers that treat ERROR as fatal would misbehave. Dead today; latent for a FreeRTOS switch.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish empty from error: return KNS_STATUS_QEMPTY on pdFALSE and demote the empty case from MGR_LOG_DEBUG[ERROR] to verbose/no log; reserve KNS_STATUS_ERROR for true failures.

findings.description: push/pop use the task-context FreeRTOS APIs (xQueueSendToBack / xQueueReceive) with no FromISR variant and no context detection, but the queue layer is explicitly documented to be invoked from ISR contexts (kns_q.h:27-33 'Source SW entity pushes event+data ... from one context (e.g. ISR)'; kns_q.h:98-102 and 115-119 flag this as a known unhandled @todo). Calling xQueueSendToBack from an ISR is a FreeRTOS API misuse (configASSERT / undefined behavior).
findings.impact: In a FreeRTOS build, the SRVC2MAC ISR->task path would call a non-ISR-safe queue API -> assert/fault or corrupted scheduler state. Classic ISR-vs-task reentrancy bug. Dead today; the header even documents it as unresolved.
findings.recommendation: Detect ISR context (e.g. __get_IPSR() != 0) and dispatch to xQueueSendToBackFromISR / xQueueReceiveFromISR with a higher-priority-task-woken yield, or document that this OS variant is unsupported for ISR producers.

findings.description: KNS_Q_create ignores the qLength/qEltByteSize==0 case and the success/else style mixes braces. xQueueCreate(0, ...) returns NULL (handled), but there is no explicit validation; and the success branch uses braces while the else (lines 52-53) is brace-less single-statement — MISRA-like inconsistency. Also the whole TU is wrapped in an #ifndef KNS_Q_FREERTOS_C / #define ... #endif include-guard around a .c file (lines 17-18,88), which only makes sense because the file is textually #included by kns_q.c rather than compiled — fragile pattern.
findings.impact: Cosmetic / style; no runtime effect. The .c-as-include pattern means a stale double-include or accidental direct compilation behaves oddly. Dead today.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit zero-arg validation, brace all branches consistently, and document the intentional include-as-translation-unit pattern (shared with baremetal/cmsis variants).

findings.description: No unit test exercises this file (the Tests tree has no FreeRTOS shim and never references kns_q_freertos.c). This is correct given it is dead — but note the #ifndef UNIT_TEST guards around the __weak__ attribute (lines 38-40,56-58,69-71) imply it was once intended to be mock-overridable in tests, which it is not here.
findings.impact: None — testing a dead, non-compilable file would be wasted effort. The live queue logic is in kns_q_baremetal.c and that is where coverage belongs.
findings.recommendation: Leave untested. If the FreeRTOS variant is ever resurrected, add Tests/unit coverage for bounds-checking and the QFULL/QEMPTY status contract before enabling it in any build.

test_coverage: n/a — file is dead and non-compilable (no FreeRTOS headers in repo, USE_FREERTOS never defined). No unit test exists or should exist for it. The equivalent live logic that DOES need coverage is in kns_q_baremetal.c, not this file.

role: Two pure string/char utilities: bUTIL_strcmp (fixed-length byte compare) and u8UTIL_convertCharToHex4bits (single ASCII hex digit -> nibble, with 0xFF failure sentinel).
compiled_in: all (Makefile:230 lists strutil_lib.c unconditionally, no config guard). Both functions are live in every config: u8UTIL_convertCharToHex4bits called from MGR_AT_CMD (mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c:232/233/242) and MGR_SPI_CMD (mgr_spi_cmd_list_user_data.c:83/84/93); bUTIL_strcmp called from mgr_at_cmd.c:252. Sealed target (UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART) uses both via the AT path.

findings.description: Header documents bUTIL_strcmp as 'This is equivalent to strncmp' (strutil_lib.h:41). It is NOT: strncmp stops at the first NUL terminator in either operand; bUTIL_strcmp unconditionally walks the full u8_strLength regardless of NUL/CR/LF. The only escape is a byte mismatch (line 27-29). So it keeps reading bytes that are logically past the end of a short, terminated input string.
findings.impact: A future caller trusting the strncmp-equivalence claim will read past the logical end of a short input into stale buffer contents. In the current sole caller (mgr_at_cmd.c:252) the input lives in au8_fifo[][FRAME_MAX_LEN] (mgr_at_cmd.c:54), NUL-terminated at i16_atcmdLen (mgr_at_cmd.c:195), and the longest table command name is far shorter than FRAME_MAX_LEN, so the over-read stays inside the allocated array (no OOB today) but compares against stale bytes from a previous longer command. That cannot cause a false positive match here (a mismatch byte before the command-name length still returns false), but the false documented contract is a latent OOB trap if STRUTIL is reused against a tightly-sized buffer.
findings.recommendation: Fix the header comment to state the real contract ('compares exactly u8_strLength bytes, does NOT stop at NUL — caller must guarantee both buffers hold u8_strLength valid bytes'). Do not claim strncmp equivalence. Optionally add an early-out on a terminator if true strncmp semantics are desired by callers, but that would change behavior — only with user OK.

findings.description: bUTIL_strcmp's first parameter pu8_Str1 is non-const (uint8_t *) although it is only read (line 27). The second parameter is correctly const. Asymmetric const-ness forces callers to cast away const: mgr_at_cmd.c:252 does '(uint8_t *)cas_atcmd_list_array[u8_k].pu8_cmdNameString' to pass a const table string.
findings.impact: Const-correctness violation; forces a cast that silently discards const at the call site, defeating compiler protection against accidental writes to the read-only command-name table (which lives in flash for the sealed image).
findings.recommendation: Change signature to 'bool bUTIL_strcmp(const uint8_t *pu8_Str1, const uint8_t *pu8_Str2, uint8_t u8_strLength)' in both .h and .c and drop the cast at mgr_at_cmd.c:252.

findings.description: Neither bUTIL_strcmp nor u8UTIL_convertCharToHex4bits has any unit test (grep for both symbols and 'strutil' across Tests/ returns no matches). Both are pure, deterministic, trivially mockable functions feeding the AT/SPI user-data hex parsers on the sealed deployment's command path. CLAUDE.md mandates a unit test for every piece of logic.
findings.impact: Untested parsing primitives on the only field-input path (AT over UART). A regression in the hex/compare logic (e.g. the boundary chars '0','9','A','F','a','f' or the 0xFF sentinel) would ship unnoticed; the AT layer's hex decode (u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiBinary) depends on the exact 0xFF failure contract.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_strutil_lib.c covering: u8UTIL_convertCharToHex4bits for '0'-'9'->0-9, 'A'-'F'/'a'-'f'->10-15, boundary chars just outside ranges ('/',':','@','G','`','g') -> 0xFF, and bUTIL_strcmp for equal/unequal/first-byte-mismatch/zero-length cases. Also assert HEX_DEC_4BIT_CONVERSION_FAILED_CODE == 0xFF to lock the sentinel the callers hardcode.

findings.description: All four call sites that check the conversion-failure return compare against the literal 0xFF instead of the public macro HEX_DEC_4BIT_CONVERSION_FAILED_CODE defined in strutil_lib.h:34. (Reported here because it is the failure-handling contract of this file's API, even though the literal is in the callers.)
findings.impact: Magic-number coupling: if the sentinel value were ever changed in strutil_lib.h, the callers would silently stop detecting conversion failures and feed garbage nibbles into TX frames. Pure maintainability risk, no current defect.
findings.recommendation: Replace the literal 0xFF with HEX_DEC_4BIT_CONVERSION_FAILED_CODE at the four caller comparisons.

findings.description: Comment rot / mislabeling: HEX_DEC_4BIT_CONVERSION_FAILED_CODE sits under a '/* Private defines */' banner (strutil_lib.h:31) but is part of the public API (referenced by external callers). File header still carries 2013/2020 authorship and 'version 1.0' (strutil_lib.c:5-8) while the longest-match AT refactor and 9-bit MC work have moved around it.
findings.impact: None functional. Minor documentation accuracy.
findings.recommendation: Relabel the define section as exported/public, or leave as-is. Low priority.

dead_code: none. Both functions and the HEX_DEC_4BIT_CONVERSION_FAILED_CODE macro are live in all configs. u8UTIL_convertCharToHex4bits is reachable from both AT (UART) and SPI command managers; bUTIL_strcmp from the AT longest-match command lookup. No unused statics, params, or unreachable branches inside the file (every branch of the hex-digit cascade is reachable, and the final fall-through return is the documented failure path).
test_coverage: No coverage. Both functions are pure, deterministic, host-buildable logic that SHOULD be unit-tested per CLAUDE.md but are not (no test file references strutil or either symbol). Concrete gaps: (1) u8UTIL_convertCharToHex4bits range boundaries and 0xFF sentinel; (2) bUTIL_strcmp equal/mismatch/zero-length and the non-strncmp full-length read behavior. See test-gap finding for the proposed test matrix.

role: User-data TX/RX library: a singly-linked-list FIFO of fixed-size message buffers (reserve/add/remove/flush/find), plus an RX payload buffer. Feeds the Kineis MAC via AT/SPI command managers.
compiled_in: TX half (lines 38-58, 75-377): compiled in ALL configs (Makefile:290 hard-defines -DUSE_USERDATA_TX unconditionally). RX half (lines 60-67, 379-403): gated by USE_USERDATA_RX, which is NOT defined in any standard build (not in Makefile/.cproject) — dead in the sealed UW_DOPPLER target and all current configs. Client-callback loops bodies (179-180, 224-226, 318-319) are gated by USERDATA_RAT_MAX which is 0 in the sealed build (no USE_USERDATA_KINEIS/LORA), so those bodies never execute.

findings.description: USERDATA_txFifoFindPayload compares the trailing partial byte at the WRONG index. The full-byte loop (357-361) walks dataIdx over [0 .. bitlen/8). The trailing partial byte therefore lives at index bitlen/8, but the code reads spTxFifoElt->u8DataBuf[bitlen % 8] and data[bitlen % 8]. For e.g. bitlen=196 (24 bytes + 4 bits) the partial byte is at index 24 but the code reads index 4 (196%8==4) — a byte already fully compared by the loop. The masked partial-byte comparison is thus meaningless: it can return a false-positive match (two payloads that differ only in the final partial byte are treated as equal) or, when bitlen%8 happens to alias a differing earlier byte, a false-negative.
findings.impact: Wrong FIFO element returned/matched. Currently latent because the function has NO live caller (orphan), so it cannot misfire in the sealed deployment today. Becomes a real data-corruption / wrong-ACK bug the moment any RAT or future code uses payload-based lookup. Should read index (bitlen/8) and mask the high bits.
findings.recommendation: Use lastIdx = bitlen/8 for the partial-byte access: compare (u8DataBuf[bitlen/8] & mask) vs (data[bitlen/8] & mask). Add a unit test covering a bitlen that is not a multiple of 8 (e.g. 196, 132).

findings.description: USERDATA_txFifoFindPayload is a genuine orphan: declared in the header but called from nowhere in the firmware (verified across all .c/.h excluding generated Doxygen; the SPI manager does not call it either). It is part of the Kineis library API surface kept for completeness.
findings.impact: No runtime impact (never linked-in as reachable). It carries the high-severity indexing bug above, so it is a latent landmine if a caller is added.
findings.recommendation: Either fix the bug now (preferred, it is small) or gate the function behind the feature that would use it so the broken code cannot be wired up unfixed.

findings.description: sUserDataClientCb[] is declared `extern struct ... sUserDataClientCb[]` (incomplete array, unknown size) but I could not find its definition anywhere in the source tree or in libkineis.a / libknsrf_wl.a (nm shows no such symbol). The three client-notify loops index sUserDataClientCb[u8IdxClient] for u8IdxClient in [0 .. USERDATA_RAT_MAX). In the sealed build no RAT macro is defined, so the enum has only USERDATA_RAT_MAX==0 and every loop body is skipped (0+1<=0 is false) — the array is never dereferenced. The link still requires the symbol to resolve.
findings.impact: Sealed config is safe at runtime (loops empty, no deref). Risk is (a) if a build ever defines USE_USERDATA_KINEIS/LORA, the table MUST be defined with at least USERDATA_RAT_MAX entries or the loop reads past an undersized/absent array (OOB / unresolved symbol); (b) reliance on an undefined extern is fragile. The size of the extern array is unchecked against USERDATA_RAT_MAX.
findings.recommendation: Add a _Static_assert (or runtime kns_assert at init) that the provided sUserDataClientCb table has >= USERDATA_RAT_MAX entries, and document where it is defined (libkineis or app). Confirm the symbol resolves in a real link of a RAT-enabled config.

findings.description: kns_assert here is NOT a no-op: kns_assert.h:43 expands to kns_assert_failed(), which (kns_assert.c:64) calls Error_Handler(), which in the UW_DOPPLER app ends in NVIC_SystemReset() (Core/Src/main.c:1217+). So several FIFO operations can trigger a full device reset on internal-invariant failure: reserve-elt double-add (146), client TxComplete cb returning false (225), flush count!=0 (333), and at the caller AddElt returning false (mgr_at:195) and FlushCb false (614). Most are 'this should never happen' invariants, which is the correct use of assert. But line 146 (USERDATA_txFifoIsEltInFifo) and 333 re-walk the list under conditions that depend on caller discipline.
findings.impact: In a sealed unit, a corrupted FIFO pointer (e.g. RAM upset, or a logic slip) converts into a silent reboot rather than a graceful recovery — acceptable as a fail-safe, but worth being explicit that these assert sites are reset points. No assert is on a normal/expected path (FIFO-full returns NULL gracefully via reserve, not assert), so this is robustness-grade, not a defect.
findings.recommendation: No code change required if reset-on-invariant is the chosen policy. Document that these are intentional fail-safe reset points; ensure crash forensics captures file:line (it does, via kns_assert_failed UART print).

findings.description: Critical sections are applied inconsistently. txFifoLog (89/101) and txFifoFlush (310/329) wrap their list walks in KNS_CS_enter/exit, but the mutating operations txFifoReserveElt, txFifoAddElt, txFifoRemoveElt, and the readers txFifoGetFirst/GetCount/IsEltInFifo/FindPayload do NOT take the critical section while traversing/modifying spFirst and ->spNext. The header (user_data.h:60-75) claims single-writer discipline makes this safe, but txFifoRemoveElt is invoked from the MAC-event processing path while AddElt runs from the AT/SPI command path. If those ever preempt each other (or an ISR walks the list), an unguarded concurrent add/remove can corrupt the linked list (lost element, cycle, dangling spNext).
findings.impact: On the sealed baremetal UW_DOPPLER target the MAC event loop and AT processing run cooperatively from the same main loop, so today there is no real preemption and the list stays consistent. The risk is latent: any future move of remove/complete into an ISR/callback context, or a second writer, silently corrupts the FIFO with no detection. Buffer itself is bounded so no OOB, but a cycle in spNext would make GetCount/Log loop until the kns_assert(u8EltCnt<=SIZE) at 299 trips -> reset.
findings.recommendation: Either document the hard single-context invariant at each unguarded function (currently only the design page mentions it), or wrap the spFirst/spNext mutations and walks in KNS_CS_enter/exit for defense-in-depth, matching what Flush/Log already do.

findings.description: USERDATA_txFifoAddElt is force-compiled at -O0 (#pragma GCC optimize("O0")) to work around a claimed optimizer issue (comment 194-199: writing spNext=elt then spNext=NULL got reordered/dropped). The real fix is already present (set spEltToAdd->spNext=NULL BEFORE spTxFifoElt->spNext=spEltToAdd, lines 200-201), so these two writes target different objects and there is no longer any reorder hazard to justify -O0. The pragma now only pessimizes this function for no reason.
findings.impact: Minor: AddElt runs unoptimized (slightly larger/slower, marginally more energy per AT+TX). Not a correctness issue. The stale workaround comment (194-199) misdescribes current code and will mislead future maintainers.
findings.recommendation: Remove the push_options/optimize("O0")/pop_options pragma and the obsolete reorder comment; the explicit ordering at 200-201 already prevents the issue. Verify with a build that the list is still correctly terminated.

findings.description: The TX FIFO buffer and head are placed in section .retentionRamData, whose NAME implies the data is retained across resets. Per the linker script (ld:135-150) .retentionRamData lives in .data2 and is RE-initialised from ROM by Sram2_Init on every cold/factory boot — i.e. it is explicitly NOT retained (the ld comment even cites 'user_data FIFO' as wanting its initialiser re-applied). The naming is the opposite of the real (and correct) behaviour.
findings.impact: No runtime bug — re-initialising the FIFO on reset is exactly what you want (stale RAM pointers must not survive a reset). The misleading section name is a trap: a maintainer could assume the FIFO persists across STOP2/reset and build logic on that false premise.
findings.recommendation: No behavioural change. Consider a one-line comment at the declaration clarifying 'this section is reloaded from ROM every boot — FIFO is intentionally reset, NOT retained' to prevent misuse.

findings.description: USERDATA_SetUserDataRxByteLen takes uint16_t but asserts u8_userdatarx_bytelen <= sizeof(au8_rxpayload) (==USERDATA_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE, 100). On an out-of-range length it does NOT clamp — it calls Error_Handler()->reset (via kns_assert). The function's own TODO (397) acknowledges clamping would be the safer recovery. The parameter name 'u8_' is also wrong (it is uint16_t). Note: this whole RX block is gated by USE_USERDATA_RX which is undefined in all current builds, so it is dead code today.
findings.impact: Dead in the sealed build (USE_USERDATA_RX never defined). If RX is ever enabled, a single oversized RX length (driven by lower-layer/satellite data) becomes a device reset instead of a clamp — undesirable for a sealed unit receiving uncontrolled downlink lengths.
findings.recommendation: When/if RX is enabled, clamp to sizeof(au8_rxpayload) and return/log rather than assert-reset, per the existing TODO. Fix the misleading u8_ parameter name.

findings.description: const-correctness: USERDATA_txFifoFindPayload(uint8_t *data, ...) only reads data; it should be const uint8_t *data. Same for the header prototype (user_data.h:324). Minor MISRA-like hygiene.
findings.impact: None functional. Prevents callers from passing read-only buffers without a cast.
findings.recommendation: Mark the data parameter const in both .c and .h.

findings.description: Two list-search idioms use uint8_t loop counters and magic structure: txFifoIsInBuf uses uint8_t eltIdx against USERDATA_TX_FIFO_SIZE (==4, fine), but FindPayload's mask construction (366-367) and the 'bitlen%8' usage carry no explanatory constant. Also the union sUserDataAttribute_t (user_data.h:166-174) uses an enum bitfield (enum eUserDataAttrService sf:3) — implementation-defined width/sign for enum bitfields; portable but worth a _Static_assert that the enum fits in 3 bits (max value ATTR_PACK_EMERGENCY==5 fits, but adding a 6th>7 service would silently truncate).
findings.impact: Style/robustness only. The 3-bit sf field silently truncates if a service value >7 is ever added.
findings.recommendation: Add a _Static_assert(ATTR_PACK_EMERGENCY <= 7) (or on the max service) near the enum to guard the bitfield width.

dead_code: RX half (declarations 60-67; functions USERDATA_GetUserDataRxPtr/GetUserDataRxByteLen/SetUserDataRxByteLen 383-401): config-gated dead code — USE_USERDATA_RX is not defined in Makefile/.cproject for any current config including the sealed UW_DOPPLER target. Intentional (feature off), not an orphan. USERDATA_txFifoFindPayload (343-375): GENUINE ORPHAN — compiled in (USE_USERDATA_TX always on) but called from nowhere in the firmware (no caller in AT or SPI managers); part of the library API kept for completeness, and it carries a real indexing bug. Client-callback loop BODIES (179-180, 224-226, 318-319): effectively dead in the sealed build because USERDATA_RAT_MAX==0 (no USE_USERDATA_KINEIS/LORA) makes the loop guard false on the first iteration; config-gated, intentional. sUserDataTxEltDflt.sRatCtrl init is deliberately omitted (comment 45) because it is empty when no RAT is configured.
test_coverage: NO unit test exists for this file (Tests/unit has 38 suites; none target user_data — confirmed by glob). The linked-list logic is pure, HAL-free, and highly testable; it is exactly the kind of code the project rules say must have a unit test. Concrete gaps: (1) USERDATA_txFifoFindPayload partial-byte matching — the index bug at 368-369 would be caught immediately by a test with bitlen not a multiple of 8; (2) add-front vs add-back ordering (AddElt bIsAddBack true/false); (3) remove head / remove middle / remove tail / remove-not-present; (4) reserve until full returns NULL then frees correctly; (5) flush empties and GetCount==0; (6) IsEltInFifo / IsInBuf boundary (pointer just outside sUserDataTxFifoBuf). Recommend a Tests/unit/test_user_data_fifo.c mocking KNS_CS_enter/exit and kns_assert.

role: UART AT-command parser: extracts "AT+...\r\n" frames from the RX stream in ISR context, stores them in a ring FIFO, and dispatches each to its handler via a longest-prefix-match table.
compiled_in: all (core AT manager compiled for every APP/BOARD/COMM; the #ifdef DEBUG trace block and MGR_LOG_DEBUG/VERBOSE calls are no-ops when DEBUG=0, which is the sealed UW_DOPPLER target)

findings.description: u8_lastChar = pu8_RxBuffer[*pi16_nbRxValidChar - 1] is read unconditionally at the top of parseStreamCb, BEFORE any check that *pi16_nbRxValidChar > 0. When *pi16_nbRxValidChar == 0 this is a 1-byte out-of-bounds read at pu8_RxBuffer[-1] (one byte below uartRxBuf[256]). This is reachable: the ISR calls parseStreamCb in a while(cb()==true) loop (mcu_at_console_stm.c:157). A successful extraction sets *pi16_nbRxValidChar = idxStart (line 174). For a cleanly sent command with no garbage before it (e.g. exactly "AT+TX\r\n"), idxStart == 0, so the next loop iteration calls the callback with nbRxValidChar == 0 -> reads index -1.
findings.impact: Undefined behaviour (OOB read of an adjacent static) on a VERY common, attacker/operator-controllable input (any AT command sent with nothing buffered before it). Blast radius is small (reads one stale byte, then the < 5 guard at line 132 bails), so it won't brick today, but it is real UB at the FW entry point and could change behaviour under different memory layout / compiler.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit guard at function entry: `if (pu8_RxBuffer == NULL || *pi16_nbRxValidChar < 5) return false;` and only then read pu8_RxBuffer[*pi16_nbRxValidChar - 1]. Move the last-char read after the length check.

findings.description: kns_assert(0) is invoked from ISR context (parseStreamCb runs inside the LPUART RX ISR). kns_assert_failed (kns_assert.c:50) does a BLOCKING HAL_UART_Transmit(...,200) and then calls Error_Handler(), which for USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP unconditionally calls MGR_ERR_logAndReset(ERR_ASSERT) -> full chip reset (main.c:1243). The comment says 'should no more happen', and under the current single-producer/single-consumer logic the prior full-FIFO guard at line 179 makes it unreachable. But it is a latent 'glitch -> reset from inside an ISR' path: any future change to the index arithmetic, an index corruption (SEU / stack smash), or reordering between the memcpy and the volatile widx++ would turn a recoverable condition into a watchdog-style reset of a sealed, in-ocean device.
findings.impact: On the epoxy-sealed deployment a spurious assert here means a blocking 200ms UART write inside the UART ISR followed by a forced reset, with no field recovery. Converting a benign 'FIFO accounting surprise' into a brick/reset is exactly the failure class the project wants to avoid.
findings.recommendation: Do not assert/reset from ISR for a queue-accounting condition. Either remove the assert (the line-179 guard already prevents the overwrite) or replace it with a non-fatal counter increment (like g_at_* diagnostics in mcu_at_console_stm.c) that main can inspect. Never call Error_Handler from the RX ISR for non-fatal state.

findings.description: Producer ordering relies on the FIFO data memcpy (lines 193-195) completing before the volatile widx++ (line 198), which is the correct release order for the lock-free SPSC ring. However au8_fifo[] is non-volatile, so the C 'volatile' guarantee only orders volatile-vs-volatile accesses; the standard does not forbid the compiler from sinking the non-volatile memcpy past the volatile increment. On Cortex-M4 single-core with this compiler it works in practice, but there is no compiler barrier (no __DMB / no `asm volatile("":::"memory")`) tying the data write to the index publish.
findings.impact: Latent, compiler-dependent: a sufficiently aggressive optimizer could publish u8_widx before the slot bytes are written, letting the main-context popNextAt read a half-written AT frame. Low probability on the current toolchain but it is an unguarded invariant on a safety-critical path.
findings.recommendation: Insert a compiler barrier between the slot write and the index increment (e.g. __DMB() or a memory clobber), or declare the FIFO storage volatile. Document the SPSC contract (single ISR producer / single main consumer) next to the struct.

findings.description: atcmd_info.ATcmdExecType is never initialized when the command is not found, or when the command name matches but the trailing terminator check fails (line 282-284 sets ATcmdIndex = ATCMD_UNKNOWN_COMMAND but leaves ATcmdExecType untouched). decodeAt then reads atcmdInfo.ATcmdExecType unconditionally in MGR_LOG_DEBUG at line 339 ('Type=%d'), i.e. it reads an indeterminate value on the unknown/bad-terminator paths.
findings.impact: Reads an uninitialized stack value into a printf. DEBUG-only (MGR_LOG_DEBUG is a no-op when DEBUG=0), so it does not affect the sealed production build, but it is genuine indeterminate-value use and would trip a sanitizer/MISRA check. The dispatch decision itself is unaffected because ExecType is only consumed when ATcmdIndex < UNKNOWN.
findings.recommendation: Initialize the whole struct at declaration: `struct atcmd_info_t atcmd_info = { .ATcmdIndex = ATCMD_UNKNOWN_COMMAND, .ATcmdExecType = ATCMD_INVALID_USAGE };` and drop the separate line-231 assignment.

findings.description: The #ifdef DEBUG trace block runs inside the UART RX ISR and performs a BLOCKING HAL_UART_Transmit(&hlpuart1, ..., 20) (up to 20 ms) whenever a control char is seen and TRACE logging passes. Long blocking work in an ISR can stall the RX path, drop incoming bytes, and delay other interrupts.
