findings.impact: DEBUG builds only (compiled out for the sealed DEBUG=0 target), so no field impact. In bench/debug it can cause self-inflicted RX byte loss and skew interrupt latency while diagnosing exotic-terminal issues.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as a DEBUG-only diagnostic. If kept, shorten the timeout (a few ms) or defer the trace to main context. Ensure it never compiles into production (it does not today).

findings.description: MGR_AT_CMD_start returns the bool from MCU_AT_CONSOLE_register (false if KINEIS_UART_StartRx_IT returns HAL_BUSY/HAL_ERROR, e.g. UART already BUSY_RX), but every caller ignores the return value (main.c:1032, main.c:1050, usart.c:217, kns_app.c:369 all discard it).
findings.impact: If RX registration fails, rxEvtCb is never set and the AT console is silently dead with no error, log, or retry. For the sealed UW_DOPPLER target the console is a secondary path (magnet/reed is primary), so low severity, but a failed console start is undetectable.
findings.recommendation: Have callers check the return and at least log / increment an error counter on failure. Out of this file's control, but the propagated bool is dead unless callers consume it.

findings.description: When the FIFO is full, the just-parsed AT command is consumed from the stream (line 174 already set *pi16_nbRxValidChar = idxStart) and then silently dropped (return true at line 180) with no +ERROR response to the operator. This is documented behaviour (comment lines 176-178) but the operator gets no feedback that the command was lost.
findings.impact: By design; FIFO depth 4 with one-at-a-time AT usage makes overflow unlikely. A burst of >3 queued commands silently loses the newest with no NACK. No brick/corruption risk.
findings.recommendation: Optional: emit an +ERROR=BUSY/overflow response when dropping so the host can retry, rather than failing silently.

findings.description: i16_atcmdLen is int16_t and computed as idxEnd - idxStart, then the overflow guard '(i16_atcmdLen + 1) > FRAME_MAX_LEN' clamps to FRAME_MAX_LEN-1. This is correct for FRAME_MAX_LEN=128 and even the USE_HDA4 1280 case (RXBUF 2560 > 1280), since idxEnd <= nbRxValidChar <= RXBUF_SIZE fits in int16_t. The clamp silently truncates an over-long command rather than rejecting it, which could feed a malformed (cut) command to a handler.
findings.impact: A pathologically long AT line (> FRAME_MAX_LEN) is truncated to 127 chars + NUL and still dispatched; the handler may parse a partial parameter list. Low risk because valid AT commands are short, but truncation-then-dispatch is silent.
findings.recommendation: Consider rejecting (drop + optional +ERROR) when i16_atcmdLen+1 > FRAME_MAX_LEN instead of truncating-and-dispatching, so handlers never see a half command.

findings.description: Mixed enum/uint8_t handling: u8foundCmdIndex is uint8_t, ATcmdIndex is enum atcmd_idx_t; assignments cross types implicitly (line 231 enum = uint8_t; line 276/281 enum = uint8_t). ATCMD_UNKNOWN_COMMAND == ATCMD_MAX_COUNT, and the index is compared/used as both a loop bound and a sentinel. It works but the implicit enum<->integer casts are MISRA 10.x nits and slightly obscure the 'found vs unknown' contract.
findings.impact: No functional defect; readability / MISRA-cleanliness only.
findings.recommendation: Use the enum type consistently for the found index, or add explicit casts and a short comment that UNKNOWN == MAX_COUNT is the sentinel.

dead_code: No dead code in this file. All five public functions have live callers (MGR_AT_CMD_start: main.c/usart.c/kns_app.c; isPendingAt: main.c + mgr_at_cmd_list_certif.c; popNextAt/decodeAt: kns_app*.c loops; getLastActivityTick: mgr_lpm_uw.c + kns_app_uw_doppler.c). Both statics (s_atcmdfifo, s_last_at_activity_tick) are used. MGR_AT_CMD_macEvtProcess is a __weak stub intentionally overridden elsewhere (not dead). The #ifdef DEBUG block (101-120) and USE_HDA4 FRAME_MAX_LEN=1280 branch (43) are config-gated, not orphans. The kns_assert(0) at line 202 is effectively unreachable under the line-179 full-FIFO guard (a defensive 'should never happen'), but reported above as a hazardous ISR-reset path rather than as dead code.
test_coverage: Partial / weak. Tests/unit/test_at_dispatch.c tests the longest-prefix-match concept but against a COPY of the logic (its own dispatch() + a mirrored TABLE), not the real MGR_AT_CMD_getAtType — so the actual terminator check (lines 271-284) and the real cas_atcmd_list_array are untested, and a divergence between the mirror and the real code would not be caught. Genuine gaps: (1) MGR_AT_CMD_parseStreamCb has ZERO unit coverage — none of the ring-buffer wrap, FIFO-full drop, idxStart==0 re-entry (the line-99 OOB trigger), '\\r' vs '\\n' vs '\\r\\n' EOL handling, length clamp, or min-length guard is tested. (2) The FIFO SPSC index arithmetic (isPendingAt/popNextAt across the uint8_t wrap at 256) is untested. These are directly unit-testable with HAL_GetTick mocked and should be added, especially a regression test for the nbRxValidChar==0 / idxStart==0 path.

role: Common helpers for the AT-command manager: emits +OK/+ERROR lines, maps libkineis KNS_status_t to the AT +ERROR=N surface, and formats all delayed RF response notifications (+TX/+RX/+DL/+SATDET/+TXACK/+RFABORT) to the UART console.
compiled_in: all (unconditionally in Makefile C_SOURCES line 219; no #ifdef around any function). Functions are exercised by the UART AT path (COMM=UART); under COMM=SPI the file still compiles and the helpers are linked, but the RF-notification path is driven by mgr_spi_cmd instead. Sealed target APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART uses it fully.

findings.description: +SATDET uses %ld for two uint32_t fields (detect_duration, detected_freq). uint32_t is `unsigned int` on this ARM EABI; %ld is the conversion for signed `long`. On STM32 long==int==32-bit so the width matches and output is correct in practice, but it is a formally mismatched conversion (signed vs unsigned, int vs long) and would mis-print on any toolchain where long != int. Correct specifier is %lu / %u.
findings.impact: None on the deployed STM32WL55 toolchain (newlib, 32-bit long). Purely a portability/MISRA-cleanliness nit; no wrong output for the sealed build.
findings.recommendation: Change to "+SATDET=%u,%u,%f\r\n" (uint32_t -> %u) to match the actual argument types.

findings.description: MGR_AT_CMD_mapKnsStatusToError() folds only KNS_STATUS_ABORT(=7) to ERROR; every other code is passed through with a raw cast `(enum ERROR_RETURN_T)s`. If a caller ever passes KNS_STATUS_OK(=0) on a perceived-error path, it yields `+ERROR=0` (no ERROR_RETURN_T enumerator has value 0; ERROR_UNKNOWN=1000). The doc comment claims it 'passes any other code through' which is intended, but 0 is a degenerate value the GUI would read as a contradictory success-coded error.
findings.impact: Cosmetic/at-most-confusing for the GUI in the unlikely case an OK status reaches an error logger. No hang/brick. All current call sites (certif/general/mac/user_data) invoke it only on non-OK branches, so unreachable today.
findings.recommendation: Optionally guard: if s==KNS_STATUS_OK return (ERROR_RETURN_T)KNS_STATUS_ERROR, or assert s!=OK. Low priority; document the invariant that callers must not pass OK.

findings.description: Unreachable `break;` statements: every case block ends with `return true;` (or `return false`/`break` in default) immediately followed by a `break;`. The breaks are dead statements. Not a bug, but several compilers/static analyzers (and MISRA) flag unreachable code; CLAUDE.md asks for MISRA-like discipline.
findings.impact: No runtime effect. Slight noise; could mask a real missing-break if a future edit converts a `return` into fall-through logic.
findings.recommendation: Remove the post-return `break;` lines, or restructure cases to a single return at the end. Cosmetic.

findings.description: ATCMD_RSP_DLOK casts atcmd_rsp_data to `struct KNS_MAC_RX_frm_ctxt_t *`, but the live caller (mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c:574) passes &srvcEvt.rx_ctxt which IS a KNS_MAC_RX_frm_ctxt_t — yet semantically DLOK is a decoded DL message whose dedicated union member is msg_ctxt (KNS_MAC_RX_dl_msg_ctxt_t). It only works because both packed structs share an identical leading layout (uint8_t data[DL_FRM_SZ]; uint16_t data_bitlen;). The handler reads exactly those two fields, so it is safe today purely by layout coincidence.
findings.impact: Currently correct. Fragile: if libkineis reorders KNS_MAC_RX_frm_ctxt_t or KNS_MAC_RX_dl_msg_ctxt_t, +DL would print garbage/over-read. Both structs are in the closed-lib ABI region we don't control.
findings.recommendation: Caller should pass &srvcEvt.msg_ctxt for DLOK and the handler cast to KNS_MAC_RX_dl_msg_ctxt_t, OR add a _Static_assert that offsetof(data) and offsetof(data_bitlen) match between the two structs. Documents the load-bearing layout assumption.

findings.description: Defensive NULL checks (lines 66,83,118,145,161) silently return true when atcmd_rsp_data==NULL for data-bearing response types (TXOK/RXOK/RXERROR/DLOK/SATDET): the function reports success to the caller but emits NO AT line. A host waiting for +TX=/+RX= would see nothing and could stall on its side.
findings.impact: No firmware hang (returns true). But a NULL passed where data is expected produces a silent no-response; for the sealed unit this only matters to a bench host, not autonomous operation. Current callers always pass non-NULL for these types, so unreachable today.
findings.recommendation: Consider emitting a fallback +ERROR for the data-expected cases when data is NULL, or at least return false so the caller knows nothing was sent. Low priority given current call sites.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. All five public functions have live callers (logSucceedMsg/logFailedMsg across mgr_at_cmd_list_*.c; mapKnsStatusToError in certif/general/mac/user_data; sendResponse in mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c). Every enum case in bMGR_AT_CMD_sendResponse is reached by an actual emitter (verified: TXOK/TXACKOK/TXACKNOTOK/SATDET/SATLOST/SATDETTO/RXOK/DLOK/RXTIMEOUT/TXTIMEOUT/RXERROR/RFABORTED all produced in mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c). The trailing `break;` after each `return` (lines 78,101,107,115,130,136,142,158,173,179) are unreachable dead STATEMENTS but harmless. The `default` branch is reachable defensive code (guards against future enum additions). No config-gated dead code in this file — it has no #ifdefs.
test_coverage: No unit test covers this file. Two pieces of pure, HW-independent logic are untested and SHOULD be: (1) MGR_AT_CMD_mapKnsStatusToError — verify ABORT(7)->ERROR(1) folding, BAD_SETTING(6) pass-through, RF_ERR(100) pass-through, and the OK(0) edge case; trivially unit-testable, no mocks. (2) bMGR_AT_CMD_sendResponse format strings per response type, by capturing MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send output (the harness already mocks console-style sinks elsewhere) — would lock the +TX=/+RX=/+SATDET= wire format the GUI parses and catch the %ld/%u regression and any future field-order change. test_at_dispatch.c exists but does not touch these symbols. The _Static_assert block (lines 24-36) already provides good compile-time ABI coverage.

role: Declarative table defining the AT-command registry: a const array cas_atcmd_list_array[ATCMD_MAX_COUNT] of {name string, name length, handler fn-ptr}, plus the atcmd_version string. Consumed by the dispatcher in mgr_at_cmd.c.
compiled_in: all (file always built). Entry set varies by config: ~23 common entries always; AT+RX gated by USE_RX_STACK; 31 UW_DOPPLER entries gated by USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP; 7 DOPPLER entries gated by USE_DOPPLER_APP (UW_DOPPLER vs DOPPLER are mutually exclusive, enforced by main.c:79-80). Sealed target APP=UW_DOPPLER builds the common+UWD set (54 entries).

findings.description: The per-command enum constants (AT_VERSION, AT_TX, AT_SWS, ...) in enum atcmd_idx_t are never used to index cas_atcmd_list_array. Verified: the dispatcher (mgr_at_cmd.c:246-258) iterates by loop counter u8_k and matches by string prefix; no .c file references cas_atcmd_list_array[AT_xxx]. The enum's only live uses are ATCMD_MAX_COUNT (array size + loop bound) and ATCMD_UNKNOWN_COMMAND (sentinel). Consequently the 1:1 positional correspondence between the enum order and the array initializer order is NOT load-bearing for dispatch; only the COUNT must match. The elaborate 'longest prefix first' / ordering comments (lines 63-67, 80, 90-92, 105, 112) imply array order matters, which is misleading for the enum side.
findings.impact: None at runtime today. Maintenance hazard: a future edit that adds an entry to the array but forgets the matching enum line (or vice-versa) silently changes ATCMD_MAX_COUNT relative to the initializer count. If the enum gains an entry the array lacks, the trailing array slots are zero-initialized (handler == NULL) and the dispatcher's NULL check at mgr_at_cmd.c:342 turns it into a harmless ERROR_UNKNOWN_AT_CMD. If the array gains an entry the enum lacks, the initializer would over-run the [ATCMD_MAX_COUNT] bound and the compiler errors (caught at build) -- so the dangerous direction is fenced, but the silent direction (enum > array) yields a dead command slot with no diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Add a _Static_assert that the number of designated array entries equals ATCMD_MAX_COUNT, or drop the per-command enum entirely (it is write-only) and derive ATCMD_MAX_COUNT via sizeof(cas_atcmd_list_array)/sizeof(its element) so the count can never desync from the initializer. At minimum, add a one-line comment stating the enum is count-only and not an index.

findings.description: atcmd_version is a hand-maintained string ('v0.8.1') with a header comment 'update AT cmd version above if you add or remove commands'. There is no compile-time link between the command set and this string, so it relies purely on the editor remembering. The Doxygen snapshot in Kineis/Doc still shows the stale 'v0.6', confirming this string has drifted from its documentation before.
findings.impact: Low. A GUI/host that gates behaviour on the reported AT version (AT+VERSION returns this) could mis-detect capabilities if the string is not bumped when commands change. Not a brick/hang risk.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is for now; if version-gating ever becomes functional, derive or assert the version against the command count. Otherwise leave a TODO; no code change required for the sealed deploy.

findings.description: AT+RX (USE_RX_STACK) and the entire USE_DOPPLER_APP block are config-gated dead code in the sealed UW_DOPPLER build: USE_RX_STACK is not defined for the sealed target and USE_DOPPLER_APP is mutually exclusive with USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP. These are intentional config gates, not orphans.
findings.impact: None. Correctly excluded from the sealed binary by preprocessor.
findings.recommendation: No action. Documented here only to mark them as intentionally-gated rather than overlooked.

findings.description: The table's load-bearing invariants are untested by a unit test: (a) every u8_cmdNameLen equals strlen(pu8_cmdNameString) -- verified correct for all 62 entries in this audit by script, but nothing guards regressions; (b) no two entries in a single compiled config share an identical command name (would make the later one unreachable, since the dispatcher keeps the first longest match); (c) the array length equals ATCMD_MAX_COUNT. A small host-side test could iterate cas_atcmd_list_array[0..ATCMD_MAX_COUNT-1] and assert these. The dispatcher's longest-prefix logic IS exercised elsewhere, but the table self-consistency is not.
findings.impact: A future entry with a wrong length field (off-by-one) would mis-dispatch or shadow a neighbour, or a duplicate name would silently disable a command. For an epoxy-sealed unit this is a permanent field-config bug with no recovery. Low probability given current correctness, but cheap to fence.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit case asserting, for the UW_DOPPLER config, that strlen(name)==u8_cmdNameLen for every entry and that all names are unique. Bonus: assert handler pointers are non-NULL (the dispatcher tolerates NULL, but a NULL here is almost certainly a mistake).

dead_code: No genuine orphans. Config-gated dead code only: AT+RX (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:50-52, requires USE_RX_STACK, absent in sealed build) and the USE_DOPPLER_APP block (:121-130, mutually exclusive with the sealed UW_DOPPLER app per main.c:79-80). The per-command enum constants in the paired header are effectively write-only (never used as array indices) but are not 'dead' in the linker sense -- they define ATCMD_MAX_COUNT. Both atcmd_version (read by mgr_at_cmd_list_general.c:52) and cas_atcmd_list_array (read by the dispatcher) are live.
test_coverage: Logic in this file is purely a static initializer (no executable code), so 'coverage' means table-invariant assertions. Currently NONE exist. Concrete gaps: (1) u8_cmdNameLen == strlen(name) per entry; (2) command-name uniqueness within a config; (3) array entry count == ATCMD_MAX_COUNT; (4) non-NULL handlers. All four are cheap host-side asserts and currently unguarded. I manually verified (1) and (3) correct for the present table during this audit.

role: Certification AT command handler: implements AT+CW (start/stop continuous-wave and modulated-wave bursts in LDA2/LDA2L/VLDA4/LDK/HDA4/CW) by pushing random bitstreams through the libkineis RF TX API, with optional ISR-driven continuous re-transmit and inter-burst delay.
compiled_in: all (unconditional in Makefile:225; AT+CW registered with no APP guard in mgr_at_cmd_list.c:55, so reachable in the sealed APP=UW_DOPPLER build too)

findings.description: On the startImmediate failure path the code ships a raw libkineis status as an AT error: `return bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg((enum ERROR_RETURN_T) KNS_STATUS_RF_ERR);`. KNS_STATUS_RF_ERR is 100 (kns_types.h:44), but valid ERROR_RETURN_T values start at ERROR_UNKNOWN = KNS_STATUS_MAX = 1000 (kineis_sw_conf.h:54, kns_types.h:87). So the GUI receives `+ERROR=100`, a value outside the entire ERROR_RETURN_T table. Every other failure path in this same function correctly routes through MGR_AT_CMD_mapKnsStatusToError(status); this one line bypasses the mapper that commit 'Kineis v11.1.0' #4 introduced precisely to stop raw KNS status leaking into the +ERROR surface.
findings.impact: AT+CW TX-start failure reports an unrecognized error code to the host/GUI parser. Cosmetic/diagnostic only for the sealed unit (AT+CW is a bench/certification command, not used in autonomous deployment), but it is an inconsistency the rest of the file already solved.
findings.recommendation: Replace with `return bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg(MGR_AT_CMD_mapKnsStatusToError(KNS_STATUS_RF_ERR));` to fold it into the stable KNS_STATUS_ERROR (=1) mapping like the other paths.

findings.description: The shared state mw_cfg (struct), isToBeTransmit (bool) and repPeriod_s (uint16_t) are plain (non-volatile) globals written by the main/AT-command context (MGR_AT_CMD_sendRandomTxData, bMGR_AT_CMD_CW_cmd) and concurrently read/written by the TX_DONE callback eoAtMW_isr_cb, which the header comment (line 138) states runs in ISR context (SUBGHZ ISR). There are no critical sections and no volatile qualifiers. mw_cfg.valid / isRfAlreadyOn / isToBeTransmit are the handshake flags between the two contexts; the compiler may cache them across the ISR boundary and reads/writes of the multi-field struct are non-atomic.
findings.impact: On the live non-blocking path (KNS_RF_IN_BLOCKING_MODE undefined), a torn or stale read between main-thread AT+CW=0 (stop) and the ISR re-trigger could miss the stop request and fire one extra burst, or read a half-updated rf_cfg. Bench-only command, low field impact, but it is a genuine main-vs-ISR data race.
findings.recommendation: Qualify the handshake flags (at least mw_cfg.valid, isRfAlreadyOn, isToBeTransmit) volatile, or guard the read-modify-write of mw_cfg in the AT-command path with a short critical section (disable SUBGHZ IRQ). Document the ownership model.

findings.description: DELAY_MS is a busy-wait spin loop (NOP loop, no systick) invoked from ISR context at line 157 (eoAtMW_isr_cb) with argument repPeriod_s*1000. repPeriod_s is uint16_t (max 65535), so the delay request can be up to 65,535,000 ms. Two problems: (a) it is a multi-minute hard busy-wait executed inside an ISR, blocking all lower/equal priority interrupts the whole time; (b) the macro computes `_count = (time_ms) * _nb_for_loop_per_ms` in uint32_t — at 32 MHz _nb_for_loop_per_ms=8000, so any time_ms above ~536870 overflows uint32_t (the header even documents the 536870 ms ceiling at line 38 but nothing enforces it), making the actual delay wrong/short for large values.
findings.impact: Reachable only via the 4-parameter AT+CW form (repPeriod_s>0), a bench/certification feature, and the live path uses the ISR callback. A large repPeriod_s pins the CPU in an ISR busy-wait for minutes (starves the system) and the requested period silently truncates past the documented ceiling. Not exercised in sealed autonomous operation, but a foot-gun if AT+CW is ever scripted on a connected unit.
findings.recommendation: Clamp repPeriod_s to the documented max at parse time, and avoid busy-waiting in ISR — for the continuous-burst case prefer scheduling the next burst from a timer/main loop rather than spinning. At minimum add a compile-time/runtime bound check so the multiply cannot overflow.

findings.description: sscanf type mismatches and narrowing on the AT+CW parse: (1) %ld is used for `&cwFrq` which is int32_t (kns_app ABI: int32_t == int, not long) — same width on this EABI so harmless in practice but a strict-conformance / portability defect. (2) cwFrq is int32_t parsed as signed, then assigned to uint32_t center_freq (line 398/411): a negative or out-of-band frequency is silently reinterpreted as a huge unsigned value with no range validation. (3) cwPwr is uint16_t parsed via %hu, then assigned to int8_t power (line 399/412): values >127 wrap to negative, values >255 are already truncated by %hu — no clamp to the valid dBm range.
findings.impact: Malformed AT+CW frequency/power on the bench can push an out-of-range value straight into KNS_RFTX_setCfg with no guard here (libkineis may reject it, but we do not validate). Bench command, host-controlled, so low severity; still an input-validation gap and a strict-aliasing/format nit.
findings.recommendation: Use a matching specifier for int32_t (e.g. parse into a long then range-check, or use SCNd32), and bounds-check cwFrq (plausible Argos band) and cwPwr (e.g. 0..127) before assigning, returning ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_VALUE on out-of-range.

findings.description: bitstream is filled with random() (line 202), but random()/srandom() is never seeded anywhere in the firmware (no srandom/srand call found). The 'random' certification payload is therefore the same deterministic sequence every boot.
findings.impact: For a certification/test signal this is usually acceptable (often even desirable for reproducibility), but the comment/intent says 'random' and it is not. No functional risk; purely a correctness-of-description issue.
findings.recommendation: Either seed once (e.g. srandom from SN/UID/RTC) if true randomness is intended, or reword the comments to 'pseudo-random fixed pattern' to avoid misleading future readers.

findings.description: HDA4 bitstream_bitlen is hardcoded to 5551 with a contradictory inline comment `// 5519-128-256=5135` (the arithmetic yields 5135, not 5551, and 5519 != 5551). Comment-rot / unexplained magic number.
findings.impact: USE_HDA4 is off by default (Makefile:98), so this is dead in the sealed build; but if HDA4 is ever enabled the value is unexplained and the comment actively misleads. The runtime assert at line 283 bounds it against the 700-byte (5600-bit) buffer so no overflow.
findings.recommendation: Fix or remove the stale comment and document where 5551 comes from (frame structure), or derive it from a named constant.

findings.description: All KNS_RF_IN_BLOCKING_MODE code is config-gated dead code: the macro is not defined anywhere in the repo (build flags, headers, or libkineis config — verified by full-tree grep). Dead in every current config: the blocking AT+CW retransmit while-loop (lines 413-427), the local `bool bool_status` (line 331), and the mgr_at_cmd.h include (lines 20-22). The complementary #ifndef path (callback eoAtMW_isr_cb, lines 132-167, and eop_isr_cb assignments) is the only live one. This is intentional portability scaffolding, not an orphan.
findings.impact: None functionally; it is correctly guarded. Slight maintenance cost (two divergent control-flow paths, only one of which is ever built/tested).
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is if blocking mode is a supported libkineis variant; otherwise consider removing to reduce the untested surface. No action required for the sealed build.

findings.description: MGR_LOG_array's loop body MGR_LOG_DEBUG_RAW expands to `do {} while(0)` when DEBUG=0 (mgr_log.h:89), so in the sealed/production build (DEBUG=0) the entire function is a no-op for-loop over `len`. The `data` param carries __attribute__((unused)) (so it does not warn) but the function is still called at line 306-307, computing ((bitstream_bitlen+7)/8) for nothing.
findings.impact: Negligible: a short empty loop on a bench-only TX path. No correctness issue.
findings.recommendation: Optionally guard the call site / whole helper under the same DEBUG condition, or mark the call so it is elided in production. Not required.

dead_code: All KNS_RF_IN_BLOCKING_MODE blocks (lines 20-22, 330-332, 413-427) are config-gated dead code: the macro is defined nowhere in the repo (verified by full-tree grep incl. Makefile/headers/libkineis conf). Intentional portability scaffolding, not an orphan. The complementary #ifndef KNS_RF_IN_BLOCKING_MODE path (eoAtMW_isr_cb callback, lines 132-167) is the live one. USE_HDA4 blocks (lines 75-79, 232-240, 385-389, 407-409) are config-gated off by default (Makefile:98) — intentional. MGR_LOG_array (122-130) degenerates to an empty loop when DEBUG=0 but is still called (live in DEBUG=1 bench builds). No genuine orphans: bMGR_AT_CMD_CW_cmd is referenced from mgr_at_cmd_list.c:55; both static helpers are used.
test_coverage: No coverage. Tests/unit has no test referencing certif / CW_cmd / sendRandomTxData / mw_cfg (verified by grep over Tests/). The testable pure logic that should be unit-tested: (1) the modulation->bitstream_bitlen mapping plus the `bitstream_bitlen <= sizeof(bitstream)*8` invariant (assert at line 283) for every modulation in both USE_HDA4=0 and =1 (the 40-byte vs 700-byte buffer) — a regression here could silently overflow if a new modulation's bitlen is added without resizing the buffer; (2) the sscanf parameter parsing/branch selection (3-param vs 4-param form, cwMode->modulation switch) including out-of-range freq/power rejection; (3) the cast at line 322 / mapKnsStatusToError consistency. HW/RF and ISR-callback paths are HW glue and not unit-testable, but the mapping and bounds logic are.

role: AT-command handlers for the DOPPLER app: AT+DPLCFG (TX config), AT+DPLWKU (boot-counter read/reset), AT+SAVE, AT+LOG (event-log dump/clear), AT+BATCFG, AT+LED, AT+DEPLOY.
compiled_in: APP=DOPPLER only (Makefile line 356 -DUSE_DOPPLER_APP, line 362 adds this .c). NOT compiled for the sealed target APP=UW_DOPPLER (that uses the separate mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c). Registered in cas_atcmd_list_array under #ifdef USE_DOPPLER_APP (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:121-130). BATCFG body and LED body are further gated by BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC / BSP_HAS_LED_RGB respectively.

findings.description: AT+DPLWKU status prints a 64-bit counter by concatenating its two 32-bit halves in decimal: "+DPLWKU=%lu%08lu" with count_hi then count_lo. Decimal concatenation of a high and low 32-bit word is mathematically wrong: a uint32_t low word ranges 0..4294967295 (up to 10 decimal digits), not 8. The %08lu is a *minimum* width pad, so it does not truncate but also cannot make the math correct. Example: count = 0x1_00000000 (=4294967296) yields count_hi=1, count_lo=0 and prints "100000000" (=100,000,000) instead of 4294967296. Any value where the low word has fewer than 10 significant digits, or where carry between halves matters, is misreported.
findings.impact: Operator reads a wrong boot/wakeup count once the wear-leveled WKU counter exceeds 2^32 (or whenever low word < 10 digits). For DOPPLER this is a diagnostic-only command so it cannot brick, but it silently corrupts a field-diagnostic value an operator may trust for deployment health checks.
findings.recommendation: Print the full 64-bit value with a single conversion: use PRIu64 from <inttypes.h> (MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send("+DPLWKU=%" PRIu64 "\r\n", count)), or if the console's vsnprintf lacks %llu support, do proper decimal conversion of the uint64_t into a local buffer rather than digit concatenation of the two halves.

findings.description: AT+BATCFG action sets the min-TX voltage via MGR_BAT_setMinTxVoltage_mV() (mgr_bat.c:198-202 sets only the runtime static min_tx_voltage_mV) but never marks the DOPPLER NVM config dirty and the value is not part of the persisted struct. The doppler NVM struct (kns_app_doppler.c:143-147) stores msg_count/led_mode/deployed/intervals but has NO bat_min_tx_mV field, and nvmSave() does not capture it. So AT+SAVE will not persist a BATCFG change, and it reverts to MGR_BAT_DEFAULT_MIN_TX_MV on the next boot. Contrast AT+LED, which correctly calls KNS_APP_doppler_markDirty() (line 227) precisely because the value IS in the persisted struct.
findings.impact: An operator configuring a unit for deployment who sets a battery TX cutoff via AT+BATCFG and runs AT+SAVE will believe the threshold is persisted; it is not. The board reverts to the default min-TX voltage after the first power cycle, defeating the configured battery-protection setpoint.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) add bat_min_tx_mV to the doppler NVM struct, restore it on load and capture it in nvmSave(), and call markDirty() here; or (b) if BATCFG is intentionally runtime-only for DOPPLER, document that in the +BATCFG help/header and reject the action mode (or print a clear non-persistent note) so the operator is not misled.

findings.description: MCU_FLASH_reset_wku_counter() returns enum KNS_status_t (mcu_flash.c:474) but the return value is ignored; AT+DPLWKU=0 always reports success (logSucceedMsg at line 118) even if the flash erase/write of the wear-leveled counter failed.
findings.impact: Operator believes the boot counter was reset when a flash failure left the old value in place. Diagnostic-only on DOPPLER, no brick, but a false-positive ACK on a flash op.
findings.recommendation: Check the return: if MCU_FLASH_reset_wku_counter() != KNS_STATUS_OK, return bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg(ERROR_...) instead of succeeding.

findings.description: AT+DPLCFG reports success and logs the raw user-entered values (MGR_LOG_DEBUG line 84-85 echoes msg_interval/seq_interval/tpl_interval) even though KNS_APP_doppler_setCfg() silently clamps sequence_interval_s to RTC_WAKEUP_MAX_S (0x20000s, kns_app_doppler.c:211-214) and still returns true. The AT response/log therefore can show a sequence_interval the device will not actually use.
findings.impact: Minor operator confusion: a configured sequence interval above ~36h is accepted and ACKed at the entered value but runs clamped. No safety impact.
findings.recommendation: After a successful setCfg, read back via KNS_APP_doppler_getCfg() and report/log the effective (post-clamp) values, or have setCfg reject out-of-range intervals so the ACK matches reality.

findings.description: Two stale comments. (1) The file-header command list (lines 4-11) does not mention AT+DEPLOY, which this file implements (bMGR_AT_CMD_DPLDEPLOY_cmd, line 241). (2) The registration comment in mgr_at_cmd_list.c:122 says 'DEPLOY before DPLCFG: longest prefix first', but the dispatcher (mgr_at_cmd.c:233-258) was changed to scan the whole table and keep the LONGEST match, so registration order no longer affects shadowing; the ordering comment is now misleading (rot).
findings.impact: Documentation drift; can mislead a future maintainer into thinking table order is load-bearing when it is not, or into missing that DEPLOY is handled here.
findings.recommendation: Add AT+DEPLOY to the file-header list; update or drop the 'longest prefix first' ordering note in the registration table now that matching is order-independent.

findings.description: AT+DPLCFG uses sscanf with %u/%lu and accepts the line if exactly 4 conversions succeed, but does not reject trailing garbage after the 4th field (e.g. 'AT+DPLCFG=3,10,14400,0,JUNK' parses OK). Same permissive pattern in DPLWKU/BATCFG/LED/DEPLOY (single %u). The interval lower bounds (>0) are delegated to setCfg, which is fine, but extra trailing tokens are silently ignored rather than flagged ERROR_PARAMETER_FORMAT.
findings.impact: Malformed-but-prefix-valid commands are accepted. Low risk (config-time, human operator), no overflow since values are range-checked downstream, but inconsistent with strict parameter validation.
findings.recommendation: Optional: append a sentinel to the sscanf format (e.g. ' %c' and require the count to be exactly N, rejecting if an extra char is consumed) to reject trailing junk, matching strict AT parsing. Low priority.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. All 7 handlers are live: each is registered in cas_atcmd_list_array under #ifdef USE_DOPPLER_APP (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:123-129) and reached via the dispatcher (mgr_at_cmd.c:343). The #else stubs in DPLBATCFG (lines 200-205) and DPLLED (lines 233-238) are config-gated dead code, intentional: compiled only when BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC / BSP_HAS_LED_RGB are undefined, and they correctly (void)-cast unused params. pu8_cmdParamString is marked __attribute__((unused)) on DPLSAVE/DPLLOG where status/action need no params — correct. No unused statics, no unreachable branches (every handler's final return covers the no-match exec-mode case).
test_coverage: No unit test exists for any handler in this file (grep of Tests/ for DPLCFG/DPLWKU/DPLDEPLOY/DPLBATCFG/bMGR_AT_CMD_DPL returns nothing; no test_at_cmd*/test_doppler* in Tests/unit). Concrete testable gaps with HW easily mockable: (1) the 64-bit DPLWKU formatting (finding above) is pure logic on a uint64_t and should have a unit test asserting the printed string for values straddling 2^32 — would have caught the %08lu bug; (2) DPLCFG msg_count>255 rejection and the 4-field sscanf parse; (3) DPLLED mode>2 rejection plus the markDirty side-effect; (4) DPLDEPLOY mode>1 rejection; (5) DPLBATCFG min_mV>4200 rejection. MGR_*/MCU_* are already mocked elsewhere in the test framework, so these are straightforward to add.

role: Implements the "general" AT command handlers (VERSION, PING, FW, SECKEY, ADDR, ID, SN, RCONF, SAVE_RCONF, LPM, MC, TCXO_WU, RCONFRAW, BOOT): parses operator input, validates, and forwards to KNS_CFG / MCU_NVM / MCU_AES / LPM / bootloader.
compiled_in: all (always compiled; the only config-gated code is the SMD_* HW-RF check in RCONF and the USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP MC-cache sync in AT+MC). Reachable in the sealed target APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART via the console AT path.

findings.description: AT+TCXO_WU action mode ignores the return value of u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiToInt32: `(void)u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiToInt32(... &tcxo_ms)`. That helper sets *u32OutputValue=0 and returns 0 on any non-numeric input (endPtr!='\0'), e.g. `AT+TCXO_WU=12a` or `AT+TCXO_WU=  ` . Because the return is discarded, tcxo_ms becomes 0, which passes the `> TCXO_MAX_WARMUP_MS` check and is accepted.
findings.impact: An operator typo (or fuzzed input) silently sets the TCXO warm-up to 0 ms instead of returning an error. Insufficient TCXO settling before TX can degrade/break RF transmission on the sealed unit, with the command reporting +OK. Contrast with the AT+ID handler (line 204-210) which DOES check the same helper's return.
findings.recommendation: Capture the return: if it is 0 (or < 1), return bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg(ERROR_PARAMETER_FORMAT). Mirror the validation already used in bMGR_AT_CMD_ID_cmd.

findings.description: AT+ADDR action mode converts the operator hex via u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiBinary into the input buffer (4 bytes for a 32-bit address, or 4 with a padded nibble for the accepted nbBits==28 case) and passes `pu8_cmdParamString + 8` to MCU_NVM_setAddr, which unconditionally writes FLASH_ADDR_BYTE_SIZE (=8) bytes to flash. Only 4 meaningful bytes were produced; bytes 5-8 written to flash are leftover raw command-string characters (the original ASCII tail / trailing NULs), not address bytes.
findings.impact: 4 bytes of garbage are persisted into the ADDR flash slot after the real 4-byte address. KNS_CFG_getAddr/MCU_NVM_getAddr only consume the first 4, so functionally tolerated today, but it is a latent layout coupling: any future reader of the full 8-byte slot, or a credential-dump/verify (MGR_CRED), would see non-deterministic trailing bytes. Also note nbBits==28 (7 hex chars) is accepted as a valid address — an odd-nibble 28-bit value silently zero-padded — which is almost certainly not a legitimate Argos address width.
findings.recommendation: Either zero/normalise the 4 trailing bytes before setAddr, or change the contract so setAddr writes only DEVICE_ADDR_LENGTH(=4) meaningful bytes. Reconsider whether nbBits==28 should be accepted at all (line 155).

findings.description: Three error paths cast a raw KNS_status_t directly to enum ERROR_RETURN_T, bypassing MGR_AT_CMD_mapKnsStatusToError: `(enum ERROR_RETURN_T)KNS_STATUS_RADIO_CONF_BAD` (=250), `(enum ERROR_RETURN_T)KNS_STATUS_FLASH_ERR` (=700), and `(enum ERROR_RETURN_T)status` in RCONFRAW. Every other failure path in this file routes KNS codes through the mapper.
findings.impact: Emits +ERROR=250 / +ERROR=700 / +ERROR=<raw> over UART. Per mgr_at_cmd_common.h:68-77 the mapper exists precisely to keep the +ERROR=N surface stable for legacy GUI parsers; these three paths defeat that, producing codes the GUI's parsing table may not recognise. Inconsistent operator-facing error reporting.
findings.recommendation: Route through MGR_AT_CMD_mapKnsStatusToError(status) like the other branches, or use a defined ERROR_RETURN_T value (e.g. ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_VALUE / a flash-error code).

findings.description: AT+BOOT sends `+BOOT=OK`, HAL_Delay(50), then calls request_dfu_mode(). request_dfu_mode validates the bootloader stack pointer and RETURNS without jumping if invalid (bl_stack out of RAM range, e.g. no/corrupt bootloader). On that return, bMGR_AT_CMD_BOOT_cmd falls through to `return true;` having already told the operator +BOOT=OK.
findings.impact: If the bootloader region is absent/corrupt, AT+BOOT claims success but the device stays in the application with no error surfaced. Not a brick (it stays running), but a sealed-unit OTA workflow would get a false-positive 'entered DFU'. Also AT+BOOT=? (STATUS_MODE) is deliberately accepted (line 521) and triggers the same reboot-to-DFU as the action form — a query that reboots is surprising and easy to issue accidentally.
findings.recommendation: On request_dfu_mode() return, emit a failure (+ERROR) instead of returning true. Consider restricting AT+BOOT to action mode only (the header doc says 'Only action mode is authorized').

findings.description: In AT+LPM with two args, `forced` is parsed by sscanf but NOT masked/range-checked before `LPM_setForcedMode((enum MgrLpm_LPM_t)forced)`. LPM_setForcedMode (lpm.c:793) silently ignores any value not in {NONE,SLEEP,STOP,STANDBY,SHUTDOWN}. The handler returns bMGR_AT_CMD_logSucceedMsg() regardless.
findings.impact: `AT+LPM=0x0F,0xFF` (or any invalid forced value) replies +OK while the forced mode is silently NOT applied. The operator believes a forced mode was set when it was not — misleading for the very low-power sealed deployment where forced mode matters. Note: the bitmap `lpm` IS masked (&0x0F), so only the forced field has this gap.
findings.recommendation: Validate `forced` against the allowed set before applying; if out of range, return ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_VALUE rather than reporting success.

findings.description: Unsigned values printed with signed %d: +ID prints uint32_t dev_id with %d (line 184), +MC prints uint16_t mc with %d (396), +TCXO prints uint32_t tcxo_ms with %d (443). For dev_id > INT_MAX this prints a negative number; mc and tcxo_ms are range-bounded so benign today.
findings.impact: Format/type mismatch (MISRA-like). ID values above 2147483647 would be displayed as negative over UART. The header documents ID as a 6-digit value so in practice it stays in range, but the +ID surface is not guaranteed correct for the full uint32 domain MCU_NVM_setID accepts (it accepts up to 32-bit per the nbBits<=32 check at line 206).
findings.recommendation: Use %u for the uint32/uint16 values (and %lu with an (unsigned long) cast for portability of tcxo_ms / dev_id).

findings.description: AT+ID accepts up to 7 decimal characters (`if (nbChar > 7) reject`), allowing values up to 9999999, but the header (mgr_at_cmd_list_general.h:66) and AT+SN docs describe the ID as a 6-digit identifier. There is no value-range validation beyond bit-count<=32, so a 7-digit ID outside the legitimate Argos ID space is persisted to flash.
findings.impact: An out-of-spec device ID can be stored and used for frame building. Low operational risk (operator-controlled, one-time provisioning), but no guard against an obviously-too-large ID.
findings.recommendation: Either tighten nbChar to 6 to match the documented width, or add an explicit max-ID range check; update the doc/comment to whichever is authoritative.

findings.description: The LPM bitmap mask ORs LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE (==0x00) into the mask expression, which contributes nothing. The mask effectively is 0x0F. Cosmetic.
findings.impact: None functional; slightly misleading to a reader who may think NONE is a maskable bit.
findings.recommendation: Drop LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE from the OR, or add a comment that it is 0 and present only for readability.

findings.description: Magic literals: SECKEY/RCONFRAW hex formatting hardcodes `for (i<16)` and `sec_key_str[32]='\0'` / `hex_str[32]='\0'` instead of deriving from DSK_BYTE_LENGTH / FLASH_RADIOCONF_BYTE_SIZE. The buffers (33) and loop bound (16) are correct today (16*2+1) but not symbolically tied to the constant. RCONFRAW's loop uses FLASH_RADIOCONF_BYTE_SIZE (good) but still hardcodes the trailing index 32.
findings.impact: If DSK_BYTE_LENGTH ever changed, the SECKEY path (loop fixed at 16, terminator fixed at 32) would silently truncate or overflow sec_key_str[33]. Latent, not a current defect.
findings.recommendation: Derive loop count and terminator index from the byte-length constant (e.g. `[2*DSK_BYTE_LENGTH]='\0'`), and consider a _Static_assert that buffer size >= 2*N+1.

dead_code: No genuine orphans and no unused statics in this file. Every handler is referenced by the command table cas_atcmd_list_array in mgr_at_cmd_list.c. Config-gated (intentional, not dead): the SMD_* HW-RF compatibility check in AT+RCONF status mode (lines 250-280, active for SMD_PA/NOPA/STDALONE/OP — i.e. live in the sealed target); the `#if !defined(LPM_SHUTDOWN_ENABLED)` SHUTDOWN-refusal guards in AT+LPM (lines 349-359, 370-373) are compiled OUT in the default/sealed build (LPM=SHUTDOWN), so those two branches are dead in the shipped config by design; the `#if defined(USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP)` KNS_APP_uw_doppler_setSessionMC sync (lines 418-424) is live in the sealed target. The pu8_cmdParamString parameter is marked __attribute__((unused)) on every prototype but is actually USED in the action-mode handlers — the attribute is misleading (it suppresses a warning that would not fire) but harmless.
test_coverage: Partial. Tests/unit/test_mc_9bit.c mirrors the AT+MC mod-512 fold invariant (at_mc_fold) and the NVM clamp, but tests a re-implemented copy, not the actual bMGR_AT_CMD_MC_cmd parser (the `%*[^=]= %ld` sscanf, the <0 / >0xFFFF rejection, the empty-param path). Gaps with no unit coverage: (1) the CR/LF trim + minimum-length guards shared by SECKEY/ADDR/ID/RCONF/TCXO action handlers (boundary: empty params, exactly-name-length, trailing \\r\\n) — high value, easy to mock; (2) the TCXO non-numeric-input -> 0ms bug (finding above) would be caught by a unit test feeding 'AT+TCXO_WU=12a'; (3) the AT+LPM sscanf parsing of the one-arg vs two-arg forms and the bitmap mask; (4) nbBits validation paths (SECKEY!=128, ADDR in {28,32}, RCONF==128). Recommend adding a test_at_cmd_general.c that drives the real handlers with mocked KNS_CFG/MCU_NVM/MCU_AES.

role: Handlers for three GUI-facing MAC AT commands: AT+KMAC (get/set MAC profile), AT+KCFG (get/set L1-timer config bitmap, set refused), AT+KEVT (drain+dump MAC-to-APP event queue). On UW_DOPPLER, KMAC is locked to BASIC.
compiled_in: all (file always compiled). bMGR_AT_CMD_KMAC_cmd has two mutually-exclusive bodies: the USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP branch (sealed target) vs the #else branch (STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER). KCFG/KEVT bodies are identical in every config.

findings.location: mgr_at_cmd_list_mac.c:194 (bMGR_AT_CMD_KEVT_cmd); shares queue with kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1434 process_mac_events
findings.description: AT+KEVT drains KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP, the SAME queue the application scheduler consumes. On UW_DOPPLER, process_mac_events() pops this queue and drives state transitions on KNS_MAC_TX_DONE — including the mandatory external-PA shutdown (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1475-1478 'MAC does NOT auto-disable PA'). The KEVT handler is NOT gated by USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP, so an AT+KEVT=? issued while a TX is in flight pops TX_DONE/TX_TIMEOUT before the app sees it. The handler's own comment (lines 189-191) asserts 'almost always emits zero events' — that is a race, not an invariant; the failure window is exactly when a TX just completed.
findings.impact: Lost TX_DONE on UW_DOPPLER => external PA stays enabled drawing ~60 mA indefinitely (catastrophic for a 12-month sealed battery) and the TX state machine can stall (never advances past the in-flight TX). Sealed units have no UART so cannot self-trigger, but this fires during pre-seal bench/magnet diagnostic windows and any GUI/SPI-bridged session; it is a latent brick/drain path that contradicts the 'AT layer must never steal app events' design used for KMAC.
findings.recommendation: Gate KEVT with #if !defined(USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP) (and any app that owns KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP) returning a benign refuse/ack, mirroring how KMAC hardcodes the UW path. Alternatively route diag through a peek API that does not consume, or a separate diagnostics queue. Do not let an AT command consume the scheduler's event queue.

findings.description: In the #else (non-UW) STATUS path, `struct KNS_MAC_prflInfo_t prfl_info` is declared uninitialized (line 73). KNS_MAC_getPrflInfo() fills it, but the union member is documented 'empty for BASIC and NONE profile' (kns_mac_prfl_cfg.h:98). For those profiles the closed-source lib may leave the 7 union bytes unwritten, and the loop at 104-105 then emits 7 bytes (14 hex chars) of stack garbage over UART. The return value of KNS_MAC_getPrflInfo() is also ignored (line 92): on lib failure the entire struct including id is uninitialized and garbage is emitted.
findings.impact: Stack-content leak over the console and non-deterministic +KMAC=? response on BASIC/NONE; can desync a strict GUI parser. GUI/STDLN/DOPPLER builds only (not the sealed UW target, where this branch is compiled out). Low security/functional impact but a genuine uninitialized read.
findings.recommendation: Zero-init `prfl_info` at declaration (`= {0}`) and check the KNS_MAC_getPrflInfo() return; on non-OK emit a defined error/empty config instead of looping over the buffer.

findings.description: The non-UW set path never range-checks the parsed profile id before forwarding it to the MAC. `temp_id` is sscanf'd, cast straight to `enum KNS_MAC_prflId_t` (line 117), and pushed to KNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC (line 143) with no bound against [KNS_MAC_PRFL_NONE .. KNS_MAC_PRFL_MAX). A GUI sending e.g. AT+KMAC=99,<ctxt> hands an out-of-range enum to the closed-source MAC. Contrast the UW branch, which explicitly whitelists {NONE,BASIC} and refuses everything else.
findings.impact: Relies entirely on libkineis to validate an out-of-range profile id; if the lib indexes a table by id this is OOB into closed code. GUI/STDLN/DOPPLER builds only. Not reachable on the sealed UW target (locked branch), so medium not high.
findings.recommendation: Reject temp_id outside [0, KNS_MAC_PRFL_MAX) with ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_VALUE before pushing, consistent with the UW branch's whitelist discipline.

findings.description: kns_assert(prflCtxtCharNb <= (sizeof(prflCtxtData)-1)) can never be false: prflCtxtData is uint8_t[15], so the bound is 14, and prflCtxtCharNb = strlen of a buffer filled by sscanf with `%14[0-9A-Fa-f]`, capped at 14. The defensive assert is unreachable-as-false. Note kns_assert -> Error_Handler() (kns_assert.c:64) resets the FW, so a real overflow here would brick — but the cap upstream makes it dead. Harmless but dead defensive code; also a HardFault-grade reaction to what is just a parse-length issue.
findings.impact: None today (dead branch). Documented because if the %14 width or buffer size ever drifts out of sync, this becomes a reset-on-bad-input path rather than a graceful +ERROR.
findings.recommendation: Either drop the assert (redundant with the sscanf width) or, if kept as a guard against future edits, convert to a graceful bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg(ERROR_PARAMETER_FORMAT) return instead of an Error_Handler reset.

findings.description: Status-response width is inconsistent across builds: the UW branch emits a fixed 10 hex chars (`+KMAC=1,0000000000`, 5 bytes) while the non-UW branch emits 14 hex chars (7 bytes = sizeof BLIND cfg). A GUI parser keyed on field width sees different lengths depending on firmware variant for the same BASIC profile.
findings.impact: Cosmetic / potential GUI-parser desync between variants. No functional effect on device.
findings.recommendation: Pick one canonical width for the BASIC/NONE context field (the 14-char/7-byte form matches the documented max accepted on set) and use it in both branches.

findings.description: UW branch parses with sscanf("AT+KMAC=%hd", &requested_id) into int16_t. On a grossly out-of-range numeric (e.g. AT+KMAC=99999) %hd into a short is technically out-of-range conversion; practically it wraps. requested_id stays -1 if sscanf matches nothing, which then correctly falls into the refuse branch. Behaviour is safe (refused) but the parse is loose.
findings.impact: No hang/brick: any unrecognized/overflowed value lands in the refuse path (WARN + ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_VALUE). Noted for completeness.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is; optionally validate the sscanf field count (==1) before trusting requested_id rather than relying on the -1 sentinel.

findings.location: mgr_at_cmd_list_mac.c (whole file); Tests/unit/test_at_dispatch.c has no coverage
findings.description: No unit test exercises bMGR_AT_CMD_KMAC_cmd / KCFG / KEVT. test_at_dispatch.c does not reference KMAC/KCFG/KEVT. The pure-logic, mockable behaviours that should be covered: UW KMAC accepts {NONE,BASIC} and refuses BLIND/SATDET/BLIND_POS; KCFG set always returns FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE while STATUS returns the bitmap; KEVT count cap at 32; and (once fixed) KEVT not draining the app queue on UW_DOPPLER.
findings.impact: Regressions in the profile-whitelist or the KCFG-refuse guard (both fix load-bearing LPM/profile invariants per the last commit) would not be caught by the suite.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_at_kmac.c mocking MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send/KNS_Q/KNS_MAC_getPrflInfo: assert UW whitelist behaviour, KCFG set-refusal, and KEVT count bound.

dead_code: No genuine orphans — all three handlers are registered in cas_atcmd_list_array (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:61/68/69) and dispatched. Config-gated: the USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP branch of bMGR_AT_CMD_KMAC_cmd (lines 33-68) is live only on the sealed UW target; the #else branch (lines 69-147) is dead there and live on STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER. Dead-as-false branch: the kns_assert at line 137 can never trigger (bound 14<=14 guaranteed by the sscanf %14 width) — defensive, never executes its failure path.
test_coverage: Not covered. No unit test references KMAC/KCFG/KEVT (confirmed against Tests/unit/test_at_dispatch.c and the suite listing). All three handlers are mockable pure logic (HW only via MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send / KNS_Q / KNS_MAC_getPrflInfo, all already mockable in the framework). Concrete gaps: UW profile whitelist, KCFG set-refusal guard, KEVT 32-cap and (post-fix) UW queue-drain prevention.

role: Two AT-command handlers (AT+PREPASS_EN, AT+UDATE) that are deliberate no-op stubs, present only so the legacy GUI gets a valid +OK reply; no functional effect on the Kineis MAC stack.
compiled_in: all (both handlers are unconditionally registered in mgr_at_cmd_list.c:58 and :74, with no APP/BOARD/COMM #ifdef guard; reachable in every UART build including the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE target)

findings.description: AT+PREPASS_EN status query always returns 0. u8_previpassSt is a function-local initialised to 0; the action-mode write (AT+PREPASS_EN=1) parses the value into a different local invocation's stack variable and discards it, so no state is retained. Every AT+PREPASS_EN=? therefore answers +PREPASS_EN=0 regardless of any prior set. The paired header (lines 35-37) documents the opposite: "replies: if PREPASS is enabled (1) or not (0)".
findings.impact: Pure GUI-compatibility stub with zero MAC effect, so no deployment hazard. But a host/GUI that reads back the prepass enable state to confirm a setting will always see 0 and may treat the set as failed or loop re-issuing it. Header doc is misleading (comment-rot).
findings.recommendation: Either persist the flag in a file-static and echo it back in status mode, or fix the header note to state plainly that the value is not retained (stub always reports 0). Given it is an intentional stub, correcting the comment is sufficient.

findings.description: AT+UDATE handler ignores e_exec_mode entirely (parameter marked __attribute__((unused))) and returns +OK for every invocation. In status mode (AT+UDATE=?) the header (lines 57-60) documents the reply must be +UDATE=<datetime>, but the stub emits +OK instead. It also performs no validation of the datetime parameter — any garbage after AT+UDATE= yields +OK.
findings.impact: Stub by design, no MAC/clock effect (the firmware does not actually set time here). A GUI expecting +UDATE=... on a status query will get +OK and may mis-parse. No brick/hang risk.
findings.recommendation: Update the header to reflect stub behaviour, or if GUI parsing breaks, emit a fixed +UDATE=<placeholder> in ATCMD_STATUS_MODE. No functional fix needed for the sealed target.

findings.description: sscanf success is gated only on return value ==1; trailing junk is not rejected. e.g. "AT+PREPASS_EN=2" (out of the 0/1 range the comment at line 39 claims to enforce) or "AT+PREPASS_EN=5garbage" both return +OK. The comment "allow only enable/disable" (line 39) is not actually enforced — no range check on u8_previpassSt.
findings.impact: None functionally (value is discarded). Comment overstates the validation that is performed (comment-rot).
findings.recommendation: Remove or correct the "allow only enable/disable" comment, since no enable/disable range check exists. Optionally validate u8_previpassSt<=1 if the stub is ever promoted to real behaviour.

findings.description: sscanf return is cast to int16_t (i16_scan_id_param_res). sscanf returns int; the value here is only ever 0, 1, or EOF(-1), so the narrowing is harmless, but the int16_t intermediate is gratuitous and slightly obscures intent. %hhu correctly matches the uint8_t target (no type mismatch / UB).
findings.impact: Cosmetic only.
findings.recommendation: Use int directly for the sscanf result. Low priority.

dead_code: None. Both bMGR_AT_CMD_PREPASS_EN_cmd and bMGR_AT_CMD_UDATE_cmd are live: registered unconditionally in the AT command dispatch table (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:58, :74) and invoked via function pointer at mgr_at_cmd.c:343. No unused statics or file-local helpers. The handler parameters of AT+UDATE are intentionally marked __attribute__((unused)) because it is a no-op stub — not dead code, an explicit unused-param annotation. Note: the ATCMD_INVALID_USAGE enum value is never produced by the dispatcher (mgr_at_cmd.c:271-284 only sets STATUS/ACTION or marks the command unknown), so the PREPASS_EN action path never sees it — but that is a dispatcher property, not dead code in this file.
test_coverage: No unit test references PREPASS_EN, UDATE, or previpass anywhere under Tests/ (grep: zero matches). The logic is trivially testable in the host harness (pure string in -> +OK/+ERROR/+PREPASS_EN out, no HW): worth a small Tests/unit case asserting (a) AT+PREPASS_EN=1 -> +OK, (b) AT+PREPASS_EN= (malformed/no value) -> +ERROR=ERROR_PARAMETER_FORMAT, (c) AT+PREPASS_EN=? -> +PREPASS_EN=0, (d) AT+UDATE... -> +OK. These would lock the documented GUI contract and catch any future regression in the stub responses. Gap, but low severity since the code has no MAC/HW effect.

role: AT-command handlers for user-data TX/RX (AT+TX, AT+RX) and the MAC->APP event pump (MGR_AT_CMD_macEvtProcess) that maps Kineis MAC service events to +TX=/+ERROR= host responses and frees the USERDATA TX FIFO element.
compiled_in: all (file always compiled); AT+RX + DL/SAT cases gated by USE_RX_STACK; HDA4 buffer sizing gated by USE_HDA4; LED stub gated by USE_TX_LED. In the sealed target (APP=UW_DOPPLER) the TX/macEvtProcess logic is effectively dead-by-config: kns_app_uw_doppler.c runs its OWN MAC2APP drain loop and never calls bMGR_AT_CMD_TX_cmd / MGR_AT_CMD_macEvtProcess. But bMGR_AT_CMD_TX_cmd is still registered unconditionally in the global AT dispatch table (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:49), so AT+TX remains reachable from a CONFIG-mode UART session even in UW_DOPPLER.

findings.description: TCXO is force-enabled at line 150 (MCU_MISC_TCXO_Force_State(true) + HAL_Delay warmup) BEFORE the FIFO reserve and parsing, but NONE of the five error-return paths turn it back off: FIFO-full (218-220), payload-too-large (186-189), KNS_Q_push failure (207-208), bad-length (211-212), missing-params (215-216). Only the success path eventually clears TCXO later, inside MGR_AT_CMD_macEvtProcess on TX_DONE/TIMEOUT. The SPI sibling does it correctly: mgr_spi_cmd_list_user_data.c:258 enables TCXO only after validation, and 269/284 disable it (plus MCU_MISC_turn_off_pa()) on push failure.
findings.impact: Every malformed/rejected AT+TX leaves the TCXO running. If macEvtProcess never runs to completion (e.g. the AT path is used in a build where nobody drains KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP for these events, which is the case in UW_DOPPLER), the TCXO stays powered -> continuous extra battery drain on a 12-month sealed deployment. On the queue-push-failure path the external PA is also left untouched (no turn_off_pa) unlike the SPI path.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the SPI flow: either enable the TCXO only just before the KNS_Q_push (after all validation), or add MCU_MISC_TCXO_Force_State(false) (and MCU_MISC_turn_off_pa() where appropriate) to every early-return error path in bMGR_AT_CMD_handleNewTxData. Add a unit test exercising each error branch and asserting the TCXO-off mock was called.

findings.description: sscanf scans the attribute with the conversion '0x%hX' into &u8UserDataAttr.u8_raw, but u8_raw is a uint8_t (union sUserDataAttribute_t is 1 byte). The 'h' length modifier makes sscanf expect an 'unsigned short *' and write sizeof(unsigned short)=2 bytes. This writes 1 byte past the 1-byte union object -> out-of-bounds write to a stack local / undefined behaviour. To capture a uint8_t the format would need a SCNx8 / 'hh' modifier or an intermediate unsigned short.
findings.impact: Whenever the optional ',0x<attr>' field is supplied on AT+TX, sscanf clobbers 1 byte of adjacent stack storage. On the current little-endian ARM stack layout it likely lands on padding and is benign, but it is genuine UB and is fragile to any reordering of locals / struct packing; could corrupt an adjacent local in a future build. Same pattern is present in the SPI/general AT code base and should be fixed consistently.
findings.recommendation: Scan into a local 'unsigned short tmp; sscanf(...,0x%hX, ..., &tmp); u8UserDataAttr.u8_raw = (uint8_t)tmp;' or use the C99 'hh' modifier ('0x%hhX') with a uint8_t target. Add a unit test that parses 'AT+TX=AB,0x12' and checks no adjacent-byte corruption.

findings.description: Several kns_assert() calls on this user-input path reset the device in the sealed build. kns_assert -> kns_assert_failed -> Error_Handler -> (UW_DOPPLER) MGR_ERR_logAndReset(ERR_ASSERT) which performs a system reset (confirmed Core/Src/main.c:1239-1244). Affected: line 195 kns_assert(USERDATA_txFifoAddElt(...)) resets if the add ever fails; line 425/450/470/486/505 kns_assert(spUserDataMsg->bIsToBeTransmit) and the NULL-asserts at 406/413 reset on any MAC-event/FIFO inconsistency. These are reachable from host AT input (or a misbehaving lib event).
findings.impact: A controlled error (FIFO add race, an unexpected MAC event ordering, a head-of-FIFO mismatch when >1 TX in flight) turns into a full firmware reset rather than a clean +ERROR= reply. On a sealed unit a reset is recoverable (not a brick) but it drops state and bursts power; repeated triggering during a CONFIG session is a denial-of-service from the field operator's view.
findings.recommendation: For the user-input-reachable cases (FIFO add failure, multi-TX head mismatch) prefer returning an error response over asserting. Keep kns_assert only for true never-happen invariants. The multi-TX case is already only WARN-logged at 400-404 but then still derefs head and asserts at 406 — make that path tolerate a NULL/mismatched head without resetting.

findings.description: In the sealed APP=UW_DOPPLER config this file's TX completion pump is config-dead: MGR_AT_CMD_macEvtProcess is only invoked from kns_app_doppler.c:738 and kns_app.c:405 (STDLN/DOPPLER), never from kns_app_uw_doppler.c which drains KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP itself (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1431-1555). However bMGR_AT_CMD_TX_cmd stays registered in the unconditional dispatch table (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:49). Net effect under UW_DOPPLER: an AT+TX in CONFIG mode WILL reserve a FIFO elt, force TCXO on, and KNS_Q_push a SEND_DATA event, but the matching completion is consumed by the UW_DOPPLER loop, so this file's free path (USERDATA_txFifoRemoveElt / TCXO-off) for that element never runs here.
findings.impact: Potential FIFO-element leak and TCXO-left-on if an operator issues AT+TX during a field magnet/CONFIG session on a sealed unit, depending on whether the UW_DOPPLER drain loop frees the same USERDATA element. This is a cross-file interaction, not provable from this file alone, but the unconditional registration makes the unhandled path reachable.
findings.recommendation: Gate AT+TX registration (or make bMGR_AT_CMD_TX_cmd refuse) under USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP, OR confirm kns_app_uw_doppler.c frees the USERDATA element and clears TCXO for AT-originated SEND_DATA. Document which app owns the MAC2APP drain so the ownership is unambiguous.

findings.description: appEvt is brace-initialized with .id, .data_ctxt.usrdata={0}, .usrdata_bitlen=0, .sf=KNS_SF_NO_SERVICE, but data_ctxt.appId (kns_mac_evt.h:139) is left to the implicit zero-init of the designated initializer. That is correct C (remaining members zeroed), but the code comment '@note appEvt.send_ctxt already filled-up at declaration' (line 204) is comment-rot: there is no 'send_ctxt' member in struct KNS_MAC_appEvt_t (the member is data_ctxt). The misleading comment could lead a maintainer to assume a field is set that does not exist.
findings.impact: No runtime bug (zero-init is correct). Risk is maintenance: the rotted comment references a non-existent field and could mask a future omission of an appId/send-context assignment.
findings.recommendation: Fix the comment to reference data_ctxt and explicitly note appId is left 0 by zero-init (and confirm the MAC ignores appId on the AT path).

findings.description: kns_assert(u16UserDataCharNb <= (USERDATA_TX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE - 1)) is effectively always-true: the sscanf field width caps the string at 49 chars (non-HDA4) / 1265 (HDA4) while USERDATA_TX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE-1 = 50 / 1266. So strlen can never exceed the bound and the assert can never fire. It is dead-true defensive code (harmless) but gives false assurance and is coupled by hand to the %49/%1265 width literals.
findings.impact: None at runtime. If someone widens the sscanf field-width literal without updating USERDATA_TX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE this assert would belatedly catch it, but the two magic numbers are not linked, so the protection is brittle.
findings.recommendation: Derive the sscanf field width from USERDATA_TX_PAYLOAD_MAX_SIZE via a macro / stringification so the width and the bound cannot drift, or add a _Static_assert binding the width literal to the buffer size.

findings.description: The __attribute__((unused)) on MGR_LOG_array is placed BEFORE the doxygen block comment (line 52), separated from the function by the comment — stylistically odd and easy to misread as applying to nothing. MGR_LOG_array is a genuine orphan: its only call sites (506-511, 538-542, 562-566, 579-583) are all commented out. Correctly suppressed, but it is dead and could be removed.
findings.impact: None functional. Dead helper kept alive only to support commented-out debug logging; minor binary/maintenance overhead.
findings.recommendation: Either delete MGR_LOG_array together with its commented call sites, or move the attribute to immediately precede the function and keep a single greppable /* DEBUG */ marker. Per CLAUDE.md, debug scaffolding should not linger.

findings.description: u16_get_padded_bitlen returns 0 ONLY when payload exceeds the modulation max; for inputs of 0 bits (empty payload) it returns the minimum valid size (e.g. LDA2 -> 32, VLDA4 -> 24), i.e. it would pad an empty message up to a full minimum frame of zeros. The empty case is normally screened earlier (sscanf result 0/EOF -> ERROR_MISSING_PARAMETERS), so 0-bit input should not reach here, but the function itself does not distinguish 'too small / empty' from a legitimate small payload. On KNS_CFG_getRadioInfo failure it returns the unpadded length (fallback, no padding) which may then be rejected by the lower encoder (per MEMORY: LDA2 min=32, LDK exact 128).
findings.impact: Benign given upstream guards, but the fallback-no-padding branch (line 79) can forward a non-conformant bitlen to the MAC encoder, producing a lower-layer rejection rather than a clear AT-level error.
findings.recommendation: On KNS_CFG_getRadioInfo failure consider returning 0 (treat as 'cannot determine padding -> reject') instead of silently forwarding unpadded data, so the failure surfaces as ERROR_INVALID_USER_DATA_LENGTH at this layer.

findings.location: Tests/unit (no test_at_cmd_user_data / no coverage of this file)
findings.description: There is no unit test covering this module. Grep over Tests/ for u16_get_padded_bitlen, convertAsciiBinary, convertAsciiToInt32, handleNewTxData returns nothing; Tests/unit has no test_at_cmd*/test_user_data* file. The pure, host-testable logic here is substantial: u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiBinary (odd/even char counts, invalid hex -> 0, back-half zeroing), u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiToInt32 (overflow/endPtr handling), and u16_get_padded_bitlen (every modulation boundary incl. too-large -> 0).
findings.impact: Conversion and padding logic that directly shapes the over-air frame size (and per MEMORY can corrupt frames if wrong) is unverified. Off-by-one in the odd-char path or a padding-table edit could ship undetected.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_at_cmd_user_data.c mocking KNS_CFG_getRadioInfo to exercise: even/odd hex strings, invalid hex char -> return 0, convertAsciiToInt32 overflow + trailing-garbage -> 0, and u16_get_padded_bitlen for each modulation at boundary (max, max+1->0, sub-min->min). These are pure functions, no HW mocking beyond KNS_CFG.

dead_code: MGR_LOG_array (57-64): genuine orphan — all call sites are commented out (506-511, 538-542, 562-566, 579-583); kept only for commented debug logging. Set_TX_LED #else stub (47-49): live no-op when USE_TX_LED undefined (default), used. AT+RX handler + DL/SAT/RX cases (318-361, 556-606): config-gated dead unless USE_RX_STACK; this is a one-way TX tracker so RX stack is normally off — intentional. HDA4 633-byte sizing (kns_mac_evt/user_data via USE_HDA4): config-gated, not used in UW_DOPPLER. WHOLE-FILE config-dead in UW_DOPPLER: bMGR_AT_CMD_TX_cmd path and MGR_AT_CMD_macEvtProcess are never invoked by kns_app_uw_doppler.c (it runs its own MAC2APP drain), yet bMGR_AT_CMD_TX_cmd stays registered in the unconditional dispatch table (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:49) so AT+TX is still reachable in CONFIG mode — see findings. Line 173 kns_assert is dead-true (can never fire given sscanf field-width). Commented dead lines: 140, 449, 506-511, 538-542, 561-566, 578-583, 595, 609, 618.
test_coverage: No unit test exists for this file. Testable pure logic is uncovered: u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiBinary (odd/even char counts, invalid-hex->0, padding zeroing), u16MGR_AT_CMD_convertAsciiToInt32 (overflow/endPtr), u16_get_padded_bitlen (per-modulation boundaries incl. >max->0). macEvtProcess and bMGR_AT_CMD_handleNewTxData are HW/queue glue (KNS_Q, USERDATA FIFO, MCU_MISC TCXO/PA) but are mockable per the project's existing MGR_*/HAL_* mock approach — at minimum the TCXO-off-on-error-path regression (finding #1) and the sscanf %hX width bug (finding #2) should get a targeted test. Concrete gap: add Tests/unit/test_at_cmd_user_data.c.

role: AT command handlers for the UW_DOPPLER app: SWS/TX/LB/DUTY/LPM config, status/diag dumps, deploy, save-to-NVM, event/PM log dumps, RESET/SHUTDOWN/STOP2/STANDBY power-path commands. Parses operator UART input into module getters/setters.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER only (Makefile line 348, inside ifeq($(APP),UW_DOPPLER); adds -DUSE_UW_DOPPLER_APP). UW_DOPPLER is restricted to BOARD=SMD_STDALONE by an #error elsewhere, so on the sealed target BSP_HAS_LED_RGB / BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC / BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH are all defined and every #if branch here is live. Handlers are reached via cas_atcmd_list_array (mgr_at_cmd_list.c lines 79-119), also USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP-gated. Runs in main-loop context (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1852), never ISR.

findings.description: AT+SWSCFG explicitly accepts max_dive_s==0 and the inline comment claims '0 disables the stuck-underwater backstop'. The handler then returns +OK. But MGR_SWS_setConfig() (mgr_sws.c:1277-1278, added in the very next commit 6cf7c7a) heals max_dive_time_s==0 back to 7200 so the backstop can NEVER actually be disabled. The comment is stale and the command lies to the operator: AT+SWSCFG=?,...,0,... will report 0 back in STATUS mode? No — getConfig now returns 7200, so the operator sees 7200 even though they set 0. Net: the documented 'disable' behavior is dead, and the +OK acknowledges a value that was silently overridden.
findings.impact: Operator-facing inconsistency on a sealed unit. An operator trying to disable the dive backstop (e.g. for a long-dive species) believes it succeeded (+OK) but it is silently forced to 7200 s. Not a brick (the heal is the safe direction), but the AT contract is wrong and the comment misleads future maintainers.
findings.recommendation: Pick one: either (a) reject max_dive_s==0 at the AT layer with ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_VALUE and fix the comment to state the backstop cannot be disabled, or (b) keep accepting 0 but update the comment to '0 is healed to the 7200 s default by MGR_SWS_setConfig — the backstop is never disabled'. Add a unit test asserting that SWSCFG with max_dive=0 round-trips to 7200.

findings.description: AT+SWSCFG bounds thr_min/thr_max to <=4095 but does NOT bound air_init/water_init to the 12-bit ADC range. They are parsed with %u into unsigned int and only checked for water_init>air_init, then narrowed by unchecked casts (uint16_t)air_init / (uint16_t)water_init at lines 147-148. A value >65535 wraps in the uint16_t cast (e.g. water_init=70000 -> 4464), and MGR_SWS_setConfig (mgr_sws.c) likewise never bounds the baselines to 4095. The pair could even pass water>air on the input yet violate it after truncation.
findings.impact: Silent value corruption of the SWS air/water baselines via integer wrap. On a sealed unit a fat-fingered or scripted baseline outside 0..4095 is accepted with +OK but stored as a wrapped, meaningless value, degrading dive/surface detection (the core safety function) with no error surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Add `air_init > 4095 || water_init > 4095` (and re-check water_init>air_init) to the line 135-140 validation, mirroring the thr_min/thr_max bound. Cheap and consistent with the existing thr checks.

findings.location: mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c (whole file); Tests/unit/test_at_dispatch.c only covers prefix resolution
findings.description: None of this file's parse/validation logic has a unit test. test_at_dispatch.c only validates longest-prefix dispatch in mgr_at_cmd.c. The high-value, fuzz-sensitive validators here are untested: SWSCFG 10-field parse + bounds, TXCFG legacy 4/5/6-arg defaulting (uninitialized-on-short-parse risk), the SHUTDOWN strict '=' guard (added specifically to fix the 'AT+SHUTDOWN=zz' brick, commit ad81ddf), DUTYCFG 3-vs-4-arg, LBCFG hysteresis, LPMTHR sleep>=spin ordering.
findings.impact: Regression risk on the exact validators that gate the most destructive commands (SHUTDOWN power-off, STANDBYTEST/STOPTEST sleep, DUTY auto-cycle) on a no-physical-access sealed device. A future refactor could silently re-open the 'garbage after = powers the tag off' brick with no failing test.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_at_uw_doppler.c exercising: SHUTDOWN '=zz'/'=5zz'/bare/'=?' cases; SWSCFG out-of-range + air/water bounds; TXCFG 4/5/6/7-arg + short-parse rejection; DUTYCFG 3 vs 4 args. Mock MGR_SWS_/KNS_APP_/MGR_LPM_UW_ setters and assert +OK vs +ERROR per the framework already used by test_sws.c.

findings.description: KNS_APP_uw_doppler_enterStandbyTest / setDutyCfg / getDutyCfg are forward-declared via local `extern` prototypes in this .c instead of a shared header (they are NOT in kns_app_uw_doppler.h — confirmed by grep). Signatures currently match the definitions (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:975-988), but there is no single source of truth, so a future signature change in the definition would not be caught at compile time of this TU (silent ABI mismatch / UB).
findings.impact: Maintenance hazard: arg-type drift between this extern and the real definition compiles cleanly and yields UB at the call site. Low probability but on a closed sealed build it would not be caught by tests.
findings.recommendation: Move the three prototypes into kns_app_uw_doppler.h and include it (already included at line 42), removing the local externs.

findings.description: mgr_reed.h is #included twice, both under #if defined(BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH). The header guard makes it harmless, but it is a duplicate include / copy-paste smell.
findings.impact: None functional. Minor clutter; signals an un-reviewed include block.
findings.recommendation: Delete one of the two BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH-guarded mgr_reed.h includes.

findings.location: mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c:519-535 vs header 109-114; also 286-290 header for PAYCFG/STATS doc
findings.description: The +STATUS line emits 15 comma-separated fields (state..sws_fault) but the header doc (mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.h:110-114) documents only 13, omitting lb_act and sws_fault. The DIAG header doc (line 118-124) similarly lists 6 fields while the code emits 7 (sws_fault appended). Comment/format drift, not a code defect.
findings.impact: A host/GUI author coding to the header would mis-parse the trailing column(s). Cosmetic but real for the integration team.
findings.recommendation: Update the header doc blocks for +STATUS and +DIAG to list all emitted fields (append <lb_act>,<sws_fault> and <sws_fault> respectively).

findings.description: AT+SWSCFG validates int_surf_ms!=0, int_uw_ms!=0, max_dive_s, and the delay pair, but min_surf_s (min_surface_time_s) is parsed and stored (line 152) with no range check at all — 0 is accepted. MGR_SWS_setConfig also does not validate it. min_surface_time_s gates re-submersion debounce; 0 means no minimum surface dwell.
findings.impact: Low: a 0 min-surface-time only affects SWS debounce hysteresis, not a power/brick path, but it is an unvalidated operator input that can defeat surface-dwell debounce and cause TX/dive chatter on a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: If a non-zero minimum is intended, add a bound (e.g. min_surf_s within a sane range); otherwise document that 0 disables the surface-dwell minimum.

findings.description: MGR_LOG_INFO("[AT] SWS enabled=%u", cfg.enabled) passes a bool to a varargs %u (default-promoted to int — fine on this ABI but technically %u expects unsigned int). Elsewhere the file is careful to cast (e.g. cfg.enabled?1:0 at line 78). Minor inconsistency only.
findings.impact: None on AAPCS (bool promotes to int 0/1). Style/MISRA nit.
findings.recommendation: Cast to (unsigned)cfg.enabled for consistency with the rest of the file.

findings.description: The #else fallbacks (LED=N/A, BATCFG=N/A, bat_ok=0, reed_present=0, led_ok=0) are config-gated dead code on the sealed target: BOARD=SMD_STDALONE defines BSP_HAS_LED_RGB, BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC and BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH, so only the #if branches compile. The #else arms exist solely for other boards that never build APP=UW_DOPPLER (UW_DOPPLER is #error-restricted to SMD_STDALONE). Intentional portability scaffolding, not orphan code.
findings.impact: None. Noting for the dead-code dimension: these branches are unreachable in every shippable UW_DOPPLER build but are deliberate and harmless.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is; they document intent. No action.

findings.description: When BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH and wake_s==0, MGR_LPM_UW_enterShutdownReed() is __attribute__((noreturn)) (mgr_lpm_uw.h:124) and does not return, so MGR_REED_releasePower() (line 935) and LPM_shutdownWithAutoWake(0) (line 937) are unreachable on that branch. This is intentional: enterShutdownReed itself drives PB7 low / loops in STOP2-with-reed-wake. The releasePower + autoWake calls are only the live path when wake_s!=0 (RTC auto-wake, the sealed-safe path). Verified consistent with the noreturn contract and the sealed_deployment memory rule (never permanent-off; RTC auto-wake path used when wake_s set).
findings.impact: No defect. The control flow is correct; flagging only because it reads like a fall-through on first inspection (noreturn makes the following two statements config-conditionally dead).
findings.recommendation: Optional: add a brief comment at line 933 noting enterShutdownReed() is noreturn so the reader knows lines 935/937 are reached only when wake_s!=0.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. (1) The #else arms for BSP_HAS_LED_RGB / BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC / BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH (lines 297-302, 415-420, 568-571, 575-577, 601-603) are config-gated dead code on every shippable UW_DOPPLER build (sealed target SMD_STDALONE defines all three; UW_DOPPLER is #error-restricted to SMD_STDALONE) — intentional portability scaffolding.
