(2) SHUTDOWN reed path: MGR_REED_releasePower() and LPM_shutdownWithAutoWake(0) at lines 935/937 are unreachable when wake_s==0 because MGR_LPM_UW_enterShutdownReed() is noreturn — intentional, correct. (3) The documented 'max_dive_s==0 disables backstop' behavior (line 138 comment) is effectively dead behavior: setConfig heals 0->7200, so the disable path can never take effect (see medium finding). No unused statics/params (all unused params carry __attribute__((unused)) or (void) casts).
test_coverage: Inadequate. This file's parse/validation logic has NO unit test. Tests/unit/test_at_dispatch.c covers only longest-prefix dispatch in mgr_at_cmd.c, not these handlers. Concrete untested logic on the sealed device: AT+SHUTDOWN strict '=' guard (the anti-brick fix), SWSCFG 10-field bounds incl. the missing air/water 4095 check, TXCFG legacy 4/5/6/7-arg defaulting and short-parse rejection, DUTYCFG 3-vs-4-arg, LBCFG hysteresis, LPMTHR sleep>=spin. Recommend a dedicated Tests/unit/test_at_uw_doppler.c mocking the module setters and asserting +OK vs +ERROR per case.

role: Local AT-command handlers for the krd_fw v11.1.0 additions AT+DL (Argos downlink RX) and AT+GNSS (GNSS position). On all current boards both hardware features are absent, so both handlers unconditionally reply +ERROR=FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE (GUI probes these to grey out UI panels).
compiled_in: all (file unconditionally listed in the AT table at mgr_at_cmd_list.c:70-71 with no APP/BOARD/COMM guard; both handlers registered for every config including the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART target)

findings.description: Both #if and #else preprocessor branches contain IDENTICAL code: return bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg(ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE). The #else (BSP_HAS_DOWNLINK/GNSS != 0) arms are commented as reserved for a future KIM-class board but currently do exactly the same thing as the #if arm, so the whole #if/#endif is a semantic no-op in every build. Also, all 4 board headers (bsp_smd_pa/nopa/op/stdalone.h:13-14/20-21) define both macros to 0, and main.h unconditionally includes exactly one board header (main.h:81-91, #error if none), so the !defined(BSP_HAS_DOWNLINK) half of each guard is always false and unreachable.
findings.impact: No functional impact on the sealed deployment; behavior is correct. Pure clutter that falsely implies the two arms diverge. A future maintainer enabling BSP_HAS_DOWNLINK=1 would get a silently-still-stubbed handler (the #else is empty too), masking an incomplete feature.
findings.recommendation: Collapse each body to the single unconditional return plus a one-line TODO comment; or make the #else arm a #error so enabling the feature cannot silently ship a stub.

findings.description: No unit test exercises bMGR_AT_CMD_DL_cmd or bMGR_AT_CMD_GNSS_cmd. Grep over Tests/ for GNSS_cmd / _DL_cmd / AT+GNSS / AT+DL / v11 returns nothing. The header (mgr_at_cmd_list_v11.h:9-11) documents a GUI-facing contract: these must return +ERROR=FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE so the GUI greys out panels. That contract is untested.
findings.impact: Low. Logic is trivial, but the returned value is a GUI ABI contract (FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE specifically, not generic UNKNOWN_AT_CMD). A regression changing the code or returning true would silently break GUI panel-gating with no test to catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit case asserting both handlers return false and log ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE (mock bMGR_AT_CMD_logFailedMsg to capture the code) for both ACTION and STATUS exec modes.

findings.description: Both handlers ignore e_exec_mode (cast to void) and return FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE for every mode including STATUS mode (AT+DL=? / AT+GNSS=?), the mode the GUI uses to probe per the header comment. Intentional and correct given the feature is absent; noting there is no per-mode differentiation.
findings.impact: None for the sealed deployment. Documents that the uniform response across modes is by design, not an oversight.
findings.recommendation: No change needed; leave as is.

dead_code: The #else arms (BSP_HAS_DOWNLINK/GNSS != 0) at lines 21-27 and 36-41 are config-gated and currently unreachable: all 4 board headers hardcode both macros to 0 and main.h forces inclusion of exactly one board header, so the macros are always defined and always 0. Both arms are functionally identical to the #if arm, so even if reached they change nothing. The !defined(...) half of each guard is permanently false (intentional defensive code, not an orphan). The two handler FUNCTIONS are NOT dead — they are live entries in the AT dispatch table (mgr_at_cmd_list.c:70-71) for every config.
test_coverage: Not covered. No test in Tests/unit references these handlers or AT+DL/AT+GNSS. The testable logic is minimal (return a fixed error code) but it is a GUI-facing ABI contract (must be ERROR_FEATURE_NOT_AVAILABLE, must return false). Concrete gap: no test asserts the specific error code or the false return value for either handler in either exec mode.

role: Battery voltage monitoring: enables an external PB9-gated resistor divider, reads PB13 (ADC_IN0) + VREFINT on the shared SWS ADC, computes VBAT in mV, and exposes level/TX-allow/min-threshold helpers.
compiled_in: Compiled in all APP/COMM configs (file is in the build); the active body is gated by BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC, which is only defined for BOARD=SMD_STDALONE (Core/Inc/bsp/bsp_smd_stdalone.h:18). For SMD_PA / SMD_NOPA / SMD_OP the file compiles the no-op stub block (lines 204-214). Sealed target (UW_DOPPLER + SMD_STDALONE) builds the real body.

findings.description: MGR_BAT_readVoltage_mV() reconfigures the single shared ADC handle `hadc` (VREFINT, then IN0, then restores IN7) with no critical section or ownership flag. SWS sampling reads the same `hadc` via ADC_ReadValueChecked() assuming it is parked on ADC_CHANNEL_7. If an SWS sample is ever issued between the channel switch (line 115) and the IN7 restore (line 130) the SWS read returns the wrong channel (VBAT/VREFINT), or the BAT read is corrupted. Today this is safe ONLY because everything runs in baremetal main-loop context (no ISR triggers ADC, no preemption) — that invariant is implicit and undocumented.
findings.impact: Latent: if SWS polling is ever moved to a timer/RTC ISR (a plausible low-power optimization, and exactly the kind of change this codebase is iterating on), SWS would silently sample the battery divider during a BAT read and flip the dive/surface detector. In a sealed unit a false SURFACE/DIVE flip wastes TX energy or misses a surfacing window. No compile-time guard prevents the regression.
findings.recommendation: Document the 'single-owner, main-loop-only' invariant on hadc at the top of mgr_bat.c and mgr_sws.c, or add a tiny ownership guard (e.g. a `bat_adc_busy` flag checked by the SWS path) so a future ISR-driven sampler cannot interleave. At minimum add a _Static_assert/comment that ADC use is non-reentrant.

findings.description: The header doc-comment is rotted and contradicts the implementation and the datasheet. It states battery is read 'via internal VBAT/3 ADC channel' and explicitly: 'PB13 (VBAT_ADC in BSP) is NOT an ADC pin on STM32WL55 (it's COMP1_INP only). We use the internal ADC_CHANNEL_VBAT instead.' The .c file reads the EXTERNAL divider on PB13 via ADC_CHANNEL_0 (ADC_IN0). DS13105 (.claude/stm/DS13105_stm32wl55jc.txt:3359) confirms PB13 = ADC_IN0, so the .c is correct and the header is wrong. No code uses ADC_CHANNEL_VBAT anywhere.
findings.impact: Misleads any maintainer auditing the battery path (directly violates CLAUDE.md 'no comment-rot' and the rule against confident-wrong HW claims). On a sealed-deploy board a maintainer trusting the header could 'fix' the .c to use the internal channel and read a disconnected pin, reporting bogus VBAT and mis-triggering low-battery shutdown.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the mgr_bat.h header block to match mgr_bat.c: external 120k/300k divider on PB13=ADC_IN0, PB9 gate, VREFINT-based VDDA. Delete the false 'COMP1_INP only / internal VBAT' sentences.

findings.description: Each MGR_BAT_readVoltage_mV() asserts VBAT_EN (PB9) HIGH and then busy-blocks HAL_Delay(2). During those 2 ms the external divider (R4+R5 = 420k across VBAT) sinks ~VBAT/420k ≈ 8-9 µA, and the CPU spins in HAL_Delay (SysTick busy-wait, no WFI). Called from multiple paths (init warm-up, every TX cycle, AT commands, LB-cfg). The current draw is tiny but the busy-wait keeps the core fully clocked for 2 ms per read.
findings.impact: On a 12-month sealed deployment the per-read cost is negligible in isolation, but it is a busy-wait rather than a low-power wait, against the project rule 'Default to LOWEST consumption... no busy-wait'. If read frequency ever rises (e.g. per-SWS-sample battery check) the aggregate matters.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is for current cadence; note it. If the read becomes frequent, replace HAL_Delay(2) with a shorter settle (datasheet RC settle on a 120k/Cpar node is < ~100 µs) or a WFI-based delay, and confirm PB9 is driven LOW on all exit paths (it is — line 136, plus lpm.c:525 / mgr_lpm_uw.c:617,952 force it low before sleep).

findings.description: Partial-failure handling is asymmetric but not wrong: if HAL_ADC_Start() fails, HAL_ADC_Stop() is NOT called (the Stop is inside the `if Start==HAL_OK` block), while a poll timeout also skips Stop here (unlike adc.c:122 which stops on timeout). A left-running ADC is then reconfigured in cleanup via HAL_ADC_ConfigChannel without an explicit Stop. The raw_vref/raw_vbat==0 guard (line 138) catches the failure and returns cached value, so no bad number is produced.
findings.impact: Low. Worst case the ADC is left enabled/converting after a HAL failure until the next ConfigChannel; on STM32WL HAL_ADC_ConfigChannel tolerates this. No hang (PollForConversion has a 100 ms bound). Slight extra current if the ADC were left converting, but the SWS path re-Starts/Stops cleanly afterward.
findings.recommendation: For symmetry and to guarantee the ADC is idle on the error path, call HAL_ADC_Stop(&hadc) unconditionally before the cleanup ConfigChannel (mirror adc.c:122). Low priority.

findings.description: The only battery test (test_bat_auto_shutdown.c) is a hand-copied MIRROR of the streak logic in kns_app_uw_doppler.c — it does NOT link or exercise mgr_bat.c at all. The pure, HW-independent logic in this file is untested: (a) MGR_BAT_getLevel() linear map clamp/round at 3000/3600/in-between; (b) MGR_BAT_isTxAllowedAt() three branches (threshold disabled=0 -> true, mV==0 -> true, mV>=thr); (c) the VBAT divider/VREFINT mV computation (lines 147-158), which is the most error-prone math and uses a uint64 intermediate to avoid 32-bit overflow.
findings.impact: A regression in the divider constants, the (R4+R5)/R5 ratio, or the isTxAllowedAt branch order could silently mis-report VBAT and cause a sealed unit to (a) inhibit TX forever on a healthy battery, or (b) keep TXing into a dying battery. None of these would be caught by the current suite.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_mgr_bat.c that factors the pure computations into testable helpers (or tests them via small static-function extraction): assert getLevel boundaries (2999->0, 3000->0, 3600->100, 3601->100, 3300->50), isTxAllowedAt all branches, and the mV formula against a few (raw_vbat, raw_vref) vectors with known expected VBAT (verifies the *1.4 de-divide and the uint64 no-overflow path at raw=4095).

findings.description: The local `#ifndef VREFINT_CAL_ADDR` fallback defines a non-const `((uint16_t *)0x1FFF75AAUL)`, whereas the HAL already defines `VREFINT_CAL_ADDR` as `((const uint16_t*)(0x1FFF75AAUL))`. When the HAL header is in the include closure the HAL (const) def wins and the local block is dead; if it is NOT in closure, the local non-const variant is used. The address and the 3300 mV calibration ref (MGR_BAT_VREFINT_CAL_MV) both match the HAL (VREFINT_CAL_VREF), so the value is correct either way.
findings.impact: None functionally. Minor const-correctness inconsistency and a normally-dead fallback that exists only to decouple from the HAL header. Dereference at line 147 reads the factory cal word correctly.
findings.recommendation: Prefer relying on the HAL define (include stm32wlxx_ll_adc.h) and drop the local fallback, or make the fallback `const uint16_t *` to match. Cosmetic.

findings.description: last_good_vbat_mV is a plain static initialized to 0; it is NOT in a retention section, so it resets to 0 across every STOP2/SHUTDOWN wake (cold .data/.bss re-init). The header/comment at line 25 advertises 'On ADC failure, returns the last known good reading (not 0)'. Immediately after a wake, before any successful read, that promise degrades to returning 0.
findings.impact: Minimal: the first post-wake read normally succeeds (init does a warm-up read; readVoltage is called early each cycle). If the very first post-wake read fails, callers get 0, which all callers treat safely (isTxAllowedAt(0)->allow, auto-shutdown ignores 0). So no false low-battery shutdown. Only effect: a transient 0 in logs/AT output on a first-read failure.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable. If a true 'last good across deep sleep' is desired, move last_good_vbat_mV into the existing .retentionRamNoload section (per the project's retention pattern) — but only if a real need arises; not required for correctness.

dead_code: No genuine orphans in the active body. (1) The no-op stub block (lines 204-214) is config-gated dead for BOARD=SMD_STDALONE (BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC=1) but LIVE for SMD_PA/SMD_NOPA/SMD_OP — intentional, every symbol still has callers in those builds. (2) The `#ifndef VREFINT_CAL_ADDR` fallback (lines 42-44) is normally dead because the HAL header pre-defines the macro — intentional decoupling, not an orphan. All public functions (init/readVoltage_mV/getLevel/isTxAllowed/isTxAllowedAt/get+setMinTxVoltage_mV) have live callers (kns_app_uw_doppler.c, kns_app_doppler.c, mgr_at_cmd_list_*.c, mgr_nvm.c). MGR_BAT_getLevel is only called within UW/DOPPLER AT/status paths but is reachable. No unused statics.
test_coverage: Inadequate. The testable, HW-independent logic in THIS file has zero direct coverage: the existing Tests/unit/test_bat_auto_shutdown.c re-implements the auto-shutdown streak from kns_app_uw_doppler.c and never links mgr_bat.c. Concrete gaps: MGR_BAT_getLevel() boundary/rounding (3000/3600/mid), MGR_BAT_isTxAllowedAt() branch matrix (thr==0, mV==0, mV>=thr, mV<thr), and the VBAT divider+VREFINT mV math (the uint64 overflow-avoidance and *1.4 de-divide). The ADC HAL interaction is HW glue (not unit-testable without mocks) but the arithmetic and decision logic are pure and should be unit-tested.

role: Credential durability: maintains a CRC-protected 64-byte mirror (page 101 @0x08032800, outside FLASH_USER) of the 48-byte page-0 credential block (ID/ADDR/SECKEY/RADIOCONF) and auto-restores page 0 from it at boot, guarding against brownout-induced credential wipe during page-0 read-modify-write counter overflows.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER (the only caller is kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1673/2106). Not referenced by STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER apps. BOARD/COMM-agnostic. Effectively part of the sealed-deploy target build (UW_DOPPLER+SMD_STDALONE+UART).

findings.description: The unit suite does NOT link mgr_cred.c. It hand-copies the algorithm (cred_crc32, mirror_valid, mirror_build, page0_fully_provisioned, sync_and_restore) into the test file. The production MGR_CRED_crc32, mirror_build, mirror_load_valid, page0_fully_provisioned, the packed MGR_CRED_Mirror_t layout, and the payload-aliasing memcmp(p0,&m,...) are never exercised by any test. A divergence between the reimplemented copy and the real code (e.g. a struct-field reorder, an off-by-one in the hardcoded CRC length 56, or the packed-struct memcmp aliasing breaking) would pass all tests undetected.
findings.impact: False confidence: the 12 green tests validate a copy, not the shipped credential-restore logic that protects the sealed unit from a TEST-identity fallback. A real bug in mgr_cred.c could ship with full test coverage reported.
findings.recommendation: Compile and link the real mgr_cred.c into the host test (stub MCU_FLASH_read/write + HAL_FLASH_* over a fake flash array, as other suites do for HAL). Call the actual MGR_CRED_syncAndRestore()/MGR_CRED_crc32() so the production struct layout and payload-aliasing memcmp are under test.

findings.description: The CRC coverage length 56 is a bare literal in two places (mirror_load_valid and mirror_build). It is only loosely coupled to the layout via the header _Static_assert(offsetof(crc32)==56). If the struct ever gained a field before crc32, the assert would fire but these two literals would still need a manual, separate edit — easy to miss, and a mismatch silently rewrites the mirror every boot (CRC over wrong span never equals stored crc).
findings.impact: Maintainability landmine on a future version bump: a wrong-length CRC means mirror_load_valid always returns false -> mirror rewritten every boot (flash wear) or, worse, a torn mirror passes/fails inconsistently. Low probability today, but the cost of getting it wrong on a sealed unit is high.
findings.recommendation: Define a single constant e.g. #define MGR_CRED_CRC_LEN offsetof(MGR_CRED_Mirror_t, crc32) (==56) in the header and use it at both sites and in the assert, so all three track the layout automatically.

findings.description: MCU_FLASH_read() return value is ignored at all three call sites. On this MCU the read is a plain memcpy from memory-mapped flash and only fails on NULL/size==0 (never the case here), so this is benign today, but it is an unchecked-error-return pattern in load-bearing restore code.
findings.impact: None in practice on STM32WL (memory-mapped flash read cannot fail for valid args). Purely a defensive-coding/consistency gap.
findings.recommendation: Either assert/ignore deliberately with a comment, or check and treat a read failure as FAIL_LOUD for symmetry with the write paths. Lowest priority.

findings.description: On restore, all 48 payload bytes including RADIOCONF are written from the mirror. If RADIOCONF was reprovisioned on page 0 AFTER the mirror was last seeded AND a brownout blanked an ID/ADDR/SECKEY field BEFORE the next boot ran syncAndRestore (which would have reseeded the mirror), the restore reverts RADIOCONF to the older mirror value. RADIOCONF has a compiled-in fallback and is intentionally excluded from page0_fully_provisioned, so it never gates restore.
findings.impact: Narrow race window only: requires a radioconf change immediately followed by a brownout with no intervening boot. Result is a reverted (not lost) radioconf, recoverable by re-provisioning. Very low likelihood; no brick/hang.
findings.recommendation: Accept as documented edge case, or note it in mgr_cred.h. Not worth code change given the mirror is reseeded on every boot where payload differs.

findings.description: mirror_program disables IRQs across up to 8 double-word programs; the page-0 restore path (MCU_FLASH_write) disables IRQs across a full-page erase + 256 double-word programs with up to 3 retries each at FLASH_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS. Both run at boot (line 1673) with the watchdog refreshed immediately after (line 1674), and again at ~1 Hz from CRED_FAIL. Worst-case IRQ-off span is bounded and the comment at the caller budgets ~25 ms << 16 s IWDG.
findings.impact: No defect: bounded, WDG-covered, runs in init/idle not in the TX ISR path. Noted for completeness because it is the longest IRQ-disabled critical section reachable on the sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: None required. If ever called from a latency-sensitive context, reconsider; today it is init/idle only.

findings.description: Both caller sites (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2082, 2107) branch only on ==FAIL_LOUD vs !=FAIL_LOUD. MIRROR_WRITTEN, RESTORED and OK_NOOP are functionally indistinguishable to the app — the distinct enum values are effectively informational/log-only, never acted on differently.
findings.impact: None — this is the intended contract (any non-FAIL means creds are usable). The distinct codes aid logging/tests. Not an orphan; not a bug.
findings.recommendation: No action. Listed only so the reviewer knows the distinction is intentional, not a missed branch.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. Every function (MGR_CRED_crc32, mirror_load_valid, mirror_erase, mirror_program, mirror_build, page0_fully_provisioned, all_ff, MGR_CRED_syncAndRestore) is reachable from MGR_CRED_syncAndRestore, which is called by kns_app_uw_doppler.c (APP=UW_DOPPLER only). The enum values MIRROR_WRITTEN/RESTORED/OK_NOOP collapse to one behavior at the caller (only FAIL_LOUD is acted on) but that is the intended contract, not dead code. The whole file is config-gated dead code for APP!=UW_DOPPLER builds (no caller), which is intentional.
test_coverage: A suite exists (Tests/unit/test_cred_mirror.c, 12 tests incl. CRC known-vector, first-boot seed, steady-state no-op, brownout restore, partial-page no-clobber, fail-loud, CRC/version reject, torn-magic-erased, reprovision, radioconf-blank). BUT it reimplements the algorithm and never links the real mgr_cred.c — so the production CRC, packed-struct layout, payload-aliasing memcmp, and the magic-last double-word program ORDER in mirror_program (dw0..5, dw7, dw6) are not actually tested. Concrete gaps: (1) link the real translation unit; (2) test the real mirror_program torn-write ordering against the real HAL_FLASH_Program sequence (currently only the test's own fake models it); (3) a static-layout test asserting the production struct offsets the CRC length 56 depends on.

role: Persistent error/crash tracker: TAMP backup regs (boot/crash counters, last fault, reset cause) + SRAM2-retention HardFault forensics struct + crash-loop "safe sleep" (STOP2) backoff.
compiled_in: all (no APP/BOARD/COMM #ifdef guards in the .c). Live callers are APP=UW_DOPPLER and APP=DOPPLER only (MGR_ERR_init/checkCrashLoop wired in main.c only under USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP / USE_DOPPLER_APP; fault capture under USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP||USE_DOPPLER_APP in stm32wlxx_it.c). In GUI/STDLN the object is compiled but its functions are unreferenced (linker may drop). Sealed target = UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART exercises every path here.

findings.description: checkCrashLoop's STOP2 safe-sleep configures the WRONG EXTI line for the RTC wakeup timer AND never enables the PWR internal wake-up line. On STM32WL55 the RTC Wakeup Timer is EXTI line 20 (RTC_EXTI_LINE_WAKEUPTIMER_EVENT == EXTI_IMR1_IM20, stm32wlxx_hal_rtc_ex.h:1231; RM0453 line 15589-15590: 'To wake up from Stop mode with an RTC wake-up event ... Configure the EXTI line 20 to be sensitive to rising edge'). This code instead sets EXTI_IMR1_IM17 / RTSR1 bit17 / FTSR1 bit17 — line 17 is the RTC *Alarm* line (RTC_EXTI_LINE_ALARM_EVENT == EXTI_IMR1_IM17, stm32wlxx_hal_rtc.h:837), a different event. The wakeup-timer EXTI (line 20) is left masked. Additionally, unlike the proven STOP2 path in mgr_lpm_uw.c:931-935 which calls HAL_PWREx_EnableInternalWakeUpLine() with the explicit comment 'Without this RTC fires its IRQ but the chip doesn't exit STOP2', this function never enables the internal wake-up line at all.
findings.impact: When a crash loop is detected (>=10 consecutive short boots), the chip enters STOP2 with no valid wake path: the RTC WUTF fires but neither the correct EXTI line (20) nor the PWR internal wake-up line is armed, so the core does not exit STOP2. On a sealed UW_DOPPLER unit this is a permanent BRICK — the very crash-loop protection meant to preserve battery instead strands the device forever (IWDG is frozen in STOP2, magnet/reed is not configured as a wake here). Exactly the failure class the deployment must never hit.
findings.recommendation: Do not hand-roll the EXTI/PWR wake plumbing. Mirror the validated mgr_lpm_uw.c STOP2 entry: use HAL_RTCEx_SetWakeUpTimer_IT(&hrtc, CRASH_LOOP_SLEEP_S-1, RTC_WAKEUPCLOCK_CK_SPRE_16BITS, 0) (handles WPR unlock, WUTWF poll, and the correct EXTI line internally) and call HAL_PWREx_EnableInternalWakeUpLine() before HAL_PWREx_EnterSTOP2Mode. If the manual register approach is kept, change IM17->IM20 (EXTI->IMR1 |= EXTI_IMR1_IM20; RTSR1/FTSR1 bit 20) and add the internal wake-up line enable. Add a unit/bench test that proves wake actually occurs. Also add an RTC-liveness gate (HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro) before entry, matching the LSE-death guard already added elsewhere — otherwise a dead crystal here is also a strand.

findings.description: Crash-loop detection only increments prev_crash when prev_tick>0 && prev_tick<MIN_UP_MS && prev_err!=ERR_NONE. A silent hang that is killed by the IWDG never calls MGR_ERR_log, so on the next boot prev_tick is still the cleared value 0 (ERR_BKP_TICK was set to 0 in the prior init, line 124) and prev_err is ERR_NONE. The IWDG override at line 94-96 promotes prev_err to ERR_WDG_RESET, but prev_tick stays 0, so the 'prev_tick>0' guard is false and prev_crash is RESET to 0 (line 116). Result: a repeating silent-hang-then-IWDG-reset loop is never recognized as a crash loop and safe-sleep never triggers.
findings.impact: The most likely real-world brick loop on a sealed unit (firmware wedged in some state, recovered only by IWDG, every boot) is exactly the case the crash-loop backoff does NOT catch. The device free-runs IWDG-reset loops at full current, draining the battery, instead of dropping to the 1h STOP2 backoff. Defeats the stated purpose of the feature for the highest-probability failure mode.
findings.recommendation: Treat an IWDG reset with prev_tick==0 (or below MIN_UP_MS) as a short/unstable boot for counting purposes: count the crash when (csr & IWDGRSTF) regardless of whether a tick was logged, since an IWDG reset is by definition an abnormal short boot. Add a unit test for the 'silent IWDG hang loop' sequence.

findings.description: No unit test exercises MGR_ERR_init boot-counter/crash-counter logic or MGR_ERR_checkCrashLoop. Tests/unit/test_crash_forensics.c only re-implements and tests the crash_info CRC/replay protocol with a LOCAL copy of the struct + crc + take() (it does not include mgr_err.c at all), so the actual functions, the crash-counting branch (line 113), the IWDG-override branch (line 94), and the EXTI/STOP2 wake config are entirely untested. The retention-struct logic is only tested via a duplicate, so a divergence between mgr_err.c and the test copy would go unnoticed.
findings.impact: The crash-loop counting bug (high finding) and the EXTI-line brick (critical finding) both live in code with zero direct test coverage. Logic regressions in the persisted-counter math ship silently.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_mgr_err.c that mocks TAMP->BKPxR and RCC->CSR as plain memory and drives MGR_ERR_init across sequences (cold boot; stable boot resets crash counter; short crashed boot increments it; IWDG silent-hang loop; counter reaches MAX). Have the test #include the real crc/getter logic where feasible, or assert the struct layout matches test_crash_forensics.c so the duplicate can't drift.

findings.description: MGR_ERR_log() and MGR_ERR_captureFault() are non-reentrant and call into MGR_LOG / HAL_GetTick. They are invoked from main-thread error paths, while fault handlers correctly use the register-only MGR_ERR_LOG_FAULT macro and captureFault (no MGR_LOG). However in stm32wlxx_it.c:158-159 captureFault then MGR_ERR_LOG_FAULT both write app_state, and captureFault reads SCB/HAL state — captureFault is fine from fault context (no MGR_LOG, stack-local build, single struct commit). The only sharp edge: if MGR_ERR_log() (which DOES call MGR_LOG_ERR) were ever called from an ISR, the log ring buffer is not ISR-safe. Currently no ISR caller exists, so this is latent, not active.
findings.impact: Latent: a future caller invoking MGR_ERR_log() from interrupt context would risk a torn log buffer / reentrancy on MGR_LOG. No current brick.
findings.recommendation: Document in the header that MGR_ERR_log()/logAndReset() are main-context only and ISR/fault paths must use MGR_ERR_LOG_FAULT + MGR_ERR_captureFault. No code change needed today.

findings.description: captureFault reads uwTick via 'extern volatile uint32_t uwTick' directly. This is the HAL tick backing variable; reading it from fault context is safe (single volatile word). Minor: captureFault uses uwTick while MGR_ERR_log() uses HAL_GetTick() — both resolve to the same source, but the inconsistency (one bypasses HAL, one doesn't) is a small comment-rot/clarity nit. Also __DMB() barriers around the struct commit guard ordering but the struct write itself is not atomic (acknowledged in the comment) — acceptable given the magic-invalidate-first scheme.
findings.impact: None functionally; readability only.
findings.recommendation: Optionally note in a comment why uwTick is read directly here (fault-safe, avoids HAL call). No behavior change.

findings.description: ERR_BKP_CRASH maps to TAMP->BKP7R, but the file-top register map comment (mgr_err.c:16) still says 'BKP7R = reserved', while the actual map comment block (mgr_err.c:39 and mgr_err.h:35) correctly says 'Consecutive crash counter'. The header doc-comment at line 12 also references a non-existent 'MGR_ERR_logFault()' (the real symbol is the MGR_ERR_LOG_FAULT macro / MGR_ERR_captureFault).
findings.impact: Documentation rot; could mislead a maintainer into reusing BKP7R as scratch and clobbering the crash counter.
findings.recommendation: Fix the line-16 comment ('BKP7R = consecutive crash counter') and the header usage note ('MGR_ERR_logFault' -> 'MGR_ERR_LOG_FAULT / MGR_ERR_captureFault').

dead_code: No genuine orphans in the sealed (UW_DOPPLER) config: every public function has a live caller (init/checkCrashLoop in main.c:1018-1019; log/logAndReset in kns_app_uw_doppler.c & main.c; captureFault/takeRetainedCrash via stm32wlxx_it.c & kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1635; getters in mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c:495-497). The two static helpers err_code_str()/reset_cause_str() are marked __attribute__((unused)) and become dead in DEBUG=0 builds (all MGR_LOG_* calls collapse to do{}while(0), so err_code_str at line 107/143 and reset_cause_str at line 101/106 are never called) — this is intentional, config-gated by DEBUG, and the attribute correctly suppresses the warning. In GUI/STDLN builds the entire translation unit's functions are unreferenced (no caller) and may be dropped by the linker — config-gated, not a defect.
test_coverage: Partial. The SRAM2 crash_info CRC + magic + take()/replay protocol is well covered by Tests/unit/test_crash_forensics.c — but via a DUPLICATE struct/crc/take implementation, not by including mgr_err.c, so coverage of the actual code is indirect and can silently drift. UNCOVERED testable logic: (1) MGR_ERR_init boot-counter increment + crash-counter state machine (line 113-125), (2) the IWDG-silent-hang override (line 94-96) and its (buggy) interaction with crash counting, (3) MGR_ERR_checkCrashLoop threshold + the STOP2 wake configuration (the EXTI-line brick would have been caught by a register-level test). These are pure integer/register logic and are mockable with the existing TAMP/RCC stub approach used in test_memory_safety.c.

role: Event logger: 256-entry circular ring (8B/entry) in SRAM2 retention RAM; survives soft/IWDG resets, re-inits on BOR/NRST; mirrors ERROR-severity events to flash post-mortem log on UW_DOPPLER.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER and APP=DOPPLER only (Makefile:343, :361). NOT compiled for APP=STDLN or APP=GUI. PMLOG mirror block (lines 78-83) is further gated by USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP, so excluded in DOPPLER builds. Sealed target (UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE) compiles the full file including PMLOG mirror.

findings.description: The unit test COPIES the source instead of including it, and the copy is STALE: it omits the defensive head/count clamps (mgr_evtlog.c:57-60), the PMLOG ERROR mirroring (lines 77-83), and the entire MGR_EVTLOG_getSeverity/MGR_EVTLOG_severityChar functions (lines 109-158). The test enum also stops at EVT_ERROR and is missing EVT_PA_STUCK..EVT_SWS_FAULT (mgr_evtlog.h:41-50). So the actual shipped logic for corruption-clamping, severity classification, and flash mirroring has ZERO unit coverage, and the test can pass while the real code regresses.
findings.impact: A regression in the clamp logic (the only thing protecting against an OOB write into entries[] when SRAM2 head is corrupted) or in the severity table (which gates flash post-mortem writes on the sealed tag) would not be caught by CI. Severity-table mis-classification could either spam the flash page (burning the only post-mortem region) or silently drop a real ERROR.
findings.recommendation: Compile the real mgr_evtlog.c into the test (or #include it) rather than re-typing it. Add cases: (a) head set to >=256 then log() must clamp and not OOB-write; (b) count set to >256 then clamped; (c) getSeverity returns INFO/WARN/ERROR for representative types and INFO for an out-of-range cast value; (d) severityChar T/I/W/E and '?' for out-of-range.

findings.description: MGR_EVTLOG_log() is non-atomic (read-modify-write of head/count plus a multi-field entry store) and is not guarded by a critical section. Audit of all 40+ call sites confirms every caller runs in main-loop/state-machine/AT-handler context; no ISR calls it (EXTI15_10_IRQHandler at stm32wlxx_it.c:367 only clears the flag; the fault handler uses MGR_ERR_*, not EVTLOG). So today there is no actual race.
findings.impact: None currently. But the function reads as ISR-safe (it touches a retention ring also used for crash forensics), and a future change that logs from an EXTI/reed/RTC ISR would silently corrupt head/count or interleave a partial entry. Latent, not a present defect.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment stating MGR_EVTLOG_log must only be called from thread/main context (not reentrant, not ISR-safe), or wrap the head/count update in a brief __disable_irq/__enable_irq if ISR logging is ever wanted.

findings.description: On UW_DOPPLER, every EVT_SEV_ERROR event triggers a synchronous MGR_PMLOG_log() inside MGR_EVTLOG_log(). When the post-mortem flash page wraps, MGR_PMLOG_log erases the page (~25 ms, IRQs disabled during HAL flash op) on the caller's stack. MGR_EVTLOG_log presents as a cheap RAM write but can block ~25 ms.
findings.impact: A logger call that callers assume is instant can stall the main loop ~25 ms and mask interrupts during the flash erase/program. Bounded (only ERROR severity, page erase is rare), and the crash-replay path (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1656) is a single guarded call at boot, so not a hang risk. Mainly a hidden-latency / hidden-IRQ-mask surprise.
findings.recommendation: Document in MGR_EVTLOG_log's header that ERROR-severity logging may block on flash (~25 ms) on UW_DOPPLER. No code change required unless ERROR events can fire in a tight loop.

findings.description: EVT_SEV_TRACE is defined in the severity enum and handled by MGR_EVTLOG_severityChar ('T'), but MGR_EVTLOG_getSeverity never returns it — no event type maps to TRACE, and the post-switch fallback returns EVT_SEV_INFO. So EVT_SEV_TRACE is an orphan value, never produced for any real event.
findings.impact: Harmless. The 'T' branch in severityChar is unreachable in practice. No functional effect; minor documentation/contract mismatch (header comment at line 59 advertises a T/I/W/E scheme but T is never emitted).
findings.recommendation: Either remove EVT_SEV_TRACE until a TRACE-classified event exists, or note it is reserved for future use. Low priority.

findings.description: MGR_EVTLOG_get() does not apply the same defensive head/count clamps that MGR_EVTLOG_log() does (lines 57-60). If SRAM2 retention is corrupted such that head/count are out of range but magic happens to still read as 0x4C4F4721 (init won't reset it), get() computes pos = (head + 256 - count + index) % 256. The mod 256 keeps the index in-bounds of entries[256] so there is no OOB read, but with a corrupt head/count it returns a wrong (stale) entry.
findings.impact: No memory-safety violation (read stays within entries[] due to %256, and entries[] is a fixed 256-slot array so any 0..255 index is valid). Worst case is a garbled AT+LOG dump after SRAM corruption — a diagnostics-only path, not a deploy hazard.
findings.recommendation: Optional: clamp head/count at the top of get()/count() the same way log() does, so a corrupt retention buffer yields a coherent (if truncated) dump rather than stale entries. Not load-bearing.

findings.description: e->state truncates g_uw_doppler_state_for_err (volatile uint32_t) to uint8_t via explicit cast. UW_DOPPLER/DOPPLER state enums fit in a byte (states 0..~12), so no information is lost today. The cast is explicit (MISRA-clean) and the volatile read is a single 32-bit access (atomic on M4).
findings.impact: None today. Would silently truncate if the state enum ever exceeds 255. Noted for completeness.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is; optionally a _Static_assert near the state enum that it stays < 256, but that belongs in kns_app_uw_doppler.c, not here.

dead_code: No genuine orphans within this file. Every public function has live callers: init/log/count/get/clear/getSeverity/severityChar are all reached from kns_app_uw_doppler.c, kns_app_doppler.c, mgr_sws.c, and the AT+LOG handlers (mgr_at_cmd_list_*.c). Config-gated, not dead: the PMLOG mirror block (lines 78-83) is live only when USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP; in DOPPLER builds the #else `(void)sev;` branch runs and getSeverity's result is computed-then-discarded (minor wasted work, not dead code). The whole translation unit is config-excluded from APP=STDLN and APP=GUI (Makefile). EVT_SEV_TRACE / the 'T' branch in severityChar is a value-level orphan (no producer) — see findings.
test_coverage: Partially covered, but by a STALE COPY not the real source (see high-severity test-gap finding). Tests/unit/test_evtlog.c covers ring mechanics well: init/magic, FIFO order, wrap-around, count saturation at 256, head modulo, out-of-range get, clear, warm-boot preservation, struct sizes (8B entry / 2056B buffer). NOT covered at all: the defensive head/count clamps (mgr_evtlog.c:57-60), MGR_EVTLOG_getSeverity classification, MGR_EVTLOG_severityChar mapping, and the PMLOG ERROR-mirror gating. Because the test re-types the functions, the real clamp/severity/mirror code is never exercised by CI.

role: Magnet-gesture FSM on top of MGR_REED/MGR_LED: maps magnet holds/taps to mode transitions (OPERATIONAL/CONFIG/SHUTDOWN) with a 2-gesture confirm window; the only field input on the epoxy-sealed tag.
compiled_in: Sealed target: APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART. Live when UW_DOPPLER_HAS_GESTURE + BSP_HAS_LED_RGB + BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH (SMD_STDALONE). Not compiled for GUI/STDLN or boards without RGB LED / reed (those use the raw-reed fallback in kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1974). UW_DOPPLER is #error-restricted to SMD_STDALONE, so effectively one config builds this.

findings.description: The unit test re-implements a SIMPLIFIED, DIVERGENT FSM (g_tick) with a different state set (FSM_ASKING_MODE_SWITCH/FSM_ASKING_SHUTDOWN + a saw_off flag) instead of exercising the real code. The production FSM uses GFSM_WAIT_CONFIRM/GFSM_ACK_BRIEF/GFSM_CONFIRMED/GFSM_WAKE_BLINK and an s_max_phase 'highest phase reached' classifier — none of which the test models. So the tests pass against a mock and validate nothing in mgr_gesture.c.
findings.impact: The load-bearing anti-brick logic is untested on a sealed device: (1) MGR_GESTURE_isInteracting() 15 s non-IDLE watchdog (RISK A: stuck FSM blocking STOP2 / battery drain), (2) the s_max_phase escalation 3 s->6 s that was the entire point of the 2026-06-06 redesign, (3) WAKE_BLINK abort-on-magnet, (4) the invalid-state SEU recovery fallback, (5) MGR_GESTURE_requestMode AT path. Regressions in any of these ship undetected.
findings.recommendation: Refactor the pure-logic core of the real FSM so it can be linked into the test (mock HAL_GetTick/MGR_REED/MGR_LED as the framework already allows), and add cases for: max-phase escalation, 15 s watchdog force-IDLE, ACK_BRIEF window, WAKE_BLINK->HOLDING abort, invalid-state recovery, and requestMode(OPERATIONAL/CONFIG/POWER_OFF).

findings.description: Comment-rot: the watchdog comment reads 'Hard reset after 60 s stuck in non-IDLE' but GESTURE_NONIDLE_MAX_MS is 15000u (15 s) — and the macro's own comment block (366-372) correctly says 15 s. The 60 s figure is stale from an earlier design.
findings.impact: Misleads the next maintainer about the actual STOP2-recovery latency budget (15 s, not 60 s) on a power-critical sealed unit. No runtime effect.
findings.recommendation: Change '60 s' to '15 s' in the line 387 comment to match GESTURE_NONIDLE_MAX_MS.

findings.description: Genuine orphan macros, no caller in any config: MGR_GESTURE_BLINK_VFAST_ON_MS/OFF_MS (header 82-83) and MGR_GESTURE_CONFIRM_SOLID_MS (header 88) are never referenced (verified by repo-wide grep). GESTURE_BKP_MAGIC_MASK (mgr_gesture.c:91) is also defined but never used. The header doc for the VFAST macros claims the WAIT_CONFIRM blink is a '10 Hz very-fast' urgent blink, but led_show_wait_confirm() actually uses MGR_GESTURE_BLINK_FAST_* (5 Hz) — so the doc describes a cadence that does not exist in code.
findings.impact: No functional risk; comment/doc rot and unused symbols. The VFAST doc actively misdescribes the implemented behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Delete the three unused header macros and GESTURE_BKP_MAGIC_MASK, or actually wire VFAST into led_show_wait_confirm() if 10 Hz was intended. Fix the WAIT_CONFIRM cadence comment either way.

findings.description: Mode persistence is WRITE-ONLY. persist_mode() writes TAMP->BKP10R, but no code ever reads it back (grep confirms only writes). MGR_GESTURE_init() unconditionally forces s_mode=OPERATIONAL on every boot (intended, lines 237-260). The file-header (40-41) and the public header (38-39) both claim 'Mode is persisted in TAMP backup so OPERATIONAL/CONFIG survive resets' — which is false: CONFIG never survives a reset by design. The BKP write, magic, and mode mask are functionally dead (kept only as an observable debug marker per line 247).
findings.impact: Doc contradicts behaviour: a reader could assume a tag that was put in CONFIG stays in CONFIG across an IWDG/HardFault reset, when in fact it always re-boots OPERATIONAL (which is the correct sealed-safety behaviour). No runtime defect, but a dangerous documentation expectation gap.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the header/file-doc to state explicitly: mode is NOT inherited across reset; every boot starts OPERATIONAL; the BKP10R write is a debug-only marker, never read. Consider removing the write entirely if no external tool reads BKP10R.

findings.location: mgr_gesture.c:545-602 (WAIT_CONFIRM) vs MGR_REED ring buffer mgr_reed.c:236-240,267-281
findings.description: WAIT_CONFIRM confirms ONLY on a buffered MGR_REED_EVT_MAGNET_ON (line 548); it does not also consult the live MGR_REED_isMagnetPresent() snapshot it already computed (line 413). The reed driver drops events when its small ring fills (mgr_reed.c:237 'if (depth < EVT_BUF_SIZE)'). If the operator's OFF then ON edges both land while the FSM is starved (e.g. STOP2 wake jitter, TX-blank window at kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1885) and the ON event is dropped or already consumed, the confirm is silently missed and the gesture reverts on window expiry.
findings.impact: Operator-facing reliability only (must redo the gesture); not a brick. Low probability because the gesture FSM is the sole reed-event consumer in this build (the raw-reed handler is a mutually-exclusive #elif) and confirm cadence is human-slow. Worth noting because mode-switch/shutdown are the only sealed-tag controls.
findings.recommendation: In WAIT_CONFIRM, also accept confirm when reed_evt==NONE but a rising edge is implied (track prior magnet_present and detect false->true), or document the single-consumer assumption so no future caller adds a second MGR_REED_getEvent() that would steal the ON event.

findings.description: gst_trace(fmt, a) passes a runtime (non-literal-to-the-compiler) format string to snprintf and always supplies one unsigned-long vararg even when fmt has no conversion (e.g. line 178/193 'phase=DETECT'/'red fast'). All 17 call sites use either '%lu' (matching the (unsigned long)a cast) or no specifier, so it is currently safe, but -Wformat-nonliteral cannot verify it and a future call site with '%s'/'%d' would be UB.
findings.impact: No current defect. Latent foot-gun if someone adds a mismatched format. Extra unused vararg is harmless.
findings.recommendation: Either keep the single-arg contract documented (already noted in comments) or split into gst_trace_msg(const char*) and gst_trace_u32(const char*, uint32_t) so the compiler can format-check each.

findings.description: FSM state is plain (non-volatile) statics mutated by MGR_GESTURE_task()/isInteracting() (main loop) and read by MGR_GESTURE_getMode()/isInteracting() (also main loop). No ISR touches them — the reed EXTI ISR only bumps its own counters and the reed driver's ring; gesture state is single-threaded on the main loop. So non-volatile is correct and there is no race.
findings.impact: None — flagged only to confirm the volatile question was checked: no ISR-vs-main sharing of gesture state, so no missing volatile/critical section.
findings.recommendation: No action. (The author's own SEU-recovery fallback at 614-620 already handles the only realistic corruption source.)

dead_code: Genuine orphans (all configs): header macros MGR_GESTURE_BLINK_VFAST_ON_MS/OFF_MS and MGR_GESTURE_CONFIRM_SOLID_MS (never referenced); GESTURE_BKP_MAGIC_MASK (mgr_gesture.c:91, never used). Functionally-dead-but-intentional: the entire BKP10R persistence path (persist_mode write at :136, GESTURE_BKP_MAGIC/MODE_MASK) is write-only — never read back because init always forces OPERATIONAL (sealed-safety); kept as a debug marker per the :247 comment. No config-gated dead branches inside this file (the single #ifndef DEBUG block at :294-297 is live in the production DEBUG=0 sealed build). The invalid-state fallback at :614-620 is reachable only via SEU/stack-smash — defensive, not dead.
test_coverage: POOR for the real code despite a green test file. Tests/unit/test_gesture_fsm.c tests a hand-written MOCK FSM (g_tick) that diverges from the production FSM in states, release classification, and confirm logic — it does NOT link or exercise mgr_gesture.c. Concretely untested in the real module: (1) MGR_GESTURE_isInteracting() 15 s non-IDLE watchdog (the anti-brick / STOP2-unblock path, RISK A), (2) s_max_phase max-phase escalation 3 s->6 s (the redesign's core), (3) GFSM_ACK_BRIEF 300 ms visibility window, (4) GFSM_WAKE_BLINK abort-on-MAGNET_ON and blink-done event re-emit, (5) MGR_GESTURE_requestMode() AT-path side effects, (6) invalid-state SEU recovery. These are exactly the paths whose failure bricks or battery-drains a sealed unit.

role: RGB LED driver for SMD_STDALONE: solid colours (direct-drive), non-blocking blink FSM, and a SysTick-driven soft-PWM rotator for composite colours on a single-anode-resistor common-anode LED. Plus a 24h auto-off mode and a blocking boot self-test.
compiled_in: Built in all configs (file always compiled). Active body gated by BSP_HAS_LED_RGB (==1 only on BOARD=SMD_STDALONE, i.e. the sealed UW_DOPPLER target); all other boards compile the no-op stub block. softTick is only wired into SysTick on SMD_STDALONE.

findings.location: mgr_led.c:86-101 (led_set_raw) called from both main context (led_apply_color, set_impl, blink_impl, MGR_LED_task, bootTest) and ISR context (MGR_LED_softTick:372)
findings.description: led_set_raw() performs THREE separate HAL_GPIO_WritePin (BSRR) writes to RED/GREEN/BLUE. It is invoked from main-loop paths (MGR_LED_set/blink/task/off) AND from MGR_LED_softTick() in the SysTick ISR. There is no critical section. A SysTick interrupt landing in the middle of a main-context led_set_raw() (e.g. between the RED write and the GREEN write inside led_apply_color for a solid colour) lets the ISR rotate the soft-PWM and overwrite the same pins, then return to finish the partial main-context write. Result: a transient wrong colour / mixed cathode state.
findings.impact: Mostly cosmetic (a one-frame colour glitch on a status LED). NOT a brick. But on the common-anode/single-resistor LED a momentary two-cathode-on state is exactly the condition the soft-PWM exists to avoid, and the glitch is hard to reproduce. The shared-pin write tear is a genuine main-vs-ISR data hazard on the GPIO ODR even though each individual BSRR write is atomic.
findings.recommendation: When transitioning soft_color in main context (led_apply_color), set soft_color=OFF BEFORE driving raw pins, or wrap the led_set_raw sequence in a __disable_irq()/__enable_irq() pair (3 BSRR writes, negligible latency). At minimum document that solid-colour glitches are accepted; the cheapest real fix is to clear soft_color first so the ISR early-returns while main drives the pins.

findings.description: Non-atomic publish of the soft-PWM (soft_color, soft_slot) pair across the main/ISR boundary. led_apply_color() writes soft_color=color (119) then soft_slot=0 (120) as two separate stores. If SysTick fires between them, MGR_LED_softTick() reads the NEW soft_color but the OLD soft_slot, advancing from a stale slot index. Both vars are volatile (good) but volatile does not give you a consistent multi-word snapshot.
findings.impact: Single-frame slot mis-selection at most (1 ms of wrong sub-colour). soft_slot is always taken modulo len in the ISR (368) so it can never index out of bounds regardless of the stale value — so this is a visual glitch only, not a memory-safety issue. Low real-world consequence on a status LED.
findings.recommendation: Set soft_slot=0 BEFORE soft_color (publish the index first, then the enable), or guard the two writes with a brief __disable_irq()/__enable_irq(). Add a comment that the ordering is load-bearing.

findings.description: Guard-predicate mismatch between the ISR and this module. mgr_led.c gates its real body with `#if defined(BSP_HAS_LED_RGB) && BSP_HAS_LED_RGB` (requires non-zero) and its #else stub block (449-464) defines every public function EXCEPT MGR_LED_softTick. The SysTick handler gates the softTick call with only `#if defined(BSP_HAS_LED_RGB)` (truthiness not checked). If anyone ever defines BSP_HAS_LED_RGB to 0 (rather than leaving it undefined), the ISR would reference MGR_LED_softTick while mgr_led.c compiles the stub block that omits it -> undefined symbol at link, or worse, a stale/other definition.
findings.impact: No effect today: BSP_HAS_LED_RGB is only ever `1` (SMD_STDALONE) or undefined, so the two predicates agree. Latent landmine for a future board variant that uses `0` to disable the LED. Would surface as a build/link failure (loud, not silent), so low runtime risk but a real config-correctness defect.
findings.recommendation: Make the two guards identical. Either change the ISR guard to `#if defined(BSP_HAS_LED_RGB) && BSP_HAS_LED_RGB`, or add a no-op MGR_LED_softTick() to the #else stub block in mgr_led.c (453-463) so the symbol always exists.

findings.description: Blinking a COMPOSITE colour interacts badly with the soft-PWM. On the off-phase MGR_LED_task calls led_apply_color(MGR_LED_OFF) which sets soft_color=OFF (correct, PWM stops). On the on-phase it calls led_apply_color(blink_color) which re-arms soft_color and re-drives only slot 0 (the immediate RED-ish kick at 123-129). For VIOLET/WHITE/YELLOW slot-0 is RED. So a blinked composite colour shows a RED flash at the start of every on-phase before the ISR rotates it to the intended hue. For short on_ms (e.g. the 100-200 ms blinks used app-wide) the RED kick is a visible fraction of each pulse.
findings.impact: Cosmetic: blinked composite colours look red-tinged / wrong-hue. No current caller blinks a composite colour (grep shows blink callers use RED/GREEN/BLUE/YELLOW only; YELLOW IS composite -> kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1960 MGR_LED_blink(MGR_LED_YELLOW,...) and gesture uses WHITE via setForced not blink). So the YELLOW blink at 1960 DOES hit this: each on-phase starts with a RED flash. Misleading status indication, not a safety issue.
findings.recommendation: Either accept (status only) and document, or in led_apply_color drive a representative middle-of-schedule slot for the immediate kick instead of always RED, or for blinked composites start soft_slot at a non-RED slot. Cheapest: note the limitation in the header alongside the existing composite-colour caveat.

findings.location: mgr_led.c:160-180 (MGR_LED_init), 68-84 (led_reinit_gpio); teardown via MGR_LED_off at mgr_lpm_uw.c:612,818,943
findings.description: After MGR_LED_off() the three pins are left as push-pull outputs driven to the OFF level (HIGH/SET for active-low common-anode = both rail and anode at ~3V3, cathode high -> no LED current, which is correct). Before STOP2 the LPM path calls MGR_LED_off() (good) but does NOT reconfigure the pins to analog/no-pull. Push-pull output held HIGH into a common-anode node draws no LED current, so this is not a leak in the normal case. Worth noting only because the file's own comment (66) says LPM 'may have reconfigured the pins to analog' — implying some path does, but this module never sets them analog for sleep itself.
findings.impact: Negligible in normal operation: LED is dark and no current flows through the diode when the cathode side is driven HIGH. Not a measurable STOP2 drain contributor. Flagged for completeness against the sealed-deployment µA budget — confirm on the bench that the LED pins contribute ~0 µA in STOP2 (they should).
findings.recommendation: No code change required unless bench µA measurement shows otherwise. If a future audit wants belt-and-braces, set the three pins to analog in the LPM teardown (outside this module) — do not change init here.

findings.description: 24h auto-off uses (HAL_GetTick() - mode_start_tick) > 86400000UL. HAL_GetTick is uint32_t ms and wraps at ~49.7 days. The unsigned subtraction handles a single wrap correctly, so the 24h window is computed correctly across one wrap. Edge: if the device runs >49.7 days with led_mode left at 24H and is_mode_active() is never called during a given window, no issue — but note that in the sealed deployment the MCU spends almost all time in STOP2 where HAL_GetTick (SysTick) is frozen, so the '24h' is 24h of CPU-awake time, NOT 24h wall-clock. The auto-off therefore takes far longer than 24h of deployment to trigger.
findings.impact: The 24h LED auto-off (the default mode, led_mode=MGR_LED_MODE_24H at line 31) measures awake-ticks, not wall time. In a duty-cycled sealed deployment the LED could stay armed for many real-world days before the awake-tick budget reaches 86.4M ms, modestly increasing power if status events keep firing it. Not a brick; a power/behaviour surprise vs the documented '24 hours'.
findings.recommendation: If wall-clock 24h is intended, derive the timeout from the RTC (which runs in STOP2) instead of HAL_GetTick. Otherwise reword the comment/docs to '~24h of cumulative awake time'. Confirm desired semantics with the deployment owner.

findings.description: The YELLOW schedule's last entry is written `SLOT_R | 0u` with comment 'hold pattern symmetry'. `| 0u` is a no-op; the slot is just SLOT_R. The comment implies intent that the code does not express, and a reader may think there's a hidden bit. Also soft_yellow_sched has 5 slots (R, G, G, OFF, R) = R:2 G:2 OFF:1; fine, but the OFF-slot 'tames brightness' comment plus the redundant `|0u` make the table harder to verify than necessary.
findings.impact: None functional. Readability / comment-rot risk: future edits may misread the `|0u` as significant. Cosmetic.
findings.recommendation: Drop `| 0u`, write plain SLOT_R, and adjust the comment to state the actual R:G:OFF ratio.

findings.description: Header doc-comment for MGR_LED_bootTest says it 'cycles R, G, B, WHITE individually (blocking, 500ms each)' and 'Logs GPIO register state for each step.' The implementation cycles R, G, B (no WHITE), uses 400 ms delays (not 500), and logs nothing. Comment rot — three inaccuracies in one doc block.
findings.impact: Documentation only; misleads a maintainer about timing, the WHITE step, and logging. No runtime effect.
findings.recommendation: Update the header comment to match: R/G/B at 400 ms, no WHITE, no logging (or add WHITE/logging if that was the intent).

findings.location: Tests/unit/test_led_swap.c (only existing test) vs mgr_led.c blink FSM (205-243,377-411), is_mode_active gating (145-156), soft_schedule_get/softTick rotation (322-375)
findings.description: The only unit test mirrors the colour->GPIO mapping table. None of the stateful logic is covered: (a) blink FSM phase transitions and count termination including the count==0 infinite case (398), (b) the idempotent-blink early-return (220-225), (c) is_mode_active gating including the 24h expiry and the OFF/24H/ON branches, (d) bypass vs gated set/blink (set_impl/blink_impl), (e) soft_schedule_get length computation and softTick slot rotation/modulo. The test also re-implements the mapping rather than including the real led_apply_color, so a real-code regression in led_apply_color's composite slot-0 kick would not be caught.
findings.impact: Stateful and config-gating logic (the parts most likely to harbour off-by-one / wrong-gate regressions) ships untested. Given the file's history of a wrong-hypothesis swap regression, the blink/mode gating deserves equivalent guard tests.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit cases for: blink termination at exactly blink_total, count==0 stays blinking, idempotent re-issue does not reset phase, is_mode_active returns false for OFF and after 24h, set_impl(bypass=true) ignores mode gate, and softTick advances soft_slot modulo schedule length without OOB. Mock HAL_GetTick/HAL_GPIO_WritePin.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. All public functions have live callers (verified by grep): MGR_LED_set/blink/setForced/blinkForced/off/setMode/getMode used across kns_app_uw_doppler.c, kns_app_doppler.c, mgr_gesture.c, mgr_at_cmd_list_*.c, mgr_nvm.c; MGR_LED_softTick called from SysTick_Handler (stm32wlxx_it.c:252); MGR_LED_bootTest is referenced (header doc/diag) — a blocking self-test, retained intentionally even if not on the hot path. The entire active body (lines 27-447) is config-gated dead on every board except SMD_STDALONE (BSP_HAS_LED_RGB!=1) — INTENTIONAL, the #else block (449-464) provides no-op stubs for those boards. MGR_LED_MODE_ON enum value is accepted by setMode but is_mode_active treats anything not OFF/24H as active, so ON works; no dead branch there. The `default:` arms in led_apply_color (141), the switch in led_apply_color composite block (128), and soft_schedule_get (346) are defensive and reachable only via an out-of-range MGR_LED_Color_t (not dead in the unreachable sense — they are the safety net).
test_coverage: Partially covered. Only the colour->GPIO mapping table is unit-tested (test_led_swap.c, 8 cases) and it RE-implements the logic rather than linking the real led_apply_color, so it cannot catch a regression in the actual source. Untested testable logic: blink FSM (phase/count/idempotency, lines 205-243 + 377-411), is_mode_active gating incl. 24h expiry (145-156), set_impl/blink_impl bypass vs gated (186-211), soft_schedule_get length math + softTick modulo rotation (322-375). These are pure logic (HAL mockable) and SHOULD be tested — see test-gap finding. GPIO/HAL_GPIO_Init plumbing is HW glue (n/a for unit test).

role: UW_DOPPLER-specific low-power manager: event-driven STOP2 duty-cycle scheduler, retention-NOLOAD duty/threshold config, magnet-only soft-off (STOP2 loop or true SHUTDOWN on WKUP boards), STANDBY test path, LPM telemetry, and runtime RTC-liveness gating.
compiled_in: all configs compile the file, but the entire functional body is gated on BOARD=SMD_STDALONE (BSP_HAS_PWR_LATCH). Other boards (SMD_PA/NOPA/OP) get the #else no-op stubs (lines 1110-1148). UW_DOPPLER app is restricted to SMD_STDALONE by an #error, and the #error at line 49-51 forces MAC_PRFL=BASIC. CONSOLE_WAKE_ON_RX block (PA3 EXTI3 wake) is active in the sealed target because BSP_REED_ON_WKUP3 is NOT set by default.

findings.location: mgr_lpm_uw.c:521-529; referenced only in a comment at kns_app_uw_doppler.c:676
findings.description: MGR_LPM_UW_tryAutoCycle() has NO live caller. The MONITORING tick was migrated to MGR_LPM_UW_idleTick() (called directly at kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2494 and 2513). tryAutoCycle is a legacy compatibility shim that derives delta_ms from MGR_SWS_get{Surf,UW}IntervalMs and forwards to idleTick.
findings.impact: No runtime impact; it is exported in the header so the linker keeps it. Pure orphan that can confuse maintainers into thinking the auto-cycle still flows through it (header doc at mgr_lpm_uw.h:166-186 still describes the OLD STANDBY/SHUTDOWN-threshold behaviour that this function no longer performs — comment-rot).
findings.recommendation: Either remove tryAutoCycle and its header decl, or keep it but fix the stale header doc (lines 166-186) which describes STANDBY/SHUTDOWN duty selection that no longer happens.

findings.description: MGR_LPM_UW_enterShutdownAutoWake() is a genuine orphan: grep across Kineis/ and Core/ finds no caller. The header (lines 153-159) says it is 'intended for the boot-loop guard's 24h retry from PERMANENT_OFF path', but that wiring was never done.
findings.impact: Dead exported function; minor binary bloat. The 'best-effort on STDALONE' caveat in the doc means if it WERE wired it might not actually re-power on battery, so the dead state is currently safer than a half-working caller.
findings.recommendation: Remove, or wire it into the boot-loop guard if the 24h-retry behaviour is still wanted. If kept, mark clearly as unused.

findings.location: mgr_lpm_uw.c:144-150, 737-832 (lptim_init_once, HAL_LPTIM_AutoReloadMatchCallback, LPTIM1_IRQHandler, enter_sleep_for_ms), and statics s_lptim/s_lptim_fired/s_lptim_initialised
findings.description: The entire retired STOP1+LPTIM 'SLEEP' tier is dead code: enter_sleep_for_ms is marked __attribute__((unused)) and idleTick routes every band to STOP2 (line 514). This is INTENTIONAL and well-documented (banner at 129-143). NOTE: HAL_LPTIM_AutoReloadMatchCallback and LPTIM1_IRQHandler have EXTERNAL linkage and override HAL weak symbols — they remain linked even though nothing arms LPTIM1, so they are harmless but not strippable by the linker.
findings.impact: No runtime effect (LPTIM1 is never initialised/armed in the live path). Carrying ~95 lines of dead HW glue plus three retained ISR/callback overrides. s_lptim is a HW handle held in BSS for a peripheral never used.
findings.recommendation: Keep per the documented 'do not re-wire without HW re-validation' note, OR move to a clearly #if 0 / separate file so it cannot be accidentally re-enabled. No action required for correctness.

findings.description: Console-wake holdoff uses the wrap-trick `(HAL_GetTick() - s_console_holdoff_until) > 0x80000000u` to mean 'now is before the deadline'. s_console_holdoff_until is set to HAL_GetTick()+2500 at line 1048 and NEVER reset to 0 after it expires. The expiry itself works (subtraction crosses below 0x80000000). But because the deadline value persists, ~49.7 days later (HAL_GetTick wraps past it) the same comparison re-enters the 'before-deadline' half-plane and spuriously blocks sleep again for up to ~24.8 days.
findings.impact: In the sealed field there is no UART traffic, so s_console_holdoff_until is normally never armed; if it is armed once during commissioning, the latent re-trigger would keep the unit awake (~5 mA at MONITORING) for up to ~24 days once the compensated tick wraps. Probability low (needs an armed holdoff to survive to a 32-bit ms wrap), impact high if it lands — hence not negligible for a 12-month deployment.
findings.recommendation: Clear s_console_holdoff_until = 0 once the holdoff has elapsed (e.g. in the else branch of the line 444 test), turning it into a one-shot. Also guard the +CONSOLE_WAKE_HOLDOFF_MS result so it can't land exactly on 0 (which would silently disable that single holdoff).

findings.description: detectSurfaceWake holds load-bearing cold-boot UW->SURFACE transition logic (sets wake_should_tx, refuses to overwrite the baseline on UNKNOWN samples). The only unit test (test_lpm_deadline.c) covers deadline aggregation and STOP2 arming math, NOT this state-transition function. The UNKNOWN-protection branch (lines 345-348) and the one-shot wake_should_tx latch are exactly the kind of cold-boot logic that needs a regression test.
findings.impact: A regression in the UW->SURF detection (e.g. an UNKNOWN sample wiping last_sws_state, or wake_should_tx not latching) would silently drop the first surface TX after a dive — the core mission event — with no test to catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit case for detectSurfaceWake: UW->SURF sets transition+latch; SURF->SURF no transition; UNKNOWN sample does NOT clobber the persisted baseline; isWakeShouldTx/clearWakeShouldTx round-trip.

findings.description: MGR_LPM_UW_setLpmThr's clamp (sleep_ms < spin_ms -> sleep_ms = spin_ms, line 230) and s_apply_lpm_thr_defaults_if_needed's magic-based default seeding are pure, mockable logic with no unit test. Likewise setDutyCfg's >=1 clamping (lines 300-301).
findings.impact: Boundary regressions (e.g. defaults not applied on magic mismatch after a struct-version bump — the exact class of bug the version byte in DUTY_CFG_MAGIC was added to prevent) would go undetected at unit level.
findings.recommendation: Add unit coverage for the threshold/duty default+clamp paths, including the magic-mismatch -> defaults branch.

findings.description: In enterStandbyTimed the HAL_RTCEx_SetWakeUpTimer_IT return value is discarded with (void) (line 550). enterStop2TimedMs correctly checks wut_st and bails out awake if arming fails (lines 924-928), but enterStandbyTimed has no such guard: if the WUT fails to arm, it still proceeds into HAL_PWR_EnterSTANDBYMode (line 590) with no wake source. STANDBY freezes the IWDG, so a failed-arm STANDBY would strand the chip until a magnet/NRST.
findings.impact: enterStandbyTimed is documented as AT+STANDBYTEST-only (not the production duty path, which uses STOP2), so the blast radius is a bench test — but it is still a hang/brick path that contradicts the safety pattern already applied to the STOP2 sibling. If ever re-promoted to a live path it brings the brick with it.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the STOP2 guard: check the SetWakeUpTimer_IT status and abort the STANDBY entry (return / fall back to a safe loop) if it is not HAL_OK. Apply the same RTC-liveness (HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro) gate used in STOP2 before entering an RTC-only STANDBY.

findings.description: enterShutdownReed de-inits PA3 and disables LPUART1_IRQn so UART can't wake the soft-off (correct). But on the non-WKUP soft-off path it then loops in STOP2 (lines 714-725) and disables only LPUART1_IRQn, not EXTI3_IRQn. When CONSOLE_WAKE_ON_RX is active (the sealed target) a prior idle-STOP2 may have armed PA3 as EXTI3 falling-edge; HAL_GPIO_DeInit(GPIOA, PIN_3) clears the pin's EXTI config bits but EXTI3_IRQn is left enabled in the NVIC and is not explicitly cleared/disabled here.
findings.impact: Low: the soft-off is entered from a gesture/AT context, not mid-idle-STOP2, and HAL_GPIO_DeInit clears the EXTI config for PA3. Worst case a stray edge wakes the soft-off STOP2 loop once, which re-checks the reed and re-sleeps — no brick, just one extra wake. It is an un-mirrored teardown relative to the idle path.
findings.recommendation: For symmetry/robustness, also HAL_NVIC_DisableIRQ(EXTI3_IRQn) and __HAL_GPIO_EXTI_CLEAR_IT(GPIO_PIN_3) in enterShutdownReed before the soft-off loop, guarded by CONSOLE_WAKE_ON_RX.

findings.description: uw_sleep_s/surf_sleep_s are explicitly LEGACY/unused by the live scheduler (defaults zeroed at 271-272, never read by idleTick). They remain settable via setDutyCfg/AT+DUTYCFG and are echoed back by getDutyCfg, so an operator setting AT+DUTYCFG sees values that have NO effect on sleep duration (now derived from the SWS interval).
findings.impact: Operator confusion / silent no-op config knob. The _pad byte and these fields also keep the struct layout that the version byte (MAGIC ...02) protects, so they can't be removed without a magic bump — that part is handled correctly.
findings.recommendation: Document in the AT+DUTYCFG help/echo that uw/surf seconds are legacy and ignored by the event-driven scheduler, or have AT+DUTYCFG reject/annotate them. No code-correctness change needed.

findings.description: s_console_rx_edge is volatile bool, written in EXTI3_IRQHandler and read/cleared in enterStop2TimedMs after wake. The read-modify-clear at 1044-1045 (if(edge){edge=false;...}) is not atomic, but EXTI3_IRQn is disabled (HAL_NVIC_DisableIRQ at line 1033) before the read, so no concurrent ISR write can race. Correctly ordered.
findings.impact: None — flagged only to record that the volatile/ISR handshake was reviewed and is sound (IRQ disabled before the non-atomic clear).
findings.recommendation: No action.

findings.location: mgr_lpm_uw.c:970-980 (PB6 reed EXTI left armed in STOP2)
findings.description: PB6 reed EXTI is intentionally left unmasked through STOP2 so a magnet edge wakes the chip. The code comment acknowledges that on the bench a Hall stuck HIGH causes ~28000 ISR/s and keeps the chip at ~5 mA (MONITORING current). The idleTick reed-debounce budget (lines 410-426) bounds the DEBOUNCING window but not a steadily-asserted line.
findings.impact: In deployment there is no magnet so the line is idle and STOP2 reaches its uA floor — documented/acceptable. But a physically failed/shorted reed or fouling that biases the Hall in the field (low-probability HW failure) would pin the unit at ~5 mA and flatten the battery in days, with no firmware mitigation on this path — high consequence for a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Consider a long-window watchdog: if reed-driven wakes exceed a threshold over N minutes with no confirmed gesture, mask PB6 EXTI for a cool-down and rely on the RTC wake only. Bench/field decision, not a code defect — recorded for risk visibility.

dead_code: Three dead items, all config/orphan as noted: (1) MGR_LPM_UW_tryAutoCycle (lines 521-529) — genuine orphan, only a comment reference, header doc is also stale. (2) MGR_LPM_UW_enterShutdownAutoWake (729-735) — genuine orphan, no caller anywhere; intended boot-loop-guard wiring never done. (3) The entire LPTIM/STOP1 SLEEP tier: enter_sleep_for_ms (marked __attribute__((unused)), 799-832), lptim_init_once (746-775), the LPTIM callback/IRQ overrides (780-789), and s_lptim/s_lptim_fired/s_lptim_initialised — INTENTIONALLY retired and documented (banner 129-143); kept-for-reference, not an accident. enterStandbyTimed (533-592) is reachable only via AT+STANDBYTEST (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:977) — not dead, but not the production path. Config-gated (not dead): the whole #else stub block (1110-1148) is the only thing compiled on non-PWR_LATCH boards; CONSOLE_WAKE_ON_RX block is live in the sealed target. (void)-marked legacy fields s_duty.shutdown_threshold_s (487) and s_lpm_thr.sleep_ms (513) are deliberately unused by the event-driven path.
test_coverage: Partial. Tests/unit/test_lpm_deadline.c covers the STOP2 RTC-arming math (DIV16 vs CK_SPRE, floor, min-one-tick, clamp) and the deadline aggregation — good coverage of enterStop2TimedMs arithmetic. GAPS: (a) detectSurfaceWake state-transition logic (UW->SURF latch, UNKNOWN-baseline protection) has NO unit test despite being the core cold-boot mission trigger; (b) LpmThr/DutyCfg default-seeding + clamp (magic-mismatch -> defaults branch, sleep<spin clamp) untested; (c) the WUT-arm-failure bail-out paths and RTC-liveness gate are HW-bound (not directly unit-testable, but the decision logic could be factored). The deep-sleep entry functions themselves are HW glue (n/a for unit).

role: NVM manager: persists UW_DOPPLER config to one flash page at 0x0803F800 with CRC-32/MPEG-2 integrity, validation, healing, and v1..v7 -> v8 migration.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER only (#error-restricted to BOARD=SMD_STDALONE). LED/BAT blocks further gated by BSP_HAS_LED_RGB / BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC. Not built for STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER.
test_coverage: Partial/misleading. Live v8 logic exercised only by mirrored slices in Tests/unit/test_nvm_heal_migration.c (SWS heals incl. ordering, max_dive=0 heal, v7->v8 prefix offset invariant, payload bounds). Tests/unit/test_nvm.c is a stale standalone v2 re-implementation that does not link the production file and asserts a flash-rewrite-on-migrate the real loader never does. Untested real logic: full validate_config bound set (TX init>max, SWS threshold ordering, LB hysteresis, rate 0/0 sentinel, lpm_sleep>=spin gate, battery>5000), every migrate_vN field mapping for v1..v6, and the byte-identical brownout save-skip (989-1011).
dead_code: No genuine orphans. All 7 legacy structs (NVM_Config_v1..v7_t) are consumed by their matching migrate_*/load branches. All migrate_* and static helpers (nvm_crc32, validate_config, apply_config, gather_config) are reachable from the public API. The four public functions have live callers (kns_app_uw_doppler.c, mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c). The BSP_HAS_LED_RGB / BSP_HAS_VBAT_ADC blocks (apply 500-506, gather 565-571) are config-gated, not dead, and present on the sealed SMD_STDALONE target. last_save_tick (329) is read/written across save+debounce. No unreachable branches.

findings.description: On successful v1..v7 migration MGR_NVM_load() applies config but NEVER writes the upgraded v8 record back to flash. Flash keeps the old version+CRC. The log emits 'Migrated vN -> v8' which is false: nothing was persisted. Every boot re-reads the legacy struct and re-runs migration. Flash upgrades only if an unrelated MGR_NVM_save() later fires.
findings.impact: Misleading forensic log on a sealed unit (claims migrated while flash is still v1). Repeated per-boot migration work (cheap, bounded). No corruption. Unit test test_migration_writes_v2_to_flash asserts a re-write that production code does not do, so that test misrepresents real behaviour.
findings.recommendation: Persist immediately after a successful migrate (re-CRC + MCU_FLASH_write before returning true) so flash self-heals, or fix the log to say the upgrade is RAM-only/not persisted.

findings.description: sws_test_interval_surface_ms = v1->sws_test_interval_ms * 5 is uint32_t with no overflow guard; a legacy interval > ~858M ms wraps. validate_config only rejects ==0, so a wrapped nonzero value passes. Migration runs before validation.
findings.impact: Extremely low: such a stored interval is implausible and CRC-protected. A wrap yields an absurd surface cadence, not a hang. Correctness/MISRA nit.
findings.recommendation: Clamp the source before multiply (cap ~600000 ms) or add an upper bound on sws_test_interval_surface_ms in validate_config.

findings.description: validate_config never bounds-checks deploy_mode or led_mode. deploy_mode is safe downstream (setDeployMode booleanizes, kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2755). led_mode is cast raw to MGR_LED_Mode_t and passed to MGR_LED_setMode() with no clamp; the enum only defines 0/1/2 (mgr_led.h:27-29). A CRC-valid record with led_mode>2 reaches the LED layer unchecked.
findings.impact: Low. Reached only via a previously-saved/forged-but-CRC-correct record (gather_config only writes valid enums). If MGR_LED_setMode lacks a range check, an out-of-range enum could mis-switch. LED block is BSP_HAS_LED_RGB-gated, present on the sealed target.
findings.recommendation: Add 'if (cfg->led_mode > 2) return false;' to validate_config, mirroring the payload_format/stat_window_h bounds already present for v8.

findings.description: test_nvm.c is a stale parallel re-implementation frozen at NVM_VERSION 2 (own 48-byte v2 struct, lines 19/46-69/381). It does NOT link production mgr_nvm.c; it tests a hand-copied v1->v2 loader. None of the live v8 logic (validate_config bounds, rate/LB/LPM apply gates, migrate_v3..v7, byte-identical save-skip, max_dive heal) is exercised. Only test_nvm_heal_migration.c covers real v8 logic, and it MIRRORS (re-types) slices rather than linking them.
findings.impact: Large blind spot for a sealed-deploy-critical module. A flipped comparison in validate_config's SWS/LB/LPM gates, a bad field map in any migrate_vN_to_v8, or a broken brownout save-skip would pass CI. test_nvm.c even encodes a migrate-rewrites-flash behaviour the production code does not perform.
findings.recommendation: Add a regression test mirroring validate_config's full bound set (LB hysteresis lb_exit<=lb_enter, rate 0/0 sentinel, lpm_sleep>=spin gate, battery>5000) and each migrate_vN_to_v8 field mapping. Delete or mark test_nvm.c so the v2 copy isn't mistaken for current coverage.

findings.description: min_interval_s * 1000 is uint32_t and overflows for min_interval_s > ~4.29e6 s (~49.7 days). The unsigned (now - last_save_tick) subtraction is correct across tick rollover; last_save_tick==0 intentionally lets the first calib save through.
findings.impact: None in practice: sole caller passes the small NVM_CALIB_SAVE_MIN_INTERVAL_S (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2315). A multi-week interval would silently defeat the debounce. Theoretical.
findings.recommendation: Compute the threshold in uint64_t or document the bound. Optional given the fixed small caller.

findings.description: Names misstate target: migrate_v1_to_v3 and migrate_v2_to_v3 actually emit a full v8 record (version=8; v4..v8 fields zero-defaulted via memset); migrate_v3_to_v4 / migrate_v5_to_v6 likewise jump straight to v8. Only v6_to_v7 and v7_to_v8 are single-step.
findings.impact: Maintenance/readability only. A future editor adding a v9 field could assume migrate_v1_to_v3 stops at v3 and forget to default the v9 field (today correct only because memset+NVM_VERSION covers it; name-fragile).
findings.recommendation: Rename to migrate_v1_to_current/_to_v8 to match behaviour, or route v1/v2/v3/v5 through the real single-step chain. No functional change needed now.

findings.description: Comment rot: header labels NVM_Config_t '(v3)' though NVM_VERSION is 8; header version-history documents only up to v5 (no v6 LPM, v7 seq_restart, v8 payload) despite those fields existing (mgr_nvm.h:89-110). The .c file-header history (10-15) stops at v3.
findings.impact: Documentation only; per-field struct comments are accurate.
findings.recommendation: Extend version-history comments to v8 and fix the '(v3)' label, or drop the redundant blocks and rely on the accurate field tags.

role: Post-mortem persistent flash log: append-only 16-byte entries in one dedicated 2KB flash page (FLASH_PMLOG @0x08032000), mirrors ERROR-severity events so a recovered dead-battery tag can be forensically dumped via AT+PMLOG.
compiled_in: Object is built in all configs (plain manager .c, no top-level #ifdef). But MGR_PMLOG_log() is only CALLED under USE_UW_DOPPLER_APP (mgr_evtlog.c:78-83 gates the mirror; mgr_lpm_uw.c:900 is UW-only) and init/get/count/clear are wired only through the UW_DOPPLER AT-command table (mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c). Effectively live only for the sealed target APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE. On STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER the code links but the page is never written.

findings.location: mgr_pmlog.c:196-206 (MGR_PMLOG_get) + the contiguity comment 198-202; interacts with init counting at 84-88 and the torn-slot design at 41-45,152-154,184-188
