findings.recommendation: In WRITETXSIZE require rx->size >= 3 before reading data[1..2]. In WRITETX, clamp/verify userTxPayloadSize <= (rx->size - 1) (the actual received payload length) before the copy loop; reject with ERROR_INVALID_USER_DATA_LENGTH otherwise.

findings.description: Type/semantics mismatch: bMGR_SPI_DRIVER_writeread() is declared `uint8_t` (mgr_spi_cmd_common.h:93) and its definition (mgr_spi_cmd_common.c:114-168) unconditionally `return HAL_OK;` on every path - it never reports a real driver failure. Here its result is stored in `HAL_StatusTypeDef ret` and tested `ret == HAL_OK` / `ret != HAL_OK`. Because the callee can only ever return HAL_OK(0), the `else return false` (line 130-131), the `ret != HAL_OK` rollback (line 220-223), and the bMGR_SPI_CMD_WRITETXSIZE/REQ failure returns are all unreachable.
findings.impact: Dead error-handling branches that give a false impression of failure recovery (e.g. the FIFO-rollback at line 221 can never fire from this check). No functional harm today, but masks the fact that SPI write failures are not actually detectable. SPI-build only.
findings.recommendation: Make bMGR_SPI_DRIVER_writeread() return a meaningful status (or void), or stop pretending: drop the HAL_StatusTypeDef wrapper and the unreachable error branches. Align the declared return type with reality.

findings.description: userTxPayloadSize is a non-static global with an `extern` declaration in mgr_spi_cmd_list.h, but every read/write is confined to this single translation unit (grep confirms no external user). It should be `static`. Exposing it as extern is unnecessary global mutable surface (also violates the project's 'static for file-local, no global mutables' rule).
findings.impact: No bug (handlers run from the main SPI dispatch loop, not ISR, so no race), but needless external linkage and a header coupling. SPI-build only.
findings.recommendation: Make it `static uint16_t userTxPayloadSize = 0;` and remove the extern from mgr_spi_cmd_list.h.

findings.description: Side-effecting calls inside kns_assert(): line 232 asserts a pointer (harmless), but line 248 is `kns_assert(USERDATA_txFifoAddElt(spUserDataMsg, true))` - the load-bearing FIFO insertion is the assert expression. In this codebase kns_assert (kns_assert.h:43) always evaluates its argument, so it works today. It is a fragile idiom: if Kineis ever ships an NDEBUG/no-op assert variant, the FIFO add silently disappears and the reserved element leaks. Same pattern pre-exists in the AT path (mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c:195).
findings.impact: None currently. Latent landmine if the assert macro is ever made compile-out. SPI-build only.
findings.recommendation: Call USERDATA_txFifoAddElt() into a local bool, then kns_assert(that_bool); handle a false return (remove reserved elt) instead of only asserting.

findings.location: Tests/unit (no test references MGR_SPI_CMD / WRITETX / convertAsciiBinary)
findings.description: No unit test exercises any function in this file. The pure-logic, easily-mockable pieces are untested: u16MGR_SPI_CMD_convertAsciiBinary (odd/even char count, 0xFF invalid-hex rejection, tail zeroing, bit-length return), the WRITETXSIZE little-endian decode + max-size rejection, and the WRITETX size/FIFO-full/queue-full branches. The AT-path converter has the same algorithm but is likewise not directly covered for the SPI variant.
findings.impact: Regressions in size validation or the (proposed) bit-length guard would ship undetected. Only host-driven SPI builds are affected, but those are the GUI/integration boards.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_spi_userdata.c covering convertAsciiBinary edge cases and WRITETXSIZE/WRITETX validation paths with mocked USERDATA_txFifo* and bMGR_SPI_DRIVER_writeread.

findings.description: Comment rot in the file banner: `@file mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c` (wrong - this is the SPI file) and `@author Kineis`, while the paired header credits `@author Arribada`. Copy-paste artifact from the AT-path file.
findings.impact: Doc/traceability only.
findings.recommendation: Fix @file to mgr_spi_cmd_list_user_data.c and reconcile authorship.

dead_code: Whole file is config-gated dead in the sealed deployment: only compiled under COMM=SPI (Makefile:412-428); sealed target is COMM=UART. Within SPI builds: (1) u16MGR_SPI_CMD_convertAsciiBinary (line 77) is a genuine orphan - exported, zero callers, SPI path uses raw bytes (this is a real dead function, not config-gating). (2) The `ret != HAL_OK` / `else return false` error branches (lines 130-132, 163-165, 220-223) are unreachable because bMGR_SPI_DRIVER_writeread() always returns HAL_OK. (3) The three WRITETX* handlers themselves are live in SPI builds (registered in the dispatch table mgr_spi_cmd_list.c:48-50). The commented-out Set_TX_LED / MGR_LOG_array block (lines 46-71) is inert (commented), not compiled.
test_coverage: Not covered. No Tests/unit file references MGR_SPI_CMD, WRITETX, or convertAsciiBinary. The testable logic (ASCII-hex conversion, little-endian size decode, size/FIFO validation branches) has no unit test; these are pure/mockable and should be covered. The HW-touching parts (bMGR_SPI_DRIVER_writeread, MCU_MISC_TCXO/PA, KNS_Q_push) are glue and can be mocked as the framework already does for HAL_/MGR_/KNS_.

role: A+ SPI framing layer: byte/buffer frame parser, CRC-8 (poly 0x07) integrity check, response builder, and legacy single-byte command backward-compat detection for the SPI command manager.
compiled_in: COMM=SPI only (Makefile guards the whole MGR_SPI_CMD source set under -DUSE_SPI_DRIVER, line 414/419-427). NOT compiled for the sealed deployment (APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART). So every defect here is dead in the sealed unit and only matters for SPI-host builds (GUI/STDLN over SPI).

findings.description: The unit suite named 'test_spi_protocol.c' does NOT compile or link mgr_spi_protocol.c. Every test exercises LOCAL mock reimplementations declared inside the test file (get_cmd_info, parse_write_req_frame, parse_verify_frame, format_response, detector_check_end, two_tx_*). The production symbols MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_crc8 / _process_buffer / _build_response / _rx_byte / is_valid_legacy_command are never called. Zero real coverage of this module.
findings.impact: The CRC-8 algorithm, the frame length/bounds validation, the A+/legacy/0xFF discrimination, and the byte-streaming state machine are all completely untested against the real code. A regression in any of them (e.g. the off-by-one CRC window, the rx_byte dead path) ships undetected. For an SPI-host build this is the integrity layer.
findings.recommendation: Add a real test that includes mgr_spi_protocol.c (with HAL/MGR_LOG mocks): known-vector CRC-8(0x07) check; process_buffer on valid A+ frame (CRC OK + CRC bad), too-short frame, data_len>SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA, legacy byte, 0xFF sync, 0x00 garbage; build_response round-trip (parse what you build); and the full rx_byte streaming path (currently 0% covered).

findings.location: mgr_spi_protocol.c:91-204 (MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_rx_byte) and the states it exclusively drives
findings.description: MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_rx_byte has no caller anywhere in the tree (grep: only its own definition + prototype). The live RX path is the whole-buffer parser MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_process_buffer (called from mgr_spi_cmd.c:122). Because of that, the per-byte state machine states SPI_PROT_RX_HEADER, SPI_PROT_RX_DATA and SPI_PROT_RX_CRC are only ever entered by rx_byte and are therefore dead too. protocol_parse_header() (line 78) is reachable only from rx_byte and is likewise dead. This is a genuine orphan, not config-gated: it is dead in ALL configs that compile the file.
findings.impact: ~110 lines of unreachable, unmaintained, untested parser logic that duplicates process_buffer with subtly different behaviour (see the rx_byte data-loss and missing-magic-in-CRC findings). It rots and invites a future caller to wire up a buggy path.
findings.recommendation: Either delete rx_byte + protocol_parse_header + the three RX_* states, or document them as a deliberately-retained alternate API and add a unit test pinning their behaviour. Do not leave a second, divergent parser silently dead.

findings.description: In the per-byte data state, if rx_index has reached SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA the incoming byte is silently dropped (line 149 guard) but rx_index is NOT incremented, so the loop-exit test 'rx_index >= data_len' (line 152) can never be satisfied for data_len > SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA. data_len is a uint8_t (max 255) and SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA is 250, so a frame claiming 251..255 data bytes would wedge the parser in RX_DATA forever (no progress, never reaches CRC). Note rx_byte never validates data_len against SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA before entering RX_DATA (unlike process_buffer at line 131 which does), so 251..255 is reachable here.
findings.impact: Hang/lock of the byte-stream parser on a crafted/corrupt length field. Currently masked because rx_byte is dead code, but it is a latent brick if anyone wires rx_byte to the driver. High-severity pattern (unbounded no-progress) downgraded to medium only because unreachable today.
findings.recommendation: If rx_byte is kept: validate data_len <= SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA on header completion (it already does at 131 — but RX_DATA must also advance or abort when the guard drops a byte). Simplest: clamp the loop on min(data_len, SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA) or transition to ERROR if data_len > SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA. If rx_byte is deleted, this finding is moot.

findings.location: mgr_spi_protocol.c:157-189 vs 161-173 (rx_byte CRC) compared to 346-352 (process_buffer CRC)
findings.description: The dead rx_byte CRC path rebuilds a temporary crc_buf with the magic byte at [0] and computes CRC over '4 + data_len' — consistent with process_buffer. So the two parsers do agree on the CRC window (magic included). Worth noting only that rx_byte allocates 'uint8_t crc_buf[SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA + 4]' (254 bytes) on the stack inside the switch case each call; process_buffer computes in place with no copy. The stack copy is wasteful but bounded.
findings.impact: 254-byte transient stack frame in a function that, if ever made live, runs in the SPI command context. Not a current risk (dead), and within budget even if live, but it is an avoidable copy of the whole payload purely to prepend one magic byte.
findings.recommendation: If rx_byte is retained, drop the crc_buf copy: CRC the stored header fields incrementally, or keep the received bytes contiguous as process_buffer does and CRC in place.

findings.description: build_response takes data_len as uint8_t (0..255) and does NO bounds check before memcpy(&tx_buf[index], data, data_len) and the trailing CRC write. It trusts every caller to (a) cap data_len at SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA and (b) supply a tx_buf large enough for 4+data_len+1 bytes. Callers do currently respect this (mgr_spi_cmd_common.c:130-133 clamps payload to SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA before calling; mgr_spi_cmd.c:137 uses error_response[8] only for data_len=0). But the function itself is an unguarded fixed-buffer writer reachable with attacker-influenced sizes if any future handler forgets to clamp. Worst case: data_len=255 writes 260 bytes; tx_buf is spiTxBuf[256] (TXBUF_SIZE) so 260>256 overflows the global TX buffer by 4 bytes.
findings.impact: Latent buffer overflow of the global spiTxBuf if a handler ever passes an unclamped uint8_t length. Low today because all live callers clamp, but the contract is implicit and undocumented in the signature. SPI-host builds only.
findings.recommendation: Defensively clamp inside build_response: if (data_len > SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA) data_len = SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA; (and ideally take a tx_buf_size param). Add a _Static_assert that TXBUF_SIZE >= SPI_FRAME_MAX_SIZE so the layout invariant is compile-time enforced.

findings.description: The parser accepts data_len up to SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA (250) and validates the buffer holds header+data+CRC. But the real SPI driver uses a FIXED transaction of SPI_TRANSACTION_SIZE=64 bytes (mcu_spi_driver.h:38); MCU_SPI_DRIVER_set_response rejects len>64. So any A+ request/response with data_len greater than ~59 is structurally impossible over the wire yet silently 'accepted' by this layer. The 250 limit is internally consistent (buffers are 256) but inconsistent with the transport, masking the true 64-byte ceiling.
findings.impact: No overflow (250<256), but a confusing/over-permissive contract: a frame this layer calls 'valid' can never be transmitted, and build_response can produce a frame set_response will then reject. Purely a correctness/clarity gap on SPI-host builds, not the sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Either bound SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA (or an effective max) to SPI_TRANSACTION_SIZE - SPI_FRAME_MIN_SIZE and reject longer frames at parse time, or add a comment + _Static_assert tying the two so the relationship is explicit. Mirrors the manual clamp already done in mgr_spi_cmd_list_general.c:130-131.

findings.description: spi_protocol_ctx and header_buf/header_index are plain (non-volatile) globals mutated by the parser. In the live design they are touched only from the main-loop SPICMD state handler (mgr_spi_cmd.c) and the SPI RX is DMA into a separate driver buffer, so there is no ISR writing these — single-threaded, no race. This is acceptable. Flagging only that header_index is reset in three different entry points (init:45, rx_byte IDLE:95, process_buffer:289, reset:259) — easy to desync if a future ISR-driven byte path is added.
findings.impact: None today (no concurrent writer). Becomes a real race only if rx_byte is ever driven from the SPI RX ISR. Documenting the invariant prevents that mistake.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment that this context is main-loop-only and must not be mutated from ISR context, or guard with SPI_ENTER/EXIT_CRITICAL if a byte-ISR path is introduced.

findings.description: Magic number 4 is used repeatedly for the header-length-without-CRC in CRC computations (crc_len = 4 + data_len; crc8 over '4 + data_len'); SPI_FRAME_HEADER_SIZE (==4) exists and is used elsewhere (327, 343) but not here, so a future change to the header size would silently break only the CRC windows. Also build_response (234) checks data!=NULL after data_len>0, whereas build_error_response passes NULL/0; consistent, just noting the implicit contract.
findings.impact: Maintainability only. A header-size change would desync CRC vs framing in three spots.
findings.recommendation: Replace the literal 4 in the three CRC-length expressions with SPI_FRAME_HEADER_SIZE.

findings.description: Several declared-but-unused members: SpiProtocolContext.last_sequence is written nowhere and read nowhere; the embedded SpiResponseFrame 'response' member (ctx.response) is never used (responses are built directly into the driver tx_buf, not this struct). MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_get_stats reports seq_error_count which is never incremented anywhere in this file (no sequence-number validation is actually performed despite SPI_PROT_STATUS_SEQ_ERROR / seq_error_count existing).
findings.impact: Dead struct fields waste ~260 bytes of static RAM (the unused SpiResponseFrame.data[250] inside the global ctx) on SPI-host builds, and get_stats advertises a SEQ-error metric that is structurally always 0 (misleading diagnostics).
findings.recommendation: Remove ctx.response (saves 250+ bytes static) and last_sequence, or implement the sequence-tracking they imply. Either drop the SEQ stat from get_stats or wire actual sequence-continuity checking that increments seq_error_count.

dead_code: GENUINE ORPHANS (dead in all configs that compile this file): (1) MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_rx_byte (91-204) — no caller; the live path is process_buffer. (2) protocol_parse_header (78-89) — only called by rx_byte. (3) Parser states SPI_PROT_RX_HEADER/RX_DATA/RX_CRC — only entered by rx_byte. CONFIG-GATED dead: the entire file is dead in the sealed deployment (COMM=UART) — it is built only under -DUSE_SPI_DRIVER. UNUSED DATA: SpiProtocolContext.last_sequence and the embedded SpiResponseFrame 'response' member are never read/written; seq_error_count is reported but never incremented. MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_get_stats and MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_crc8 (as a public symbol) are referenced only internally — get_stats has no external caller found (potential orphan, lower confidence).
test_coverage: FAILS its own intent. Tests/unit/test_spi_protocol.c does not link this .c file — it tests local mock copies instead, so real coverage is 0%. Concrete gaps that need real tests against this module: (a) MGR_SPI_PROTOCOL_crc8 against known CCITT-0x07 vectors; (b) process_buffer: valid A+ frame (CRC ok/bad), length>SPI_FRAME_MAX_DATA rejection (line 319), too-short (<MIN_SIZE, line 301), incomplete (line 328), legacy byte, 0xFF sync, 0x00 error; (c) build_response/build_error_response round-trip and the implicit data_len<=250 / tx_buf>=255 bounds; (d) the entire rx_byte streaming state machine (incl. the RX_DATA no-progress hang on data_len 251..255) — currently untested. This is testable pure logic (no HW dependency beyond MGR_LOG mocks), so the gaps are fully closable in Tests/unit.

role: Salt-Water-Switch manager: 5-level adaptive underwater/surface detector driving PA12 sensor power + PA11/ADC_IN7, with baseline EMA calibration, sensor-fault detection, dive-timeout/degraded-beacon backstop, and LPM GPIO park/restore.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER (BOARD=SMD_STDALONE, COMM=UART) — the sealed-deploy target. Called from kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2014 main loop and the AT handler in mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c; GPIO park/restore from mgr_lpm_uw.c. Not compiled for STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER (no callers there).

findings.description: The unit tests do NOT compile/link the real mgr_sws.c. They re-implement ("extracted"/"mirrors") the detection math as a parallel copy: test_sws.c:53 'FUNCTIONS UNDER TEST (extracted from mgr_sws.c)', test_sws_l4_guards.c:20 'mirroring mgr_sws.c', and constants are hand-copied (test_sws.c:36 even warns 'a drift here means the tests validate a different algorithm'). So detector_state(), the L2/L3 trend state machine, the observed_peak anti-spike block (sec 6b), the coherence recalib (lines 639-658), the dive-timeout escalation (sec 7) and degraded-beacon (sec 9) are validated only against a hand-maintained twin that can silently diverge from the shipped code.
findings.impact: On the sealed 12-month deployment, a regression in the real mgr_sws.c (e.g. an off-by-one in the L4 debounce or a sign error in a drop %) would pass CI because CI runs the mirror, not the firmware. Tests give false confidence on the single most safety-relevant state machine (false-surface = spurious TX = battery drain; false-underwater = no beacon = lost tag).
findings.recommendation: Refactor detector_state() to take its ADC input via a seam (function pointer or weak sws_read_adc) and link the actual mgr_sws.c translation unit into the test target so the deployed algorithm is exercised. At minimum, add a build assertion / generation step that fails if the mirrored constants drift.

findings.description: Continuous-coherence counter reset is over-eager. coherence_high_count is reset to 0 whenever the current raw is NOT > water_baseline*2 (else branch line 635-636) or when calib_incoherent is true. COHERENCE_HIGH_REQUIRED=3 therefore needs 3 strictly-consecutive >2x samples with zero tolerance, unlike the L3 trend which deliberately tolerates one flat/up dip (line 745 decrements instead of resetting).
findings.impact: A genuine salinity ramp / deployment move that the slow EMA should catch via the fast coherence path can be repeatedly denied if readings are noisy (one sub-2x dip zeroes the 3-streak), leaving a stale water_baseline and degraded threshold longer than intended. Not a brick, but weakens one of the documented hardening features on the sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Match the L3 pattern: decrement (tolerate one) instead of hard-reset, or document that strict consecutiveness is intended.

findings.description: surface_lockout_ms = sws_config.min_surface_time_s * 1000 (line 1011) and window_ms = (uint32_t)max_dive_time_s * 1000u (line 1077) multiply uint32 seconds by 1000 with no upper bound. MGR_SWS_setConfig validates ordering/zero but never caps min_surface_time_s or max_dive_time_s, so an AT-set value > ~4.29e6 s wraps the ms product. max_dive_time_s is auto-healed only when 0 (line 1277).
findings.impact: An out-of-range config (operator typo over AT) silently produces a tiny or huge lockout/degraded window instead of being rejected. Default config is safe (10 s / 7200 s). Low likelihood on a sealed unit (config frozen pre-seal) but a robustness gap in the setter.
findings.recommendation: Add upper-bound validation in MGR_SWS_setConfig (e.g. reject min_surface_time_s > 86400 and max_dive_time_s > 86400) so the ms math can't wrap.

findings.description: sws_read_adc() busy-waits `count = sample_delay_us * 8; while(count--) __NOP();` with the SWS rail (PA12) driven HIGH the whole time. The 'x8 NOP per us at 32MHz' comment is an open-loop approximation; the project's clock paths include lower MSI/HSE configs (system_stm32wlxx.c shows 4 MHz MSI at startup, 32 MHz HSE), so the real delay scales with whatever HCLK is active and is not anchored to a timer. At the 10 ms ceiling this spins ~80k NOPs with the sensor energized, blocking the main loop.
findings.impact: Two concerns: (1) the discrimination delay is clock-coupled — if HCLK differs from the assumed 32 MHz the RC charge window is wrong, mis-reading water as air or vice-versa (the exact failure the ceiling was raised to fix); (2) it is a CPU busy-wait (no WFI) holding the electrode powered, contrary to the CLAUDE.md 'lowest consumption / no busy-wait' rule. Up to ~80k cycles per sample, every 0.5–1 s while monitoring.
findings.recommendation: Anchor the delay to a HW timer / DWT cycle counter scaled by SystemCoreClock instead of a fixed NOP multiplier, and/or document that SWS sampling assumes the 32 MHz HSE domain so the RC charge time stays correct across clock configs.

findings.description: MGR_SWS_enterLowPower()/exitLowPower() only re-mode PA12 (sensor power). The PA11 ADC analog pin and the ADC peripheral clock are managed by the ADC driver's MspInit/DeInit (adc.c). Nothing in this file asserts that the ADC clock is gated or PA11 left ANALOG when SWS parks for STOP — the coupling is implicit across modules.
findings.impact: No defect today (PA11 ANALOG = no leakage, STOP gates the ADC clock at the bus level), but the SWS park path does not verify PA11/ADC state, so a future ADC-driver change could leave the ADC clocked in STOP without this module noticing. Maintainability note for the sealed target.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment in enterLowPower() noting PA11/ADC low-power state is owned by adc.c MspDeInit, so the cross-module coupling is explicit.

findings.description: prev_raw is refreshed to the current raw on EVERY detector_state() call (line 663) but is NOT reset on the SURFACE->UNDERWATER transition (only consecutive_raw_drops/drop_reference are, lines 1224-1225). On the first detector_state() of a new dive, saved_prev_raw still holds the last SURFACE-state raw, so L1/L2 would compare an underwater raw against a stale surface raw. The is_underwater && saved_prev_raw>0 && time_in_state>=OVERRIDE_MIN_TIME_SEC guard (line 682-683) suppresses acting on it for the first second, by which time prev_raw has refreshed — so it is masked today.
findings.impact: No observable misbehaviour because the 1 s gate suppresses the first-second comparisons. Flagged because the cross-state prev_raw carry is non-obvious and reducing OVERRIDE_MIN_TIME_SEC to 0 would expose a spurious L1/L2 surface trigger right at dive entry.
findings.recommendation: Reset prev_raw (and drop_reference) on the SURFACE->UNDERWATER transition alongside the other L1/L2 state (lines 1222-1231) to make the masking explicit and robust to gate changes.

findings.description: last_measurement_tick==0 is overloaded as a 'never measured' sentinel: MGR_SWS_msUntilNextSample returns 0 (due now) when it is 0 (line 304-305) and MGR_SWS_task force-samples when it is 0 (line 1193 guard `last_measurement_tick != 0`). HAL_GetTick() legitimately returns 0 for the first 1 ms after reset and once per 49.7-day wrap; on that single tick the just-stored value becomes 0 and the next call treats it as 'never measured'.
findings.impact: Cosmetic: at most one extra SWS sample in the first millisecond after init or once every 49.7 days. No corruption, no hang. Listed because the file otherwise went to lengths to be tick-wrap-safe (lines 211-216, 232).
findings.recommendation: Use a separate `bool measured_once` flag instead of the 0 sentinel, or accept and document the 1-sample cosmetic edge.

findings.description: MGR_SWS_getSampleDelayUs() has no live caller (repo-wide search: only its definition and prototype appear). The code comment already labels it an 'Unwired diagnostic hook'. Intentional, documented orphan (future AT status readout), not config-gated dead code.
findings.impact: None functional; negligible code-size. Honest, already-annotated dead code.
findings.recommendation: Keep as-is (annotated) or wire it into AT+STATUS. No action required.

findings.description: Verified the NO_VARIANCE math is bounds-safe: d = adc-mean with both <=4095 gives |d|<=4095, d*d<=~16.8M, summed over 30 samples => max ~5e8, within uint32; division by SWS_FAULT_VAR_WINDOW (compile-time 30, non-zero) is safe. No overflow / no div-by-zero.
findings.impact: None — the fault-detector integer math is sound. Included to explicitly clear it rather than leave it unexamined.
findings.recommendation: No change.

dead_code: One intentional, annotated orphan: MGR_SWS_getSampleDelayUs() (lines 1306-1309) — no caller anywhere in the repo, self-documented as a future AT-status hook; not config-gated. All other public functions have live callers (kns_app_uw_doppler.c, mgr_lpm_uw.c, mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c, mgr_nvm.c). No unreachable branches inside detector_state(): every level/guard is reachable for some ADC/state combination. The whole file is inert for APP!=UW_DOPPLER, but that is config-gating (UW_DOPPLER is #error-restricted to SMD_STDALONE), not orphaning.
test_coverage: Testable logic (threshold math, MA filter, L1-L5, lockout, dive-timeout, degraded beacon, fault detector) is NOMINALLY covered by Tests/unit/test_sws.c, test_sws_l4_guards.c, test_sws_degraded.c — BUT those tests compile a hand-copied MIRROR of the algorithm, not the real mgr_sws.c (test_sws.c:53 'extracted', l4_guards:20 'mirroring', constants duplicated). So coverage of the SHIPPED translation unit is effectively zero; CI cannot catch a regression in mgr_sws.c itself. Concretely untested against real code: sec 6b observed_peak anti-spike/decay/coherence (lines 933-988), coherence recalib (639-658), sec 7 escalation + degraded entry (1018-1063), and MGR_SWS_setConfig validation (1254-1288). This is the top gap (see high finding).

role: Persistent TX health counters (attempts/done/timeouts/errors + failure streak) in SRAM2 retention, validated by magic+CRC32, surfaced via AT+TXSTATS.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER (BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART). Only kns_app_uw_doppler.c and the UW_DOPPLER AT-cmd list call these symbols; under STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER the TU compiles but every public function is unreferenced (linker garbage-collects). Effectively UW_DOPPLER-only.

findings.description: The retention struct 'stats' is shared, mutating state with no critical-section protection. All record*/get/clear writers and stats_commit run unguarded. This is SAFE in the current build because every caller (process_mac_events KNS_Q_pop loop at kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1428-1559, recordAttempt at :2635, and the AT+TXSTATS get/clear at mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c:1018/1029) executes in the single baremetal main loop — no ISR touches it. The invariant is undocumented though: nothing in the file states 'main-loop-only, not ISR-safe'.
findings.impact: No defect today. Latent: if any future code calls a record*() from an ISR/callback (e.g. a MAC done-callback), a get() during a partial multi-field update (recordTimeout writes timeouts, then consecutive_fail/worst_consecutive, then crc) could read a torn snapshot or race the commit. Not a sealed-deploy brick.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment asserting 'callers must be main-loop context (not ISR-safe)' to lock the invariant, matching the header's stated hook points.

findings.description: stats_commit() is called on every single counter bump (recordAttempt/Done/Timeout/Error). Each commit recomputes a bytewise CRC32 over the 28-byte image (txs_crc32, :25-35: 28*8 = 224 iterations of the inner loop). This is correct but the per-event CRC is pure overhead vs. correctness benefit: the struct lives in volatile SRAM2 retention (not flash), so there is no wear concern and no torn-write-to-NVM concern — the CRC only guards against an external section wipe (Sram2_Init) or SEU, which a commit-on-every-bump does not improve over commit-once.
findings.impact: Negligible CPU/power cost (~sub-microsecond per TX event, TX is infrequent). No functional bug. Noted for completeness; not worth changing.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is, or document that per-bump commit is for crash-window consistency. No action required.

findings.description: txs_crc32() is a verbatim third copy of the CRC-32/MPEG-2 routine (also in MGR_RATE rate_crc32 at mgr_rate.c:41-56 and referenced as 'same routine as MGR_NVM'). Three independent hand-rolled copies of the same polynomial loop. The comment at :24 claims consistency 'for consistency' but consistency is by convention, not by shared code — a fix to one (e.g. an endianness or init-value change) would silently diverge.
findings.impact: Maintenance hazard only; all three are currently byte-identical in behavior. No runtime defect.
findings.recommendation: Optionally factor the CRC-32/MPEG-2 routine into a shared util (e.g. MGR_CRC) used by NVM/RATE/TXSTATS. The existing Tests/unit/test_crc32.c already pins the expected polynomial/vectors.

findings.location: mgr_txstats.c (whole file); Tests/unit/ has no test_txstats.c
findings.description: No unit test exists for MGR_TXSTATS (confirmed: Tests/unit/ has no txstats file). The module has genuinely testable, HW-free logic: (a) saturating increment at 0xFFFFFFFF (inc_saturating :70-73), (b) failure-streak bump + worst-ever tracking (bump_fail_streak :77-82), (c) consecutive_fail reset on recordDone (:93), (d) magic+CRC validation / first-boot zeroing path (stats_valid/init :48-68), (e) get() NULL-guard (:113), (f) clear() resetting s but re-committing magic/crc (:117-122). None of these are exercised. Project rule (CLAUDE.md) requires a unit test for every new logic module.
findings.impact: Regressions in streak accounting or CRC validation (which gate sealed-deploy health telemetry) would ship undetected. The counters are the operator's only pre-shutdown radio-health signal (header :8-9).
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_txstats.c: mock MGR_LOG, drive record* sequences, assert counters/streak/worst, assert saturation, and assert that a corrupted magic/crc triggers zeroing in init().

findings.description: Semantic edge case (documented, not a bug): worst_consecutive only updates inside bump_fail_streak (:80-82), so it tracks the worst COMPLETED-or-current failure streak. consecutive_fail is reset to 0 on recordDone (:93) but worst_consecutive is correctly preserved — verified correct. Separately, the header (:7-8) claims counters 'survive brown-out resets', but the .c comment (:13-16) correctly states .retentionRamBss is re-zeroed by Sram2_Init on BOR/NRST(PIN)/OBL and is 'NOT brownout-persistent'. The two docstrings contradict each other on brown-out survival.
findings.impact: No runtime defect — code behavior matches the .c comment (counters DO reset on BOR via Sram2_Init + magic/CRC mismatch). But the header misleads the operator into believing post-brownout counters are valid history when they may have been zeroed.
findings.recommendation: Fix the header comment (mgr_txstats.h:7) to match reality: counters survive SFT/IWDG software resets but are re-zeroed on BOR/NRST-pin/OBL (Sram2_Init re-runs), and lost on SHUTDOWN/VBAT-loss.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. txs_crc32/stats_crc/stats_commit/stats_valid/inc_saturating/bump_fail_streak are all reachable from the public API. All 8 public functions have live callers under APP=UW_DOPPLER (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1463/1502/1540/1667/2635 and mgr_at_cmd_list_uw_doppler.c:1018/1029). Under non-UW_DOPPLER configs the entire TU's public symbols are unreferenced and removed by --gc-sections — this is config-gated dead code, not an orphan (the module is intentionally UW_DOPPLER-scoped). No unused statics, params, or ignored returns; all functions are void or their returns are consumed.
test_coverage: Testable logic is NOT covered — there is no Tests/unit/test_txstats.c. Concrete uncovered logic: saturating increment ceiling (inc_saturating :72), failure-streak + worst-ever tracking (bump_fail_streak :80-82), streak reset on DONE (:93), magic+CRC first-boot/corruption zeroing (stats_valid/init :48-68), get() NULL-guard (:113), clear() (:119-120). The CRC routine itself is indirectly pinned by Tests/unit/test_crc32.c (same polynomial 0x04C11DB7) but txs_crc32's offsetof-bounded coverage of the struct is untested.

role: IWDG watchdog manager via direct register access: ensures the IWDG_STOP option byte is FREEZE (OB program + reset), arms a ~16s IWDG, refreshes it, and provides a WDG-kicking blocking delay.
compiled_in: all (no APP/BOARD/COMM guards in the file; MGR_WDG_* called from the UW_DOPPLER app path — sealed deployment config APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART uses all of init/refresh/ensureIwdgStopOptionByte; delayWithKick's only caller is compiled out by default)

findings.description: MGR_WDG_delayWithKick() is reachable only from the TCXO pre-warmup block, which is wrapped in `#if UW_DOPPLER_PREWARM_TCXO` and that macro defaults to 0 (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2557-2559). No other caller exists anywhere in the tree (grep confirms only the gated site + docs). So in every default build, including the sealed UW_DOPPLER target, this function is dead code linked but never invoked.
findings.impact: No runtime effect in the sealed deployment; the chunked-kick logic it implements (the protection it was written to provide) never runs. Latent: if someone flips the pre-warm flag, the function's unverified math (below) suddenly becomes live on the surface->TX critical path.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the function and its header decl, or add a unit test and a comment that its sole caller is compile-gated off by default. Mark as intentionally-config-gated (orphan-pending) so it isn't mistaken for live code.

findings.description: Comment-rot / spec mismatch in MGR_WDG_delayWithKick. The header doc says "The watchdog is refreshed every ~1 s" then immediately "Granularity is 50 ms (the inner HAL_Delay step)" and "callers asking for shorter waits should still use HAL_Delay". The implementation uses a 1000 ms chunk (`chunk = remaining > 1000 ? 1000 : remaining`, line 188) and HAL_Delay(chunk) — there is no 50 ms inner step. The 50 ms claim is stale from an earlier implementation.
findings.impact: Misleading contract for any future caller (the function is currently dead). A caller trusting the 50 ms granularity note would pick the wrong API.
findings.recommendation: Update the header doc to match the 1000 ms chunk granularity (or restore 50 ms chunking if fine-grained kicking was the intent).

findings.description: In MGR_WDG_delayWithKick the loop recomputes `elapsed` and `remaining` but the `while` condition already guarantees `(HAL_GetTick()-start) < total_ms`, so the inner `(elapsed < total_ms)` ternary (line 187) can only ever take the true branch; the `: 0` arm is unreachable. Minor redundancy, not a bug (HAL_GetTick wrap is handled correctly by unsigned subtraction).
findings.impact: None functional. Slight dead-branch noise.
findings.recommendation: Simplify: `remaining = total_ms - elapsed;` (unsigned, condition already holds). Low priority.

findings.description: Header doc-rot: the @return note for MGR_WDG_ensureIwdgStopOptionByte says failures are "logged via MGR_LOG_DEBUG", but the implementation logs via MGR_LOG_ERR / MGR_LOG_WARN / MGR_LOG_INFO (mgr_wdg.c:78,82,87,91,102). MGR_LOG_DEBUG is also a compile-time no-op when DEBUG=0, which would imply silence in production — the actual code uses MGR_LOG_ERR which is emitted in production (LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL=ERROR). The doc understates production logging.
findings.impact: Documentation only; could mislead someone debugging a commissioning failure into thinking these logs are DEBUG-gated and absent in a production binary, when they are in fact ERROR/WARN and visible.
findings.recommendation: Update the doc to reference MGR_LOG_ERR/WARN/INFO and note they are emitted in production builds.

findings.description: Wrong reference-manual citation. The file header (line 15) and MGR_WDG_init comment (line 136) cite "RM0461" for the IWDG init sequence. RM0461 is the STM32WLE5/WL5x... no — RM0461 is the STM32U0 reference manual; the STM32WL55 reference manual is RM0453 (correctly cited elsewhere in this same file at lines 63 and 161). The init sequence is generic so the code is correct, but the citation is wrong.
findings.impact: None functional. A maintainer cross-checking the IWDG sequence against RM0461 would be looking in the wrong document.
findings.recommendation: Change RM0461 -> RM0453 in the two comments to match the rest of the file.

findings.description: Header summary comment claims the IWDG_STOP option byte "should be set (default on STM32WL) so the watchdog is frozen during STOP mode". The entire existence and commit history of MGR_WDG_ensureIwdgStopOptionByte() (and the B4 regression fix) establishes that on a FRESH chip the bit is 1 = RUN (counting in STOP), i.e. NOT frozen by default — that is precisely the brick this module exists to prevent. The header's "default = frozen" statement contradicts the .c body comments (lines 63-70, 121-129) and is the original inverted-polarity assumption that caused the prior cold-boot-loop bug.
findings.impact: Documentation contradiction on a safety-critical invariant. A reader trusting the header could conclude the OB-ensure step is unnecessary and remove it, reintroducing the STOP2 reboot-loop brick on sealed units.
findings.recommendation: Fix the header summary to state that a fresh STM32WL ships with IWDG_STOP=1 (RUN-in-STOP) and that this module forces it to FREEZE; align it with the corrected polarity notes in the .c.

findings.description: The SR update-complete wait is bounded by an iteration count (`timeout = 100000U`), not by time. The comment claims "timeout ~100ms" but the real wall-clock duration of 100000 empty-body loop iterations depends entirely on CPU clock and compiler optimization of the `while (IWDG->SR != 0U && --timeout > 0U)` body. At 48 MHz this is far under 100 ms; under -O0 or a slower clock it differs. PVU/RVU normally clear within a few LSI cycles (sub-ms) so the loop almost never spins long, but the comment is misleading and the bound is not deterministic across build configs.
findings.impact: Low: PR/RLR write completes quickly in practice; on timeout the code only WARNs and proceeds (still refreshes), so no hang. But a wedged SR (e.g. LSI not ready) would still arm the IWDG with possibly-unwritten PR/RLR — defaulting to a SHORTER timeout (PR resets to 0 => /4 => much faster reset) on a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Bound the wait by HAL_GetTick() delta (e.g. 5 ms) for determinism, and on timeout consider not relying on the partially-written prescaler. Add a unit test for the SR-timeout branch.

findings.description: wdg_vdd_safe_for_ob() is a near-verbatim copy of main.c:vdd_safe_for_ob_program() — same PVDLEVEL_3, same `for (volatile uint32_t i=0; i<4000u; i++) __NOP();` settling magic number, same PVDO read. Two independent copies of a safety gate (PVD comparator settle time) that must stay in lock-step. The 4000-iteration settle is an undocumented magic number whose real settle-vs-CPU-clock margin is unverified in both copies.
findings.impact: Maintenance hazard: a fix to the PVD settle time or level in one copy won't propagate to the other; the two OB-program gates could diverge and one could pass on a marginal supply the other rejects.
findings.recommendation: Factor the VDD-safe-for-OB check into one shared helper (e.g. in mcu_misc or a pwr util) and call it from both main.c and mgr_wdg.c. Document the 4000-iteration settle basis (or switch to a time-based settle).

findings.description: IWDG timeout math (16 s) is computed against LSI nominal 32 kHz, but the WL55 datasheet (DS13105 line 6080-6082) specifies fLSI 31.04 kHz min over the full -40..125 C / 1.8..3.6 V range. At the low-frequency corner the real timeout stretches (~16.5 s) — safe direction. The concern is the high-frequency corner: a faster LSI shortens the window below 16 s, reducing margin for the longest legitimately-blocking CPU-active op between kicks. Not a defect (the design refreshes well inside the window), but the comment presents 16 s as exact when it is +/- a few percent over temperature.
findings.impact: None expected in the sealed deployment given frequent refreshes; worth noting only if a future code path approaches the 16 s budget on a hot/cold unit.
findings.recommendation: Note the LSI tolerance in the comment (effective window ~15.5..16.5 s) so future budget calculations use the worst-case short side.

findings.description: The unit test mirrors only the ensureIwdgStopOptionByte() decision tree and the MGR_WDG_init() arm-gate boolean. Untested logic: (a) the SR-update wait/timeout branch in MGR_WDG_init (lines 150-156), (b) the entire MGR_WDG_delayWithKick chunking + HAL_GetTick-wrap-safe loop (lines 178-192) — which is also the dead function, so it ships completely unverified, and (c) the VDD-gate deferral path of ensure (wdg_vdd_safe_for_ob -> early return false at line 77-80) is not mirrored in the test's `ensure_optionbyte` mock.
findings.impact: The delayWithKick math (chunk clamping, remaining computation, wrap handling) is the kind of code that breaks subtly; it would go live with zero coverage if pre-warm is enabled. The VDD-deferral branch is a sealed-deployment safety path with no host test.
findings.recommendation: Add a host test for the delayWithKick chunk/remaining/wrap logic (mock HAL_GetTick to advance and to wrap near UINT32_MAX) and a test mirroring the VDD-deferral early-return in the ensure decision tree.

dead_code: MGR_WDG_delayWithKick (mgr_wdg.c:178-192) is dead in all default builds: its sole caller (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2579) is inside `#if UW_DOPPLER_PREWARM_TCXO`, and that macro defaults to 0 (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:2557-2559). No other caller in the tree. This is config-gated dead code (not an orphan — it has a guarded caller), but the gate is off by default so it never runs in the sealed UW_DOPPLER target. Inside MGR_WDG_delayWithKick, the `: 0` arm of the `remaining` ternary (line 187) is an unreachable branch given the `while` condition. Everything else (init/refresh/ensureIwdgStopOptionByte, the VDD gate, the PVD settle loop) is live in the sealed config. No unused statics or params.
test_coverage: Partially covered. Tests/unit/test_iwdg_optionbyte.c mirrors the ensureIwdgStopOptionByte() decision tree (bit-set/clear, unlock failures, program failure, idempotency) and the MGR_WDG_init() arm-gate (FREEZE vs RUN). These mirror the LOGIC but not the actual register/HAL code (the .c is HW glue not directly compiled in tests). Gaps: (1) MGR_WDG_delayWithKick chunk/remaining/wrap logic — zero coverage (and it's the dead function); (2) the SR-update-complete timeout branch in MGR_WDG_init (lines 150-156); (3) the VDD-deferral early-return path (wdg_vdd_safe_for_ob, lines 77-80) is not represented in the test mock. The directly testable pure logic that is missing a test is (1) and (3).

role: Thin uC-dispatch shim for the AT console wrapper: includes mcu_at_console_axm0.c under #ifdef AXM0, else mcu_at_console_stm.c (the real implementation for STM32WL55). Audited the STM implementation it pulls in plus the paired header.
compiled_in: all (the file is in Makefile:217, always compiled). For our targets AXM0 is never defined, so it always includes mcu_at_console_stm.c. USE_HDA4 (default 0) is off for the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE build, so the 256-byte TX/RX buffers are used.

findings.description: MGR_LOG_pause/resume use a single boolean (log_paused, mgr_log.c:61) with NO nesting counter. MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send_dataBuf pauses logs once for the whole buffer (line 305), then in a loop calls MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send per byte (lines 311/315/317). Each MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send unconditionally calls MGR_LOG_pause() (280) and MGR_LOG_resume() (287). The inner resume() clears log_paused mid-buffer, so the 'pause once for the entire data buffer transfer' intent (comment line 302) is defeated: log flushing is re-enabled between hex bytes and a queued log line can interleave inside the '+TX=0,<hex>' response. The was_paused guard at 303/321 only protects the OUTER pause/resume, not the per-byte inner ones.
findings.impact: Corrupted AT response framing: a debug/heartbeat log line can be injected between hex nibbles of a +TX data dump. A host parser expecting a clean '+TX=0,<hexstring>\r\n' stream sees garbage and may mis-decode the transmitted Argos payload. Harmless to the chip but breaks the documented 'AT has absolute priority' contract; visible whenever UART logging is enabled (DEBUG build, or AT+UARTLOG=1 in the field).
findings.recommendation: Make MGR_LOG_pause/resume a depth counter (pause increments, resume decrements, flush gated on count>0), OR have MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send not touch pause/resume when already paused (mirror the was_paused pattern using MGR_LOG_is_paused() inside send). Add a unit test that pauses, calls send N times, and asserts still-paused.

findings.description: Every MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send call enters MGR_LOG_pause(), which busy-waits a bounded spin loop (up to 1,000,000 iterations while log_uart_busy) plus a fixed 1000-iteration __NOP() delay (mgr_log.c:469-471) on EVERY call. MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send_dataBuf issues one MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send per payload byte (up to 16 bytes for a 128-bit LDK frame, far more for HDA4 1280-bit), so a single +TX response spins the fixed NOP delay dozens of times back-to-back in the main loop.
findings.impact: Pure busy-wait CPU burn on the main loop during AT responses; the >=1000 __NOP delay is paid per byte. Not a brick, but it is wasted active-mode time/energy on a battery-critical sealed device, and it lengthens the window where the main loop is blocked (delaying SWS polling / LPM entry). Worse with HDA4.
findings.recommendation: Pause logs once around the whole dataBuf transfer (depends on fixing the counter issue above) so the per-byte spin/NOP is paid once, not per byte. Consider dropping the unconditional 1000x __NOP 'extra safety' delay (mgr_log.c:469) since HAL_UART_Transmit is already blocking and log_uart_busy already gates.

findings.description: In KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT, pu8_RxBuffer (init NULL line 113) and i16_nbRxValidChar (init 0 line 114) are computed at lines 116-117 BEFORE the RxState check, but those values are never read: the BUSY_RX branch recomputes both at lines 153-154, and the else branch (166-169) uses neither. Lines 116-117 are dead stores executed on every RX interrupt.
findings.impact: Negligible runtime cost (a subtraction and pointer arithmetic per ISR entry), but it is misleading: a reader assumes the early computation is used. No correctness impact.
findings.recommendation: Delete lines 116-117 and move the declarations/initialisation of pu8_RxBuffer and i16_nbRxValidChar into the if(rxEvtCb != NULL) block where they are actually used (153-154).

findings.description: The #ifdef AXM0 branch (line 16) includes mcu_at_console_axm0.c (line 22), but AXM0 is never defined in the build (grep: only appears in this file and generated Doxygen HTML), and the file mcu_at_console_axm0.c does not exist in the tree. Genuine config-gated dead branch; if anyone ever defines AXM0 the build breaks on a missing include. The #error guard at 17-21 only fires when AXM0 AND an STM32 macro are both set.
findings.impact: None for any shipping config (STM path at line 24 always taken). Latent footgun only: defining AXM0 yields a confusing 'file not found' rather than a clear unsupported-target message.
findings.recommendation: Either remove the AXM0 branch entirely (the axm0 source is absent), or add an explicit #error 'AXM0 console not present in this tree' so the failure mode is legible.

findings.description: No unit test exercises this file. test_at_dispatch.c only mirrors the longest-prefix-match logic of mgr_at_cmd.c, not this module. Two pieces of pure, mockable logic are untested: (1) MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send_dataBuf hex-conversion incl. the partial-byte boundaries (remainingBits >4 -> %02X, 1..4 -> %01X, 0 -> nothing; exact-multiple-of-8 case; and that pu8_hex stops one-past-end without deref when remaining==0); (2) the KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT realignment math (pu8_RxBuffPtr/RxXferCount recompute after the parser consumes data, and the overflow wrap when RxXferCount==1).
findings.impact: Off-by-one in the partial-bit hex emission or in the ISR realignment would silently corrupt TX echoes / drop AT commands in the field with no regression guard. The realign math is real-time critical (comment in mgr_at_cmd.c:78) and runs in ISR context.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit coverage: feed send_dataBuf known buffers at bitlengths {8,12,13,16,5,7,1} and assert the emitted hex string. Extract the ISR realignment arithmetic into a testable helper (or replicate it) and assert pRxBuffPtr/RxXferCount after a parser that consumes 0 / partial / all bytes, plus the RxXferCount==1 wrap.

findings.description: *huart->pRxBuffPtr = (uint8_t)(uhdata & (uint8_t)uhMask): the inner (uint8_t) cast on uhMask is redundant. huart->Mask for this ISR is at most 0x00FF (8-bit no parity) or 0x007F (7-bit); KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT is only assigned when WordLength!=9B or Parity!=NONE (line 214-217), so the 9-bit 0x01FF mask never reaches here. The cast happens to be harmless but masks intent and would silently wrong-truncate if the assignment guard ever changed.
findings.impact: None today. Style/robustness only.
findings.recommendation: Drop the inner (uint8_t) cast: write (uhdata & uhMask) and let the outer (uint8_t) cast do the truncation, matching the HAL base UART_RxISR_8BIT it is derived from.

findings.description: The ISR drains the parser with `while (rxEvtCb(pu8_RxBuffer, &i16_nbRxValidChar) == true) { }` (empty body). Loop termination relies entirely on the closed-boundary contract that the callback eventually returns false and/or strictly shrinks i16_nbRxValidChar. MGR_AT_CMD_parseStreamCb does set *pi16_nbRxValidChar = idxStart (strictly < input) before returning true (mgr_at_cmd.c:174), and returns false when no full frame remains, so it terminates. But this is an UNBOUNDED loop running in ISR context with no iteration cap; a future/alternate rxEvtCb that returns true without shrinking the count would hang the ISR forever and brick a sealed unit.
findings.impact: Currently safe given the only registered callback. Latent: any rxEvtCb that violates the shrink-or-false contract becomes an infinite loop inside the LPUART1 ISR -> watchdog reset at best, hard hang if IWDG disabled. High blast radius for a sealed deployment, low probability given the single known caller.
findings.recommendation: Add a defensive iteration cap (e.g. bounded by RxXferSize) or assert that i16_nbRxValidChar strictly decreases each pass; break out if it does not. Document the shrink-or-return-false contract at the rx_evt_cb typedef in mcu_at_console.h.

dead_code:
Dispatcher file (mcu_at_console.c): the #ifdef AXM0 include of mcu_at_console_axm0.c (line 22) is dead in every build (AXM0 never defined; the axm0 source file is absent from the tree) — config-gated dead branch, see finding. STM path (line 24) always compiled.
In the included mcu_at_console_stm.c: (a) USE_HDA4 buffer sizing (2560 B, lines 36-37) is config-gated dead for the sealed target (USE_HDA4 defaults 0 in Makefile:98). (b) Lines 116-117 are genuine dead stores (recomputed at 153-154 before use) — see finding. (c) Commented-out strlen/memset (66-83) and HAL_UART_ErrorCallback (336-340) are intentionally-disabled reference code, not orphans. No genuine orphan functions: KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT/KINEIS_UART_StartRx_IT are reached via MCU_AT_CONSOLE_register -> huart->RxISR -> HAL_UART_IRQHandler (stm32wlxx_it.c:334). Diagnostic counters g_at_isr_bytes/parse_calls/cb_null are live (consumed in kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1828-1830 heartbeat).
test_coverage: Effectively zero direct coverage. test_at_dispatch.c only mirrors mgr_at_cmd.c's prefix dispatch, not this module. Two pure/mockable logic units are untested and SHOULD be: (1) MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send_dataBuf hex emission, esp. partial-byte boundaries (remainingBits 0/1-4/5-7/8, exact-multiple-of-8); (2) the KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT realignment arithmetic (pRxBuffPtr/RxXferCount after consume-none/partial/all, and the RxXferCount==1 overflow wrap at 137-140). The vsnprintf truncation/error handling in MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send is also unit-testable. The pause/resume nesting defeat (send_dataBuf) is the highest-value missing test.

role: MCU/STM32 wrapper for the AT-command console over LPUART1: custom byte-at-a-time RX ISR that feeds a stream parser callback, plus printf-style and binary-hex TX helpers. Sealed-deploy config (UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART) uses this as the only host I/O path.
compiled_in: all (no APP/BOARD/COMM guards in this file; built whenever the AT console wrapper is linked, i.e. every config including the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART target). USE_HDA4 only swaps buffer sizes.

findings.description: The RX ISR drains the FIFO in an unbounded `while ((ISR & RXNE) != 0)` loop. With no error/overrun handling inside the loop and the RXNE bit cleared only by reading RDR, a continuous byte stream (or a stuck/noisy line that keeps RXNE asserted, e.g. ORE-driven framing storms) keeps the loop spinning in interrupt context. Error interrupts (EIE/PEIE) are enabled but ORE is never checked or cleared here, so an overrun condition is not acknowledged in this path — the generic HAL error path is bypassed because RxISR was overridden (line 216) and HAL_UART_ErrorCallback is commented out (336-340).
findings.impact: On the sealed deployment the host UART is the only input; a noisy/floating RX line or sustained garbage during a magnet/config session can pin the CPU in the ISR, starving the main loop (SWS polling, LPM entry, MAC servicing) and inflating power. No watchdog kick happens inside the ISR. Low probability in a clean bench, but a sealed unit has no recovery if it occurs.
findings.recommendation: Bound the drain loop (e.g. cap iterations to RxXferSize) and explicitly check/clear USART_ISR_ORE inside the loop; or restore a minimal HAL_UART_ErrorCallback that flushes ORE and re-arms RX instead of silently relying on the override.

findings.description: Documented overflow behaviour: when RxXferCount reaches 1 (buffer about to fill), the code resets pRxBuffPtr to the start and RxXferCount to RxXferSize, discarding the ENTIRE accumulated buffer (256 bytes) rather than the last byte or wrapping. The just-received byte at the last slot is also overwritten on the next char. The header @note and @todo acknowledge this is lossy and that a circular buffer 'may be implemented instead'.
findings.impact: If a user pastes/streams >255 bytes before a CR/LF (multiple AT commands batched, or leading garbage), the whole pending buffer including any valid in-flight AT command is dropped, so commands are silently lost with no error returned to the host. In a sealed unit during a field config session this looks like the module ignoring commands. Not a memory-safety bug (bounds are respected), but a silent data-loss correctness issue.
findings.recommendation: Implement the noted circular buffer, or at minimum emit a diagnostic counter/flag (an overflow counter alongside g_at_isr_bytes) so the host/heartbeat can observe drops instead of silent loss.

findings.description: rxEvtCb is read in ISR context without being declared volatile (static bare function pointer at line 49). It is written once in MCU_AT_CONSOLE_register (line 241) AFTER KINEIS_UART_StartRx_IT has already enabled RXNEIE (line 223). There is a window where the ISR can fire with rxEvtCb still NULL (handled, increments g_at_cb_null) — so no crash — but the ordering (enable RX interrupt, THEN set the callback) is inverted relative to intent: characters arriving in that window are accumulated but never parsed until the next char after the pointer is set. Also the non-volatile read relies on the single-store-before-use assumption holding across the compiler.
findings.impact: Benign in practice (single late store, M4 single-word access), but the register-order inversion means the first AT command(s) typed in the microscopic window between StartRx and the callback assignment could be parsed late or contribute to a g_at_cb_null bump. Mainly a latent-fragility / correctness-of-ordering concern.
findings.recommendation: Set rxEvtCb = rx_evt_cb BEFORE calling KINEIS_UART_StartRx_IT, and qualify rxEvtCb as volatile (it is shared main<->ISR).

findings.description: i16_nbRxValidChar and pu8_RxBuffer are computed at function entry (before the RxState==BUSY_RX check), but both are unconditionally recomputed inside the callback branch (lines 153-154), and the values are not used on the else/flush branch (166-169). The initial computation at 116-117 is therefore dead (its result is always overwritten before use). pu8_RxBuffer is initialised to NULL at 113 then to this dead value at 117.
findings.impact: No functional effect; minor wasted cycles in the ISR and reader confusion (the dead computation suggests the values are valid for the whole function when they are only used in one branch).
findings.recommendation: Remove the entry-point computation at lines 116-117; keep only the in-branch computation at 153-154.

findings.description: Partial-byte hex output: u16_remainingBits = u16_dataLenBit % 8 (range 0..7). The code prints two nibbles (%02X) for 5,6,7 remaining bits and one nibble (%01X) for 1..4. For 5-7 bits it prints the full byte unmasked, so bits above the valid count are emitted verbatim (no masking of the trailing byte). This matches the legacy Kineis hex-dump contract but means undefined/padding bits in the source buffer's last byte are leaked into the AT response.
findings.impact: Cosmetic/protocol: an AT data response for a non-byte-aligned length may show stale high bits in the final hex pair. No memory safety issue (the trailing byte is within the caller's buffer for all current callers in mgr_at_cmd_common.c). Could matter if a host parses the trailing nibble strictly.
findings.recommendation: If strict output is required, mask the trailing byte to the valid bit count before printing; otherwise document that the final hex pair may contain don't-care low bits.

findings.description: TX uses HAL_UART_Transmit (blocking, polling) with a fixed 500 ms timeout. The return status is ignored on both the error-message path (266) and the main response path (284). If the UART is wedged (CTS, clock, or peripheral fault), each send blocks up to 500 ms with no indication. MGR_LOG_pause() at line 280 additionally spins waiting for log_uart_busy with its own timeout before this send.
findings.impact: On a sealed unit a wedged LPUART would impose up to 500 ms blocking per AT response in the main loop, delaying SWS/LPM servicing. Bounded (won't hang forever), so low severity, but the ignored return means a persistent TX failure is invisible to the caller and not counted.
findings.recommendation: Capture the HAL_UART_Transmit return and increment a diagnostic counter (like the g_at_* counters) on non-OK, so chronic TX failure is observable; consider reducing the timeout for the response path.

findings.description: uartTxBuf (256 B, or 2560 B under USE_HDA4) and uartRxBuf (256/2560 B) are file-static. uartTxBuf is a shared scratch reused by every MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send call. All current senders run from main/task context (parser callback in the ISR only memcpys into the AT FIFO, it never calls _send), so there is no current reentrancy hazard — but MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send is NOT reentrant: a nested or ISR-context call would corrupt uartTxBuf mid-format. This invariant is undocumented.
findings.impact: No defect today (no ISR-context _send caller exists). Latent trap: any future call to MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send from an ISR or from within HAL_UART_Transmit's window would interleave on the single static buffer and produce garbled/overlapping AT output.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment stating MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send is non-reentrant / main-context-only, to prevent a future ISR-context caller.

findings.description: The header opens `extern "C" {` under #ifdef __cplusplus (line 39-41) but never closes it with a matching `}` before #endif (line 91). The closing brace is missing entirely.
findings.impact: Harmless for this C-only firmware (CLAUDE.md confirms C-only; __cplusplus never defined). But if any C++ TU ever includes this header it will fail to compile (unbalanced brace). Pure latent footgun, zero impact in current builds.
findings.recommendation: Add the matching `#ifdef __cplusplus } #endif` before the include guard's #endif, or drop the extern "C" block since the project is C-only.

findings.description: APP_UART_noteRxActivity is declared via a local `extern void` inside the ISR loop body and called on EVERY received byte. The lazy-extern (rather than including usart.h) is documented as intentional to avoid forcing usart.h on non-LPUART1 paths, but the prototype already exists in Core/Inc/usart.h:68, so the local extern duplicates it and is called per-byte in the hot ISR loop (extra function-call + HAL_GetTick store per char).
findings.impact: Negligible runtime cost; minor. The function is unconditional even when no LED/CONFIG-mode indicator is active for the current board, adding a tick write per RX byte. No correctness issue.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is; if minimizing ISR work matters, gate the call behind the LED/CONFIG feature flag or hoist it out of the per-byte loop (note once per ISR entry is sufficient for an idle/active indicator).

dead_code: No genuine orphan functions. KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT, KINEIS_UART_StartRx_IT are static and reachable via MCU_AT_CONSOLE_register (called from mgr_at_cmd.c:294). All three public APIs (register/send/send_dataBuf) have live callers. g_at_isr_bytes/g_at_parse_calls/g_at_cb_null are extern diagnostic counters referenced by the heartbeat trace in kns_app_uw_doppler.c (per file comment). Only DEAD computation: the entry-point assignment of i16_nbRxValidChar and pu8_RxBuffer at lines 116-117 (always overwritten before use — see finding). Commented-out blocks (66-83 strlen/memset alternatives; 336-340 HAL_UART_ErrorCallback) are inert comments, not compiled.
test_coverage: Partially testable, currently a gap. The pure logic worth unit-testing: (1) MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send truncation/error handling (vsnprintf >= size path, written<0 path) — no Tests/unit case observed for the wrapper; (2) MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send_dataBuf nibble/byte boundary logic (u16_dataLenBit not byte-aligned: 0,1..4,5..7 remaining bits) — the >4 vs >0 branch selection is a classic off-by-threshold area that should have a table-driven test asserting the emitted hex string for several bit lengths. The ISR (KINEIS_RxISR_8BIT) and StartRx are HW-glue (HAL register access) — hard to unit test without mocking the UART_HandleTypeDef state machine, but the buffer-pointer/overflow-reset arithmetic (lines 137-144, 161-162) is pure pointer math that COULD be exercised with a faked huart struct in Tests/unit and currently is not. Recommend adding send_dataBuf boundary tests and a faked-huart ISR pointer-accounting test.

role: SPI1 slave driver implementing a pipelined fixed-64-byte DMA transaction protocol (master command / slave responds with previous response); arms TxRx DMA, polls DMA RX counter for transaction-end via a stability timeout, sets responses, and resets/recovers the SPI peripheral.
compiled_in: COMM=SPI only (guarded by USE_SPI_DRIVER in the paired header; the whole header body is #ifdef USE_SPI_DRIVER, and kns_app.c calls the SPI state handler under #if defined(USE_SPI_DRIVER)). NOT compiled for the sealed deployment (APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART). Live only in GUI/STDLN SPI-host configurations.

findings.description: MCU_SPI_DRIVER_arm_busy() is a genuine orphan: a grep across the whole tree (*.c) shows the only occurrence is its own definition and its prototype in the header. The header documents it as 'Call this before starting long operations (like flash write)' but no caller exists (mgr_spi_cmd*.c never invokes it; the busy pattern is never armed). fill_busy_pattern() (lines 81-85) is reachable ONLY via this dead function, so it is dead too.
findings.impact: The advertised BUSY-handshake (master detects 0xBB and retries during a long flash write) is non-functional. During a long synchronous command (e.g. firmware-update flash write) the slave never arms BUSY; any master transaction in that window is missed/garbled, and the host has no protocol-level way to know the slave was busy. For an SPI-DFU host this is a latent reliability gap, not a sealed-deploy brick (SPI is excluded from the sealed target).
findings.recommendation: Either wire MCU_SPI_DRIVER_arm_busy() into MGR_SPI_CMD before long blocking handlers (flash write in mgr_spi_cmd_list_general.c) so the BUSY pattern is actually presented, or delete arm_busy()+fill_busy_pattern()+SPI_BUSY_PATTERN if the protocol no longer relies on a busy handshake. Don't ship documented-but-uncalled API.

findings.description: spi_stats (rx_count/tx_count/error_count/last_error) is a plain non-volatile struct incremented from both ISR context (HAL_SPI_TxRxCpltCallback, HAL_SPI_ErrorCallback) and main context (arm_busy/read/reset on error paths) with no critical section. The header even defines SPI_ENTER_CRITICAL/SPI_EXIT_CRITICAL (mcu_spi_driver.h:53-54) but they are never used in the .c. ++ on a 32-bit field is non-atomic on Cortex-M4 (load/modify/store) so an ISR firing between a main-loop read-modify-write loses an increment.
findings.impact: Statistics counters can drop counts under contention. These are diagnostic-only (no control flow depends on them), so the consequence is inaccurate telemetry, not a hang/brick. Worth noting because the codebase already provides the critical-section macros and silently ignores them.
findings.recommendation: Either accept the imprecision and document it, or guard the shared-counter updates with the provided SPI_ENTER_CRITICAL/EXIT macros, or split into ISR-only vs main-only counters. At minimum mark spi_stats volatile to prevent the compiler caching stale values across the ISR boundary.

findings.description: last_rx_count and expected_transfer_size are declared volatile uint16_t. On Cortex-M4 16-bit aligned accesses are atomic so this is fine, but the volatile set {startTickTimeout(u32), response_ready(bool)} is shared ISR/main without barriers. response_ready is cleared in the ISR? No — actually response_ready is only touched in main; startTickTimeout is written 0 in the ISR (line 93) and read/written in main (mgr_spi_cmd.c:224-233). u32 aligned write is atomic so no torn value, but there is no compiler barrier guaranteeing ordering between the ISR clear and the main-loop timeout arithmetic. In practice harmless (timeout is advisory logging only).
findings.impact: No functional bug today (single-word atomic accesses on M4). Flagged as a latent fragility: the timeout/stat sharing relies on aligned single-word atomicity rather than explicit synchronization, so any future widening or struct-packing could introduce a race.
findings.recommendation: Keep startTickTimeout volatile (already is) and add a short comment that ISR/main sharing relies on 32-bit aligned atomic access; do not let any shared field grow past a single word without a critical section.

findings.description: current = (remaining <= total) ? (total - remaining) : 0; silently clamps to 0 when the DMA counter reports MORE remaining than expected_transfer_size. That condition means the DMA counter is inconsistent with the saved transfer size (e.g. peripheral was re-armed/aborted out from under the poll, or expected_transfer_size desynced). The code swallows it as 'zero bytes received' with no error counter, no log, no SPICMD_ERROR transition.
findings.impact: A genuine DMA/state desync is masked as an idle line. The transaction-end detector will then never fire (current stays 0, rx_activity_detected stays false), so the host's command is silently dropped until the next clean transaction. For an SPI host this is a silent missed-command, exactly the class of 'silently corrupt/drop' the project forbids. Not reachable in the sealed (UART) target.
findings.recommendation: On the remaining>total branch, increment spi_stats.error_count and emit MGR_LOG_DEBUG so the desync is observable, and consider forcing a re-arm (abort+read) rather than reporting a phantom idle.

findings.description: RX_STABLE_TIMEOUT_MS is hard-coded to 3 ms with a comment 'At 125kHz, 64 bytes takes ~4ms'. The transaction-end heuristic assumes a fixed SPI clock and HAL_GetTick() granularity of 1 ms. If the master clocks faster the 3 ms wait is wasted latency; if the master clocks slower than ~170 kb/s effective, a legitimate inter-byte gap longer than 3 ms inside one transaction would be mis-detected as transaction-end, splitting one frame into two and corrupting the parse. The threshold is a magic number tied to an unverified master clock assumption.
findings.impact: Frame mis-segmentation if the SPI master's effective byte cadence (incl. master-side gaps) exceeds 3 ms between bytes. Produces partial frames (handled as 'Partial frame discarded' in mgr_spi_cmd.c) or CRC errors. Robustness depends on an external master timing contract that is not enforced or documented at the bus level. SPI-only, not sealed target.
findings.recommendation: Document the required minimum master clock / max inter-byte gap in the header protocol description, and/or derive the timeout from the configured SPI baud rather than a fixed 3 ms. Add a 1ms-granularity caveat: elapsed>=3 can be as little as ~2ms of real time due to tick rounding.

findings.description: arm_busy(), read(), and reset() dereference hspi_handle (->State, ->ErrorCode, ->Instance) with NO NULL check, whereas check_transaction_end() (line 241) and abort_transfer() (line 287) DO guard against hspi_handle==NULL. Inconsistent. In register() (line 300-318), the case handle==NULL && hspi_handle==NULL hits kns_assert(0) which calls Error_Handler() (halts), masking the subsequent NULL read at line 316->199. But the case handle==NULL && hspi_handle!=NULL falls through BOTH branches of the if/else-if with no assert and proceeds normally — only safe because hspi_handle was set by a prior register.
findings.impact: If MCU_SPI_DRIVER_read()/arm_busy()/reset() were ever called before a successful register (or after a register that asserted), they would dereference a NULL hspi_handle -> HardFault. Currently masked by call ordering and the assert-then-Error_Handler in register. Latent, not currently reachable.
findings.recommendation: Add a uniform `if (hspi_handle == NULL) return HAL_ERROR;` guard at the top of arm_busy/read/reset to match the existing guards in check_transaction_end/abort_transfer, so the API is defensively NULL-safe regardless of call order.

findings.description: Recovery from a non-READY SPI state is done by HAL_SPI_Abort() then manually forcing hspi_handle->State = HAL_SPI_STATE_READY. Writing the HAL state field directly bypasses HAL's own bookkeeping; if Abort failed (returns non-OK, ignored here) the peripheral may not actually be idle while the code believes it is READY and immediately arms a new DMA.
findings.impact: A failed Abort is ignored and the driver proceeds to arm a fresh TxRx DMA on a peripheral that may still have a transfer/lock pending, which HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive_DMA would reject (HAL_BUSY) — that path IS handled (ret!=HAL_OK -> SPICMD_ERROR -> reset). So self-healing eventually triggers, but via the error path rather than clean abort. Low risk, SPI-only.
findings.recommendation: Check the return of HAL_SPI_Abort(); if it fails, escalate directly to the full MCU_SPI_DRIVER_reset() path instead of forcing State=READY and hoping the next arm rejects cleanly.

findings.description: Header file banner is wrong/rotted: file is mcu_spi_driver.h but @file says 'mcu_spi_console.h' and the include guard is __MCU_SPI_CONSOLE_H. Comment-rot violates the project's naming/consistency discipline.
findings.impact: No functional impact; cosmetic/maintainability. Mismatched include guard name is harmless as long as it stays unique but is confusing.
findings.recommendation: Fix @file to mcu_spi_driver.h and rename guard to __MCU_SPI_DRIVER_H for consistency.

findings.description: Legacy compatibility shims `#define MCU_SPI_DRIVER_writeread MCU_SPI_DRIVER_read` and `#define MCU_SPI_DRIVER_check_tx_complete() (true)` are defined. A whole-tree grep shows no caller of either symbol — both are dead aliases. check_tx_complete()==(true) is a misleading stub that would always report success.
findings.impact: No functional impact (unused). Dead API surface; the always-true stub is a trap if a future caller relies on it for real completion checking.
findings.recommendation: Remove both legacy defines unless an external/host build still references them; if kept, comment why and that check_tx_complete is intentionally a no-op.

findings.description: MCU_SPI_DRIVER_check_transaction_end() contains the only non-HAL pure logic in the file (new-byte detection, stability-timeout state machine, remaining<=total clamp, reset-on-complete) and has NO unit test. Tests/unit/test_spi_protocol.c covers only the protocol/CRC layer (grep for MCU_SPI_DRIVER/check_transaction_end/expected_transfer_size returns 0 matches). The DMA counter and HAL_GetTick are trivially mockable in the existing Tests/unit harness.
findings.impact: The transaction-segmentation logic — the part most likely to mis-detect frame boundaries (see the 3ms-timeout and clamp findings) — is unverified. Regressions in the stability heuristic would only be caught on hardware.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_spi_driver.c mocking __HAL_DMA_GET_COUNTER and HAL_GetTick to cover: (a) no-activity -> returns false; (b) bytes arriving then stable >=RX_STABLE_TIMEOUT_MS -> returns true with correct count and state reset; (c) remaining>total clamp branch; (d) activity resetting the stability timer.

findings.description: TXBUF_SIZE/RXBUF_SIZE are 256 (or 2560 under USE_HDA4) but the driver only ever transfers/uses SPI_TRANSACTION_SIZE (64) bytes; fill_idle/fill_busy/set_response all operate on the first 64 bytes only. The extra 192 bytes of each static buffer are never used by this driver in the non-HDA4 build. rxBuf/txBuf .size and .next_req plumbing (SPI_Buffer) is partly vestigial here (next_req set but the driver itself does not consume rxBuf.next_req).
findings.impact: Wasted static RAM (.bss) — 384 bytes idle in the common 64-byte protocol, 4.9KB under USE_HDA4. No correctness impact. SPI-only build.
findings.recommendation: If the 64-byte fixed protocol is final, size the static buffers to SPI_TRANSACTION_SIZE (or document why the larger HDA4/legacy sizes are retained). Minor RAM saving.

dead_code: Genuine orphans (not config-gated): MCU_SPI_DRIVER_arm_busy() (mcu_spi_driver.c:126) has zero callers tree-wide; fill_busy_pattern() (:81) and the SPI_BUSY_PATTERN are reachable only through it, so all three are dead. Header legacy macros MCU_SPI_DRIVER_writeread and MCU_SPI_DRIVER_check_tx_complete() (mcu_spi_driver.h:167-168) are unused aliases. The whole file is config-gated dead for the sealed target (excluded when COMM=UART). The rx_spi_evt_cb parameter of MCU_SPI_DRIVER_register is intentionally unused ((void)-cast at :302, documented 'not used in pipelined mode').
test_coverage: Inadequate. The file's only mockable pure logic — the transaction-end stability/timeout state machine in MCU_SPI_DRIVER_check_transaction_end() — has no unit test (test_spi_protocol.c covers only the CRC/framing layer in mgr_spi_protocol.c). The remaining functions are thin HAL glue (HAL_SPI_*_DMA, abort, reset, register) that are HW-bound and reasonably left to integration tests, but the byte-count/stability heuristic should be unit-tested with mocked __HAL_DMA_GET_COUNTER + HAL_GetTick. Concrete gap: no coverage of the remaining>total clamp branch, the stability-timer reset-on-new-byte path, or the >=RX_STABLE_TIMEOUT_MS completion path.

role: Two reference example application loops driving the closed-source Kineis MAC: KNS_APP_stdln_loop (standalone self-test FSM that sends one random message and stops) and KNS_APP_gui_init/KNS_APP_gui_loop (AT/SPI-command-driven GUI app).
compiled_in: KNS_APP_stdln_loop: only when APP=STDLN (define USE_STDALONE_APP — note: NOT USE_STDLN_APP as the task brief states; that symbol does not exist anywhere in the tree). KNS_APP_gui_init/KNS_APP_gui_loop: only when APP=GUI (USE_GUI_APP). NONE of this file's functions are compiled for the sealed deployment target (APP=UW_DOPPLER, which registers KNS_APP_uw_doppler_loop instead, main.c:1038). So every finding here is non-sealed-deployment.

findings.description: In case 3, the KNS_MAC_OK / KNS_MAC_ERROR branches (where app_evt == KNS_MAC_SEND_DATA, i.e. an OK/ERROR reply to a send-data request) read srvcEvt.tx_ctxt.frm_hdlr. For a send-data reply the MAC populates the sendreply_ctxt union member (struct KNS_MAC_sendDataReply_ctxt_t { uint32_t appId; int16_t frm_hdlr; }, kns_mac_evt.h:187-193), whose frm_hdlr sits at offset +4. tx_ctxt is struct KNS_MAC_TX_cplt_ctxt_t { int16_t frm_hdlr; } at offset 0 (kns_mac_evt.h:215-217). So tx_ctxt.frm_hdlr aliases the low 16 bits of appId, not the real handler. The reference manager (mgr_at_cmd_list_user_data.c:387-407) only uses tx_ctxt.frm_hdlr on terminal TX events and uses a FIFO lookup for send-data replies, confirming tx_ctxt is the wrong member here. This is the same union-aliasing class flagged as CRITICAL #2 in commit 'Kineis v11.1.0' for AT+KMAC.
findings.impact: Debug log only: '[..] OK to send hdlr=%d' and the KNS_MAC_ERROR 'cannot send hdlr=%d' print a garbage handler value (low half of appId). No functional/control-flow effect; the value is not used to drive logic. Not in the sealed build.
findings.recommendation: Read srvcEvt.sendreply_ctxt.frm_hdlr in the app_evt==KNS_MAC_SEND_DATA OK/ERROR branches; keep tx_ctxt.frm_hdlr for KNS_MAC_TX_DONE/TIMEOUT/ABORT (lines 278/288/294) where it is correct.

findings.description: Several kns_assert() calls on error paths cause a reset/halt instead of graceful recovery: kns_assert(KNS_CFG_getRadioInfo(...)==KNS_STATUS_OK) at line 223, kns_assert(0) on unknown modulation at line 245, and kns_assert(0) in the FSM default at line 352.
