If NVM radio config is corrupt or absent, getRadioInfo fails and the device resets every pass through case 2 — a reset loop with no progress.
findings.impact: On STDLN/GUI builds with bad/unprovisioned radio config this self-test loop can reset-loop. Not in the sealed UW_DOPPLER build, so no ocean-deploy brick risk. This is reference/example code by design, but the assert-on-config-error pattern is brittle.
findings.recommendation: On STDLN/GUI these are acceptable for a reference example; if hardened, log the error and advance to the terminal idle state (case 5) instead of asserting, so a misprovisioned unit idles quietly rather than reset-looping.

findings.description: KNS_APP_stdln_stopMacPrfl is reachable only from case 3 KNS_MAC_TX_DONE (line 284), i.e. only in the STDLN build. It is functionally identical to KNS_APP_stdln_startMacPrfl except it forces init_prfl_ctxt.id = KNS_MAC_PRFL_NONE; the duplicated push/error/assert block is copy-pasted. Not dead, but redundant. The log string at line 144/151 still says 'Cannot initialize MAC protocol' / 'Initialize Kineis MAC profile' even though this function STOPS the profile — comment/log rot.
findings.impact: None functional. Minor maintainability and misleading logs.
findings.recommendation: Factor the two into one helper taking the profile id; fix the stop-path log text to say 'stop' not 'init'.

findings.description: static uint8_t state and static uint32_t seed are declared with no initializer but forced into __section__(".retentionRamData"), which is a .data2 (load-from-ROM, copied by Sram2_Init — STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:142-150) section, not .bss2. A tentative definition placed in an explicit data section relies on the toolchain emitting a zero ROM image so that state starts at 0 on cold boot. This works with current GCC but is non-obvious and fragile: an uninitialized var in a copy-initialised section reads as 'whatever ROM holds'. seed=0 as the rand_r seed also makes the 'random' payload deterministic on first boot.
findings.impact: Currently benign (GCC zero-fills, so state starts at 0 → FSM begins at case 0). If a future toolchain/linker change stopped zero-filling, state could start non-zero and hit the default kns_assert(0). seed==0 → identical first payload across boots (only a test-data concern). STDLN/GUI only.
findings.recommendation: Give explicit initializers: static uint8_t state = 0; static uint32_t seed = SOME_NONZERO; to make the cold-boot value intentional and self-documenting rather than relying on section-emit behavior.

findings.description: rand_r(((unsigned int *)&seed)) casts a uint32_t* to unsigned int*. Benign on this target (unsigned int == uint32_t, same size/alignment), but it is an implicit-type-pun via cast that MISRA-like rules discourage; if seed's type ever changed it would silently misread.
findings.impact: None on STM32WL55 (32-bit int). Portability/MISRA nit only.
findings.recommendation: Declare seed as 'unsigned int' (the exact type rand_r wants) and pass &seed without the cast.

findings.description: No unit test in Tests/unit exercises KNS_APP_stdln_loop or KNS_APP_gui_loop/gui_init (grep for the symbols returns no test references; the 'kns_app' test matches are all for kns_app_uw_doppler). The FSM state transitions, the per-modulation usrdata_bitlen mapping (case 2, lines 230-247), and the srvcEvt event dispatch (cases 1/3/4) are pure logic that is mockable (KNS_Q_*, KNS_CFG_getRadioInfo, MGR_LOG are already mocked elsewhere in the suite).
findings.impact: Regressions in the modulation->bitlen table or the FSM (e.g. the TX_ABORT case added in v11.1.0, or the union-aliasing finding above) ship without a guard. These are STDLN/GUI builds, not sealed, so lower priority.
findings.recommendation: Add a small Tests/unit suite that drives KNS_APP_stdln_loop with mocked queue replies through states 0..5 and asserts the pushed appEvt.data_ctxt.usrdata_bitlen for each KNS_TX_MOD_* modulation.

findings.description: In cases 1 and 4 the inner switch sets state++ on KNS_MAC_OK while still inside the for-loop that keeps popping the queue until QEMPTY. If more than one event is queued, subsequent pops are processed against the already-advanced 'state' variable's switch is unaffected (state is only read at function entry), so this is safe — but any KNS_MAC_OK followed by another event in the same drain still logs/handles under the same case. This is benign given the test protocol (one reply expected) but is an easy place to double-advance state if the MAC ever emitted two OKs in one drain.
findings.impact: None with current MAC behavior (single OK per init). Latent fragility if the queue ever holds 2+ OK events: state would increment once per OK within a single loop pass, skipping a state. STDLN/GUI only.
findings.recommendation: Break out of the drain loop after the state-advancing event, or guard the increment so at most one advance happens per invocation.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. Whole file is config-gated: KNS_APP_stdln_loop is live only in USE_STDALONE_APP builds (registered main.c:985); KNS_APP_gui_init/loop only in USE_GUI_APP (main.c:1003/1012/1015). KNS_APP_stdln_startMacPrfl/stopMacPrfl and KNS_APP_assert_failed are static and reachable within the STDLN path. MGR_LOG_array is __attribute__((unused)) and only called at line 251 (STDLN) — the unused attribute is defensive so GUI builds (which never call it) don't warn; intentional, not dead. prflBlindUserCfg is gated by USE_MAC_PRFL_BLIND (the default when neither BASIC nor BLIND is pre-defined, lines 36-39) and used in both stdln and gui init. Case 5 (line 348) is the intended terminal idle state (test complete, do nothing forever) — not dead, by design.
test_coverage: Gap: zero unit coverage of this file. No Tests/unit suite references KNS_APP_stdln_loop / KNS_APP_gui_loop / KNS_APP_gui_init. The testable logic is the FSM (states 0-5) and the modulation->usrdata_bitlen table (lines 230-247), both mockable with the existing KNS_Q/KNS_CFG/MGR_LOG mocks. Lower priority since neither function is in the sealed UW_DOPPLER deployment, but the per-modulation bitlen mapping and the v11.1.0 TX_ABORT/event handling are unguarded.

role: UW_DOPPLER autonomous tracker app: SWS dive/surface FSM, surface-driven Argos TX scheduling (exponential ramp + jitter + LB mode + backoff + rate limit), boot-loop guard, session-MC management, payload packing, and LPM/duty-cycle wiring for the sealed 12-month deployment.
compiled_in: APP=UW_DOPPLER only (sealed target: APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART). Hard #error gates require MAC_PRFL=BASIC and BSP_HAS_REED_SWITCH+BSP_HAS_LED_RGB+BSP_HAS_PWR_LATCH, so effectively this TU compiles only for SMD_STDALONE. Never built for STDLN/GUI/DOPPLER apps or other boards.

findings.description: The first-TX anti-collision random offset is dead in practice. All three surface-detection paths set last_tx_tick=0 immediately before arming surface_tx_pending. The first-TX gate then computes since_last_tx = HAL_GetTick() - last_tx_tick = HAL_GetTick() (a large value, already > 500 ms within the first half-second of any boot), so the test `since_last_tx >= first_tx_random_offset_ms` (offset in [0,500] ms) is satisfied unconditionally. first_tx_random_offset_ms is drawn fresh each surface event but never actually delays anything.
findings.impact: Fleet first-frame de-bunching (FIRST_TX_RANDOM_WINDOW_MS spread, documented as anti-collision measure #a at lines 636-645) is silently defeated. Multiple tags surfacing together transmit their first frame with no per-tag spread, raising Argos ALOHA collision probability for the most important (first) frame. Not a brick; degraded RF performance only. Per-TX jitter on 2nd/3rd repetitions still works.
findings.recommendation: Gate the random offset against an absolute deadline instead of since_last_tx: capture surface_tick at detection and require HAL_GetTick() >= surface_tick + first_tx_random_offset_ms, or apply the offset as part of current_interval_ms/MIN floor for the first TX. Add a unit test asserting the first TX is deferred by ~offset ms.

findings.description: MGR_GESTURE_isInteracting() is called WITHOUT a `#if defined(UW_DOPPLER_HAS_GESTURE)` guard, unlike every other call site in the file (1953, 2121, 2479, 2505 and getMode at 1962/2009/2347/2480 are all guarded). It happens to compile for the sealed target because SMD_STDALONE defines UW_DOPPLER_HAS_GESTURE, but it is an inconsistency: any board that satisfies the top-of-file #error (reed+LED+latch) yet somehow lacks the gesture combo would fail to compile here, and it reads as an unintended unconditional dependency.
findings.impact: No effect on the sealed SMD_STDALONE build (gesture always present). Latent compile breakage / maintenance hazard if the board matrix changes. Defensive only.
findings.recommendation: Wrap line 2464-2465 in `#if defined(UW_DOPPLER_HAS_GESTURE) ... #endif` to match the surrounding call sites, or define a `gesture_in_config`-style local already computed above and reuse it.

findings.description: lat_trace/state_trace/uw_trace3/UWDPL_TRACE use file-scope or function-local `static char buf[]` scratch buffers and are not reentrant. In the current baremetal single-threaded model nothing calls them from an ISR, so this is safe today. Flagging because it is an implicit invariant (no ISR may ever log via these) that is not asserted anywhere.
findings.impact: None in the shipped config. Would corrupt trace output (not memory outside the buffer) if a future ISR ever called one of these helpers.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is for now; if logging is ever needed from ISR context, switch to stack buffers or add a comment documenting the no-ISR invariant.

findings.description: Episode-stats sliding window conflates two different time units. Buckets advance by STAT_BUCKET_MS = 3,600,000 ms of wall-clock (1 real hour) in stat_observe(), but getEpisodeStats() treats `nbk = stat_window_h` as a count of buckets ('1 bucket = 1 hour', line 540). This is only correct if exactly one bucket is consumed per hour. Because HAL_GetTick() is paused during STOP2, bucket_start_tick advances in ACTIVE time, not wall-clock — during long underwater STOP2 sleeps far fewer than one bucket per real hour are produced, so 'last stat_window_h hours' actually spans many more than stat_window_h real hours. The averages are biased but bounded (still over real episodes), and stat_ring is .bss (reset on reboot).
findings.impact: avg_uw_min/avg_surf_min reported via AT+STATS and packed into payload_format 1 (5-bit avg_surf field) represent a longer-than-intended real-time window under heavy STOP2 duty cycling. Telemetry accuracy issue, not a safety/brick issue.
findings.recommendation: Either drive bucket rollover from an RTC wall-clock source instead of HAL_GetTick(), or document that the window is in 'active hours' not wall-clock hours. Add a unit test for the bucket-advance vs window-read relationship.

findings.description: The payload packers and CRC are partly covered: Tests/unit/test_payload_mini.c exercises the format-1 mini frame and argos_crc8 for the VLDA4/LDA2/LDA2L cases, and test_tx_interval.c covers compute_next_interval_ms. But there is NO unit test for the legacy format-0 build_tx_payload path (lines 1351-1405) including the LDA2/LDA2L 184-bit-over-192/196 CRC placement at byte 23, the default/unknown-modulation fallback (line 1382), or argos_pack_bits bit-exact MSB-first packing of the 3+8+7+1 layout. The buffer is exactly KNS_MAC_USRDATA_MAXLEN=25 bytes (non-HDA4) and writes reach index 23 (LDA2_FRAME_BYTES-1); a unit test would lock in that bound.
findings.impact: A regression in bit packing, CRC offset, or bitlen selection for the legacy format would ship a corrupt frame undetected. argos_crc8's internal buffer[LDA2_FRAME_BYTES] is sized for the max 184-bit input; a future caller passing nbits>184 would overflow it with no test catching it.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test for build_tx_payload format-0 across all four modulations asserting exact bytes + bitlen + CRC position, plus a guard/static_assert that argos_crc8 inputs never exceed LDA2_DATA_BITS (or bound the internal buffer to KNS_MAC_USRDATA_MAXLEN).

findings.description: Comment-vs-code drift / fragile self-describing-header assumption. The file header (lines 36-46) documents the legacy layout placing battery at bits [11..17]; the format-1 layout places battery at bits [8..14] (after hdr3+sf5). The two formats put telemetry at different bit offsets but share the same 3-bit header 0b011, so a ground-segment decoder cannot distinguish format 0 from format 1 from the frame alone (payload_format is an NVM-side setting, not transmitted). This is a protocol-robustness concern, not a firmware defect.
findings.impact: If a unit's payload_format is changed (AT+PAYCFG / NVM migration) the receiver has no in-band signal of which layout was sent; mis-decode is possible across the fleet if format is not tracked per-unit on the ground.
findings.recommendation: Either carry a format bit in-band or freeze payload_format for the sealed deployment and document the binding. At minimum reconcile the header-comment bit map with both actual layouts.

findings.description: KNS_APP_uw_doppler_getTestBurstRemaining() is an exported orphan: declared in the header (line 147) and self-documented as 'Unwired diagnostic hook ... No AT query reads it back today'. Confirmed no live caller in the codebase. Intentional (kept for a future AT status command), not a genuine bug.
findings.impact: None. Tiny code-size cost; exported symbol so the linker cannot drop it.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable to keep given the documented intent; otherwise remove until a caller exists.

findings.description: The seq-restart deadline in uw_ms_until_next_action() uses `since = HAL_GetTick() - last_tx_tick` against tx_seq_restart_s, but in MONITORING the seq-restart firing condition (line 2408) ALSO requires sws_state==SURFACE and deploy_mode and !gesture_in_config, none of which are re-checked in uw_ms_until_next_action. The deadline computation can therefore schedule a wake for a seq-restart that will not actually fire (e.g. tag dived). Worst case is a spurious early wake (the next loop re-evaluates and goes back to sleep), so it costs a little extra current, not correctness.
findings.impact: Minor extra wake-ups / current draw in edge cases where the cap was reached at surface and then state changed. Bounded, self-correcting on the next loop pass.
findings.recommendation: Optionally guard the seq-restart branch in uw_ms_until_next_action with the same surface/deploy conditions, or accept the conservative early-wake as harmless.

dead_code: No genuine orphans that are dangerous. KNS_APP_uw_doppler_getTestBurstRemaining() (2821) is an intentionally-kept unwired diagnostic hook (documented). The non-gesture #elif raw-reed shutdown path (1974-1999, REED_SHUTDOWN_HOLD_MS, magnet_on_tick, shutdown_triggered, enter_shutdown legacy deadman at 2688-2702) is config-gated dead for the sealed build: UW_DOPPLER_HAS_GESTURE is always defined on SMD_STDALONE (reed+LED both present), so those statics are marked __attribute__((unused)) and the legacy branches compile out. The UW_DOPPLER_PREWARM_TCXO block (2560-2581) and UW_DOPPLER_LAT_TRACE / verbose-trace blocks are compile-flag-gated diagnostics, intentional. compute_next_interval_ms LB-override branch is live only when lb_cfg.lb_enter_mV != 0 (LB disabled by default) — reachable, just dormant. No unreachable-by-control-flow code found inside the active config.
test_coverage: Partial. Covered: compute_next_interval_ms (test_tx_interval.c), format-1 mini payload + argos_crc8 (test_payload_mini.c), cooldown/seq-MC/boot-loop/state-machine via their dedicated suites. GAPS: (1) build_tx_payload legacy format-0 path across all four modulations incl. 184-bit-over-192/196 CRC@byte23 placement and the unknown-modulation fallback — untested; (2) argos_pack_bits bit-exact MSB-first packing — untested directly; (3) the dead first-TX anti-collision offset (finding at 2377) — no test asserts the offset actually delays; (4) episode-stats window unit-mismatch (getEpisodeStats vs stat_observe) — untested; (5) no bound assertion that argos_crc8 inputs never exceed its internal buffer[LDA2_FRAME_BYTES].

role: Platform hook that closed-source libkineis.a calls (undefined symbol kns_assert_failed) when an internal MAC assertion fails: prints file:line over direct UART, logs via the ring buffer, then enters the global Error_Handler (which, on UW_DOPPLER, resets the chip via MGR_ERR_logAndReset). Terminal fault path.
compiled_in: all (unconditional entry in Makefile C_SOURCES line 205; no APP/BOARD/COMM guard). It is the resolution for the libkineis undefined symbol kns_assert_failed (Kineis/Lib/libkineis_undefined_symbols.txt:30), so it links into every config.

findings.description: The MGR_LOG_ERR path passes the raw `file` pointer to a `%s` conversion with NO null guard. The direct-UART block just above (line 59) correctly guards it: `(file ? (const char *)file : "(null)")`. MGR_LOG_ERR -> vMGR_LOG_printf_ts_lvl -> log_emit_ts -> vsnprintf(... format, args) (mgr_log.c:290) feeds `file` straight to vsnprintf. If libkineis ever calls kns_assert_failed with file==NULL, printf-family %s on a NULL pointer is undefined behavior per C11 7.21.6.1; newlib happens to print "(null)" but that is not guaranteed and is not the intended contract.
findings.impact: On the sealed UW_DOPPLER deployment this is the terminal assert path. A NULL file argument from the MAC would invoke UB inside the log formatter while the chip is already trying to report a fatal fault — at best a garbled forensic line, at worst a secondary fault that masks the original assert site right before reset. Low probability (the kns_assert macro always passes __FILE__, never NULL) but the direct path already defends against it asymmetrically.
findings.recommendation: Mirror the direct-UART guard: pass `(file ? (const char *)file : (uint8_t*)"(null)")` (or a local `const char *fn = file ? (const char*)file : "(null)";`) to the MGR_LOG_ERR call so both emit paths are NULL-safe and consistent.

findings.description: Format-specifier mismatches in MGR_LOG_ERR("ASSERT FAIL: %ld %s\r\n", line, file): `line` is uint32_t printed with `%ld` (expects `long`, no cast), and `file` is `uint8_t *` printed with `%s` (expects `char *`, no cast). On ARM EABI `long` is 32-bit so the value is preserved, but it is still a type-mismatched variadic argument (technically UB / would warn under -Wformat). The direct-UART snprintf above does it correctly with `(unsigned long)line` + `%lu`. Note also the argument order/format here (`%ld %s` = line then file) is inconsistent with the human-readable direct line above (file:line).
findings.impact: Cosmetic on this toolchain (32-bit long); could become a real defect if ported to an LP64/ILP-mismatched target. Mildly inconsistent forensic output between the two emit paths.
findings.recommendation: Use `%lu` with `(unsigned long)line` and cast file: `MGR_LOG_ERR("ASSERT FAIL: %s:%lu\r\n", (file?(const char*)file:"(null)"), (unsigned long)line);` to match the direct-UART line and silence -Wformat.

findings.description: Redundant dual emission: the direct synchronous UART block (lines 54-62) and the MGR_LOG_ERR ring-buffer call (line 63) both print an ERROR-grade assert line for the same event, gated by the same MGR_LOG_passes(MGR_LOG_LVL_ERROR). The direct block exists precisely because it survives log-buffer issues; the ring-buffer line only reaches the host if Error_Handler -> MGR_ERR_logAndReset flushes before reset (it does, per main.c:1241-1243). Not a bug, but the second line is largely duplicate forensic output.
findings.impact: None functional. Slight extra UART traffic on the fault path and two slightly different formats for the same fault (potential confusion when reading logs).
findings.recommendation: Optional: keep the robust direct-UART line and drop or downgrade the duplicate MGR_LOG_ERR, or make the two formats identical. No action required for correctness.

findings.description: kns_assert can be invoked from any libkineis context, including potentially an interrupt (e.g. radio IRQ / KNS_MAC dispatch). Both emit paths do blocking work: HAL_UART_Transmit with a 200 ms timeout (line 61), and MGR_LOG_ERR -> log_emit_ts which calls HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro / HAL_RTC_GetTime/GetDate (mgr_log.c:276-278). If reached from an ISR before the RTC is initialised/synchronised, HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro can spin to its own HAL timeout. This is a terminal path that resets, so it is bounded, but it is not an instant fault-and-reset.
findings.impact: Worst case a few hundred ms of blocking inside an ISR on the fatal path before Error_Handler resets the chip. Bounded (HAL timeouts + 200 ms), never an infinite hang, so not brick-class — but it delays the reset and runs non-trivial code (RTC HAL) at the most fragile moment.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is for a terminal path. If hardening is desired, keep only the minimal direct-UART line in kns_assert_failed and let Error_Handler/MGR_ERR_logAndReset own the richer logging, avoiding RTC HAL calls from a possibly-ISR fault context.

dead_code: none. kns_assert_failed is the link-time resolution of the libkineis undefined symbol `kns_assert_failed` (Kineis/Lib/libkineis_undefined_symbols.txt:30) and is also reachable from in-tree kns_assert(...) call sites (mgr_lpm.c:207/229/325/350, mcu_spi_driver.c:98/308/330, mgr_spi_cmd_list_user_data.c:232, etc.). The `static char ka_buf[168]` is used. `#pragma GCC visibility push(default)` is meaningful here because it forces the symbol to be externally visible to the closed-source archive. No unused statics, params, or returns (void).
test_coverage: No unit test exists for this file (grep for kns_assert under Tests/ returns nothing). The pure logic worth covering is the NULL-file handling and the format/length of the emitted assert string. A Tests/unit case could call kns_assert_failed with (a) a valid file ptr and (b) file==NULL, with HAL_UART_Transmit/MGR_LOG/Error_Handler mocked, asserting that (1) the direct-UART buffer never overflows ka_buf[168], (2) NULL file does not crash, and (3) Error_Handler is invoked exactly once. This is the natural place to lock in the medium NULL-guard finding above as a regression test. Currently n/a — untested HW-adjacent glue, but the NULL path is unit-testable.

role: Vendor (Kineis) nestable critical-section primitive: KNS_CS_enter/exit save PRIMASK on a small stack and disable/restore IRQs. Called by libkineis.a MAC (undefined-symbol boundary), KNS_Q baremetal queues, and USERDATA FIFO.
compiled_in: all (Makefile:206 — unconditionally in KINEIS sources for every APP/BOARD/COMM; KNS_CS_enter/exit are required undefined symbols of libkineis.a per Kineis/Lib/libkineis_undefined_symbols.txt:1-2)

findings.description: The nesting depth counter 'idx' (and the 'prim[]' save stack) is shared between main context and ISR context with no protection of the increment/decrement itself, and 'idx' is not volatile. The MAC timer/RF callbacks run in ISR context (e.g. HAL_TIM_PeriodElapsedCallback at Kineis/Extdep/Mcu/Src/mcu_tim.c:131, HAL_RTCEx_WakeUpTimerEventCallback at :153) and can enqueue events via KNS_Q_push -> KNS_CS_enter/exit (kns_q_baremetal.c:83,95,109). In KNS_CS_enter the sequence is: read PRIMASK into prim[idx%N]; __disable_irq(); idx++. The save into prim[] and the disable are NOT atomic relative to a pre-existing nesting: if an IRQ fires after __get_PRIMASK but logic relies on idx, the index bookkeeping can interleave. More concretely, because the same 'idx'/'prim[]' are used by both contexts, an enter on the main side that is preempted between writing prim[idx] and idx++ by an ISR that also enters/exits will leave idx/prim[] inconsistent. There is no separate per-context save.
findings.impact: In the sealed UW_DOPPLER deployment, MAC ISR activity concurrent with main-loop queue access can corrupt the save stack, causing IRQs to be re-enabled while a critical section is still nominally held (silent data race on queue indices) or left disabled. A queue-index corruption or a wrongly-enabled IRQ window can drop/duplicate a MAC event or hang the stack — a no-physical-access brick risk.
findings.recommendation: Treat as vendor boundary but harden the call sites: ensure KNS_CS is only entered with IRQs already masked from the same context, or replace with the proven save/restore idiom used elsewhere (uint32_t prim = __get_PRIMASK(); __disable_irq(); ... __set_PRIMASK(prim);) which needs no shared counter. Mark 'idx' volatile and static. Add a unit test exercising nested enter/exit balance.

findings.description: Unbalanced-exit / underflow has no guard. 'idx' is uint8_t (line 39). KNS_CS_exit does 'idx--' first (line 53) then reads prim[idx % 8]. If KNS_CS_exit is ever called once more than KNS_CS_enter (or first), idx wraps 0 -> 255, prim[255 % 8] = prim[7] is read (an uninitialized or stale saved value, never written this round), and __enable_irq() may be executed (or skipped) based on garbage. There is no kns_assert and no clamp.
findings.impact: A single mispaired exit (e.g. an early-return path in vendor MAC or a future edit in KNS_Q/USERDATA) silently re-enables interrupts inside a still-active outer critical section, or leaves them disabled forever (hang). Either is a brick/corruption vector with no recovery in a sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Add 'if (idx == 0) { kns_assert_failed(...); return; }' before the decrement, or use an idiom that does not depend on a fragile counter. At minimum _Static_assert and an assert on idx>0 at entry to exit.

findings.description: No overflow protection beyond the depth of PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE (8). KNS_CS_enter always writes prim[idx % 8] and increments idx unconditionally. If real nesting exceeds 8 (vendor MAC depth is opaque), prim[idx%8] aliases an earlier still-active slot and overwrites its saved PRIMASK; the matching exit then restores the wrong value. The modulo masks the overflow instead of detecting it.
findings.impact: Deep nesting silently corrupts the saved interrupt state, prematurely re-enabling IRQs mid-section. Probability low (depth 8 is generous) but consequence is the same silent-corruption brick class; undetectable without an assert.
findings.recommendation: Assert idx < PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE on entry (kns_assert) so an overflow is caught in test/bench rather than silently wrapping. The '% PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE' should be a safety net behind an assert, not the primary mechanism.

findings.description: 'idx' is declared as a non-static global (no 'static', no 'volatile'). It pollutes the global namespace with a common 3-letter name 'idx' that can collide at link time with any other translation unit defining a non-static 'idx', and it is mutable global state shared across ISR/main without volatile. The paired 'prim[]' is correctly 'static' (line 38) but 'idx' is inconsistent.
findings.impact: Linker-level symbol collision risk (silent merge of two unrelated 'idx' globals if another TU exports one) and missing volatile means the compiler may cache 'idx' across the __disable_irq boundary in aggressive optimization, defeating the nesting count under LTO/-O2.
findings.recommendation: Make 'idx' 'static volatile uint8_t idx'. Confirm no external linkage is needed (header declares only the two functions, kns_cs.h:31,35 — 'idx' is not exported).

findings.description: Restore-by-reconstruction instead of restore-by-write. Exit re-enables IRQs via 'if (!prim[idx%N]) __enable_irq()' rather than the canonical 'uint32_t prim=__get_PRIMASK(); __disable_irq(); ...; __set_PRIMASK(prim);' pattern used by the HAL (stm32wlxx_hal_flash.c:728-749, hal_lptim.c:2536-2669) and by mgr_log.c:50-51. The reconstruction happens to be correct for the PRIMASK-only case but is fragile: it assumes the only relevant masking bit is PRIMASK and that no other code path (FAULTMASK/BASEPRI) participates.
findings.impact: Works today on Cortex-M4 with PRIMASK-only masking, but diverges from the rest of the codebase's interrupt-state save/restore idiom, making it an outlier that is easy to misread and that cannot be unified with __set_PRIMASK-based nesting.
findings.recommendation: Prefer __set_PRIMASK(saved) for symmetry and to drop the shared counter entirely. Vendor file — flag to Kineis rather than patch locally unless the concurrency findings above force a local fix.

findings.description: K&R-style empty parameter lists 'void KNS_CS_enter()' / 'KNS_CS_exit()' in the definitions, whereas the header (kns_cs.h:31,35) correctly uses '(void)'. Under C (not C++), '()' means 'unspecified args', not 'no args', so the definitions do not enforce the no-argument contract.
findings.impact: Cosmetic/MISRA-like; no functional effect since callers pass nothing. Minor prototype-mismatch hygiene issue.
findings.recommendation: Use '(void)' in the definitions to match the header and enforce no-args. Vendor file — low priority.

dead_code: none. Both KNS_CS_enter and KNS_CS_exit are live in all configs: they are required undefined symbols of libkineis.a (Kineis/Lib/libkineis_undefined_symbols.txt:1-2, the closed-source MAC calls them) and are also called directly by KNS_Q baremetal (kns_q_baremetal.c:83,95,109,138,148,161) and USERDATA (user_data.c:89,101,310,329). 'prim[]' and 'idx' are both used. No unused statics/params/returns (functions return void). The '% PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE' branch and the PRIM_ARRAY_SIZE>=4 comment are reachable.
test_coverage: NONE. No file under Tests/unit references KNS_CS or kns_cs (verified: the only Glob hit Tests/unit/test_crash_forensics.c contains no KNS_CS reference). This is pure, mockable logic (PRIMASK is the only HW dependency and is trivially stubbed) and should be tested: (1) balanced nested enter/exit restores IRQ state correctly at each level; (2) entry with IRQs already disabled stays disabled after a full enter/exit pair (the 'prim==1' path, line 54); (3) entry with IRQs enabled re-enables on outermost exit only; (4) the underflow guard (once added) on a stray exit; (5) the overflow guard (once added) past depth 8. The high/medium findings above (underflow, overflow, restore correctness) are exactly the cases that a unit test would have caught.

role: Static definition of the Kineis baremetal queue pool: 5 FIFO queues (descriptors + backing byte arrays) wired into qPool[KNS_Q_MAX], plus an optional debug name table qIdx2Str. Pure data/config; no executable logic.
compiled_in: all (gated on USE_BAREMETAL, which is the project OS for every shipped config: STDLN/GUI/UW_DOPPLER/DOPPLER x all boards x UART/SPI). qIdx2Str block additionally gated on DEBUG||VERBOSE; Makefile default DEBUG=1 VERBOSE=1, bench=DEBUG=1, release=DEBUG=0.

findings.description: Missing comma after the first string literal "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST" (line 111). C adjacent-string-literal concatenation fuses it with "KNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC" (line 112) into a single element. The qIdx2Str[KNS_Q_MAX] array therefore gets only 4 initializers for 5 slots: idx0="KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LISTKNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC", idx1="KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP", idx2="KNS_Q_UL_INFRA2MAC", idx3="KNS_Q_UL_SRVC2MAC", idx4=NULL (default zero-fill). Two distinct defects: (a) labels for handles 1..3 are shifted/wrong vs the enum (e.g. handle KNS_Q_DL_APP2MAC=1 now prints "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP"); (b) qIdx2Str[KNS_Q_UL_SRVC2MAC]=qIdx2Str[4]=NULL.
findings.impact: In the bench config (DEBUG=1), MGR_LOG_DEBUG/MGR_LOG_VERBOSE expand to vMGR_LOG_printf. kns_q_baremetal.c:96/111/163/177/194 do qIdx2Str[qHandle] with a %s. A QFULL or any verbose push/pop on the SRVC2MAC queue (the highest-priority RF-driver-to-MAC queue, exercised on every TX/RX) passes a NULL pointer to printf %s -> undefined behaviour (best case prints '(null)', worst case faults inside the formatter). This corrupts/hangs the very log path used to diagnose a queue-full RF event on the bench. Release (DEBUG=0) compiles qIdx2Str out, so the sealed image is unaffected at runtime, but every bench validation run carries the landmine.
findings.recommendation: Add the missing comma after "KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST" and verify all 5 labels match the enum order exactly (EVT_LIST, DL_APP2MAC, UL_MAC2APP, UL_INFRA2MAC, UL_SRVC2MAC). Add a _Static_assert / designated-initializer or compile guard so a count mismatch is a build error.

findings.description: Neither qPool[KNS_Q_MAX] nor qIdx2Str[KNS_Q_MAX] is protected by a compile-time size check tying element count to KNS_Q_MAX, and both are hand-maintained in parallel with the KNS_Q_handle_t enum in the header. The header itself only says 'align this enum with content of qPool' as a comment. C silently zero-fills missing initializers (exactly what masked finding #1) and silently ignores excess only with a warning that is easy to miss.
findings.impact: Any future edit that adds/reorders/removes a queue, or any typo like the missing comma, produces a silent index/label desync rather than a build failure. A desync between qPool ordering and the enum would mis-route events between MAC and APP queues — a corruption class that is hard to spot and would ship.
findings.recommendation: Add _Static_assert(sizeof(qPool)/sizeof(qPool[0]) == KNS_Q_MAX, ...) and the same for qIdx2Str. Prefer designated initializers (qPool[KNS_Q_UL_SRVC2MAC] = &qSrvc2Mac, ...) so position is explicit and a missing slot is visible.

findings.description: Header comment (lines 28-30) states the EVT_LIST queue is placed in retention RAM 'as we want external MCU to be able to retrieve events after a while, including LPM periods'. The backing array and descriptor use .retentionRamData (lines 32, 36). Per the linker script comment (STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:135-139), .retentionRamData lives in .data2 and is copy-from-ROM re-initialised by Sram2_Init on every cold/factory/reset boot; only items in .retentionRamNoload survive software resets. SRAM2 content is retained across STOP2 (no Sram2_Init), so the comment holds for STOP wake, but NOT across the reed/SHUTDOWN->reset wake path used by the sealed UW_DOPPLER deployment, which re-runs Sram2_Init and resets rIdx/wIdx/data to the ROM image (empty queue).
findings.impact: After a reed-triggered SHUTDOWN+reset cycle (the normal sealed power-cycle path), any events the external/host MCU had not yet drained from the EVT_LIST are lost and the queue is silently re-zeroed, despite the comment promising persistence 'including LPM periods'. Comment over-promises; could mislead a future maintainer into relying on cross-reset persistence that does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Either move qDataMac2AppEvtList + qMac2AppEvtList to .retentionRamNoload if true cross-reset persistence is required (note: would then need explicit reset of rIdx/wIdx/mutex on factory boot to avoid stale-index reads), or correct the comment to clarify it survives STOP-class retention only, not reset-class wakes.

findings.description: There is no unit test for the queue-pool invariants. Tests/unit/ has no test_kns_q*; the ordering of qPool vs KNS_Q_handle_t, the label-count of qIdx2Str, and the per-queue LEN/ITEM_BYTESIZE consistency (the contract KNS_Q_create validates) are all unverified by the host test suite. A simple host test compiling this TU would have caught the missing-comma label/NULL defect.
findings.impact: Config-level regressions (reordering, off-by-one in label table, LEN/size mismatch) are caught only at runtime on hardware, if at all (the EVT_LIST queue is not even validated by a KNS_Q_create call, see next finding).
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit/test_kns_q_conf.c that (1) _Static_asserts qPool/qIdx2Str element count == KNS_Q_MAX, (2) checks qPool[i] order matches the enum, (3) checks each descriptor's nbElt/eltSize equals the corresponding KNS_Q_*_LEN / *_ITEM_BYTESIZE macro, (4) asserts no qIdx2Str entry is NULL.

findings.description: main.c validates 4 of the 5 queues via assert_param(KNS_Q_create(...)==OK) but never validates KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST. KNS_Q_create compares the passed length/size against the descriptor's nbElt/eltSize (kns_q_baremetal.c:61-64). The EVT_LIST descriptor (nbElt=20, eltSize=sizeof(KNS_MAC_srvcEvt_t)) is thus never cross-checked against its KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST_LEN/ITEM_BYTESIZE macros.
findings.impact: If the EVT_LIST descriptor and its macros ever diverge (e.g. someone changes the byte-size macro but not the array, or vice versa), the mismatch goes undetected; the queue would read/write with a wrong stride into qDataMac2AppEvtList -> out-of-bounds or truncated event records in retention RAM. Low likelihood today (values are macro-derived) but unguarded.
findings.recommendation: Add assert_param(KNS_Q_create(KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST, KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST_LEN, KNS_Q_UL_MAC2APP_EVT_LIST_ITEM_BYTESIZE) == KNS_STATUS_OK); in main.c, or add a _Static_assert in this file binding the descriptor fields to the macros.

findings.description: isLpmBlocker is true for the four MAC-internal queues and false for qMac2AppEvtList (line 44). This is correct and intentional: KNS_Q_isEvtInSomeQ (kns_q_baremetal.c:185-200) gates LPM entry on isLpmBlocker, and the EVT_LIST is an APP-facing reporting mirror that must NOT keep the chip awake. But the WHY is undocumented at the field, and per CLAUDE.md power rules an accidental flip to true here would block STOP/SHUTDOWN whenever an unread +KEVT sits in the list — a silent battery drain.
findings.impact: No current defect. Risk is a future edit flipping the flag and silently defeating low-power entry in the sealed deployment.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment at qMac2AppEvtList.isLpmBlocker=false explaining it is an APP-drained reporting queue and must stay non-blocking to permit LPM.

findings.description: Comment typos / rot: 'bahaviour' (line 94, also header equivalent), 'align this enum wit hcontent' (line 95), 'appplication' (lines 92,106), header 'descriptio' (kns_q_conf.h:112), 'queue description queue' (kns_q_conf.h:110). Also the kns_q.h page comment (kns_q.h:29-33) lists queue priorities with a numbering (4/3/2/1) and omits INFRA2MAC, inconsistent with the actual enum order in kns_q_conf.h:96-100.
findings.impact: None functional. The inconsistent priority documentation between kns_q.h and the enum can mislead a maintainer reasoning about preemption order (KNS_Q_isEvtInHigherPrioQ uses enum index, higher index = higher priority).
findings.recommendation: Fix typos; reconcile the kns_q.h priority list with the actual KNS_Q_handle_t enum (include INFRA2MAC, match ordering).

dead_code: No genuine orphans in this file. qIdx2Str (lines 105-116) is config-gated dead in the release/sealed build (DEBUG=0 && VERBOSE=0 strips it and all its call sites in kns_q_baremetal.c), and live in the bench build (DEBUG=1) where the missing-comma bug bites — so it is NOT safe to ignore. qPool and all five qData*/q* descriptors are live in every USE_BAREMETAL config (consumed by kns_q_baremetal.c and libkineis MAC). The file-guard macros KNS_Q_CONF_C/H are include-guard boilerplate (this .c is #include-guarded, unusual but harmless). No unused statics: every static is referenced via qPool or directly by the MAC.
test_coverage: Not covered. The testable invariants here are pure compile-time/data: (1) qPool order == KNS_Q_handle_t enum, (2) qIdx2Str has KNS_Q_MAX non-NULL labels in enum order, (3) each descriptor nbElt/eltSize == its KNS_Q_*_LEN / *_ITEM_BYTESIZE macro, (4) isLpmBlocker policy (EVT_LIST=false, rest=true). None of these has a test in Tests/unit (no test_kns_q*). A trivial host test compiling this TU would have caught the line-111 missing comma (NULL label) at assertion time.

role: Thread-safe-ish non-blocking ring-buffer logger: formats timestamped/level-tagged messages into a 4 KB ring, flushed to LPUART1 in chunks from the main loop; runtime AT-controllable enable flag + severity threshold persisted in retention NOLOAD RAM.
compiled_in: all (entire body gated on USE_LOCAL_PRINTF, which the Makefile defines unconditionally at C_DEFS line 289 → compiled in every APP/BOARD/COMM incl. the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART target). LOG_FLUSH_* sizing branches on USE_SPI_DRIVER vs UART.

findings.description: The pause/flush mutual-exclusion machinery (log_uart_busy flag, the busy-wait `while (timeout>0 && log_uart_busy)` loop, and the double-check of log_paused at line 384) is designed for a preemptive scheduler. In this baremetal build both MGR_LOG_pause() (called from MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send) and MGR_LOG_flush() (called from KNS_OS_main) run in the SAME single main-loop thread, and no ISR ever calls flush or a log macro (verified: stm32wlxx_it.c, mgr_reed.c HAL_GPIO_EXTI_Callback do not log). Therefore log_uart_busy can never be observed true inside pause(): flush() has always already returned. The whole guard is inert.
findings.impact: No corruption risk, but it is dead defensive logic that obscures the actual (already-safe) invariant and could mislead a future maintainer into believing a real cross-context race is being handled here.
findings.recommendation: Document that producer/consumer/pause all share the main-loop thread, or simplify pause() to just set log_paused. If a future change moves logging into an ISR, the head/tail design (uint16_t writes under __disable_irq) is the part that actually matters, not these flags.

findings.description: MGR_LOG_pause() unconditionally executes a fixed `for (i=0; i<1000) __NOP();` spin (lines 469-471) on EVERY AT response, and can additionally spin up to 600000/1000000 iterations on log_uart_busy. Per finding above, the busy condition is never true here, so the variable spin is skipped, but the fixed 1000-NOP delay always runs. MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send calls pause() on every reply, and MCU_AT_CONSOLE_send_dataBuf wraps a whole hex dump.
findings.impact: Pure busy-wait CPU burn (small, ~tens of µs) added to every AT transaction. Negligible energy but unnecessary in a power-sensitive sealed build; also adds latency to AT responsiveness, the very thing the comment claims to protect.
findings.recommendation: Remove the fixed __NOP spin; in baremetal HAL_UART_Transmit is blocking so on pause() the transmit is provably already complete.

findings.description: When a single logged line is longer than LOG_FLUSH_MAX_BYTES (128 at UART) and contains no '\n' within the scanned window, last_nl stays -1 and the code consumes the entire 128-byte chunk mid-line (comment line 147 'consume all to prevent starvation'). The next flush sends the remainder. If MGR_LOG_pause() lands between those two flushes, the line is split across an AT response — exactly the interleaving the line-alignment logic at 142-146 exists to prevent.
findings.impact: Cosmetic log fragmentation / a debug line can straddle an AT reply for messages >128 bytes. No memory or control-flow hazard. LOGGING_PURPOSE_STORAGE_MAX_MESSAGE_LEN is 256 so this is reachable for long-format lines.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as-is (logs only). If clean framing matters, hold back a no-newline chunk until either a newline arrives or the ring is full; document the 128<256 size mismatch.

findings.description: HAL_UART_Transmit return value is ignored. Bytes are already removed from the ring by log_ring_get_string() before the transmit; if the UART times out (LOG_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS) or errors, those bytes are lost with no retry and no diagnostic counter (unlike the overflow path which increments log_overflow_count).
findings.impact: Silent loss of a log chunk on UART fault. For pure debug logging this is tolerable; it only matters for the MGR_ERR_logAndReset drain (mgr_err.c:154) where a forensic message could be partially lost right before reset — but that path is already best-effort and bounded.
findings.recommendation: Optionally check the HAL return and bump a dropped-tx counter for diagnostics; not required for correctness.

findings.description: Every timestamped log (all MGR_LOG_INFO/WARN/ERR that pass the gate) calls HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro(&hrtc) before reading time. This blocks until the RTC shadow registers resync (up to ~2 RTCCLK periods). It runs on the hot format path inside the main loop.
findings.impact: Added blocking latency per emitted log line; with BYPSHAD typically unnecessary. Minor — only affects lines that pass the level filter, and the default level is ERROR (DEBUG=0) so production is rarely hit.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether RTC bypass-shadow (BYPSHAD) is set in init; if so the WaitForSynchro can be dropped. Low priority.

findings.description: Zero unit coverage for this module. Tests/unit has no test exercising log_ring_put_string/get_string (wrap-around, all-or-nothing overflow drop, free-space arithmetic, line-boundary consumption), MGR_LOG_passes/getLevel/setLevel clamping, MGR_LOG_levelTag index clamp, or the retention-magic fallback in vMGR_LOG_isEnabled/MGR_LOG_getLevel. (test_evtlog.c / test_pmlog_torn.c are unrelated modules.) Per CLAUDE.md every fix/logic needs a Tests/unit case; this is testable host-side logic (the ring + level math are pure, HAL only at the edges).
findings.impact: Ring wrap-around and the power-of-two modulo masking, the overflow drop semantics, and the level-threshold gate are exactly the kind of arithmetic that silently regresses. The gate also governs whether sealed-deploy forensic ERR lines are emitted, so a regression could mute the only field diagnostics.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit suite that drives the static ring via the public put/get (or by including the .c with mocked HAL_RTC_*) covering: fill-to-N-1, exact-fit, one-byte-short drop (+overflow count), head/tail wrap, line-boundary get, level clamp >NONE, levelTag clamp, and isEnabled/getLevel magic-mismatch fallback to LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL/LOG_DEFAULT_ENABLED.

findings.description: Comment rot. Makefile line 591 states 'Unset → header picks TRACE for DEBUG=1 builds, INFO for DEBUG=0', but mgr_log.h actually sets LOG_DEFAULT_LEVEL = MGR_LOG_LVL_INFO for DEBUG=1 (line 151) and MGR_LOG_LVL_ERROR for DEBUG=0 (line 155). Both claims in the Makefile comment are wrong.
findings.impact: Misleading documentation could cause a maintainer to expect more verbose production logging than they get; the sealed build is actually ERROR-only, which is the intended quiet default — so the code is right, the comment is wrong.
findings.recommendation: Fix the Makefile comment to read 'INFO for DEBUG=1, ERROR for DEBUG=0'.

findings.description: vMGR_LOG_resetToDefault() sets s_uart_log_enabled_word = 0u in addition to clearing the magic. Because vMGR_LOG_isEnabled() short-circuits on a magic mismatch, the word value is irrelevant after the magic is cleared — writing 0 looks like it forces 'off' but actually has no effect. Reads as a latent bug to a casual reviewer.
findings.impact: None functional; readability only. The behaviour (fall back to compile-time default) is correct.
findings.recommendation: Drop the redundant word write or add a one-line comment that only the magic matters.

findings.description: In log_ring_get_string, last_nl is a signed int used as a position into a uint16_t-indexed chunk while count/tail are uint16_t. Mixing is harmless here (max_count <= 128, well within int range and the -1 sentinel needs the sign), but it is an implicit-cast/type-consistency nit against the MISRA-like discipline in CLAUDE.md.
findings.impact: None; cosmetic.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is or make the sentinel explicit (e.g. a found flag + uint16_t pos).

dead_code: No genuine orphans. Entire file is config-gated by USE_LOCAL_PRINTF, which is always defined (Makefile:289) → all functions compile in every config. The pause/flush busy-wait + log_uart_busy double-check (lines 380-388, 451-464) is effectively inert in this baremetal single-thread build (no ISR producer, pause and flush share the main-loop thread) — it is defensive code that can never trigger here, not dead code in the linker sense. All public symbols (pause/resume/is_paused/is_uart_busy/get_overflow_count/has_pending) have live callers (mcu_at_console_stm.c, kns_os.c, mgr_err.c, mgr_gesture.c). vMGR_LOG_printf_ts (level-less legacy path, line 303) is reached via mgr_log_rtc.c:62 MGR_LOG_RtcDateTime.
test_coverage: NOT covered. No Tests/unit suite touches mgr_log.c. The ring-buffer arithmetic (wrap, power-of-2 mask, all-or-nothing overflow drop, line-boundary get), the level threshold/clamp logic (MGR_LOG_passes/getLevel/setLevel/levelTag), and the retention-magic validity fallback (vMGR_LOG_isEnabled, MGR_LOG_getLevel) are all pure, host-testable logic with HAL only at the edges and currently have zero tests. This is the principal gap. See the test-gap finding for the concrete suite to add.

role: Formats the RTC date+time into a "YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM:SS" string and pushes it to the log ring buffer via vMGR_LOG_printf. Single public function MGR_LOG_RtcDateTime().
compiled_in: all — listed unconditionally in Makefile:209, so the translation unit is built for every APP/BOARD/COMM config. (The function body is NOT #ifdef-guarded.)

findings.description: MGR_LOG_RtcDateTime() is a genuine orphan: it has ZERO live call sites anywhere in the firmware source tree. A whole-tree grep for the symbol (excluding Kineis/Doc/**) finds only the definition (mgr_log_rtc.c:38), the prototype (mgr_log_rtc.h:34) and the include lines. The only call sites that exist are inside generated Doxygen HTML under Kineis/Doc/ (e.g. mgr__log_8h_source.html lines 61/71) which reflect a LEGACY version of mgr_log.h where the DEBUG/VERBOSE macros expanded to MGR_LOG_RtcDateTime(); the current mgr_log.h (lines 64-93) no longer references it — the macros now route through vMGR_LOG_printf_ts_lvl(). So this is not config-gated dead code; it is dead in every config. The TU is still compiled (Makefile:209) and the function is exported (non-static, prototyped in a header), so the linker keeps it (or GC-sections drops it). Net effect today: ~70 lines of compiled-but-unreachable code carrying a live HAL_RTC dependency.
findings.impact: No runtime harm in the sealed deployment, but it is a maintenance/audit landmine: it pulls HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro/GetTime/GetDate into the dependency graph and uses unbounded sprintf, so any future reuse inherits the issues below. Misleads readers into thinking RTC timestamps are emitted from here (they are actually produced by log_emit_ts() in mgr_log.c).
findings.recommendation: Either delete mgr_log_rtc.{c,h} and drop the Makefile:209 line, or, if kept for API compatibility, add a comment marking it unused and gate it behind a feature flag. Confirm with the user before removing (file appears in Makefile and README tree listings).

findings.description: Return values of HAL_RTC_WaitForSynchro(), HAL_RTC_GetTime() and HAL_RTC_GetDate() are all ignored. If WaitForSynchro times out (RTC clock — LSE — not running, a real scenario on this board per the LSE-death deploy blocker noted in project memory) or GetTime/GetDate return HAL_ERROR, the date/time structs are used regardless. Additionally there is a hard HAL ordering invariant: GetTime MUST be read before GetDate (reading TR locks the shadow registers, reading DR unlocks them). The order here is correct (Time at line 48, Date at line 50), but it is undocumented and fragile — a future reorder would silently desync date vs time.
findings.impact: On LSE failure / RTC desync this emits a wrong or stale timestamp into the log. Cosmetic for logs only (no control path depends on it), so low — but in a sealed unit the timestamp is the only forensic anchor in the log, and a silently-wrong one misleads post-recovery analysis.
findings.recommendation: Check each HAL return; on non-HAL_OK emit a sentinel (e.g. "----/--/-- --:--:--") instead of garbage. Add a one-line comment stating the GetTime-before-GetDate shadow-register lock invariant.

findings.description: Unbounded sprintf into a fixed 32-byte stack buffer. With the current struct types this cannot overflow: RTC_DateTypeDef.{Year,Month,Date} and RTC_TimeTypeDef.{Hours,Minutes,Seconds} are uint8_t, so the worst printable case '2255/255/255 255:255:255' is 24 chars + NUL = 25 bytes, within 32. So no overflow TODAY — but the safety relies entirely on the HAL field widths staying uint8_t and on RTC_FORMAT_BIN (BCD format would change ranges). The structs are also passed to HAL by pointer without being zero-initialized (line 40-41); if a HAL read fails and leaves fields untouched, sprintf formats uninitialized stack bytes.
findings.impact: No overflow in the current build. Residual risk is reading uninitialized struct fields when a HAL read fails (see finding above), producing junk in the timestamp; and a latent overflow if anyone widens the fields or switches to a wider format. Low because the buffer margin (25/32) currently holds.
findings.recommendation: Use snprintf(timestamp, sizeof(timestamp), ...) instead of sprintf (defense-in-depth, no downside), and zero-init the two structs ({0}) so a failed HAL read yields zeros not stack garbage.

findings.description: Relies on a loose extern of the global HAL handle (extern RTC_HandleTypeDef hrtc; line 33) defined elsewhere (rtc.c), and on vMGR_LOG_printf which — when USE_LOCAL_PRINTF is NOT defined — macro-expands to plain blocking printf (mgr_log.h:257). The function/comments call this an 'atomic ring-buffer add' (lines 61-62), but that is only true under USE_LOCAL_PRINTF; in the printf fallback build the comment is wrong (rotted). Also the '%s' indirection (line 62) is correct/safe (avoids treating the timestamp as a format string) but redundant given the content is fixed digits.
findings.impact: Comment-rot only; no functional defect. The 'atomic' claim could mislead a maintainer into assuming ISR-safety that does not hold in a non-USE_LOCAL_PRINTF build.
findings.recommendation: Drop or qualify the 'atomic' comment, or assert USE_LOCAL_PRINTF if this path is meant to be ring-buffered. If the function is deleted per the dead-code finding, this is moot.

findings.description: No unit test exercises MGR_LOG_RtcDateTime(). The formatting logic (zero-padding, 2000+Year base, BIN format) is pure and trivially testable with a mocked HAL_RTC_GetTime/GetDate returning known values, plus an out-of-range case (e.g. Year=255) to lock in the 32-byte buffer-bound assumption.
findings.impact: If the function is ever revived, a struct-field-width change or format change could silently overflow the buffer with no regression guard.
findings.recommendation: If the function is kept, add a Tests/unit case mocking the HAL RTC getters and asserting the exact output string and that the formatted length stays < sizeof(timestamp). If it is deleted, no test is needed.

dead_code: MGR_LOG_RtcDateTime() (the file's only function, lines 38-63) is a genuine orphan — no live caller in any config. It is NOT config-gated: the TU is built unconditionally (Makefile:209) and the function is unguarded. The only references are in generated Doxygen HTML under Kineis/Doc/ that mirror a legacy mgr_log.h whose DEBUG/VERBOSE macros once expanded to this function; the current mgr_log.h (lines 64-93) routes logging through vMGR_LOG_printf_ts_lvl() instead. Likely linker-GC'd if -ffunction-sections/--gc-sections is enabled, otherwise dead weight in the image.
test_coverage: n/a today (the function is unreachable, so absence of a test has no live impact). If revived, the pure formatting path SHOULD have a Tests/unit case with mocked HAL_RTC getters covering nominal and out-of-range (Year=255) inputs to guard the 32-byte buffer bound. No such test exists.

role: Brian Gladman 8-bit reference AES (ECB single-block + CBC, prekeyed enc/dec). Backs the mcu_aes.c wrapper (MCU_AES_128_cbc_*) which libkineis.a uses to AES-CBC the Argos protocol payload.
compiled_in: all (in C_SOURCES unconditionally, Makefile:213). Function-level gating via AES_*_PREKEYED / *_OTFK in aes.h: only AES_ENC_PREKEYED + AES_DEC_PREKEYED are enabled; all OTFK variants are #if 0.

findings.description: HAVE_UINT_32T is gated on `#if ( __CORTEX_M != 0 )`, but __CORTEX_M is a CMSIS macro defined only inside core_cm4.h / core_cm0.h etc. aes.c includes only <stdlib.h>, <stdint.h>, <aes.h> (which pulls only <stdint.h>) before line 50, and no CMSIS/stm32wlxx.h header is force-included by the Makefile (it defines -DCORE_CM4, NOT __CORTEX_M). At line 50 __CORTEX_M is therefore UNDEFINED, so the preprocessor evaluates `#if (0 != 0)` = false and HAVE_UINT_32T is never defined.
findings.impact: All block ops (copy_block, xor_block, copy_and_key) fall back to the 16x byte-at-a-time path instead of 4x 32-bit. AES is functionally correct but ~3-4x slower. On a sealed battery deployment every extra CPU cycle awake during MAC frame encryption is energy; AES runs on every TX. This is the opposite of the intent of the gate (Cortex-M4 is supposed to take the fast path).
findings.recommendation: Replace the fragile CMSIS-macro test with the project's own build flag, e.g. `#if defined(CORE_CM4) || defined(STM32WL55xx)` (both are -D'd by the Makefile), or include stm32wlxx.h before the test. WARNING: enabling the 32-bit path also activates the strict-aliasing/unaligned casts below — do NOT flip it without first guaranteeing 4-byte alignment of all in/out/iv/ksch buffers. Add an AES KAT unit test so a flag flip is validated.

findings.description: The HAVE_UINT_32T branches cast void*/uint8_t* to uint32_t* and dereference (((uint32_t*)d)[0]). This is both a strict-aliasing violation (UB) and an unaligned-access hazard if the underlying buffer is not 4-byte aligned. The single-block scratch arrays (s1/s2[N_BLOCK] uint8_t) and ksch are not guaranteed 32-bit aligned, and caller in/out/iv come from libkineis with unknown alignment.
findings.impact: Currently DORMANT because HAVE_UINT_32T is not defined (see build-config finding), so these branches do not compile. Latent landmine: if the __CORTEX_M gate is 'fixed' to enable the fast path, these casts become live and can fault or be miscompiled (aliasing UB). The two findings interact — naively fixing the perf gate re-introduces a brick/corruption risk.
findings.recommendation: If/when the 32-bit path is enabled, force alignment with an aligned scratch buffer and memcpy the caller's in/out, or keep byte ops. Do not enable without the alignment guarantee.

findings.description: All four 'on-the-fly' keying variants (aes_encrypt_128, aes_decrypt_128, aes_encrypt_256, aes_decrypt_256) and their static helpers (update_encrypt_key_128/256, update_decrypt_key_128/256) are gated by AES_ENC/DEC_128/256_OTFK, every one of which is #if 0 in aes.h:46-57. Dead in ALL build configs — intentional, config-gated (upstream reference ships them; this project only uses prekeyed CBC).
findings.impact: No functional impact. ~265 lines of never-compiled code carried for upstream parity. Slight maintenance/audit noise only.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is (preserve upstream diffability) OR strip the OTFK blocks to shrink the audit surface of a security-sensitive file. Do not 'fix' bugs inside these dead blocks.

findings.description: Three sets of mutually-exclusive alternative implementations are permanently selected at compile time: USE_TABLES is #if 1 so the runtime field-math path (hibit, gf_inv, fwd_affine, inv_affine, function-form s_box, lines 223-306) is dead; HAVE_MEMCPY is #if 0 so block_copy_nn always maps to copy_block_nn; VERSION_1 is #if 1 so all the #else two-buffer (s2) variants are dead. All three are intentional config switches, not orphans.
findings.impact: None functionally. With USE_TABLES on, the f4/fd/fe/d2 macros are used only as compile-time table initializers, never at runtime. No risk.
findings.recommendation: No action. Recorded only so a future reader does not 'clean up' the live table path by mistake.

findings.description: Inconsistent error-return style. aes_set_key (526) and aes_encrypt (592) return ( uint8_t )-1 with an explicit cast; aes_decrypt (644) returns bare -1. return_type is uint8_t (aes.h:64), so -1 is implicitly converted to 255 — same value, but it is an implicit signed-to-unsigned narrowing (MISRA 10.x) and asymmetric with the siblings.
findings.impact: No behavioral bug: callers test != EXIT_SUCCESS (0) / != 0, and 255 != 0. Purely a consistency / static-analysis nit.
findings.recommendation: Make line 644 `return ( uint8_t )-1;` to match. No semantic change.

findings.description: aes_cbc_encrypt/decrypt return EXIT_SUCCESS/EXIT_FAILURE (from <stdlib.h>, 0/1) while the declared return_type is uint8_t and the rest of the file uses 0 / (uint8_t)-1. The wrapper mcu_aes.c:69,78 correctly tests != EXIT_SUCCESS, so the contract holds end-to-end, but mixing conventions in one file is a readability trap.
findings.impact: None — EXIT_SUCCESS==0 matches the success convention and the wrapper compares against EXIT_SUCCESS. Cosmetic.
findings.recommendation: Optional: standardize on one success/fail convention across aes.c.

findings.description: No unit test exists for AES anywhere in Tests/ (grep for aes_set_key/aes_cbc_encrypt/MCU_AES across Tests/ returns nothing; no Tests/**/*aes* file). This is the cryptographic core of the Argos uplink: a silent miscompile (e.g. the alignment/aliasing landmine if the 32-bit path is enabled, or table corruption) would produce frames the satellite cannot decode, with no on-device feedback in a sealed unit.
findings.impact: An AES regression is not caught by the suite (506 tests, none touch AES). In a sealed 12-month deployment a broken cipher means total, silent loss of all telemetry — high consequence, currently zero guard.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit using FIPS-197 / NIST CBC vectors: (1) aes_set_key + aes_encrypt single-block KAT; (2) aes_cbc_encrypt then aes_cbc_decrypt round-trip, multi-block, non-zero IV; (3) the MCU_AES wrapper incl. the flash-empty -> test key fallback (mcu_aes.c:104). Run with and without HAVE_UINT_32T forced so the perf-path fix can be validated before flashing.

dead_code: Config-gated (intentional, not orphans): (1) All OTFK functions and helpers, aes.c:671-937 — AES_*_OTFK all #if 0 in aes.h, dead in every config. (2) Non-table field-math path hibit/gf_inv/fwd_affine/inv_affine and function-form s_box/gfm macros, aes.c:223-306 — USE_TABLES is #if 1. (3) HAVE_MEMCPY branch (aes.c:35-42, 308-310) — #if 0, block_copy_nn always uses copy_block_nn. (4) All VERSION_1 #else two-buffer variants (453-455,484-486,582-587,635-640,711-716,766-770,838-848,922-933) — VERSION_1 is #if 1. (5) HAVE_UINT_32T branches in copy_block/xor_block/copy_and_key — dead because __CORTEX_M is undefined at the gate; this one is dead UNINTENTIONALLY (broken gate, see build-config finding). No genuine orphans: every live static is reachable (copy_block_nn<-block_copy_nn<-aes_set_key; copy_block/xor_block/copy_and_key/add_round_key/shift_sub_rows/inv_shift_sub_rows/mix_sub_columns/inv_mix_sub_columns all used by prekeyed enc/dec which the wrapper calls).
test_coverage: NONE. No AES unit test in Tests/ at all. The testable logic is pure, deterministic, HW-free (table-driven AES on byte arrays) and is ideally unit-testable with NIST KAT/CBC vectors, yet has zero coverage. Highest-value gap: a known-answer + CBC round-trip test, runnable with and without HAVE_UINT_32T, to lock correctness and gate any future fix of the broken __CORTEX_M perf flag. The wrapper's flash-empty -> test_device_secret_key fallback (mcu_aes.c:96-106) is also untested.

role: MCU wrapper that adapts the closed-source libkineis AES contract (MCU_AES_128_init/cbc_encrypt/cbc_decrypt) to Brian Gladman's software AES-128 (aes.c), and stores/loads the 16-byte Device Secret Key (DSK) in FLASH_USER.
compiled_in: all (linked into every APP/BOARD/COMM config; MCU_AES_128_init is an undefined symbol required by libkineis.a, so it is always pulled in for the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE/UART target)

findings.description: When the flash SECKEY region reads all-0xFF (erased / never provisioned / page-corrupted), MCU_AES_get_device_sec_key silently substitutes the hard-coded, publicly-known test key {00 11 22 ... FF} and returns KNS_STATUS_OK. MCU_AES_128_init(NULL) then also returns OK. No error is propagated to any caller.
findings.impact: On a sealed, epoxy-potted UW_DOPPLER unit there is no way to detect this on the bench after potting. If credentials were not correctly written (or the FLASH_USER page was erased by a stray erase / wear-leveling bug), the device transmits Argos frames encrypted with a well-known key for ~12 months with no indication of failure. It also makes 'device not provisioned' indistinguishable from 'device provisioned' at the AES layer. This silently defeats the security model the file's own header (lines 32-42) claims to uphold.
findings.recommendation: Do not silently fall back to a fixed test key in a production build. Either: (a) gate the test-key fallback behind a DEBUG/non-sealed build flag and return a distinct status (e.g. KNS_STATUS_MCU_AES_ERR or a new CRED-missing code) in production so the upper layer can refuse to TX / signal via LED; or (b) keep the fallback but log a loud one-shot warning and surface a queryable 'using default key' flag. The sealed-deploy path must treat all-0xFF DSK as a hard fault, not a usable key.

findings.description: MCU_AES_128_cbc_encrypt/decrypt forward in/out/iv/nb_block straight to aes_cbc_encrypt/decrypt with no NULL or range validation. aes.c uses `while(n_block--)`, so a negative nb_block (int32_t) loops ~2^31 times reading/writing far past the buffers; a NULL in/out/iv faults inside aes.c.
findings.impact: Caller is closed-source libkineis (a trusted boundary per the audit rules), so this is not currently reachable from our code. But the wrapper is the only place WE control the boundary, and an out-of-range nb_block would be an unbounded out-of-bounds memcpy/encrypt (brick/corruption) rather than a clean KNS error return.
findings.recommendation: Add cheap guards at the wrapper: reject in==NULL || out==NULL || iv==NULL and nb_block<=0 (or an upper sanity bound) returning KNS_STATUS_MCU_AES_ERR. Pure defensive hardening at the trust boundary; no behavior change for valid calls.

findings.description: Inconsistent error codes: MCU_AES_128_init returns KNS_STATUS_MCU_AES_ERR on every failure, but MCU_AES_set/get_device_sec_key return the generic KNS_STATUS_ERROR on a NULL argument and propagate the raw MCU_FLASH_* status otherwise. The AES-specific code 400 is never used by the get/set helpers.
findings.impact: Callers (mgr_at_cmd_list_general.c:87/117, mgr_spi_cmd_list_general.c:258/320) only test `!= KNS_STATUS_OK`, so behavior is correct today, but diagnostics/log triage can't distinguish an AES-key fault from a generic error.
findings.recommendation: Use KNS_STATUS_MCU_AES_ERR consistently for AES-domain failures, or document why FLASH status is intentionally passed through.

findings.description: MCU_AES_128_init always passes DSK_BYTE_LENGTH (16) as keylen to aes_set_key for BOTH the NULL (DSK) path and the caller-supplied key[] path. The API `uint8_t key[]` decays to a pointer with no length, so a caller-supplied buffer shorter than 16 bytes would be over-read inside aes_set_key/block_copy_nn.
findings.impact: libkineis is the only caller of MCU_AES_128_init (undefined symbol), and it is assumed to pass 16-byte keys, so not reachable from our code. Latent over-read if the contract ever changes; only 16/24/32 are valid keylens for aes_set_key, and the wrapper hard-codes 16.
findings.recommendation: Document the 16-byte precondition on the public key[] parameter in mcu_aes.h (it currently says nothing about required length), and add a _Static_assert(DSK_BYTE_LENGTH==16) to lock the assumption.

findings.description: The file header (lines 32-42) states the DSK 'cannot appear clearly inside device memory' and should be stored encrypted, yet: the static `ctx` holds the expanded plaintext key schedule for the device lifetime, the DSK is written to flash in cleartext (mcu_aes.h:92 'No AES key encryption used for the moment'), and the stack copies device_secret_key (line 52) and callers' sec_key buffers are never scrubbed (no memset-to-zero) after use.
findings.impact: On a sealed deployment a flash/RAM dump (e.g. via an exposed SWD pad before potting, or an RDP-bypass) trivially recovers the DSK. The comment over-claims the security posture, which is a comment-rot/false-assurance risk.
findings.recommendation: Either implement the at-rest protection the header promises (out of scope per CLAUDE 'TX power / crypto' boundaries — confirm with user), or soften the header comment to reflect the actual cleartext storage so future readers aren't misled. As a minimal hardening, memset the transient stack key buffers after aes_set_key/flash write.

findings.description: No unit test in Tests/unit exercises mcu_aes.c (grep for MCU_AES in Tests returns nothing). The all-0xFF -> test-key fallback, the NULL-argument guards, and the flash round-trip are all pure, mockable logic (MCU_FLASH_read/write are already the kind of HAL/MCU functions the test framework mocks, e.g. test_nvm.c / test_cred_mirror.c).
findings.impact: The highest-severity finding here (silent test-key fallback on erased flash) is exactly the sort of regression a unit test would catch, and it ships in the sealed build.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_mcu_aes.c: (1) get_device_sec_key with mocked all-0xFF flash returns the test key AND/OR a distinct 'unprovisioned' status (per the fix chosen); (2) get/set with NULL returns error and performs no flash write; (3) set then get round-trips a non-0xFF key; (4) init(NULL) propagates a get failure as KNS_STATUS_MCU_AES_ERR.

dead_code: none. All five functions are live: MCU_AES_128_init is an undefined symbol resolved for libkineis.a (Kineis/Lib/libkineis_undefined_symbols.txt:13); cbc_encrypt/decrypt are the AES primitives the MAC calls; set/get_device_sec_key are called from AT (mgr_at_cmd_list_general.c:87,117) and SPI (mgr_spi_cmd_list_general.c:258,320) command handlers. The static test_device_secret_key[] IS referenced (line 105) — not dead, but its use is the high-severity concern above. No unused statics/params/returns.
test_coverage: Currently zero coverage (no test references MCU_AES). The testable logic (0xFF-fallback decision, NULL guards, flash offset/size usage) is fully unit-testable with mocked MCU_FLASH_read/write — see the test-gap finding. The aes.c primitive itself is third-party (Gladman) and out of this file's scope.

role: Low-level STM32WL flash driver: page read-modify-write of FLASH_USER (creds/config) plus wear-leveled MSG/WKU counters (slot-fill + overflow word).
compiled_in: all (no APP/BOARD/COMM guards; entire file always compiled. Counter APIs only exercised by UW_DOPPLER/DOPPLER via mcu_nvm.c; MCU_FLASH_read/write used by all apps via mcu_nvm/mgr_cred/mcu_aes)

findings.description: Every write/erase path uses bare __disable_irq()/__enable_irq() instead of save/restore of PRIMASK. __enable_irq() is UNCONDITIONAL: if any caller invokes these with interrupts already masked (its own critical section), the flash op forcibly re-enables IRQs mid-operation, corrupting the caller's atomicity. Also each function leaves a window where it enables IRQs at function entry-state regardless of prior state.
findings.impact: In the sealed deployment, MCU_NVM_setMC / credential restore / WKU increment run from main context today (verified callers: mcu_nvm.c, kns_app_doppler.c, mgr_cred.c — none in ISR), so currently latent. But it is a brittle invariant: any future caller holding a critical section (e.g. during STOP entry or a credential atomic restore) would have its IRQ mask silently dropped, risking a spurious wake/reentrancy during a flash erase. Should save PRIMASK and restore it.
findings.recommendation: Replace each __disable_irq()/__enable_irq() pair with `uint32_t pm = __get_PRIMASK(); __disable_irq(); ...; __set_PRIMASK(pm);` so the prior interrupt state is restored, never force-enabled.

findings.description: The WL-full overflow branch first calls MCU_FLASH_write(of_addr,...) (which internally does its own full unlock/disable/erase/program/enable/lock cycle and RE-ENABLES IRQs + LOCKS flash on return), then immediately does a SECOND independent HAL_FLASH_Unlock()/__disable_irq()/erase/program/__enable_irq()/HAL_FLASH_Lock() to reset the WL area. There are thus two non-atomic flash transactions for one logical 'overflow' event: a brownout/reset BETWEEN them leaves the overflow word incremented but the WL slots still full (or partially reset), so read_wear_counter returns overflow*1024 + 1024 = a double-count jump of up to 1023 on next boot.
findings.impact: Counter (MSG or WKU) can jump by up to ~1024 across a reset that lands in this rare window (~every 1024 counts). For WKU this skews the duty-cycle modulo boot decision; for MSG the high-water shadow leaps forward, skipping MC values (no on-air replay, but wasted MC space). Not a brick, but a silent correctness defect in a sealed unit. The in-code comment (lines 283-290) already warns the page-0 erase here can corrupt credentials on brownout.
findings.recommendation: Document the non-atomicity explicitly and accept the forward-only skew, OR reorder so the WL-area erase/reset completes before the overflow word is bumped (overflow word is the authoritative high digit; bumping it last keeps monotonicity). Add a unit test that simulates a reset between the two transactions.

findings.description: MCU_FLASH_read does memcpy(buffer,(void*)address,size) with NO bounds check on address/size — only a null/zero-size guard. address is a fully attacker/caller-controlled uint32_t; it will happily memcpy from any mapped address (peripheral regs, outside flash, wrap past 0xFFFFFFFF). Unlike MCU_FLASH_write, which validates against FLASH_USER range, the read path is unguarded.
findings.impact: A bad address from a future caller (or a corrupted offset constant) reads arbitrary memory into the destination buffer instead of failing — could leak/garble credentials or fault. Low probability with current fixed-offset callers, but it is an unbounded-trust primitive in a safety-critical file.
findings.recommendation: Add a sanity check that [address, address+size) lies within the readable flash window (FLASH_BASE..FLASH_END_ADDR) before the memcpy; return KNS_STATUS_FLASH_ERR otherwise. Watch for address+size integer overflow in the check.

findings.description: WaitReady only polls FLASH_FLAG_BSY then unconditionally CLEARS all error flags (WRPERR/PGAERR/SIZERR/PGSERR/EOP) and returns OK. It never INSPECTS those flags. So a prior write-protect or programming-alignment error is wiped without being reported. It is called BEFORE erase/program (correct: clear stale flags) but there is no post-operation verify other than HAL_FLASH_Program's own return — and after HAL_FLASHEx_Erase the error flags from a failed erase could be masked on the next WaitReady call.
findings.impact: Genuine flash faults (e.g. WRPERR because a page is option-byte write-protected, or PGSERR) are silently swallowed by the flag-clear, so the retry loop in MCU_FLASH_write may report success on a page that did not actually take. For sealed creds/counters that is a silent-corruption path. Mitigated partly because HAL_FLASH_Program returns the HAL error, but the clear-before-check ordering defeats post-mortem diagnosis.
findings.recommendation: Either rename to reflect it is a clear-stale-flags helper, or have it return the error-flag state so callers can distinguish a real WRPERR. Consider a read-back verify of programmed double-words for the credential page.

findings.description: The BSY wait loop uses HAL_GetTick() for its timeout. These flash ops run inside __disable_irq() (lines 133/226/303/345/387). On STM32WL, HAL_GetTick increments via the SysTick interrupt; with IRQs disabled SysTick does not advance, so `HAL_GetTick() - start` stays 0 forever and the 500 ms timeout NEVER fires. If BSY were ever stuck, this becomes an infinite hang with interrupts off — an unrecoverable brick (no watchdog kick, no wake).
findings.impact: Critical-class failure mode IF BSY hangs: in the sealed unit the CPU would spin forever with IRQs masked, requiring physical power-cycle which is impossible (epoxy-sealed). In practice flash BSY clears in microseconds so the timeout is effectively dead code, but the safety-net it claims to provide does not exist while IRQs are masked. The first WaitReady in MCU_FLASH_write (line 135) runs after __disable_irq at 133, so its timeout is non-functional.
findings.recommendation: Don't rely on HAL_GetTick inside an IRQ-disabled section. Use a bounded busy-loop counter (cycle budget) for the timeout, or read DWT->CYCCNT, so the timeout actually fires with IRQs off. Confirm IWDG is configured to reset on a stuck-BSY hang as a backstop.

findings.description: After HAL_FLASHEx_Erase, set_wear_counter programs `index` slots in a loop with HAL_FLASH_Program but does NOT call MCU_FLASH_WaitReady between iterations (HAL_FLASH_Program internally waits, so functionally OK), yet it also never re-waits/verifies after the LAST program before HAL_FLASH_Lock. More importantly: index = value % wl_size with wl_size=1024; if a caller passes value with a large modulus the loop runs up to 1023 double-word programs under __disable_irq() — a long (~ms) critical section with IRQs fully masked. WKU setter (MCU_NVM_setWUC) feeds a 16-bit value, so index can be up to 1023.
findings.impact: Up to ~1023 sequential blocking flash programs with all interrupts disabled = multi-millisecond IRQ blackout on an operator AT+DPLWKU set / MC far-jump. Spurious-wake and timing-sensitive paths (RTC, SWS) are blind during this. Rare (operator-triggered), but worth bounding.
findings.recommendation: Move the per-iteration work outside the global IRQ-disable, or chunk the disable around each program rather than the whole loop. Confirm worst-case latency is acceptable vs IWDG window.

findings.description: page_backup is a function-static 2 KB buffer (256 x uint64_t = 2048 B in .bss). It is the full-page RMW scratch for MCU_FLASH_write. Being static (not stack) it is safe for stack budget, but it is a permanently-resident 2 KB and is NOT reentrant: two concurrent MCU_FLASH_write calls would clobber each other's backup. Current callers are single-threaded main context (baremetal), so safe today.
findings.impact: 2 KB permanent RAM cost on a RAM-constrained part; reentrancy hazard if any flash write were ever triggered from both main and an ISR/callback. No current defect.
findings.recommendation: Keep static (stack would be worse) but add a comment that MCU_FLASH_write is not reentrant and must only be called from main context. Optionally _Static_assert the buffer size matches FLASH_PAGE_SIZE.

findings.description: MCU_FLASH_increment_wku_counter() returns KNS_status_t but the return is IGNORED at its only live caller (kns_app_doppler.c:346). If the increment fails (flash fault / timeout), the boot counter does not advance and the duty-cycle modulo decision repeats the same boot_count next cycle.
findings.impact: A persistent flash failure would freeze the WKU counter, making the duty-cycle either always-skip or always-transmit depending on modulo phase — degraded but not a brick. Low likelihood.
findings.recommendation: At least log on failure at the call site; consider a fallback (e.g. RAM-retained counter) so a flash-write fault does not lock the duty cycle.

findings.description: MCU_FLASH_reset_msg_counter has ZERO live callers (grep confirms only its own definition + the doc comment). Its twin MCU_FLASH_reset_wku_counter IS wired via AT+DPLWKU=0 (mgr_at_cmd_list_doppler.c:113).
