This is a documented intentional orphan (commit 15d349d / file doc-comment lines 435-438) kept for a future AT+DPLMC=0/SAV reset.
findings.impact: None functional — config-independent genuine orphan, explicitly documented as a kept future hook. No reachability risk; included in all builds (small code size cost).
findings.recommendation: Acceptable as documented. If size matters, gate behind a feature macro. No action required.

findings.description: extern uint32_t _sflash_user_data is declared (linker symbol from STM32WL55XX_FLASH_APP.ld:273) and marked 'optional use' but is referenced nowhere in C (grep: only the .ld definitions + this extern). Lines 111-115 are a commented-out legacy counter API. Both are documentation/legacy cruft.
findings.impact: None — unused extern and dead comments. No code emitted.
findings.recommendation: Remove the unused extern and the commented-out prototypes to reduce rot, or leave with a note. Cosmetic.

findings.description: The entire counter/write block is wrapped in #pragma GCC optimize("O0"), disabling all optimization for ~380 lines. This is presumably to keep the IRQ-disabled flash timing deterministic / avoid reordering, but it is undocumented (no comment explaining WHY). O0 here bloats code size and slows the IRQ-disabled critical sections (worsening the long-blackout concern in the set_wear_counter finding).
findings.impact: Larger code, longer IRQ-off windows than necessary, and unclear intent for future maintainers. Not a correctness bug.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment justifying the O0 region (e.g. 'avoid reordering of flash unlock/program sequence' or 'retain proven timing'), or replace with targeted `volatile`/barriers and re-enable optimization. The __DSB/__ISB at 201-202 suggest barriers are already used.

findings.description: Validation order: (1) FLASH_USER range, (2) single-page / page-crossing, (3) 64-bit alignment. The alignment check is LAST, after page math (line 102 `address % FLASH_PAGE_SIZE`) already ran on a possibly-misaligned address. The math is still correct, but checking alignment before the page-boundary computation would be cleaner and is the conventional order. Also error logs use %lu with `size` (size_t) — on this target size_t is 32-bit so it matches, but it is technically format-mismatch-prone if size_t width changes.
findings.impact: No functional defect on this target. Style/robustness nit.
findings.recommendation: Move the alignment check ahead of the page-boundary math; cast size to (unsigned long) in the %lu logs for portability.

findings.location: Tests/unit (no direct test of mcu_flash.c logic)
findings.description: The wear-counter math (read_wear_counter, increment_wear_counter overflow/reset, set_wear_counter index loop) is unit-tested only via a MIRRORED COPY of the logic inside test_mc_wear.c (lines 44-92) and an OUTDATED mirror in test_mc_wrap.c — NOT the actual mcu_flash.c functions. The real functions' flash-address arithmetic (start_addr+i*8, page-number = (addr-FLASH_BASE)/PAGE, NbPages=(wl_size*8)/PAGE), the overflow*wl_size+valid_index reconstruction, and the two-transaction overflow path have NO direct test. test_memory_safety.c/test_nvm.c mock MCU_FLASH_read/write entirely, so the page-RMW backup/range/page-cross logic of the real MCU_FLASH_write is also untested.
findings.impact: The mirror in test_mc_wear.c already DIVERGED from the real code (it masks &0xFFFF where the real mcu_nvm.c masks &0x1FF, and lacks the 9-bit ring-distance fix) — proof the mirror does not guard the real implementation. Real off-by-one or address-math regressions in mcu_flash.c would pass CI. For a sealed-deploy file that erases the credential page, this is a meaningful coverage gap.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit test that compiles the REAL mcu_flash.c counter functions against a fake flash array (HAL_FLASH_Program/Erase mocked to a RAM model), exercising: valid_index reconstruction across overflow, WL-full -> overflow+reset, set_wear_counter for value%1024 boundary (0, 1, 1023, exactly 1024), and MCU_FLASH_write range/page-cross/alignment rejections + correct RMW preservation of untouched bytes.

dead_code: MCU_FLASH_reset_msg_counter (mcu_flash.c:441) — genuine orphan, 0 callers, intentionally kept + documented for a future AT+DPLMC=0 reset (twin reset_wku IS wired via AT+DPLWKU=0). extern _sflash_user_data (mcu_flash.h:104) — declared, never referenced in C (only the .ld symbol). Commented-out legacy counter prototypes (mcu_flash.h:111-115). The 500ms HAL_GetTick timeout in MCU_FLASH_WaitReady is effectively dead inside IRQ-disabled sections (SysTick frozen, can never expire). #ifdef DEBUG error log (line 184-188) compiled out for DEBUG=0. No config-gated dead code — file is built in all configs.
test_coverage: Partial / indirect only. The wear-counter semantics are tested via a hand-mirrored copy in Tests/unit/test_mc_wear.c (and a stale mirror in test_mc_wrap.c), NOT the real mcu_flash.c functions — and that mirror has already drifted from the real implementation (0xFFFF vs 0x1FF mask), so it does not protect the shipped code. MCU_FLASH_read/write are fully mocked in test_memory_safety.c/test_nvm.c, leaving the real page read-modify-write, FLASH_USER range guard, page-cross/alignment rejection, and the two-transaction overflow path with NO direct unit test. Concrete gap: no test compiles the actual counter/write code against a RAM-backed fake flash. Recommend adding one (see test-gap finding).

role: MCU wrappers for the RF driver: external-PA on/off (PSU_EN GPIO + delays), RF power-level settings, TCXO force-state/warmup, a PA stuck-on watchdog, and the TPS63901 VSEL (1.8V/3V3) control on SMD_STDALONE.
compiled_in: all (file always compiled). Most of the PA body is gated by SMD_PA||SMD_STDALONE||SMD_OP; SMD_NOPA gets empty turn_on/off_pa. Sealed target = APP=UW_DOPPLER BOARD=SMD_STDALONE COMM=UART.

findings.description: MCU_MISC_turn_on_pa() and turn_off_pa() are explicitly documented (lines 76, 187) to run under the SUBGHZ ISR during continuous modulated wave. Yet they call MGR_LOG_DEBUG (line 91, line 191) which in DEBUG builds aliases to MGR_LOG_AT(LVL_TRACE,...) -> vMGR_LOG_printf_ts_lvl, a variadic ring-buffer printf (mgr_log.h:68, 184). getSettingsHwRf() also uses MGR_LOG_VERBOSE (same TRACE ring path). The ring-buffer log writer is the same code path that main-loop and other contexts use; it is not documented as reentrant/ISR-safe and does RTC-timestamp + ring index manipulation. An ISR-time PA toggle interleaving with a main-loop MGR_LOG_flush can corrupt the ring head/tail or produce a torn line.
findings.impact: In a DEBUG-instrumented sealed unit, a TX (ISR) firing while the main loop is flushing the log ring can corrupt the log ring buffer (lost/garbled diagnostics) or, depending on the ring implementation, hang the flush. Not a brick by itself, but it poisons exactly the forensic logs you rely on for a sealed deployment. Compiled out in DEBUG=0 production, so the shipped binary is safe — risk is confined to debug-instrumented field units.
findings.recommendation: Drop the unconditional MGR_LOG_DEBUG/MGR_LOG_VERBOSE from these ISR-reachable functions, or move them behind the same direct-UART HAL_UART_Transmit pattern already used for the TRACE markers (lines 84-89), which bypasses the ring. At minimum confirm the ring writer disables IRQs around the head/tail update.

findings.description: MGR_LED_off() is called from inside turn_on_pa(), which per the file's own header (line 76) may execute in SUBGHZ ISR context. MGR_LED control typically reconfigures GPIO / soft-PWM state shared with the main-loop LED manager. If the LED manager mutates shared state without a critical section, an ISR-time MGR_LED_off() racing a main-loop LED update can leave the LED driver in an inconsistent mode.
findings.impact: On SMD_STDALONE only. Worst case is a stuck/wrong LED color after TX (cosmetic) or a GPIO mode left wrong on a pin shared with the bootloader SPI bus. Not power/brick critical, but a shared-state race in an ISR path.
findings.recommendation: Verify MGR_LED_off() is ISR-safe (no long work, no unguarded shared-state mutation). If it is not, shed LED current via a direct HAL_GPIO_WritePin on the three LED pins instead of the manager call, or guard the call so it only runs when invoked from main-loop TX setup, not the continuous-wave ISR.

findings.description: On SMD_STDALONE turn_on_pa() busy-waits via the __NOP() DELAY_MS macro for MCU_PA_PRECHARGE_DELAY_MS(5) + MCU_PA_BOOTDELAY_MS(250, mcu_misc.h:33) + MCU_PA_TCXO_STABILIZATION_MS(200) = 455 ms of pure spin with no WFI and no watchdog refresh. Because this can run in the SUBGHZ ISR, that is up to 455 ms with the CPU pinned in an interrupt, blocking the main loop (and thus MGR_WDG_refresh at kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1750) for that entire window.
findings.impact: 455 ms of busy-wait per PA-on burns CPU current (no low-power wait) and, if it occurs in ISR, stalls the main loop including IWDG refresh. A normal TX is well under the IWDG window so it won't reset, but it both wastes battery (spin instead of WFI) and narrows the IWDG margin during multi-frame TX bursts. The PA pre-charge/boot/TCXO delays are real HW requirements (caps confirmed, memory/pa_brownout.md), so they cannot simply be removed.
findings.recommendation: Accept the delay length (HW-mandated) but document that it is ISR-blocking, and ensure the longest BLIND retx pattern plus 455 ms stays inside PA_WDG_THRESHOLD_MS(30 s) and the IWDG window. Consider whether the 200 ms TCXO stabilization can overlap MAC warmup instead of being a second serial spin after the 250 ms boot delay.

findings.description: No unit test references mcu_misc or MCU_MISC anywhere in Tests/unit (grep over Tests/ returns nothing). The pure-logic, HW-independent parts are eminently testable: getSettingsHwRf() power-level math + clamp + KNS_STATUS_BAD_SETTING boundary (rficPaLevel = rf_level_dBm - externalPaGain, range [-17..15] for STDALONE), and the PA watchdog arithmetic MCU_MISC_PA_isStuck()/PA_onDuration_ms() including the pa_on_tick==0 'off' sentinel and the tick-wrap subtraction.
findings.impact: The RF-level clamp guards against requesting an out-of-range PA setting (could push the RFIC out of spec) and the PA watchdog is a battery-saving / anti-brick safety net for the sealed unit — both ship untested. A regression in the clamp boundary or the isStuck threshold comparison would not be caught.
findings.recommendation: Add Tests/unit/test_mcu_misc.c mocking HAL_GetTick: cover getSettingsHwRf boundaries (-17, 15, -18, 16 after gain) for SMD_STDALONE and SMD_NOPA, and PA watchdog (armed/disarmed, exactly-at-threshold, just-over, tick wrap across 0).

findings.description: pa_on_tick uses 0 as the 'PA off' sentinel and remaps a genuine tick of 0 to 1 (line 167). Correct as written. But the isStuck/onDuration math uses unsigned subtraction HAL_GetTick()-armed; if HAL_GetTick() wraps (32-bit ms ~49.7 days) while a stale 'armed' is held, the wrap is handled correctly by modular arithmetic ONLY for durations < 2^31 ms. With the 30 s threshold this is never a real risk, so this is a latent/theoretical note rather than a bug.
findings.impact: No practical impact at a 30 s threshold over a 12-month deployment (tick wraps ~7 times but each measured PA-on window is seconds). Documented here for completeness since the file comments call out the torn-read but not the wrap reasoning.
findings.recommendation: No code change needed. Optionally add a one-line comment that the unsigned-wrap subtraction is safe because measured windows are << 2^31 ms.

findings.description: tcxo_warmup_time_ms (line 40) is a file-static set by MCU_MISC_TCXO_set_warmup() and read back by MCU_MISC_TCXO_get_warmup(). The value is only ever stored/retrieved here; mcu_misc.c never uses it to actually delay or program anything. The real warmup behavior lives in the MAC stack / app (kns_app_uw_doppler.c get/set around the first-TX skip). So within this file the variable is effectively a dumb getter/setter cell.
findings.impact: Not a bug — the app (UW_DOPPLER) does call get/set to save and restore warmup around the first-TX TCXO skip (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1483, 2204). The value is consumed by the closed-source MAC, not by this file. Just non-obvious that set_warmup has no local effect.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment that this is a config cell read by the MAC/app, not applied locally, so a future reader doesn't expect turn_on_pa to honor it.

findings.description: PC1 (PA_PSU_SEL) is overloaded: on non-STDALONE boards it is the PA PSU SEL line driven HIGH in turn_on_pa/turn_off_pa (lines 111/128/211, all under #if !defined(SMD_STDALONE)), while on SMD_STDALONE the SAME pin is the TPS63901 whole-board VSEL controlled by MCU_MISC_VSEL_set (line 346). The two roles are correctly separated by #if guards so they never both compile, and the header (mcu_misc.h:149-168) loudly warns VSEL_set drives the entire VSYS rail. This is correct but fragile: a future edit that forgets a guard would let RF/ISR code drive the board supply select.
findings.impact: No defect today. The danger is latent: VSEL_set drops the whole MCU+radio+TCXO rail to 1.8 V; if it were ever reachable from the PA/ISR path on STDALONE it would brown out mid-TX. The current guarding prevents that, and VSEL_set has no caller in the PA path.
findings.recommendation: Keep the guards. Consider a _Static_assert or a build-time check that PA_PSU_SEL writes and VSEL_set are mutually exclusive per board, so the invariant is enforced by the compiler rather than by convention.

findings.description: Config-gated dead code in the sealed target (UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE), all intentional: (a) the #if !defined(SMD_STDALONE) PA_PSU_SEL drive blocks (lines 106-130, 205-212) are skipped on STDALONE; (b) the #else branches of VSEL_set/VSEL_isHigh (lines 348-350, 357-359) are skipped on STDALONE; (c) USE_SMPS_BYPASS_TX blocks (93-99, 214-219) are off unless that flag is defined (not in the sealed build per the config list); (d) TCXO_FORCE_STATE_ENABLED is hardcoded 1 so the #else no-op (310-312) is dead; (e) MCU_PA_GPIO_ENABLE defaults to 1 so the skip-GPIO path (158-163) is a build-time escape hatch, not shipped. None are genuine orphans.
findings.impact: No runtime impact. All are board/flag-gated and serve other configs or are documented escape hatches.
findings.recommendation: No action. Noted for the reachability map: in the sealed config the live PA body is only lines 77-105, 114-119, 132-182 (turn_on) and 188-204 (turn_off).

findings.description: getSettingsHwRf() takes void* rfSettings and immediately casts to struct rfSettings_t* with no NULL check before dereferencing settings->externalPaGain (line 244). The caller is the closed-source MAC, which is a trusted boundary, so a NULL here would be a MAC bug. Flagging only because it's an external-facing API with a void* contract.
findings.impact: A NULL/garbage pointer from the MAC would fault on first write. Treated as trusted-boundary, so acceptable, but there is zero defensive handling.
findings.recommendation: Optional: early-return KNS_STATUS_ERROR (or equivalent) if rfSettings is NULL, to fail gracefully instead of HardFault if the MAC ABI ever changes.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. All dead code is config-gated and intentional (see the dead-code finding): the !defined(SMD_STDALONE) PA_PSU_SEL blocks, the VSEL #else branches, USE_SMPS_BYPASS_TX blocks, the TCXO_FORCE_STATE_ENABLED=0 no-op, and the MCU_PA_GPIO_ENABLE=0 escape hatch are each excluded in the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE build but live in other board/flag configs. tcxo_warmup_time_ms is a getter/setter cell consumed by the app/MAC, not locally — not dead, just non-obvious.
test_coverage: GAP. Zero tests reference mcu_misc/MCU_MISC across Tests/. Two HW-independent pieces should be unit-tested: (1) getSettingsHwRf() power math + clamp + KNS_STATUS_BAD_SETTING boundaries per board; (2) PA watchdog (PA_isStuck/PA_onDuration_ms) with mocked HAL_GetTick covering off-sentinel, at/over threshold, and tick-wrap. The GPIO/delay/SMPS/TCXO bodies are HW glue (HAL_GPIO/HAL_RCC) and reasonably n/a for unit test, but the two logic functions above are testable and currently uncovered.

role: Minimal stub wrappers for the BLIND_POS MAC-profile NVM resources (PER map, PER-to-BLIND abacus, UL-PER calibration offset). Every function is a no-op returning KNS_STATUS_DISABLED so the closed-source libkineis.a links even though BLIND_POS is never configured on any of our boards.
compiled_in: all (Makefile:215, unconditional in C_SOURCES — no APP/BOARD/COMM guard). However the 6 symbols are only *referenced* by libkineis.a when the MAC is configured for BLIND_POS, which never occurs in any shipped config (and is hard-blocked for the sealed UW_DOPPLER target).
dead_code: All 6 functions are dead at runtime in every shipped configuration — but this is intentional, not orphan code. They exist purely to satisfy the linker for libkineis.a's BLIND_POS symbol table. BLIND_POS is never selected: UW_DOPPLER forces KNS_MAC_PRFL_BASIC (Kineis/App/kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1418) and an #error guards against MAC_PRFL=BLIND_POS at compile time (kns_app_uw_doppler.c:69-71); other APPs select BASIC or BLIND, never BLIND_POS. The (void)ptr / (void)byte_size / (void)ulPerCal casts correctly suppress unused-parameter warnings — not dead code, deliberate API-contract conformance. No unused statics (file has none).

findings.description: These stubs silently disable BLIND_POS NVM persistence with no compile-time tripwire. If a future board ever enables the BLIND_POS MAC profile (the header @page and the .c top comment both describe this as a real future path), the lib will call MCU_NVM_getPerMap/getPerToBlindAbacus/getUlPerCalOffset, receive KNS_STATUS_DISABLED + NULL/0.0f, and the PER-map / abacus / UL-PER-cal persistence (part of Kineis credentials) will be silently absent. Nothing prevents a build with BLIND_POS from linking against these no-ops.
findings.impact: No impact on the current sealed deployment (UW_DOPPLER=BASIC, BLIND_POS impossible). Latent footgun only: a future BLIND_POS bring-up would appear to build and run but silently lose credential-class NVM state, degrading UL performance with no error surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Add a compile-time tripwire so this file is a hard error rather than a silent no-op under BLIND_POS, e.g. `#if defined(USE_MAC_PRFL_BLIND_POS)\n#error "mcu_nvm_blind_pos.c is a stub; BLIND_POS requires a real FLASH_USER-backed implementation"\n#endif`. Keeps the linker satisfied in all real configs while making accidental BLIND_POS adoption fail loudly.

findings.description: Header @file tag is wrong: '@file mcu_mvm_blind_pos.h' (typo 'mvm' instead of 'nvm'). Doxygen will index this file under a non-existent name and the cross-reference breaks. Vendor-origin (author Kineis), carried verbatim.
findings.impact: Documentation only; no runtime effect. Broken Doxygen anchor for this wrapper.
findings.recommendation: Correct to '@file mcu_nvm_blind_pos.h'.

findings.description: Include-guard closing comment reads '#endif /* MCU_NVM_H */' but the guard macro is MCU_NVM_BLIND_POS_H (line 70). Comment rot — risks confusion with the separate mcu_nvm.h guard.
findings.impact: None at runtime; minor readability/maintenance hazard.
findings.recommendation: Change closing comment to '/* MCU_NVM_BLIND_POS_H */'.

findings.description: const-correctness: MCU_NVM_setPerMap(void *ptr, ...) and MCU_NVM_setPerToBlindAbacus(void *ptr, ...) take a non-const input pointer for a copy-into-NVM operation; the data being read could be 'const void *'. The signatures are dictated by the libkineis ABI (must match the lib's expected prototype), so this cannot be changed unilaterally in the wrapper.
findings.impact: None — cosmetic / API-fidelity constraint. Cannot fix without the lib changing its contract.
findings.recommendation: Leave as-is to preserve ABI match with libkineis.a; note only.

findings.description: Contract consistency note: getPerMap and getPerToBlindAbacus set *ptr = NULL and return KNS_STATUS_DISABLED. The lib must treat DISABLED as 'no data, do not dereference'. Since BLIND_POS is unreachable this is never exercised, but if it ever is, the lib relying on these returning a valid pointer would NULL-deref. The NULL-write-then-DISABLED ordering is the safest possible stub behavior given the void** out-param contract.
findings.impact: None in shipped configs. Defensive behavior is already correct (NULL out + DISABLED status).
findings.recommendation: No change needed; covered by the tripwire recommendation above for the BLIND_POS-enabled future case.

test_coverage: n/a (pure no-op HW/NVM glue). No branching logic worth a unit test beyond the trivial NULL-guards. A defensive unit test could assert all 6 functions return KNS_STATUS_DISABLED and that getPerMap/getPerToBlindAbacus write NULL and getUlPerCalOffset writes 0.0f even when passed a non-NULL out-pointer — cheap and would lock the stub contract — but absence of such a test poses zero deployment risk since the code is unreachable in all shipped builds. Confirmed no existing test references these symbols.

role: MCU timer wrappers for the Kineis MAC: TX_TIMEOUT via TIM16 (500us tick) and TX_PERIOD via the RTC wake-up timer (1s tick); dispatches HAL TIM/RTC ISR callbacks through a function-pointer table stored in RTC backup registers (.lpmSection).
compiled_in: all (compiled in every APP/BOARD/COMM config; functions are exported wrappers required by closed-source libkineis/libknsrf_wl per Kineis/Lib/*_undefined_symbols.txt). No config gating in this file.

findings.description: MCU_TIM_getCount for TX_PERIOD returns `1000 * HAL_RTCEx_GetWakeUpTimer()`. HAL_RTCEx_GetWakeUpTimer reads the WUTR reload register (the configured countdown value), NOT elapsed time. The [out] param is named elapsed_time_ms but this path yields the *programmed period* in ms (e.g. always ~the full period), never a monotonically increasing elapsed time. The TX_TIMEOUT path (line 303) genuinely returns elapsed counter/2. The two handlers have inconsistent and, for TX_PERIOD, incorrect semantics vs the documented contract in mcu_tim.h:110-120 ('decrementing or incrementing timing in ms ... from start of the timer').
findings.impact: If the closed-source MAC ever calls MCU_TIM_getCount(TX_PERIOD) to measure elapsed time (e.g. to compute remaining duty-cycle or adjust scheduling), it gets a constant/wrong value. In the sealed UW_DOPPLER deployment any mis-scheduling of the TX period directly affects satellite-pass hit rate over the 12-month mission. Severity bounded by the fact that the lib's undefined-symbol list shows getCount is not required by the MAC, so it may be unreached today.
findings.recommendation: Confirm whether the MAC calls getCount(TX_PERIOD); if it does, return elapsed = programmed_period - current_countdown (period_ms - 1000*HAL_RTCEx_GetWakeUpTimer). If it does not, mark the TX_PERIOD case as unsupported/return error rather than shipping a wrong value. Fix the copy-pasted '500us-step / divide by 2' comment at line 307 which describes the TIM16 path, not RTC.

findings.description: Comment '/** Get counter value and divide it by 2 as it is currently a 500us-step counter */' is copy-pasted verbatim from the TX_TIMEOUT branch (line 302) but the TX_PERIOD code does `1000 *` (no divide-by-2, 1s RTC tick). Comment-rot: it describes the wrong timer.
findings.impact: Misleads future maintainers about the RTC tick rate; can lead to a wrong 'fix' that introduces a real 2x error.
findings.recommendation: Replace with a comment describing the 1s SPRE tick (e.g. 'RTC wake-up tick is 1s; scale to ms').

findings.description: TX_PERIOD: `cnt_val = timeout_ms / 1000; cnt_val--;` underflows for any timeout_ms < 1000 (incl. 0): cnt_val becomes 0xFFFFFFFF, then the `> cnt_val_max` check returns MCU_TIM_STATUS_ERROR. So sub-1s periods are silently rejected. The error relies on unsigned wraparound rather than an explicit guard, and there is no lower-bound validation. Also the integer division truncates: timeout_ms in [1000,1999] all map to a 1s period (1000..1999ms requested → exactly 1s armed), a quantization the caller is not told about.
findings.impact: If the MAC requests a TX period < 1000ms it gets a silent ERROR (relying on the lib to check the return); if it ignores the return the period is simply never armed and TX never fires — a stall in the sealed deployment. The truncation also means requested period accuracy is +0/-999ms.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit `if (timeout_ms < 1000) return MCU_TIM_STATUS_ERROR;` guard before the decrement to make intent clear and avoid reliance on unsigned underflow. Document the 1s quantization. Verify the MAC checks the return value of MCU_TIM_start.

findings.description: TX_TIMEOUT: `cnt_val = timeout_ms * 2 - 1;` is computed in uint32_t. For timeout_ms == 0 it underflows to 0xFFFFFFFF (caught by the > cnt_val_max check → ERROR). For large timeout_ms, `timeout_ms * 2` can overflow uint32_t before the range check (e.g. timeout_ms >= 0x80000000 wraps), so a pathological large value could wrap into the valid <=65535 window and arm a wrong (too-short) timeout. The intended limit is timeout_ms <= 32768ms (ARR 16-bit at 500us tick).
findings.impact: A bogus very-large timeout from the MAC would not be rejected and would arm a short TX-timeout, potentially aborting a transmit early. Low likelihood (MAC timeouts are small) but the guard is unsound. TX_TIMEOUT is noted 'not used so far, directly set in RFLL_WL' (mcu_tim.h:50), reducing current exposure.
findings.recommendation: Validate the input range before arithmetic: `if (timeout_ms == 0 || timeout_ms > 32768) return ERROR;` then compute cnt_val. Avoids both underflow and the multiply overflow.

findings.description: timer[].isr_cb is shared between ISR context (HAL_TIM_PeriodElapsedCallback / HAL_RTCEx_WakeUpTimerEventCallback) and main context (MCU_TIM_init/deinit writes, MCU_TIM_resetState). The struct field is not declared volatile and writes are not in a critical section. A 32-bit aligned pointer store is atomic on Cortex-M4, so tearing is not possible, but there is a benign TOCTOU window: the ISR reads cb into a local then validates+calls; if deinit NULLs it between read and call, the ISR still calls the old (still-valid, in-flash) pointer. The validity check (mcu_tim_cb_is_valid) makes a stale-pointer HardFault impossible, so impact is limited to one extra spurious callback after deinit.
findings.impact: At most one extra MAC callback invocation right after a deinit/stop race; the callback itself must tolerate being called once after disarm. No HardFault (flash-range check). Not a corruption/brick risk.
findings.recommendation: Mark isr_cb volatile for intent and/or stop the HW IRQ before clearing the pointer in deinit (HAL_TIM_Base_Stop_IT is already implicit via deinit; for the RTC path note deinit does NOT deactivate the wake-up timer — see separate finding). Document that callbacks must be idempotent after disarm.

findings.description: MCU_TIM_deinit(TX_PERIOD) does NOT call HAL_RTCEx_DeactivateWakeUpTimer — the RTC HAL DeInit is commented out (lines 220-221) to avoid clobbering RTC alarms/clock logging, and only timer[hdlr].isr_cb is NULLed. So after deinit the RTC wake-up timer HW can still be armed and will still fire WUTF; the ISR then hits the NULL-cb defensive branch (lines 160-167) which deactivates it. Functionally self-healing but means 'deinit' leaves the wake source live until the next spurious fire.
findings.impact: A wake-up timer can survive a TX_PERIOD deinit and fire once more, waking the MCU from STOP/STANDBY unexpectedly (extra wake = extra power) before the defensive branch disarms it. In the sealed low-power deployment a stray wake costs energy but the self-disarm bounds it to one event.
findings.recommendation: In the TX_PERIOD deinit case, explicitly call HAL_RTCEx_DeactivateWakeUpTimer(&hrtc) (the wake-up timer, not full RTC DeInit) so deinit truly frees the wake source. This does not touch RTC alarms/clock.

findings.description: DFU-flag aliasing comment asserts 'timer[0] overlaps TAMP BKP0R/BKP1R'. But lpm_ctxt (lpm.c:117-120, also in .lpmSection) and the .msgCntSectionData input are collected into the same .rtc_bkpr output BEFORE/around timer[] (linker .ld:256-263 lists *(.lpmSection) once, so all .lpmSection objects are grouped in link order). Whichever of lpm_ctxt/timer[] the linker places first sits at origin 0x4000B100 (BKP0R). main.c:772 documents lpm_ctxt.low_power_mode as the .lpmSection variable at that origin, implying timer[] is NOT at BKP0R but offset after lpm_ctxt. The exact BKPxR index for timer[0] is therefore link-order-dependent, not necessarily 0/1 as stated.
findings.impact: The load-bearing invariant (do NOT add a TAMP-based DFU path while the MAC owns these backup cells) remains correct regardless of exact index, so no functional bug. But the specific 'BKP0R/BKP1R' claim may be inaccurate and could mislead someone reasoning about which backup register holds the DFU flag.
findings.recommendation: Either confirm placement from the .map file and cite the actual BKPxR index, or soften the comment to 'timer[] occupies TAMP backup registers shared with lpm_ctxt and msgCnt; the bootloader DFU flag must not be routed through TAMP'. No code change needed.

findings.description: `(1 << 16)` is a signed-int literal shift. On a 32-bit int this is well-defined (65536 fits), but it is assigned to a uint32_t cnt_val_max and used in an unsigned comparison; MISRA-like discipline (per CLAUDE.md: no implicit casts, no magic numbers) prefers `(1u << 16)` or a named constant. The value 65535 is the 16-bit ARR / RTC SPRE-16BITS max and appears as a magic number in two places.
findings.impact: No runtime defect today. Style/MISRA nit; the implicit signed->unsigned conversion is the kind of thing the project's stated discipline flags.
findings.recommendation: Use `0xFFFFu` or a named `#define MCU_TIM_ARR16_MAX 0xFFFFu` for both branches; use `1u << 16` if the shift form is kept.

findings.description: MGR_LOG_VERBOSE uses %d for uint32_t and enum arguments (hdlr, timeout_ms, cnt_val, *elapsed_time_ms). Format/type mismatch (%d vs uint32_t) is technically UB per the C standard and would warn under -Wformat. These are compiled out unless VERBOSE is defined (note: line 22 '#undef VERBOSE' is itself commented out), so normally inert.
findings.impact: None in release (logs compiled out). If VERBOSE is enabled for debugging, large uint32_t values print as signed and the variadic mismatch is UB; on this ABI it is harmless in practice but violates the project's no-implicit-cast discipline.
findings.recommendation: Use %lu / %u with appropriate casts, or %PRIu32, in the verbose logs if/when re-enabled.

findings.description: MCU_TIM_start(TX_PERIOD) calls Error_Handler() if HAL_RTCEx_SetWakeUpTimer_IT fails, instead of returning MCU_TIM_STATUS_ERROR like every other failure path in this file. Error_Handler() on this project typically spins/resets. The TX_TIMEOUT branch and all switch defaults return ERROR cleanly; only this one branch escalates to a system error handler.
findings.impact: A transient RTC-arm failure converts a recoverable 'failed to start period timer' into a hard Error_Handler (potential reset/hang) in the sealed deployment, where the MAC could otherwise retry. Inconsistent error policy.
findings.recommendation: Return MCU_TIM_STATUS_ERROR instead of calling Error_Handler(), letting the caller decide. If Error_Handler is intended, document why this failure is non-recoverable.

dead_code: No genuine orphans. All exported functions (MCU_TIM_init/deinit/start/stop/suspend/resume) are required by closed-source libkineis/libknsrf_wl (Kineis/Lib/*_undefined_symbols.txt). MCU_TIM_resetState is called from main.c:831. The two HAL callbacks override HAL weak symbols (single definition, no conflict). MCU_TIM_getCount is exported but does NOT appear in the lib undefined-symbols lists, so it may currently have no live caller (effectively dead today) — but it is part of the public wrapper API and config-independent, so treat as latent rather than orphan. MCU_TIM_HDLR_TX_TIMEOUT path is largely exercise-only per mcu_tim.h:50 ('not use so far, directly set in RFLL_WL'); its branches are compiled in every config and reachable if the lib ever arms it.
test_coverage: No unit tests reference any MCU_TIM_* symbol or HAL_TIM_PeriodElapsedCallback (grep over Tests/ returns nothing). Concrete gaps that ARE pure logic and mockable: (1) MCU_TIM_start arithmetic/bounds — TX_TIMEOUT cnt_val = timeout_ms*2-1 with the 65535 cap incl. the timeout_ms==0 and overflow edge; TX_PERIOD timeout_ms/1000-1 incl. the <1000 underflow-to-ERROR case and the 1s quantization. (2) mcu_tim_cb_is_valid: NULL, below-flash (<0x08000000), at/above flash-end (>=0x08040000), and in-range pointer — the HardFault guard logic. (3) HAL_RTCEx_WakeUpTimerEventCallback NULL-cb defensive-disarm branch (verify it deactivates + clears WUTF + NULLs the entry). (4) MCU_TIM_resetState zeroes all MCU_TIM_HDLR_MAX entries. These need only HAL_* and htim16/hrtc mocks already used elsewhere in the framework. HW glue (actual HAL_TIM/RTC register effects) is n/a for unit test.

role: Kineis-stack LPM client: implements the 3 MGR_LPM client callbacks (request deepest LPM, notify-enter, notify-exit). KSTK_lpmReq maps the closed-source MAC resource bitmap (KNS_MAC_getRsrcStatus) plus a manual forced-mode override (LPM_getForcedMode) into a requested MgrLpm_LPM_t.
compiled_in: all (registered unconditionally via MGR_LPM_registerClient(mgrLpmCliKstk) at lpm.c:775; no APP/BOARD/COMM guards). Live in the sealed UW_DOPPLER/SMD_STDALONE build.

findings.description: The `if (rsrc.raw == 0x0) return LOW_POWER_MODE_SHUTDOWN;` branch is effectively unreachable in the sealed deployment after MAC init. The union's bit0 is `keepKnsCtxt`, and this file's own comment (line 42) states the Kineis MAC keeps `keepKnsCtxt=1` once initialized; kns_mac.h:71 documents the same. With keepKnsCtxt latched to 1, `rsrc.raw` is never 0, so this branch never returns SHUTDOWN via the heuristic path. SHUTDOWN is instead reached only through the forced-mode override (line 53) or the app-level LPM_shutdown* helpers. This is a config/runtime-gated dead branch, not an orphan, but the header docstring (lpm_cli_kstk.h:38 'SHUTDOWN if kineis stack is not started yet') describes behavior that effectively cannot fire in production.
findings.impact: No functional harm, but misleading: a reader/maintainer may believe the resource-driven heuristic can autonomously select SHUTDOWN, which it cannot once the MAC is running. Risk is documentation-rot leading to a wrong assumption during a future LPM change on the sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Add a one-line comment at line 70 noting keepKnsCtxt stays 1 post-init so raw is never 0 in practice (SHUTDOWN comes from the forced/app path), or gate the branch behind an explicit `!keepKnsCtxt` test to make intent obvious. Reconcile the header docstring (lpm_cli_kstk.h:35-39) with actual behavior.

findings.description: The forced-mode override returns `forced` directly when no radio op is in progress, relying on MGR_LPM_enter to mask it against lpm_config.allowedLPMbitmap. But the masking loop in mgr_lpm.c only shifts the mode RIGHT toward shallower modes (`deepest_lpm >> 1`) until a bit matches the bitmap or it underflows to 0/NONE. Consequence: if you force a mode that is NOT enabled in the bitmap, you get an arbitrary SHALLOWER allowed mode, not the forced one. Concretely, forcing SHUTDOWN (0x08) while the bitmap only allows STOP (0x02) yields STANDBY-miss->STOP, i.e. STOP, never SHUTDOWN. The header comment at lpm.h:124-127 documents that the forced mode 'must also be enabled in the bitmap', so this is by-design masking — but the masking can silently substitute a DIFFERENT mode rather than rejecting, which is surprising and not validated here.
findings.impact: On the sealed unit, an operator using AT+LPM forced override (mgr_at_cmd_list_general.c:361) to request a deep mode that is not in the bitmap will silently get a shallower mode with no error. If the operator intended SHUTDOWN for storage and the bitmap excludes it, the chip enters a shallower mode and drains battery faster than expected. Low probability (config mismatch) but it is a silent power regression with no diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: This is primarily an mgr_lpm.c masking-semantics issue, but document at the KSTK_lpmReq return site that forced modes not present in allowedLPMbitmap are silently downgraded to a shallower mode (not rejected). Consider having the AT/SPI handler reject a forced mode absent from the bitmap up front so the operator gets feedback.

findings.description: The radio-in-progress guard checks modemOn || txTimeout || rxTimeout || satDetTimeout but deliberately omits `txPeriod`, `satPassStart`, `satPassEnd` (the remaining bits of KNS_MAC_rsrcStatus_t, kns_mac.h:76-78). txPeriod is the periodic-TX timer; if it is the only active resource while a forced deep mode is set, the override returns the deep mode and the periodic-TX timer's TIM context can be lost across STOP/STANDBY/SHUTDOWN. Whether this matters depends on closed-source MAC internals (whether txPeriod must survive LPM), which cannot be verified here.
findings.impact: Potential loss of the periodic-TX cadence if a forced deep mode is applied exactly while only the txPeriod timer is pending. On a sealed unit this could shift or drop a scheduled Argos transmission until the next wake. Low probability because forced mode is an operator action, not autonomous.
findings.recommendation: Confirm with Kineis whether txPeriod (and satPassStart/End) must be preserved across LPM. If yes, add them to the SLEEP-downgrade guard at line 51. If no, add a comment explaining why they are intentionally excluded so the asymmetry is not read as an oversight.

findings.description: Inconsistent bitfield testing style and a missing-brace pattern. Line 51 tests bits by truthiness (rsrc.modemOn) while line 72 uses `rsrc.txTimeout == 1`; both are correct for 1-bit fields but the mix is noise. Also the `if (...) return LOW_POWER_MODE_SLEEP;` at lines 51-52 is a brace-less multi-line if, which the project's MISRA-like rule discourages (single-statement bodies should still be braced for safety against future edits).
findings.impact: No runtime impact. Style only; the brace-less if is a minor future-edit hazard.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on truthiness for 1-bit fields and brace the single-statement if bodies.

findings.description: KSTK_lpmReq has no dedicated unit test. The existing Tests/unit/test_lpm_gating.c mirrors `uw_doppler_lpmReq` (a different app-level function), not this stack client. None of test_lpm_gating/test_lpm_deadline/test_lpm_uw reference KSTK_lpmReq, LPM_getForcedMode, or KNS_MAC_getRsrcStatus. The forced-mode-with-radio-busy downgrade-to-SLEEP path (lines 50-53) and the rsrc->mode mapping (lines 70-74) are exactly the kind of pure decision logic the test harness can cover by mocking KNS_MAC_getRsrcStatus and LPM_getForcedMode.
findings.impact: A regression in the forced-mode safety net (e.g. dropping the modemOn check, or returning forced while TX is active) would not be caught by CI and could corrupt an in-flight TX or lose timer/SRAM context on the sealed unit.
findings.recommendation: Add a Tests/unit test for KSTK_lpmReq: (a) forced=NONE + raw=0 -> SHUTDOWN; (b) forced=NONE + txTimeout=1 -> SLEEP; (c) forced=NONE + other bits -> STANDBY; (d) forced=SHUTDOWN + modemOn=1 -> SLEEP (safety net); (e) forced=SHUTDOWN + idle -> SHUTDOWN; (f) each radio-busy bit individually triggers the SLEEP downgrade. Mock KNS_MAC_getRsrcStatus and LPM_getForcedMode.

dead_code: One config/runtime-gated dead branch: `rsrc.raw == 0x0 -> SHUTDOWN` (line 70-71) is unreachable after MAC init because keepKnsCtxt latches to 1 (per this file's comment line 42 and kns_mac.h:71). Not an orphan — it is structurally reachable but the MAC never presents raw==0 in production. KSTK_lpmNotifEnter/Exit (lines 77-85) are intentionally trivial stubs that always return true; both params are explicitly marked __attribute__((unused)). No unused statics; the mgrLpmCliKstk struct is consumed at lpm.c:775. No orphan functions.
test_coverage: Not covered. The decision logic in KSTK_lpmReq (forced override, radio-busy SLEEP downgrade, rsrc->mode mapping) is pure and mockable but has zero unit tests — existing test_lpm_gating.c tests a different function (uw_doppler_lpmReq). Concrete gaps listed in the test-gap finding. The two notify stubs are trivially true and need no test.

role: Generic low-power-mode manager: collects deepest-LPM requests from registered clients, picks the shallowest mode within the allowed bitmap, notifies clients enter/exit, and dispatches to the SLEEP/STOP/STANDBY/SHUTDOWN HAL entry helpers.
compiled_in: all (built for every APP/BOARD/COMM; MGR_LPM_enter is reached via LPM_enter() from main.c idle loop). STM32WL55xx-guarded blocks active on the sealed target; STM32L0/L4/WLE5 branches dead for this product.

findings.description: vMGR_LPM_clientNotifyEnter/Exit call kns_assert(0) -> kns_assert_failed() -> device RESET whenever a client's NotifEnter/NotifExit callback returns false. But the header contract (mgr_lpm.h:96-102) defines the false return as a legitimate 'Unable to enter/exit this LPM' veto, i.e. a normal soft signal ('not now'), not a fatal fault. The manager has no way to honor a veto (it does not skip the sleep on a false return); it just asserts and resets.
findings.impact: On a sealed UW_DOPPLER unit, any client that legitimately returns false on an LPM-enter/exit notification forces a full chip reset every time MGR_LPM_enter() runs (main-loop cadence). If a client's veto condition is persistent, this becomes a reset loop. The whole client/veto design is unusable: a 'no' from a client is treated as a brick-class assert rather than 'stay awake'. Latent today because the production UW_DOPPLER client returns true and resolves to NONE, but it is a live trap for GUI/STDLN and for any future client that uses the documented false return.
findings.recommendation: Do not assert on a false callback return. Honor the contract: on NotifEnter returning false, abort the sleep (skip the switch / treat as LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE for this cycle) and propagate the rejection upward; on NotifExit failure, log only. Reserve kns_assert for a genuinely impossible state, not for a documented client veto.

findings.description: Downgrade loop assumes the deepest_lpm bitmap value always has at least one bit at or below an allowed bit, but it can silently fall through to LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE without that being an error. More importantly, eMGR_LPM_clientRequest() returns LOW_POWER_MODE_SHUTDOWN (0x08, the deepest) as its default seed when mgrLpmClientNbr != 0 but every populated client returns a SHALLOWER mode via '<' comparison; that is correct. However, if a registered client's fpMGR_LPM_LpmReqCb is non-NULL while mgrLpmClientNbr was left stale (see decrement path), the seed SHUTDOWN can leak out. The deeper concern: the '<' comparison treats the enum's numeric ordering as the depth ordering — this is asserted only by a header comment (mgr_lpm.h:62-64), with no _Static_assert guarding NONE<SLEEP<STOP<STANDBY<SHUTDOWN. A future reorder of the enum silently inverts LPM selection.
findings.impact: A reordered/extended MgrLpm_LPM_t enum would silently pick the wrong (possibly deeper) sleep mode — e.g. SHUTDOWN where SLEEP was intended — bricking a sealed unit that then never wakes on the expected source. No compile-time protection today.
findings.recommendation: Add _Static_assert(LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE < LOW_POWER_MODE_SLEEP && LOW_POWER_MODE_SLEEP < LOW_POWER_MODE_STOP && LOW_POWER_MODE_STOP < LOW_POWER_MODE_STANDBY && LOW_POWER_MODE_STANDBY < LOW_POWER_MODE_SHUTDOWN, ...) so the depth invariant the algorithm relies on is enforced at build time.

findings.description: MGR_LPM_enter's switch sets mgr_lpm_ctxt->low_power_mode BEFORE calling the enter helper for STANDBY (line 142-143) and SHUTDOWN (line 146-147). vMGR_LPM_enterStandBy/Shutdown never return (they call HAL_PWR_EnterSTANDBY/SHUTDOWN then NVIC_SystemReset). For STANDBY/SHUTDOWN the ctxt write into RAM is pointless if RAM is not retained, but here lpm_ctxt lives in .lpmSection (retained BKP, lpm.c:117-120) — OK. The real issue: mgr_lpm_ctxt is dereferenced (line 131 etc.) with no NULL check. MGR_LPM_enter takes a raw pointer; a NULL ctxt (or the cast-from-BKP-struct in LPM_enter, lpm.c:780) faults inside the switch before any sleep, in the idle path of a sealed unit.
findings.impact: If any caller ever passes a NULL or misaligned mgr_lpm_ctxt, MGR_LPM_enter hard-faults in the main idle loop. Current sole caller passes &lpm_ctxt so not triggered today, but there is zero defensive check on a pointer that is written unconditionally in 5 switch arms.
findings.recommendation: Early-return KNS_STATUS_ERROR if mgr_lpm_ctxt == NULL at function entry (cheap, before any deref).

findings.description: mgrLpmClientTab[] and mgrLpmClientNbr are plain (non-volatile) file-scope globals mutated by register/unregister and read by MGR_LPM_enter/eMGR_LPM_clientRequest with no critical section. Verified all callers (lpm.c:775, kns_app_uw_doppler.c:1720, kns_app_doppler.c:699) register only at init from main context, and no runtime unregister exists, so there is no actual concurrent mutation today. Flagging because the table is the shared state the whole manager pivots on and the API is public (MGR_LPM_unregisterClient is exported) — a future AT-command-driven unregister would race the idle-loop MGR_LPM_enter with no protection.
findings.impact: No live race today (init-only registration). Latent: a runtime unregister concurrent with eMGR_LPM_clientRequest could read a half-cleared entry (function-pointer tearing on a non-atomic struct member set), potentially calling a stale/NULL callback.
findings.recommendation: Document the 'register at init only' invariant in the header, or wrap table mutation/iteration in __disable_irq()/__enable_irq() if runtime (re)registration is ever intended.

findings.description: mgrLpmClientNbr is effectively redundant bookkeeping. Its only read is the `== 0` fast-path in eMGR_LPM_clientRequest (line 175); the loop right below it (179-185) already skips NULL entries and would return the SHUTDOWN seed if all are NULL — but note that without the count check, an all-NULL table returns the seed SHUTDOWN, NOT NONE, so the counter's early-return is actually load-bearing for correctness, not pure dead code. It also is not static (no `static` qualifier) though it is not referenced in any other TU — it leaks a global symbol unnecessarily.
findings.impact: Symbol-pollution / maintenance smell only. The `==0` guard masks the fact that the all-NULL path of eMGR_LPM_clientRequest would otherwise wrongly return SHUTDOWN instead of NONE.
findings.recommendation: Either make the loop itself NONE-safe (seed deepest_lpm = LOW_POWER_MODE_NONE and track whether any client was consulted) and drop the counter, or mark mgrLpmClientNbr `static`. Same for mgrLpmClientTab (line 38) — not referenced cross-TU, should be static.

findings.description: On STM32WL55xx the STOP path calls HAL_PWREx_EnterSTOP2Mode (line 294, with EnterSTOP1Mode commented out at 293). For the sealed UW_DOPPLER target the production deep-sleep actually goes through the separate MGR_LPM_UW module (mgr_lpm_uw.c), and the kstk client returns NONE in MONITORING, so this generic STOP path is effectively dead in the sealed config (config-gated dead, not orphan). The preventive flag-clear block (lines 256-277) is documented as dormant. This is fine, but the comment at 270-277 force-sets PWR->C2CR1 LPMS to SHUTDOWN even on the STOP entry path; that is intentional ('no floor') but means a STOP request on WL55 reprograms the CPU2 mode floor to SHUTDOWN — correct per the comment, just non-obvious and worth a _Static_assert/centralization since it is duplicated verbatim in 3 helpers (lines 276, 319, 344) and in lpm.c:932.
findings.impact: No runtime defect. Maintenance hazard: the LPMS-floor MODIFY_REG is copy-pasted 4 times across two files; a fix in one site can drift from the others.
findings.recommendation: Factor the PWR->C2CR1 LPMS 'open the floor' write into a single inline helper shared by the three mgr_lpm.c helpers (and lpm.c) so the WL55 floor handling cannot drift.

findings.description: vMGR_LPM_enterStandBy and vMGR_LPM_enterShutdown call HAL_PWR_EnterSTANDBYMode()/HAL_PWREx_EnterSHUTDOWNMode() and then, if the chip did NOT actually power down (e.g. a pending wake flag makes the HAL call return), fall through to NVIC_SystemReset() then kns_assert(0). The NVIC_SystemReset is a reasonable recovery, but kns_assert(0) after it is unreachable-by-design dead code (reset never returns). More importantly, there is no clearing of a stale wake flag retry: if entry repeatedly returns immediately (sticky WUF the clears at 314-316/339-341 didn't catch), the result is a reset, which is acceptable but undocumented as the recovery contract.
findings.impact: Benign: reset is a safe fallback. kns_assert(0) at 325/350 is genuinely unreachable (post-reset) — harmless dead statement. The comment 'standby exit performs a reset of the uC' is correct but the manual NVIC_SystemReset is the real safety net for the no-power-down case.
findings.recommendation: Drop the unreachable kns_assert(0) after NVIC_SystemReset() (it can never run), or replace the pair with a tight for(;;) { NVIC_SystemReset(); } to make the 'never returns' intent explicit. No functional change.

findings.description: MGR_LPM_init, MGR_LPM_enter and all four enter-helpers take struct MgrLpm_EnvConfig_t BY VALUE (not const-ref). The struct is ~7 pointers + a byte (~32-60 bytes); each MGR_LPM_enter call copies it onto the stack and again into each helper. In the idle loop this is a per-iteration copy of a const config. Also env_config in the helpers is never modified -> should be const.
findings.impact: Minor stack/cycle overhead in the hottest idle path; no correctness issue. Misses const-correctness.
findings.recommendation: Pass `const struct MgrLpm_EnvConfig_t *` to the helpers and MGR_LPM_enter to avoid the repeated by-value copy and document immutability.

findings.description: Tests/unit/test_lpm_gating.c covers the CLIENT-side gating (uw_doppler_lpmReq/NotifEnter/Exit mirrors) but NOT the MGR_LPM core selection logic in this file: (a) eMGR_LPM_clientRequest picking the shallowest of several clients via the '<' comparison; (b) the allowedLPMbitmap downgrade loop (lines 113-117), including the case where the requested mode is not allowed and must degrade (e.g. client wants STOP, bitmap allows only SLEEP -> must yield SLEEP, and the all-disallowed -> NONE case); (c) the all-NULL-table -> NONE behavior that hinges on mgrLpmClientNbr; (d) register/unregister table fill/slot-reuse and duplicate-registration rejection (line 71-72). None of these have unit coverage.
findings.impact: The mode-selection arithmetic — the part most likely to silently pick the wrong sleep depth and brick a sealed unit — is untested. The downgrade loop and enum-ordering dependency are exactly the kind of logic a refactor could break unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: Add a unit suite that links the real eMGR_LPM_clientRequest/MGR_LPM_enter selection (with HAL enter-helpers mocked to no-op) and asserts: shallowest-of-N selection, bitmap downgrade for each allowed mask, all-disallowed -> NONE, duplicate register rejected (KNS_STATUS_ERROR), unregister-then-register slot reuse, and register-full table returns ERROR.

dead_code: Config-gated dead (not orphans): the STM32L476/WLE5/G491/L071 branches in vMGR_LPM_enterStop (lines 279-288) are dead for this WL55 product. The WL55 STOP path (vMGR_LPM_enterStop, 289-294) and the STOP preventive-clear block (256-277) are dormant in the sealed UW_DOPPLER config because the kstk client returns NONE in MONITORING and real deep-sleep uses the separate MGR_LPM_UW module — reachable in GUI/STDLN configs, so not removable. Genuinely unreachable statements: kns_assert(0) at lines 325 and 350 (placed AFTER NVIC_SystemReset(), which never returns) — harmless but dead. Redundant-but-load-bearing: mgrLpmClientNbr (line 39) is only read at line 175; without that guard the all-NULL path would mis-return SHUTDOWN, so it is not pure dead code. mgrLpmClientTab/mgrLpmClientNbr are non-static globals not referenced cross-TU (symbol leak, should be static).
test_coverage: Partial. Tests/unit/test_lpm_gating.c tests CLIENT-side mirrors (lpmReq boot-gate, NotifEnter/Exit NONE early-return) but does NOT exercise this file's core: client-request shallowest-of-N selection, the allowedLPMbitmap downgrade loop, all-NULL->NONE, or register/unregister table management. The mode-selection arithmetic — the highest-risk logic for picking a wrong/too-deep sleep on a sealed unit — has no unit coverage. See test-gap finding for the concrete suite to add.
